t: Auto enrolment
s: As the owners of this process the Pensions team should contact us about testing and implementing this process at the appropriate time. However, it is usually the case that we contact them. This is a legislative requirement that is carried out every three years.
ss: Auto-enrolment re-enrolment is a legislative pension process that updates Core|PAY every three years to automatically re-enrol eligible employees into their relevant pension scheme (OSPS, USS, NEST, or NHS) based on contract type and grade. HR Functional Analysts and the Payroll team manage testing and implementation through the Payroll Dashboard by updating pay group settings and verifying three standard scenarios: employees who opted out over 12 months ago, those contractually re-enrolled, and those who opted out within the last 12 months. Open this document when preparing for a scheduled re-enrolment exercise (typically June for the main University, next due June 2025) or when you need to understand the change management process, testing requirements, and employee communication steps involved.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing the Auto Enrolment re-enrolment process within Core|PAY, which is a mandatory legislative requirement carried out every three years to automatically re-enrol eligible employees into relevant pension schemes (OSPS, USS, NEST, or NHS) based on their contract type and grade. The document outlines that changes must be processed through the standard change management procedure by creating a change request in OSM, with HR Functional Analysts responsible for testing in collaboration with the Payroll team, and notes that re-enrolment periods are updated automatically so this may qualify as a Standard Change. The technical process involves navigating to Payroll Dashboard > UK Tax Rates > General > Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters, selecting Auto-Enrolment and then Pay Groups to manage the configuration settings for pay groups 20, 21 (main University) and 60 (Linacre College). Testing requires validation of three standard scenarios: employees who opted out more than 12 months ago (or earned over £833 in June if casual) should be auto-enrolled, those who opted out and were contractually re-enrolled should not be reassessed, and those who opted out less than 12 months ago should not be reassessed, with verification completed by reviewing employee records via Additional > Pension after May and June payroll runs. The Pensions team initiates the process and must contact affected employees at least six weeks before re-enrolment to provide advance notice, while also ensuring exclusions are properly identified for directors, proctors, and those with Fixed Protection status. For the main University, re-enrolment exercises occur in June (with the next scheduled for June 2025), while Linacre College conducts theirs in July (next due July 2023), and the SQL report titled "Employees who have opted out of a Pension scheme" and the standard report PERPEN15 are available to support identification of eligible employees.

t: Bank Sort Codes
s: The list of UK bank sort codes is periodically updated by external companies, and we must incorporate these updates into our list of sort codes within CoreHR’s reference library. We periodically receive a link to the updated list of UK sort codes in an email from helpdesk@mailservice.sortingcodeselectronic.co.uk. This email is sent to InternalServices@it.ox.ac.uk; it is then logged as an Incident in HEAT and assigned to the HRIS Analysis team for processing.
ss: Bank Sort Codes in CoreHR's reference library are periodically updated to reflect changes to UK banking data, and this document covers the approved process for incorporating those updates. The HRIS Analysis team receives updated sort code lists from an external provider, logs them as incidents in HEAT, and implements changes either by manual entry or bulk upload using the Data Migration tool. Open this document when you need to understand the change management workflow, testing requirements, or approval procedures for updating bank sort codes in Core|Personnel, or when troubleshooting outdated reference data that's causing user errors.
sl: This document provides the approved change management process for updating UK bank sort codes within CoreHR's reference system, which is owned and maintained by the HRIS Analysis team. The document describes two distinct methods for managing bank sort code changes: manual add/amend/remove operations processed as changes in OSM and approved by the Senior HRIS Analyst, and bulk uploads of new codes using CoreHR's Data Migration tool, which are managed as Standard Changes in OSM. When external companies periodically send updated UK sort code lists via email to helpdesk@mailservice.sortingcodeselectronic.co.uk, these notifications are logged as incidents in HEAT and assigned to the HRIS Analysis team for processing. The document details the complete change management workflow, including testing requirements in both UOXC/UOXU test environments before final migration to UOXP production, and includes a standardized template for documenting changes with specific fields such as Details, Justification, Risk Assessment, Testing Plan, and Back Out Plan. Bulk uploads require creating a test file with sample data, validating it through the Staff Portal Data Migration Tool, and then performing the full upload only after successful testing, with the ability to delete affected records from the "Maintain Bank Details" screen at Reference > Reference A–C > Bank Sort Codes if issues arise. The process handles the scenario where users would receive errors when attempting to enter sort codes not yet in the system, thus keeping reference data current and preventing operational disruptions. No formal business owner approval is required for Standard Changes if the documented process is followed, and no downtime or communications are necessary for sort code updates.

ss: This is a master index document organizing 51 change management knowledge articles across 8 topic areas, including payroll, people management, recruitment, time management (WFM), and system administration for HR systems like PeopleXD, CoreHR, and Power BI. Open this document when you need to locate specific change control guidance for PeopleXD or related HR systems—it serves as a navigation hub pointing you to detailed articles on processes like auto-enrolment, bank sort codes, pay codes, grades and rates, and portal configuration. Use it to quickly identify which knowledge article covers the change management process you're implementing, then follow the reference to the full documentation.
sl: This document is a comprehensive index of 51 change management knowledge articles organized across eight topic areas covering HR systems and processes within the PeopleXD, WFM, and Power BI/Reporting systems. The index encompasses articles on general change management processes including auto-enrolment and bank sort code updates, payroll and pension configuration such as casual payment submissions and pay codes, people management procedures like continuous service rules, recruitment and applicant tracking, system administration, reporting capabilities, time management and workforce management features, and various templates and reference materials. Specific processes described include the auto-enrolment legislative requirement carried out every three years by the Pensions team within PeopleXD, bank sort code updates received via email from external sorting code providers and processed through the HEAT incident system by the HRIS Analysis team, and payroll control reports generated for the payroll team's internal use to flag exceptions. Key configuration areas include portal configuration requiring HRSEG approval before implementation, grade and rates setup requiring confirmation from the Reward and HR Analytics Teams, and continuous service eligibility rules that must align with university policy. The document serves HR professionals, payroll administrators, system administrators, and change management teams who need to understand approved processes for implementing changes, who must approve requests, and how changes flow through the organization's change control governance. All changes referenced across these 51 articles must follow the standard change request and approval process in effect at the time of implementation, with many requiring oversight from governance bodies such as HRSEG or specific functional teams.

t: Payroll_Control Report
s: Payroll Dashboard: Payroll Checking Control Reports The payroll checking control reports are generated and used purely by the payroll team so any queries or requests would only be made via that route. The payroll team may utilise the information from the control reports to provide information to departments such as exceptions, but the control reports would not be available directly to departmental users of PeopleXD. Payroll are responsible for running the validation and...
ss: The Payroll Dashboard control reports—including the Nett Pay Curr-Prev Exceptions, Payroll Exceptions, and Payroll Controls (PAYB141) reports—help the payroll team validate and verify payroll accuracy by comparing pay periods, identifying exceptions, and tracking amendments. Open this document when you need to enable or configure a specific control report for a pay group, run validation checks after payroll processing, or understand which reports are available to identify errors and discrepancies in payroll data. The document walks through the technical setup in the Payroll Dashboard, approval processes via change management, and the testing requirements that must be completed before reports can be generated and sent to the Report Centre.
sl: This document is a change management guide for implementing and managing payroll checking control reports within the Payroll Dashboard system, specifically addressing how to enable the Nett Pay Curr-Prev Exceptions report for particular pay groups. The core technical process involves navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Pay Groups, selecting the affected pay group from the dropdown menu, navigating to the configuration page using the Next Page button, and populating the Net Pay Current/Previous Exception field with the relevant value (such as 0.10) before clicking Save. The document outlines the approval workflow requiring system owner sign-off via change request in OSM, typically managed as a minor change, and specifies that the HR Systems Functional Analysis team is responsible for testing with input from the payroll team, who must run validation job PAY140 before the reports become available. After validation completion, users can access control reports via Payroll Dashboard > Manage Payroll > Payroll Checking > Control Reports, where multiple report types are available including the Nett Pay Curr-Prev Exceptions Report (which compares current and previous period net pay), Payroll Exceptions Report (showing top/bottom 10 earners and observation messages), Payroll Controls report PAYB141 (verifying payroll balance and amendments), the Detailed Amendments Report, and the Gross to Nett Report. The payroll team exclusively generates and uses these reports internally, though they may share exception data with other departments such as the Linacre HR/Finance Administrator, and there are no integrated downstream systems dependent on these control reports. Communication is limited to keeping the change requestor informed, as only the payroll team are directly affected by this functionality.

t: Portal Configuration
s: A request for change could come from any source and are most likely to be a business requirement due to changes in existing process or implementation of new processes. Any changes to any area of the Portal must follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change. Changes may need to be presented at HRSEG for agreement before being implemented and possibly shared with the relevant POG.
ss: Portal Configuration covers the PeopleXD Portal change management process, including how to request, approve, test, and implement changes to recruitment, people management, and self-service dashboards. Use this document when you need to understand the consultation requirements, approval workflows, testing procedures, and communication steps required before modifying portal features, dashboards, or configurations. It provides guidance on stakeholder involvement—such as consulting the central recruitment team, Business Change, and the System Owner—and outlines downstream impacts like updates needed to training materials, QRGs, and Common Design Documents. This is your reference for following proper change control procedures and ensuring all affected systems and users are informed when portal modifications are made.
sl: This Portal Configuration document provides comprehensive guidance for managing changes to the PeopleXD Portal, a University system that includes multiple dashboards and modules for recruitment, people management, and employee self-service. The document outlines the complete change management workflow, requiring that all Portal modifications follow the University's Change Management process and be approved by the System Owner (Head of HRIS Support) via a change request in HEAT before implementation. Technical configuration changes are processed using the Dashboard Configuration tool and Language Pack, with guidance referencing the "HOW TO - Configure the Portal" document for adding, changing, or removing portal elements. Testing responsibilities fall to the HRIS Analyst team, who must validate changes across different user access roles and menu profiles—for example, changes to departmental user access should be tested using the relevant menu profiles assigned to those users. The document specifies that multiple stakeholder groups must be consulted (University central recruitment team, Business Change) and informed (departmental users via HRIS bulletin, first-line support team, HRIS Trainer) at appropriate stages in the process. Downstream impacts include updates to Quick Reference Guides (QRGs), training materials, Common Design Documents (CDDs) for six specific components including Recruitment Dashboard and Infrastructure settings, and standard reports that may be affected depending on the nature of the change. The document also covers technical specifications such as image size limits (background images under 10MB with maximum resolution of 4,000px width × 2,500px height, applied in release 28.0.43) and describes the structure of key dashboards including Employee Self Service (ESS), Manager Self Service (MSS), Recruitment Dashboard, People Management Dashboard, and HR Administration Dashboard, each containing specific tabs, sections, and widgets used by different user roles.

Changes to paycodes should be requested/approved by Payroll. Changes to visa restrictions/requirements will be requested by the Staff Immigration Team All changes will need to follow the standard change request and approval process in force at the time of...
ss: The Casual Payment Submission spreadsheet is an Excel-based tool used to submit casual worker payments and weekly working hours to the Payroll module and CorePay system. Open this document when you need to understand the approved process for requesting changes to the spreadsheet—such as updates to hourly rates following pay uplifts, paycode modifications, or visa-related adjustments—and when you're responsible for testing, implementing, or communicating those changes. It covers the full change management workflow including consultation and approval requirements (Payroll must approve all changes), testing responsibilities for the HRIS analyst team and Payroll, and communication plans for publishing updates. Use this as your reference for the technical specifications, validation rules, password protection details, and step-by-step guidance on editing and publishing the spreadsheet to users and downstream systems.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing changes to the Casual Payment Submission spreadsheet used in the payroll process, which was implemented in 2016 to ensure legal compliance for casual workers and support the capture of weekly working hours for Tier 4 workers. The spreadsheet is located at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Payroll\Casual payment submission spreadsheet and contains validation rules and macros that convert entered data into a format compatible with the payroll module, with protected sheets and hidden calculations to prevent unauthorized modifications. All changes to the spreadsheet must follow the standard change request and approval process, with specific routing requirements: pay uplift changes are requested through the pay uplift process by the Reward Team, paycode changes must be requested and approved by Payroll, and visa-related changes are submitted by the Staff Immigration Team. The change management process requires completion of a 14-section change template covering details, justification, impact assessment, testing plans, implementation approach, communications strategy, and back-out procedures, with approval from the Head of HR Systems. Testing responsibilities are divided among the HRIS analyst team (who test spreadsheet changes and dropdown validation), Payroll (who test uploading to CorePay), and potentially TSS for significant modifications, with specific pre-publication requirements including cursor positioning at cell A5, password protection, alphabetical sorting of paycodes, and ascending order for hourly rates. Implementation involves distributing the revised spreadsheet to Payroll for publication on the Finance website and directly emailing the TSS version, with user communication typically occurring through the HRIS bulletin and targeted emails when new versions are released.

t: Continuous Service
s: PeopleXD|People Management: Continuous Service PeopleXD holds rules which determine whether or not a given appointment is eligible to be counted towards an employee’s Continuous Service. Those rules must be aligned with the University’s policy around Continuous Service and should be updated whenever this policy changes or any aspect used within the configuration is added to. The configuration has been set up so that there shouldn’t need to be any reconfiguration required...
ss: The Continuous Service configuration in PeopleXD determines which employee appointments count toward continuous service eligibility based on University policy rules. Use this document when you need to understand the approval process, consultation requirements, and technical steps for updating continuous service rules—such as when the University's eligibility policy changes, new departments are added, or reference data like Employee Status is modified. You'll also find guidance on testing affected employees, documenting business decisions, and understanding how changes impact CoreTime long service leave calculations. Open this if you're responsible for maintaining HRIS configuration or need to coordinate a continuous service change request through the Business Change team.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing changes to the Continuous Service configuration within PeopleXD, the University's HRIS system, covering the complete lifecycle of raising, approving, implementing, and testing such changes. The document outlines that PeopleXD contains rules determining whether appointments count toward an employee's Continuous Service, and these rules must align with the University's Continuous Service policy, requiring updates whenever policy changes or new reference data such as Employee Status, Sub Division, or pay scales are added. The approved process for raising changes specifies that new "Societies" departments require business change consultation to determine eligibility, while standard departmental structures do not require reconfiguration, and any policy changes affecting eligibility or break-in-service rules must be submitted by the HR Policy Team and confirmed by the Business Change team before implementation. Changes are classified as minor change requests requiring approval from the Head of HR Systems, and technically are processed using a how-to guide located at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\How to guides\HOW TO - Maintain Continuous Service Eligibility Rules in the Portal.docx. Testing responsibilities include verifying continuous service calculations for affected employees, those transferring between eligible appointments, and reviewing impacts on long service awards for annual leave within Core Time if applicable. Implementation requires updating the configuration document and recording decisions in the final decisions and config document stored at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Continuous Service, as well as potentially updating the 'Staff Groups in Core' document and 'People Profile Matrix' managed by the Business Change team. The document notes that continuous service calculations are triggered by commencement, updates, or end of post appointments through a nightly database job, and can be accessed via CorePersonnel > Reference > Reference Q-Z > Service Rules > Eligible Service Rules, with manual override options available for dates and TUPE transfers. This guidance is primarily used by HR Systems administrators, Business Change teams, and HR Policy teams when managing changes to continuous service eligibility rules and their downstream impacts on long service leave entitlements.

t: Funding Source
s: HRSEG should be advised about the addition of data into this field, specifically HR Analystics and Reward Teams. The field is currently being used to capture sources of funding in line with the 2020 recruitment protocol so any changes must be made in line with this protocol while it is in place.
ss: The Funding Source field in Core|Recruit captures budget allocation information used in the 2020 recruitment protocol and staff request processes. Open this document when you need to add, modify, or remove funding source codes in the Reference Data section of the HR Admin Dashboard, or when implementing changes that affect how recruitment costs are tracked and reported. You'll also need this if you're updating processes that impact Staff Request and Recruitment users, since the HR Analytics team relies on this data for their protocol reports. The HRIS Analyst team uses this as a standard change that requires environment owner approval before implementation.
sl: This document provides a change management guide for the "Funding Source" field within the Core|Recruit system, specifically addressing how to manage funding source data in accordance with the 2020 recruitment protocol. The document outlines the complete lifecycle for managing funding sources, including the approved process for raising changes, consultation requirements with the HRSEG, HR Analytics, and Reward Teams, and the standard change approval process handled by the HRIS Analyst team. The technical implementation procedures are detailed with specific navigation paths: Core Portal > HR Admin Dashboard > Data Centre > Reference Data, where users can add new funding sources by enabling the active indicator, modify existing sources by amending code labels, or remove sources by toggling the active indicator on or off. The document addresses potential complications when removing funding sources, noting that fully inactive sources may not appear in the "cost allocation" screen within staff requests but will still display in the "advertisement" source of funds screen, and that only unused funding sources can be deleted entirely. Communications about any funding source changes must be distributed to Staff Request and Recruitment users to inform them of process modifications, and the HR Analytics team must be aware of changes since they maintain hard-coded rules related to this field in their 2020 recruitment protocol reporting. This document is primarily used by HRIS Analysts and system administrators who need to manage reference data configurations and ensure compliance with established recruitment protocols and downstream reporting requirements.

t: Grade and Rates
s: Grades and Rates Knowledge Article The Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming the rates for existing grades. Requests for the creation of any new grades should be raised through these teams, or via the HRSEG on which these teams are represented. To set up a new grade, the following items must be confirmed by the Reward and HR Analytics Teams: Grade Code (e.g.
ss: Employee grades and pay scales are managed through the HRIS system's People Management portal, with the Reward Team and HR Analytics Team responsible for creating new grades and confirming rates. Use this document when you need to understand the approved process for requesting grade changes, including required specifications (grade code, scale points, pay rates, full-time hours), consultation requirements with Payroll, Pensions, and X5 teams, and the change management approval workflow through OSM. This is essential reading before submitting any grade or rate change request to ensure you have all necessary approvals and documentation in place. The document also covers how grade changes impact downstream systems and employee records, and includes a template for formally raising changes in OSM.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing grades and rates within an organization's human resources system, covering the complete lifecycle from initial requests through implementation and downstream impacts. The document outlines that the Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming rates for existing grades, with new grade requests raised through these teams or via the HRSEG (Human Resources Systems Evaluation Group), and specifies the exact information required to establish a new grade including Grade Code, Grade Description, Scale Points, Scale Narrative, Bar Points, Yearly Full Time Rates, Full Time Hours, and the Effective Date. The change management process requires creating a change request in OSM (the organization's change management system) that must be approved by the relevant approver, ideally prior to QA testing, with the HRIS Functional Analysis Team responsible for implementing the setup of new grades and points in the People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Pay Scales section of the Portal. The document addresses specific scenarios such as removing scale points that fall below minimum Living Wage requirements, which necessitates moving affected employees to higher scale points, a task typically performed by the HRIS Data Service Administrator in consultation with individual departments. Multiple stakeholder teams must be consulted including Pensions (for Pension Scheme assignment), Payroll (for web publication via reports like PERCTR01_Staff Request List), and the X5 system team (for research grant costing tool integration), with the BFT Team and Financials FSM team requiring notification of potential downstream impacts related to GL to R12 interface changes. The document includes a detailed OSM change request template with 14 sections guiding users through documenting what is changing, the justification for the change, dependent changes, and impacts on connected systems, making it an essential reference for HR administrators and system support staff managing compensation structure modifications.

t: Pay Code Access Groups
s: A request for change could come from any source and is most likely to be a business requirement due to changes in existing process or implementation of new processes. Alternatively it could be a fix or enhancement that has been provided by the supplier. Any changes to any area of the Portal must follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change.
ss: Pay Code Groups in Core|WFM control which pay codes employees and managers can see and use when entering timesheets, absences, and time exceptions. Use this document when you need to create, modify, or remove pay code groups, or when you're implementing access controls to limit which pay codes are available to specific users or work groups. The document walks through the step-by-step process in the WFM Configuration settings and explains the required change management approvals, testing, and downstream impacts on linked work groups and reports. Open this if you're managing timesheet configuration, setting up employee or manager access restrictions, or handling a change request related to pay code availability.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to managing Pay Code Access Groups within the Core|WFM system, specifically detailing the change management processes and technical implementation steps required to configure pay code restrictions for employees and managers in timesheet and absence entry screens. The document covers the formal approval workflow, requiring changes to follow the organization's Change Management process with potential presentation to HRSEG and CoreTime POG for agreement, and mandating System Owner approval via change request in OSM before implementation. The technical "How to" section provides step-by-step instructions for navigating to WFM Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Configuration Settings > Pay Code Groups, where users can add new groups by entering a Group Code (maximum 6 characters) and Group Description (maximum 40 characters), then populate those groups by selecting individual pay codes from dropdown lists, with similar processes for modifying and removing pay codes from existing groups. The document explains that Pay Code Groups are linked to Work Groups and may require Systems Administrators to create corresponding work groups or establish linkages, and that these groups apply filtering rules across multiple screens including Timesheet Input, Absence Details, Time Exceptions, and back-office functions like Record Absence Details and Maintain Hours. Testing responsibility falls to the Functional Analyst team, who must validate changes in appropriate test environments across different user access roles, while communication to departmental users via HRIS bulletin, HR Systems support, and Business Change and Training teams must occur before implementation. The document clarifies that pay code groups are assigned at multiple hierarchy levels—System User/Organisational Role level takes precedence over Work Groups, with manager configuration defaulting to no grouping applied, meaning all pay codes are returned unless specifically restricted, and these groups are essential for enabling staff to record time against specific pay codes for Accrual Balances functionality.

t: Pay Codes (Allowances Deductions)
s: (Allowances/Deductions) The Payroll Team are responsible for raising a request for a new pay code or changes to an existing pay code. The Reward Team are also important in deciding which allowances we pay and record within the system and are responsible for informing the Payroll team and HR Systems (usually through HRSEG) of any changes to allowances/rates etc. The Payroll Team have a new pay code request template which must be used to record details of the pay code.
ss: Pay Codes in Core|Pay covers the process for creating and modifying allowances and deductions in the payroll system, including how to submit requests, define pay code details, and configure them for downstream systems like Student Loans and USS Pension. Use this document when you need to add a new pay code or change an existing one, as it outlines the consultation requirements with Payroll, Reward Team, and HR Analytics, plus the technical setup steps. It explains the approved workflow from initial request through testing and explains which teams are responsible for different aspects—such as whether departments or Payroll will administer the code and whether cost-of-living uplifts apply. Reference this guide to understand naming conventions, reporting inclusion decisions (like PERDEP20 and PERDEP01), and how percentage allowances must be configured with retro codes.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on the Core|Pay system's process for creating, modifying, and managing pay codes related to allowances and deductions within the payroll system. The document outlines that the Payroll Team is responsible for raising requests using a designated template saved to P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\pay codes, and requires confirmation of specific details including whether the pay code applies to clinical allowances, Linacre College reporting inclusion, and student loan or USS Pension Cash Supplement integration. The Reward Team must provide additional information such as who administers the pay code, whether pay uplift applies, and details for inclusion in the Allowance Guide and reports (PERDEP20 and PERDEP01), which are recorded in the Pay Code List spreadsheet at P:\PUBLIC\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Pay Codes\Pay Code List v5.0.xlsx. The HR Analytics Team and Reward Team must be consulted early in the process as they may require report amendments and need to approve allowance descriptions before implementation. Pay codes are technically set up by the HRIS Functional Analyst team following detailed guidance in the HOW TO_Maintain Pay Codes document, with particular attention required for percentage allowances in software version 26 and above, which must have two retro codes: a system retro code (starting with 9, prefixed "SYS –") set to a multiplier of 0, and a manual retro code for Payroll use. The type of change classification—whether minor/locally approved or requiring Change Management sign-off—depends on the pay code's breadth of use and communication requirements, and all changes must be recorded through a change request in OSM for testing and production migration.

t: Payroll Officer Calculations
s: The Payroll team is responsible for informing the HR Functional Analysis team of any changes to the Payroll Officer calculations used across the catalogue of reports. A member of Payroll (normally the Payroll Systems Administrator, Tracy Roberts) will raise an incident with the HRIS Support Centre detailing the changes to be made to the different calculation variants (New Starter, Leaver, Pay Audit, and Casual Worker). HR Functional Analysis will then raise a change...
ss: Payroll Officer calculations are used across HR Reporting reports to assign departments and divisions to specific payroll officers, and this document outlines the process for updating them when organizational changes occur. The Payroll team initiates change requests through the HRIS Support Centre, specifying updates to calculation variants (New Starter, Leaver, Pay Audit, and Casual Worker), which the HR Functional Analysis team then implements in SQL code within .RDL report files. You would open this document when you need to modify a Payroll Officer calculation in the HR Reporting system, understand the approval and testing workflow, or determine which teams own each step of the change process.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing changes to Payroll Officer calculations within the Core|BI system, detailing the workflows, responsibilities, and technical procedures required when updates are needed. The Payroll team, typically led by the Payroll Systems Administrator Tracy Roberts, must first raise an incident with the HRIS Support Centre specifying changes to the four calculation variants (New Starter, Leaver, Pay Audit, and Casual Worker), which HR Functional Analysis then converts into a formal change request. Changes to Payroll Officer calculations are classified as Minor Changes within OSM and require approval from the Head of HR Systems (Jenny Lister) before implementation on the HR Reporting LIVE server. Technically, Payroll Officers calculations are embedded within SQL queries in .RDL files that can be accessed in Visual Studio by searching for "payroll_officer" in the main report dataset, where only the yellow-highlighted CASE WHEN logic section is editable. The HR Functional Analysis team owns the process of updating the affected reports, and they must replace only the editable portion of the calculation (beginning with CASE WHEN) with the new logic provided by Payroll, which specifies which officers are responsible for which departments and divisions using department/division codes like 'AJDEP' or 'ACDIV'. After making changes to the .RDL file, the updated report must be deployed to the HR Reporting QA server where the Payroll team conducts testing and validation before final OSM change approval and implementation to the LIVE environment. This document also references downstream impacts on affected reports and shared data sets, establishing a structured change control process that ensures the accuracy of payroll officer assignments across the HR reporting catalogue.

t: Pension Scheme
s: New Pension Schemes The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for requesting the creation of new pension schemes. Pensions should discuss the requirements for the new pension scheme with Payroll. Payroll must then complete a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and send it through to the HRIS Support Centre, together with details of any new or amended pay codes which are required to support the new scheme.
ss: Pension Scheme covers the Core|Pay system processes for setting up new pension schemes, modifying existing schemes, and managing related configuration in the HRIS environment. Use this document when you need to understand the approved workflow for requesting pension scheme changes—including new schemes, contribution rate updates, State Pension Age adjustments, auto-enrolment modifications, report changes, and Profund Interface updates. The document outlines which teams (Pensions, Payroll, HRIS Functional Analysis) are responsible at each stage, what documentation and approvals are required, and how changes flow through OSM change management. Open this if you're setting up a pension scheme request, need to know who to contact, or want to understand testing and sign-off requirements before implementation.
sl: This document outlines the Core|Pay pension scheme change management procedures for organizations using the HRIS system, covering the approved processes, approval workflows, and implementation steps required when creating new pension schemes or modifying existing ones. The document describes five main categories of changes: new pension scheme creation, modifications to existing schemes, State Pension Age (SPA) updates, Auto-Enrolment functionality changes, and pension report modifications, each with defined responsibilities for the Pensions team, Payroll team, and HRIS Functional Analysis team. For new pension schemes, the Payroll team completes a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and submits it to the HRIS Support Centre along with details of any new or amended pay codes, after which the HRIS Functional Analysis team processes the request as a change within OSM (organizational service management). Changes to contribution rates, State Pension Age parameters, Auto-Enrolment parameters (including earnings thresholds and default schemes), and pension reports all follow similar workflows requiring support-desk calls from the Pensions team and testing coordination between the Functional Analysis team and relevant stakeholders. The document addresses specific integrations including the Profund Interface (requiring coordination with The Access Group Community service desk for updates to the PERPEN26 report) and USS Interface configuration for new USS pension schemes. Key stakeholders include the Pensions team as business owner, the Payroll team who must sign off on all changes before going live, and the Head of HR Systems who must approve changes before implementation in the live environment. The document has evolved through multiple versions since July 2015, with the most recent update in December 2023 including information about the Auto Enrolment PDF documentation location and navigation updates following a portal migration.

t: Pension Scheme
s: New Pension Schemes The Payroll and Pensions teams are responsible for requesting the creation of new pension schemes. Pensions should discuss the requirements for the new pension scheme with Payroll. Payroll must then complete a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and send it through to the HRIS Support Centre, together with details of any new or amended pay codes which are required to support the new scheme.
ss: The Core|Pay system manages pension scheme setup and changes, including new schemes, contribution rate updates, State Pension Age parameters, auto-enrolment functionality, and related reports. Use this document when the Pensions or Payroll teams need to create a new pension scheme, modify an existing scheme's details, adjust auto-enrolment settings, or request changes to pension reporting. It outlines the approved process for submitting requests through the HRIS Support Centre, required approvals from Payroll, testing procedures, and interfaces with systems like Profund and USS. Open this if you're involved in pension administration changes and need to understand the proper workflow, required documentation, and stakeholder consultation steps.
sl: This document outlines the procedures for managing pension schemes within the Core|Pay system, covering the creation of new pension schemes, modifications to existing schemes, and related administrative changes. The Payroll and Pensions teams initiate requests for new pension schemes by completing a Pension Scheme Template spreadsheet and submitting it to the HRIS Support Centre, where the HRIS Functional Analysis team processes the request as a change within the OSM system; similar support-desk call procedures apply for modifications to existing schemes, State Pension Age updates, Auto-Enrolment changes, pension reports, and Profund Interface configurations. The document specifies that changes to contribution rates must be accompanied by the official schedule of contributions from the scheme provider, and that the Pensions team should provide several months' advance notice to allow adequate testing in a test environment. All changes require consultation and sign-off between the Pensions team (business owner), Payroll team, and HRIS Functional Analysis team, with testing completed before implementations go live. The document also addresses specialized integrations including the USS Interface configuration for new USS pension schemes and the Profund Interface Report (PERPEN26), which requires coordination with The Access Group for mapping new schemes and Additional Voluntary Contribution (AVC) arrangements to relevant report fields and pay codes. This guide is used by Payroll, Pensions, and HRIS support teams throughout the change management process to ensure proper governance, testing, and system configuration when pension scheme modifications occur.

t: Diversity and Disability
s: The requirement for changing this data may be as a result of requirements for the HESA return or other legislative changes relating to any element of the Diversity or Disability data. EDU effectively ‘own’ the diversity and disability data. Any proposed changes that have not come from the EDU team must be confirmed with them in advance of the changes being made.
ss: Diversity and disability data management in Core|People covers how to add, update, and remove diversity and disability fields across the recruitment application forms, reference data, and Employee Self Service within the HRIS system. Use this document when you need to change diversity or disability data fields, modify equal opportunities monitoring options, or update related configurations in line with HESA returns or legislative requirements. You'll also need it to understand the approval process, which requires consultation with the EDU team and HR Analytics before implementation, and to identify which PERDEP reports may be affected by your changes. Open this guide whenever you're planning a change to diversity or disability data to ensure you follow the proper change management route and notify all required stakeholders.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive change management guide for modifying diversity and disability data within the Core|People Management system, covering the complete lifecycle from approval through implementation and testing. The document specifies that the EDU team owns diversity and disability data, and any proposed changes must be confirmed with EDU in advance and discussed with the HR Analytics team due to potential impacts on statutory reporting, with additional consultation required from Pension administrators if pension reports are affected. All changes must follow the standard Change Management process by raising a request in OSM and obtaining approval from the Head of HR Systems or their nominated deputy before proceeding. The technical implementation sections detail specific navigation paths for adding, updating, or removing diversity data, including access points such as Recruitment Toolbox > Recruitment Admin > Equal Opportunities Monitoring for application form templates, People Management > Reference Data for reference items, and People Management > HR Admin Setup setting > Diversity Config for Employee Self Service fields, with a note that diversity details must be changed individually in each form profile. Hard-coded field labels can be edited through Admin Dashboard > Admin > Language Pack, and similar updates may be required across multiple PERDEP reports (such as PERDEP01 variants and PERDEP09) that contain hard-coded diversity and disability fields. Testing responsibilities typically fall to Functional Analysts for initial changes, with the HR Analytics and EDU teams conducting further testing depending on the nature and reason for changes, with standard testing including Employee Self Service functionality and applicant vacancy processes. Communication about changes may range from low-key updates to HR data policy to inclusion in user bulletins, typically occurring around the time of implementation or shortly thereafter, depending on the scope and significance of the modifications being made.

s: Core Portal|Employee Self Service Approved process for raising - TBC A request for change is likely to be the result of a Business Change Process or possibly a technical fix. Consultation & Approval - TBC There are a number of groups who may need to approve changes to the ESS and/or MSS portal before they are made. As a guide approval should be sought from the following as applicable: HR Policy team about Contract Details and what Managers have access to, Equality and...
ss: The Employee Self Service (ESS) and Manager Self Service (MSS) portals in Core Portal allow employees and managers to view and update HR information including contracts, personal details, payslips, and P60s. This document covers the change management process for modifying these portals, including how to add, change, or remove elements like email notifications, payroll calendars, workgroups, and field names through CoreHR and Core Portal back office settings. Open this if you need to request or implement a change to ESS/MSS functionality, understand the approval workflow involving HR, Payroll, and the System Owner, or learn the technical navigation steps for common portal modifications.
sl: This document serves as a comprehensive guide for managing changes to the Employee Self Service (ESS) and Manager Self Service (MSS) portals within the Core Portal system. The document outlines the complete change management workflow, including the required approvals from multiple stakeholder teams such as HR Policy, Payroll, HR Information, and Staff Immigration teams, with final system approval required from the Head of HRIS Support via a change request in HEAT. It provides specific technical instructions for adding, changing, and removing system components, including navigation paths such as CoreHR > Utilities > HR Event Configuration for email notifications, Core|Portal>Back Office LINK > Admin Settings > Payroll Calendar Parameters for payroll calendars, and Portal|Administrator Dashboard > Language Pack for updating field names and descriptions. The document identifies key configuration areas managed by System Administrators, particularly workgroups that are essential for Manager Self Service functionality and are maintained through People Management > Employee Administration > Maintain Organisation Roles. It addresses critical operational processes including payroll calendar management, where separate calendars must be created annually for each pay group, and explains how the ESS landing page displays pay day information through the Important Dates section. The document is designed for HRIS Support Centre staff and System Administrators who implement changes, along with designated approvers and testers, providing them with standardized procedures, standard icons and button terminology, and guidance on downstream system impacts and affected reports such as PERDEP20 Monthly Personnel Changes.

t: Employee Status
s: Auto-summary unavailable. See source for details.
ss: Employee Status in Core|Personnel covers the process for adding, changing, or removing employee status codes in your HRIS system and the downstream impacts of those changes. Use this document when you need to understand how employee status changes affect related systems including Continuous Service rules, CoreTime balance pro-rata entitlements, payroll interfaces, and reports like PERDEP02. It outlines the approval workflows, testing requirements, and which teams need to be consulted or informed before implementing any employee status modifications. Open this if you're managing a change that involves new employee classifications or status types across your organization.
sl: This document from the Change Management function provides a structured guide for managing changes to employee status information within the Core|Personnel system. The document outlines the framework for raising, consulting on, and implementing employee status changes, though many specific approval routes and ownership details are marked as "TBC" (to be confirmed). The "How to" section references technical processes for adding, changing, and removing employee status records, along with standard system icons, button names, and navigation paths formatted as Core|Personnel menu routes. The document identifies critical downstream system impacts, including the requirement to update Continuous Service rules for each affected staff sub-group or department, and the necessity to map new employee statuses to all existing and future Core Time Balance pro-rata entitlements. Any employee status changes are expected to affect filtering logic in system interfaces and may impact the PERDEP02 suite of reports, which currently maintains a custom list of values (LOV) containing FIXED TERM, NON EMPLOYEE, and WORKER statuses. This document is typically used by HR system administrators, change managers, and HRIS Support Centre personnel who need to implement employee status modifications while ensuring consistency across related processes and reporting systems.

t: Job Titles
s: Requests for Job Titles or Post Titles can be made by any user of Core or consumer of its information. It should ideally be requested with the following information although my not be dependent upon the individual raising: Job Title Description (mandatory) Job Title Code (max 6 chars – alpha numeric) Is the Job Title to be active on Staff Requests? Is the job title to be used for casuals or non-employees?
ss: The Core|Personnel system uses a standardized process for adding, changing, or removing job titles that must follow consultation and approval workflows with the HRSEG group and Reward Team. Open this document when you need to submit a new job title request, understand who must approve it, or learn how job title changes flow through downstream systems like X5 and affect staff request options. The process ensures job titles remain generic descriptions of roles rather than seniority markers, and coordinates updates across the HRIS system and related reporting tools.
sl: This document outlines the complete process for managing job title changes within the Core|Personnel HRIS system, covering everything from initial requests through implementation and downstream effects. Any user or information consumer can submit a job title request by providing a mandatory Job Title Description and optional Job Title Code (maximum 6 alphanumeric characters), along with specifications about whether the title should be active on Staff Requests or used for casual and non-employee positions. The HRIS Support Centre must validate new requests against existing titles and reject any submissions where the Job Title Description inappropriately includes grade or seniority indicators, as generic job titles should not reflect such distinctions. All new job title requests require consultation and approval from the HRSEG group, with Liz Mitchell or an HR Information Team representative providing formal approval, though the Reward Team makes the final decision on Staff Request activation. The technical implementation follows section 7.12 (Job Title Codes) in the "HOW TO – View and Maintain Reference Data v26" document for adding, changing, or removing job titles, and Susanne Hemmerich (Head of HRIS Support Centre) must approve the change request in HEAT as a standard change rather than an enhancement request. Critical downstream processes include notifying the X5 team before implementing changes so matching job titles can be set up in advance, updating the published "List of Job Titles on Core" document, and communicating all new titles to HRIS system users via the HRIS Bulletin. For casual or non-employee-only job titles, the code should begin with "Z%" to ensure proper exclusion from relevant interfaces; otherwise codes without this prefix should be used to allow inclusion in appropriate data feeds.

f: Leaving Reason and Location after Leaving Knowledge Article_V0.2.docx
s: Changes should be requested by the HRIS Analysis team and authorised via a change request in OSM following the approved change request process. Requests may need to be taken to HRSEG. However, as the data is used for HESA reporting if a change has not been requested by the HR Analytics team they must be consulted before any changes are made.
ss: Managing Leaving Reason Codes, Location after Leaving (LVDEST), and Leaving Destination (LOCLEA) codes in Core|Portal through People Management Reference Data is covered in this process document. Use this when you need to add, edit, or retire employee departure-related reference codes in the HRIS system, or when you're implementing changes that affect how employee exits are categorized and reported. This document guides you through the technical steps in test environments, approval workflows via OSM and HEAT, and required notifications to HR Analytics and Payroll teams. Open it if you're responsible for maintaining HR reference data or supporting employee termination processes in People XD.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance for managing leaving reason codes, location after leaving codes (LVDEST), and leaving destination codes (LOCLEA) within the Core|Portal > People Management > Reference Data section of an HRIS system. The document outlines the approved process for raising changes, which requires requests to be submitted by the HRIS Analysis team and authorized via change request in OSM, with consultation from the HR Analytics team if HESA reporting is affected and potential approval from HRSEG. Technical implementation involves navigating to specific menu paths (Core|Portal > People Management > Reference Data > Leaving Reason Codes for leaving reasons, and Other References for LVDEST and LOCLEA codes), where users can add new codes by clicking the ADD button and entering code, description, and active status details, or edit existing codes by locating and modifying them in the system. The document addresses the common scenario where leaving codes are no longer needed by requiring them to be marked as "Do Not use" and potentially prefixed with "ZZ" rather than being deleted. Changes requiring location code creation in HRISPRD must follow standard change procedures in HEAT with Senior HRIS Analyst authorization and must be tested in HRISTEST and HRISQA environments before production implementation. Testing is typically performed by the Functional Analysts Team through opening an employee contract record and confirming the new codes are selectable, while communications must be sent to the HR Analytics team, Payroll, and HR Systems Support before or after implementation depending on who requested the change.

t: Location
s: The standard process for creating or amending a location code is for the request to be made via an Incident that will be assigned to the Functional Analysis team within OSM. It should be clear from the Incident if the request is for a new location or an amendment to an existing location. Full address details should be provided in order to determine the requirements of the change.
ss: Location codes in PeopleXD control where employees are assigned for payroll and reporting purposes, including address details and messenger delivery area codes. Use this document when you need to create a new location code, update an existing one, or understand how location changes affect payslips and downstream systems like the departments database. Follow the approved process outlined here to submit requests through an Incident to the Functional Analysis team, ensure proper testing, and notify UAS Payroll before implementation. This is essential reading if departments request location changes or if you're managing reference data in the Core|Personnel system.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on the approved process for creating and amending location codes within the Core|Personnel system in PeopleXD, covering the complete lifecycle from initial request through implementation and testing. Location code requests must be submitted via an Incident assigned to the Functional Analysis team within OSM, clearly indicating whether the request is for a new location or an amendment to an existing one, and should include full address details to determine change requirements. The location description must follow a specific format of a 2-digit alphanumeric code followed by a hyphen and space, with a maximum of 34 characters total, such as "AL – BIOCHEMISTRY," because this format is required for downstream interface compatibility and payslip display (limited to 25 characters). The area code, known colloquially as the "Beat Bike" number, is a messenger code maintained by Data Services in an Access database and can be verified using the PERSUP06 report or reference data files stored in P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Locations. Changes to existing location codes affect all employees assigned to that code, necessitating verification that all impacted employees are covered or that employees be shifted to alternative codes before implementation. The standard change process requires cloning change 20006881 in UOXP with 12 mandatory sections covering details, justification, impact assessment, and a testing plan that includes confirming the new location appears in the Location LOV on the Amend Appointment screen. Implementation is the responsibility of the Functional Analysis team in conjunction with the Data Services team, who must also update the departments database, and the Payroll team must be notified via payroll@admin.ox.ac.uk prior to implementation when existing locations are updated.

t: Maintain Position Types
s: Maintain Position Type Knowledge Article The Standard process for creating or amending a Position Type is for the request to be made via an Incident that will be assigned to the Functional Analysis team within OSM the Oxford Service Management tool. It should be clear from the incident if the request is for a new Position Type or an amendment to an existing. Position Types are linked heavily with the Staff Request process.
ss: Position Types are reference data codes in PeopleXD that categorize staff positions and appear on the Staff Request form for users to select from. Use this document when you need to create, modify, or remove a Position Type code, or when you're implementing changes to how positions are classified in your organization. All requests must be submitted as incidents through OSM (Oxford Service Management tool) to the Functional Analysis team, and changes are classified as Minor Changes requiring UAT testing before production deployment. The Reward Team owns approval of new Position Types or amendments, while HR Systems maintains the data in PeopleXD.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing Position Types within the PeopleXD system, covering the complete lifecycle from creation through modification and removal of position type codes. All requests to create or amend Position Types must be submitted as incidents through OSM (Oxford Service Management tool) and assigned to the Functional Analysis team, with the Reward Team responsible for approving the changes and the HR Systems team responsible for maintaining data within PeopleXD. Position Type changes are classified as Minor Changes within OSM and require testing in a UAT environment before deployment to the live production environment. The technical process involves navigating to PeopleXD > People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Position Types, where users can add new codes by clicking the Add button, update descriptions (limited to 40 characters including spaces), or delete unused codes via the Ellipses button. Once a Position Type Code is used in the Recruitment Table through a Staff Request or Vacancy, it cannot be deleted or marked inactive; instead, obsolete codes must be renamed with the prefix "ZZ DO NOT USE" followed by the original description in parentheses. Functional testing should verify that new or amended codes work correctly on Staff Request and Vacancy Profile screens, while User Acceptance Testing ensures the changes align with the Reward Team's processes. The Reward Team is responsible for communicating changes to stakeholders, and related documentation such as the Staff Request Decision Matrix and Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) must be reviewed and updated following any modifications to Position Types.

ss: Organisational structure changes in Core|HR cover adding, renaming, moving, or removing departments and units within your company hierarchy. Use this document when you need to request or implement structural changes—such as creating new departments, updating department names, reorganizing reporting lines, or deleting obsolete units. You'll also need it to understand the approval process (which requires PRAS authorization and OSM change requests), manage employee transfers during restructures using the Data Services Team, and coordinate with HR Analytics on data quality. Open this when planning organizational changes or processing restructuring requests that come through annually (typically July/August) or as ad hoc updates.
sl: This Core|HR document provides comprehensive guidance on managing organisational structure changes within the HR Information System, covering the complete lifecycle from approval through implementation and testing. The document outlines the approved process for raising changes, which must be requested by Functional Analysts and authorised via change requests in OSM, with requests typically coming from PRAS either ad hoc or during the annual organisation chart cycle in July/August. It details specific technical procedures for common tasks including navigating to Core Personnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy to add new departments or units, using People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data to change names, and employing the Post Restructuring Tool for moving departments. The document addresses critical governance requirements, specifying that permanent system changes must be approved by the System Owner or their deputy before implementation, while temporary changes to enable user access updates can be made as standard changes. It identifies key stakeholders including the Data Service Team and HR Analytics Team, who must coordinate on timescales and data quality when employee records are transferred using the Restructure Tool, and provides audit guidance that while routine changes like creating or renaming departments do not require full testing, at least one example of each change type should be tested for compliance purposes. The guidance also covers edge cases such as conditions under which historical department codes can be reused and procedures for removing departments completely, including the use of the PERDEP01 Discoverer report to verify no active employees remain.

t: Personal Titles
s: Requests can be made from a variety of sources, the list of titles is used in multiple downstream systems which may rely on a unified list, the list of titles is used in e-Recruitment as well as People Management so requests may come from applicants or staff. HRSEG must be consulted on any request to add new titles, new title requests will be accepted or rejected by HRSEG and any agreed new title must be authorised by the HR Policy Team.
ss: Personal titles in CoreHR are maintained through People Management > Reference Data > Title Setup, where you can add, edit, or remove job titles used across multiple systems including e-Recruitment, UniCard, USS Pensions, and SAP Concur. When you make any changes to titles, you must notify the Pensions team, Card Office, Finance team, and the SSM-BITE integration team, as title changes automatically propagate to downstream systems and databases. Open this document when you need to request a new job title, modify an existing one, or understand the approval workflow and system impacts before making changes to the CoreHR titles list.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance for managing personal titles within the CoreHR system's People Management module, specifically covering how to add, edit, and remove titles through the Reference Data > Title Setup menu path. The document outlines the complete change management process, including that requests for new titles must be consulted with HRSEG for acceptance or rejection and then authorized by the HR Policy Team, as the title list serves multiple downstream systems and is used in both e-Recruitment and People Management. The technical procedures are straightforward: to add a new title, users navigate to People Management > Reference Data > Title Setup and click ADD to insert a new row with the Active button automatically enabled, while editing involves locating and overtyping existing details, and removal requires toggling the Active button to OFF, with all changes requiring updates to the master document located at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Titles\Current List of CoreHR Titles.xlsx. The document details critical downstream system integrations that must be managed whenever titles change, including the USS Pensions interface (which requires mapping new titles to USS Mapped Codes through CoreHR > Core DataTalk > Data Mapping: USSTTL), the UNICARD system (which filters titles through a gen_lookup_values mapping table to suppress non-professional titles like "Mr" and "Ms" from displaying on staff ID cards and requires SSM-BITE team involvement via OSM tasks), SAP Concur (which requires Finance team notification for title mapping updates), and the X5 system (which receives title data via CoreXD feed INT.027). Communications requirements stipulate that the Card Office, Finance team, and Pensions team must be notified whenever titles are added, removed, or changed, and the document emphasizes that the master title list must be manually checked and updated each time Core releases a new version to ensure consistency across all systems.

t: Reason Codes
s: Normally raised by a member of HRSEG for a specific purpose. May also be requested by a department as an enhancement request. The following information must be gathered when requesting a new reason code: Reason Code (6 alpha characters) Reason Code Description (max 40 characters) The deadline for the code be made active Person responsible/contact for follow up queries Intended purpose of reason code Does the new reason code need to be included in the PERDEP45 report?
ss: Reason Codes in Core|Personnel are used to track the purpose of salary and appointment changes within PeopleXD. This document covers the complete change management process for adding, amending, or deleting reason codes, including consultation requirements with HR Information, Reward, and Payroll teams, and approval workflows through the HRIS Support Centre. Open this guide when you need to create a new reason code, understand who must approve changes, or ensure that downstream systems like PERDEP45 reports and SSRS datasets are properly updated. It also documents known system issues with allowance reason codes and testing requirements to verify codes appear correctly in the system's lookup values.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance for managing reason codes in the Core Personnel system within the Change Management framework. It covers the complete lifecycle of reason code administration, including the approved process for raising requests (which normally originate from HRSEG members or department enhancement requests), the specific information that must be gathered such as the 6-character alpha code, description, deadline, and intended purpose, and the consultation requirements with HR Information, Reward, and Payroll teams. The technical implementation is classified as a "Minor" change managed through OSM, with approval required from the Senior HRIS Analyst before deployment to the live UOXP environment, and the actual steps for creating, amending, or deleting codes are found in the referenced "HOW TO - View and Maintain Reference Data" guidance document. Testing responsibilities fall to the HRIS Analyst managing the change, with standard tests including verification that new or amended codes appear correctly in the Reason Code LOV (List of Values) under both "Amend Pay Rate" and "Amend Appointment" screens, and that deleted codes no longer appear in these LOVs. The document details critical downstream impacts including updates required to SSRS datasets (LOV_Optional_AbsenceReason, LOV_Optional_AbsenceStartReasons, and LOV_Optional_AbsenceReturnReasons) when absence-related codes are created, amended, or deleted, and highlights a known PeopleXD system issue where allowances data-migrated without reason codes cannot be ended if the Amendment Reason Required field is set as mandatory. All users must be informed of reason code changes through the HRIS Bulletin or email to hris-all-users@maillist.admin.ox.ac.uk, and the document emphasizes that user guidance documents (QRGs) should be reviewed and updated as part of the change process to reflect new or amended codes.

t: Reference Data
s: Dec 20 | 0.2 | HC | Reviewed following the implementation of V28 in the Portal A request for change to reference data could come from any source and may often be the result of legislative changes or a business Requirement. Changes should follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change. Some will be standard changes that do not require approval, e.g. a new location code.
ss: Reference data maintenance across all Core|HR modules covers the complete process for adding, changing, and removing reference items like location codes, pay groups, and recruitment data within the system. Use this document when you need to understand the approval workflows, change management procedures, and technical steps required before modifying reference data in the Portal or back office. It guides you through consultation requirements, testing protocols, and communication planning, as well as how to handle scenarios where reference data is already in use in the database. This is essential reading for HRIS analysts and change requestors who need to follow the proper governance and implementation process for any reference data updates.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for maintaining reference data across all modules within the Core|HR system, addressing the complete lifecycle of reference data changes from initiation through implementation. The document outlines the approved process for raising reference data changes, which may originate from any source including legislative requirements or business needs, and specifies that changes must follow the organization's Change Management process, with some standard changes (such as new location codes) requiring no approval while others require approval via Change Request in HEAT or presentation to HRSEG. It details the consultation and approval requirements, explaining that stakeholders relevant to the specific reference data being changed must be consulted, and that system changes require approval from the System Owner (Head of HRIS Support) or their nominated deputy before implementation. The "How to" section provides technical navigation paths for adding, changing, or removing reference data items, which are primarily accessed through Core|Portal>People Management>Data Centre>Reference Data or through the back office via Core Personnel > Reference with alphabetically organized categories (A-C, D-J, K-P, Q-Z). The document addresses the critical scenario of removing reference data by explaining that items can only be deleted if not in use within the database, and if an item is in use, the preferred practice is to rename it with a prefix such as "Z – DO NOT USE" rather than delete it, or alternatively to deactivate it using an Active flag if available. Additional responsibilities outlined include testing in relevant test environments before promotion to live (typically performed by HRIS Support Centre with stakeholder testing for specialized areas like Payroll or Immigration), communicating changes to users via monthly HRIS bulletins or targeted emails, updating Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) and relevant reports, and consulting supporting documentation such as the Common Design Document (CDD) and Reference Data Master (RDM) for detailed field utilization information.

t: Training Module
s: A request could come from any user or potential user of the module. The request should be reviewed by the Business Process Adviser and HRIS trainer in the first instance. Any changes must follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change.
ss: The Core|Personnel Training Module handles the creation, modification, and removal of training courses and related data within the HRIS system, used by the HRIS Support Centre, Oxford Learning Institute, and Bodleian Libraries. Open this document when you need to understand the approval process for training module changes, including who must review requests, how to implement changes in the system, and what testing and communications are required. You'll also find guidance on system navigation, downstream impacts on reports and quick reference guides, and critical configuration rules such as the "All Personnel" flag that must remain unticked to prevent unintended qualification assignments. Use this as your reference for managing any modifications to training administration processes in Core|Personnel.
sl: This document is a training module guide within the Core|Personnel system that outlines the approved processes, procedures, and governance for managing changes to the Training Module used across the University of Oxford. The document establishes that any change requests to the Training Module must first be reviewed by the Business Process Adviser and HRIS trainer, then follow the formal Change Management process, with final approval required from the System Owner (Head of HRIS Support) or their nominated deputy via a change request submitted in HEAT before implementation. The module is owned and managed by the HRIS Support Centre but is also used by other departments including Oxford Learning Institute and Bodleian Libraries, with previous users such as the Ashmolean Museum and UAS Finance whose current usage status is unclear. Key technical guidance includes navigation paths through the Core|Personnel menu structure, standard button names and icons used in the system, and instructions for adding, changing, or removing training records, though the specific procedural steps for these actions appear to be detailed elsewhere in the document. The HRIS Analysis team and HRIS Trainer are responsible for testing all changes to the Training Module, and any modifications must be communicated to the HRIS Trainer and relevant departments, with Quick Reference Guides and affected reports requiring updates as needed. A critical configuration warning notes that the "All Personnel" flag in the Course Detail screen must remain unticked for all courses, as enabling this flag triggers unintended system actions such as inserting dummy qualifications into employee Personal Profile records across the entire organization, as documented in HEAT Incident #10373713.
