s: The requirement for a UDF will often come from a Business requirement, so the Business Process Advisor within the HRIS Support Centre will usually lead on gathering requirements for a new UDF. A “MASTER UDF Template” excel file is stored in the following folder which should be completed, usually by or with assistance from an HRIS Analyst, outlining how the UDF should be set up within the system: P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs Completed UDF...
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in Core|Personnel allow you to create custom forms within the Personnel module to store additional employee information that cannot be recorded elsewhere, configured at the Person, Appointment, or Recruitment level. Open this document when you need to understand the approved process for creating new UDFs or modifying existing ones, including the consultation, approval, and change management requirements through OSM. This guide covers the technical setup in the Portal (People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects), configuration options like text fields and dropdown lists, and critical considerations for editing existing UDFs—particularly that manual updates to employee records are required when list items are edited.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to User Defined Fields (UDFs) within the Core Personnel module of an HRIS system, covering the complete lifecycle from initial business requirements through implementation and ongoing maintenance. UDFs are configured forms that store additional employee information at the Person (employee), Appointment, or Recruitment level, accessed within People Management under the User Defined Field section or within online Application Forms for recruitment purposes. The approved process for raising a new UDF begins with a business requirement submitted to the HRIS Support Centre, where a Business Process Adviser leads requirement gathering and completion of the "MASTER UDF Template" (stored in P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs), which is then saved in a sub-folder specific to that UDF. All new UDFs and changes to existing UDFs must follow the Change Request process in OSM and receive approval from the Head of HRIS or their nominated deputy, with early notification required to the HR Analytics team or HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager due to data warehouse impacts. Technically, UDFs are configured in the Portal via People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects, with each UDF consisting of up to 12 fields that can be set as List items (drop-down selections), Text (free text), or Date fields, identified by a 6-character Reference Code and a 40-character Description. When amending existing UDFs, particular care must be taken because changes to List Items or field descriptions do not automatically update previously entered data; editing existing List Items requires manual updates to each affected employee record and agreement from all affected parties, whereas adding new List Items has no impact on existing data. This document is primarily used by HRIS Business Process Advisers, HRIS Analysts, and business area stakeholders within Personnel Services who need to create, modify, or manage custom data fields in the personnel system, with detailed technical steps referenced in an accompanying How To guide.

t: User Defined Fields (UDF)
s: The requirement for a UDF will often come from a Business requirement, so the Business Process Advisor within the HRIS Support Centre will usually lead on gathering requirements for a new UDF. Support\Reference Data\UDFs Completed UDF...
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in Core|Personnel allow you to create custom forms for storing additional employee information at the Appointment, Person, or Recruitment level that cannot be recorded elsewhere in the system. Open this document when you need to understand the approved process for creating new UDFs or modifying existing ones, including consultation requirements, change management procedures, and technical configuration steps. This guide covers how to set up UDFs with reference codes and descriptions, configure fields as list items or text/date fields, and manage changes to existing UDFs—particularly important since editing existing data requires manual updates across affected employee records. You'll also find details on testing, downstream system impacts, and affected reports before implementing changes through the OSM change request process.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing User Defined Fields (UDFs) within the Core Personnel module, explaining how to create, modify, and implement changes to these custom data collection forms. UDFs are configured as forms that store additional employee information at the Person, Appointment, or Recruitment level and are accessed through People Management > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects in the Portal, with each UDF consisting of up to 12 fields that can be configured as List items, Text fields, or Dates. The document outlines that new UDF requests typically originate from business areas and must be processed through the Change Request system in OSM, with the HRIS Business Process Adviser leading requirements gathering and the Head of HRIS or their deputy providing approval. The technical implementation requires completing a "MASTER UDF Template" excel file stored in P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs, with each UDF assigned a 6-character alphanumeric Reference Code for reporting purposes and a 40-character maximum Description displayed in selection menus. Critical to understanding this document is the data storage mechanism: data is stored against generic Item Numbers rather than field-specific identifiers, which creates significant challenges when editing existing list items since changes apply to all affected records but do not automatically propagate, requiring manual updates to each employee record where the field was previously selected. The document also emphasizes the necessity of providing early notification to the HR Analytics team or HR Systems Analysis and Insights Manager to assess impact on the data warehouse before implementing changes. This document is essential for HRIS analysts, Business Process Advisers, and system administrators who manage personnel data configuration and need to understand the approval, implementation, and data management implications of creating or modifying UDFs.

t: Applicant Cleardown
s: There are two main uses of the applicant clear down: Applicant Requests Data Removed From System, referred to hereon as the “Applicant Request Process” Periodic clear down of data to comply with Data Protection laws, referred to hereon as the “Bulk Clear down Process” The first, where an applicant requests that their details are removed from our system, will be raised via an incident. The second, where the HRIS Support Centre needs to fulfil its legal obligation to clear...
ss: The Applicant Cleardown process in the e-Recruitment system handles two distinct scenarios: removing individual applicant data when requested and performing annual bulk cleardowns to comply with Data Protection laws. For individual requests, applicants can delete their profiles, though recruitment data must be legally retained for six months after a final hiring decision. The bulk cleardown runs annually at the start of the HESA year and is managed by the HRIS Support Centre 1st line team. Open this document when processing applicant deletion requests, scheduling annual data cleardowns, or understanding the retention requirements and approval workflows involved.
sl: This document outlines the applicant cleardown process for the University of Oxford's e-Recruitment and HRIS systems, covering procedures for removing applicant data from the system through two distinct pathways. The first pathway handles individual applicant requests to delete their e-Recruitment profiles, which are raised via incident tickets and managed according to data protection requirements that mandate retention of recruitment data for six months following final vacancy decisions. The second pathway involves annual bulk cleardown of historical applicant data to maintain compliance with data protection legislation, scheduled to coincide with the start of each HESA year beginning August 1st and managed as a business-as-usual exercise following initial implementation. The document specifies the technical process accessed through the Core | Recruitment > Applicant Maintenance > Applicant Clear Down menu path, with bulk cleardown covering a rolling two-year retention window (current year plus previous HESA year). Implementation responsibility falls to the HRIS Support Centre 1st line support team lead, with approval required from the HRIS Service Manager for bulk processes and coordination with Heads of HRIS Support and HR Information regarding scheduling. The cleardown process incorporates security controls that restrict users to clearing down applicants only within departments they have access to, and includes standard template communications for applicants whose requests cannot be immediately fulfilled due to the six-month retention requirement. Extensive testing has already been completed on both cleardown processes, with further testing required only if system or procedural changes affect the cleardown functionality.

Open this if you're managing recruitment process changes that require Change Management approval, testing coordination, or updates to training materials and user communications.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing applicant statuses within the Core|Recruitment module of the university's HR system, covering the complete change management lifecycle for this configuration area. The document outlines the specific navigation path (Core|Portal > Recruitment > Toolbox > Applicant Statuses) for adding, changing, or removing applicant statuses, along with a critical constraint that statuses cannot be fully deleted if they have been historically used, as this would compromise applicant history and reporting integrity. The change approval process requires that all modifications to the Recruitment Portal follow the university's established Change Management procedures, with system changes requiring approval from the Head of HR Systems or their deputy via a change request in OSM, and potentially requiring presentation at HRSEG for formal agreement. The University's central recruitment team within Human Resources must be consulted on any changes they did not initiate, as they own recruitment strategy and policies. Testing of applicant status changes falls to the Functional Analysis team and must account for different user access roles, particularly when changes affect departmental user menus. Communication about changes must reach departmental users via HRIS bulletin ideally before implementation, while the HR Systems support team and trainer must be informed at appropriate stages to ensure support materials and training modules are updated accordingly. The applicant statuses are configured to control both process and reporting requirements and govern specific workflow triggers, such as the "Offer Accepted – Personnel" status which enables successful applicants to appear in the People Management system for appointment processing, and changes may affect the standard report RECDEP41_Applicant and Vacancy Details.

ss: The Internal Jobs Board widget in Core|Portal allows employees to view, search, and apply for active internal and external vacancies directly through the Employee Self Service portal. sl: This document provides guidance on managing changes to the Core|Portal Internal Jobs Board, a recruitment system widget that allows employees to view, search, and apply for internal and external vacancies through the Employee Self Service Portal. The document outlines the complete change management process, including that all requests for changes must follow the Change Management process and may require presentation at HRSEG for agreement before implementation, with the Head of HRIS Support or their deputy providing final approval via a change request in HEAT. The technical implementation procedures describe how to add, amend, or remove widgets by navigating to Core|Portal > Administrator Dashboard > Dashboard Configuration > Employee Dashboard, where amendments are limited to reordering widgets or renaming them. The document identifies key stakeholders requiring consultation, including the University's central recruitment team within Personnel Services who must be consulted on changes affecting recruitment strategy and policies, along with Business Change involvement for process modifications. Testing responsibilities fall to the HRIS Analyst team, who must validate changes in a suitable test environment and may involve other users with Self Service Portal access to verify functionality. The document addresses known issues with the system where applicant accounts created through the Internal Jobs Board may not properly link to employee numbers, creating problems for employees applying through the Employee Self Service Portal that require further investigation and testing. Additionally, the document specifies downstream updates needed to guidance documentation, applicant help pages, the Employee and Manager Portals configuration guide, and CDD following any changes, with communication required to employees, HRIS first line support, and HRIS trainers regarding implementation impacts.

t: Maintain Vacancy Types
s: Maintain Vacancy Types Knowledge Article The Standard process for creating or amending Vacancy Types is for the request to be made via an Incident that will be assigned to the Functional Analysis team within OSM the Oxford Service Management tool. It should be clear from the incident if the request is for a new Vacancy Type or an amendment to an existing. Vacancy Types are linked heavily with the Recruitment process.
ss: Vacancy Types in PeopleXD are reference data codes that categorize job positions and appear on the jobs website search screen for end users. Use this document when you need to create, modify, or remove a Vacancy Type code—all requests must be submitted as a Medium Change incident to the Functional Analysis team and approved by the Head of Recruitment. The process covers technical steps for adding and amending codes in PeopleXD's Data Centre, important constraints (such as codes that cannot be deleted once linked to a recruitment record), and testing requirements in the UAT environment before going live.
sl: This document provides guidance on creating, modifying, and removing vacancy types within the PeopleXD system, which are integral to the recruitment process. Requests to add new vacancy types or amend existing ones must be submitted via an Incident in OSM (Oxford Service Management tool) and assigned to the Functional Analysis team, with the Head of Recruitment responsible for approving all changes. Changes are classified as Medium Changes within OSM and must be tested in a UAT environment before implementation in the live production environment. The technical process involves navigating to PeopleXD > People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Vacancy Types, where users can add new codes (which cannot be changed once set) and modify descriptions (limited to 40 characters, displayed to end users on the jobs website search screen). Vacancy Type Codes cannot be deleted if linked to the Recruitment Maintenance Table through active vacancy records; if a code has been used, data must be migrated to another type before deletion is possible. Functional testing should include using new or amended codes on actual vacancies and the jobs website, followed by User Acceptance Testing to ensure alignment with central recruitment processes. The HR Systems Functional Analysis team maintains the reference data, while the Business Change team manages communications to inform stakeholders of any recruitment process changes resulting from vacancy type modifications. Downstream impacts may include updates to Quick Reference Guides (QRGs) and relevant reports containing the modified reference data.

sl: This Change Management document provides a comprehensive guide for managing modifications to the onboarding process and checklist system within an HRIS environment. The document outlines the approved process for raising changes, including consultation and approval workflows that differ based on implementation phase—during the pilot phase, pilot departments are consulted unless changes are legally required or address security concerns, while after full rollout the Product Ownership Group scores and prioritizes requests. Changes must be formally requested through the standard Change Request process in OSM and approved by the Head of HR Systems or their deputy. The technical implementation section details specific navigation paths within the Administrator Dashboard to add, change, or remove various checklist components including Tasks, Custom Pages, Surveys, Staff Groups, and Landing Page Configuration tiles under Social Hub Configuration. Testing is the responsibility of Functional or Senior Functional Analysts with possible involvement from the Business Change team, and may require User Acceptance Testing. The document addresses downstream impacts such as the need to review and test automated notifications after changes and to update the Onboarding Insight reports if checklist tasks are modified. This guide is used by HR system administrators, functional analysts, and change managers implementing modifications to the onboarding checklist system, which was fully rolled out university-wide on November 1, 2023, and applies to new starters, rehires, and new appointments through staff group configuration.

s: Approved process A request to change an application form(s) could come from any source and may often be the result of legislative changes or a business Requirement. Any changes to the online application form profile(s) must follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change.
ss: Online recruitment application forms are maintained through the Staff Portal and back office systems, with changes governed by a formal change management process requiring approval from the Head of HRIS Support. Open this document when you need to modify application form profiles, add or remove questions, or update sections in the recruitment system—whether due to legislative changes like GDPR updates or new business requirements. The document covers the complete workflow including consultation requirements, technical navigation steps, testing procedures with test vacancies, and impacts on downstream systems like training materials, QRGs, and recruitment reports (RECDEP40-RECDEP48). Use it to ensure all stakeholder groups (departmental users, HRIS support, trainers) are informed and that affected documentation and reports are updated alongside your form changes.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing changes to online recruitment application forms within an organization's HRIS system, covering the complete lifecycle from request through implementation. The document outlines that changes to application forms can originate from various sources—such as legislative requirements around GDPR or Equality and Diversity—and must follow the organization's Change Management process, potentially requiring approval at HRSEG before implementation. Specific technical navigation paths are detailed for maintaining forms through the Portal via Portal > Recruitment Dashboard > Toolbox > Recruitment Admin > Form Profile > Edit Profile, as well as for managing standard and non-standard additional questions through either the back office (Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference > Question Category) or the Portal interface. The document identifies the HRIS Analyst as responsible for testing changes by creating test vacancies, advertising them, and submitting test applicant applications to verify that form changes display correctly in both the online interface and generated PDF applicant packs. Key approval workflows require sign-off from the System Owner (Head of HRIS Support) via change request in HEAT before implementation, while consultation with the University's central recruitment team within Personnel Services is necessary if they did not originate the request. The document addresses downstream impacts including updates needed to training materials, Quick Reference Guides (QRGs), the Common Design Document (CDD), and potentially eight standard recruitment reports (RECDEP40-RECDEP48) depending on the nature of the changes. Communication protocols require that departmental users be informed via HRIS bulletin before changes, the HRIS first line support team be notified when changes are made, and the HRIS Trainer be informed in advance to assess impacts on the training environment.

ss: The Core|Portal Onboarding process manages configuration changes to the employee onboarding checklist and related components in the HRIS system, including surveys, custom pages, and staff grouping rules. Use this document when you need to understand the approval workflow, testing requirements, and downstream impacts of onboarding changes—such as updates to checklist items, Insight reports, or guidance documents. This is essential reading if you're implementing onboarding modifications that require People Management POG consultation, system owner approval, or changes affecting new starters and rehires across departments.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive change management guide for the Social Hub and Onboarding module within the Core|Portal system, explaining how to process, approve, test, and communicate changes to onboarding configurations and related processes. The document outlines the approved process for raising changes, which may originate from user enhancement requests, the Access group's automatic release programme, or statutory reporting requirements such as HESA data collection changes, with all changes requiring approval from the System Owner (Head of HR Systems) or their nominated deputy via change request in OSM before implementation. The People Management POG must be consulted on onboarding configuration changes, though they may only be informed rather than consulted if the change relates to statutory reporting. The technical "How to" section provides standardized navigation paths through the Core|Portal system using consistent button names and terminology, with examples like Core|Personnel > Reference and Core|Pay > Reference to guide users through menu structures. Testing responsibilities fall to the Functional Analyst for checklist modifications and to the HR Administrator for Insight reports, with new checklist items requiring re-release and test appointments added to employee records. Communications must reach departments currently piloting the onboarding checklist (NDM, Cont Ed, and PHCS) before go-live, while downstream impacts include necessary updates to Insight reports tracking completed and incomplete checklist items, plus amendments to guidance documents and self-service materials. The document details the configurable components of the onboarding checklist—including Input Items, User Defined Forms, Surveys, Custom Pages, and Landing Pages—along with Staff Grouping (also called Criteria Groups) which restricts checklist items to specific employee categories based on appointment reasons, divisions, departments, or grades, with all new starters and rehires identified through the Staff Group 'University_of_Oxford_CMS_and_Casual' triggered by appointment reason codes. Access to the Social Hub Onboarding is controlled through ESS single sign-on and cannot be enabled before an employee's actual start date, with the Social Hub integrated into the new starter Portal configuration.

ss: Core|Portal Insight reports cover the process for creating, modifying, and managing reports within the Insight reporting system, particularly for onboarding survey data and employee task tracking. sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing changes to Insight reports within the Core|Portal system, specifically focused on onboarding survey reporting functionality. The document outlines the complete change management lifecycle, including approved processes for raising requests through the HRIS Support Centre, with different procedures for the pilot phase versus full rollout, and consultation requirements involving either pilot departments or the Product Ownership Group depending on the implementation stage. Technical procedures are detailed for creating new reports via Insight > Actions > Create Report, modifying existing reports through Insight > Admin Area with cloning functionality via Ellipses > Manage > Actions > Clone, and removing reports through an archiving process that prefixes report names with "ZZ ARCHIVED" followed by version numbers. The document specifies a naming convention for reports using module abbreviations (such as PER for People Management) followed by INS and a sequential number—for example, PERINS01 and PERINS02 for the configured onboarding reports—with a 100-character title limit and explicit instructions not to include version numbers in active report names. Testing responsibilities fall to the report creator and support team members, with potential user acceptance testing, and all HR Systems users across University departments must be informed of changes following the November 2023 onboarding rollout. The reports incorporate hard-coded and user-defined filters for parameters like department code, person reference, division, and date ranges, along with calculations and sort orders, with security inherited from People Management and managed through the AG_INSIGHT menu profile for Functional Analysts and the ONB - Onboarding Administrator organizational role. This document is primarily used by HRIS support teams, functional analysts, and change managers implementing report modifications within the established governance framework.

t: Active Roles Web Interface
f: Active Roles Web Interface Knowledge Article_v1.0.docx
s: Active Roles Web Interface The Active Roles Web Interface is used by HR Systems to manage access to the HR Reporting environments. Individuals are added to Active Directory (“AD”) groups, and the groups are granted read-only access to folders and sub-folders within the HR Reporting environments. Which AD groups are granted access to which folders/sub-folders is determined by consultation, usually within the Functional Analysis or HR Analytics teams, but often with input...
ss: The Active Roles Web Interface is used by HR Systems to manage access to HR Reporting environments through Active Directory groups, with two group types: normal groups (HRIS-RR-…) maintained by the Functional Analysis team and super-groups (HRIS-RS-…) maintained only by Microsoft Platform Services. All requests to create new groups, modify existing groups, or grant access to the Active Roles Web Interface itself must be raised as Minor Changes in OSM, with super-group changes requiring written approval from designated senior staff members. Open this document when you need to request access to HR Reporting environments, create or modify AD groups for reporting access, or understand the approval and consultation requirements for changes to HR Reporting security and user permissions.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing access to HR Reporting environments through the Active Roles Web Interface, which is owned and maintained by the Microsoft Platform Services Team (MPST). The document outlines the approved process for raising changes, including detailed procedures for creating and modifying two types of Active Directory groups: normal groups prefixed with "HRIS-RR-" that can be maintained by the Functional Analysis team, and "super-groups" prefixed with "HRIS-RS-" that are restricted to report writers and support teams and require written approval from designated approvers such as Simon Burford, Athena Artuso, or Mandy Zaccheo. All requests for new normal AD groups or changes to existing groups must be raised as Minor Changes on the OSM system with specific required information including the group name in the proper format and a descriptive purpose. Super-group creation requires pre-approval in writing followed by an OSM Minor Change request with a task assigned to MPST that includes the group name format and a list of individual members with their SSO identifiers. Access to the Active Roles Web Interface itself is restricted and can only be granted or revoked by MPST through an OSM Minor Change request, with approval authority depending on the access level—read-only access requires Mandy Zaccheo's approval while read-write access requires Simon Burford's approval. The document specifies that only the Functional Analysis team should have read-write access to the interface, while other teams like the HRIS Support Centre may receive read-only access to investigate customer queries. All changes are categorized as "Minor Changes" in the change management system under Service Line Business Systems and Administration Support, Service HRIS, and Category HR Reporting, with the justification being Configuration.

ss: Core|Recruitment automated email notifications are triggered by specific events configured in CoreHR's Event Management system, such as applicant updates, vacancy postings, and staff requests. The document provides step-by-step instructions for navigating CoreHR's Event Notification maintenance window, viewing the email queue, and understanding the change management approval process required before implementing notification changes. Open this guide if you're managing recruitment communications and need to ensure the right emails are triggered at the right time for the right people.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on managing automated email notifications within the CoreHR system's Event Management module, specifically addressing how to add, edit, remove, and monitor event-triggered emails for recruitment and HR processes. The document outlines the approved change management process, which requires that any changes to notifications follow the University's formal Change Management procedures and may need presentation to HRSEG for agreement, with approval ultimately sought from the Head of HRIS Support or their deputy via a change request in HEAT. The technical implementation involves navigating to CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration to manage notifications, where users can select an Event Category and Event Type, then add new notifications through the Event Notification maintenance window, edit existing notifications by clicking the Edit button, or delete notifications using the Delete button at the bottom of the screen. The document specifies different consultation and approval requirements depending on the notification type: Applicant and Vacancy notifications require consultation with the Head of Recruitment, Auto-enrolment changes need approval from the Head of Pensions, Staff Requests go through HRSEG, and Reward Team changes follow standard Change Management procedures. Testing responsibilities fall to the HRIS Support Centre, with verification required to confirm that emails are created at the appropriate time when triggered by their linked event, sent to specified recipients, and successfully received. Additional monitoring and viewing capabilities are available through Personnel > Reference > Utilities > View Email Queue to check processed emails in date order, and through Personnel > Recruitment > Recruitment Reference > ERecruitment Web Parameters to view when vacancy notification emails were last sent. The document notes that departmental users affected by notification changes should be informed either before or after implementation through monthly bulletins or email, and that QRGs may require updating following changes, though no standard reports are affected.

ss: IP filtering and firewall configuration controls access to CorePortal and the BI layer through two methods: IP restrictions on CorePortal access and VPN firewall rules for the BI layer. This document outlines the complete change process including how to raise requests, obtain approvals from the HRIS Service Manager, implement technical changes via Access Group and MPST, and test connectivity in the appropriate IP ranges. Open this if you need to add or modify IP address restrictions for CorePortal or BI layer access, manage firewall changes for HR Reporting or SSIS interfaces, or understand the approval workflow and testing requirements for infrastructure changes affecting PeopleXD systems.
sl: This document outlines the change management process for implementing IP filtering and cloud-hosted firewall restrictions within an organization's HRIS systems, covering two primary restriction methods: IP restrictions on CorePortal access and firewall restrictions on the VPN tunnel to the BI layer. The approved process for raising changes involves either incident management routes or new public subnet creation within the University Network, with specific consideration given to module go-lives and periodic reviews of Access Group's filtering configuration options. Changes to VPN tunnel firewall access for HR Reporting solutions and SSIS Interfaces controlled by Software Solutions require approval from the HRIS Service Manager, with potential consultation from software solutions, MPST, and infosec teams to validate requests and assess security risks. Implementation follows standard change management procedures, with the infosec team potentially conducting security risk assessments and recommending testing methods such as pen testing when justified. The technical process for adding IP ranges to CorePortal access requires following instructions in P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\IP Filtering\How to apply IP filtering to CorePortal.docx, while adding ranges to the BI layer involves raising cases with Access Group to update firewall rules at both CW (Citywest Production) and PW (Penrose Wharf UAT) data centres, followed by a corresponding task to MPST via OSM. Testing must confirm connectivity from the new IP range to test environments with the updated filtering applied, and communications must notify HR Reporting users and UPST Interface Staging infrastructure users of connectivity interruptions during implementation. The document notes that e-Recruitment has no IP filtering restrictions, users on private VPN or Eduroam networks must tunnel into the Oxford Network to access CoreHR as an infosec requirement, and IP addresses can be verified against the University's network blocks list at https://networks.it.ox.ac.uk/itss/netblocks/subnets.

Consultation and approval requirements vary depending on the specific text being changed and its origin—for example, changes to Recruitment module text require Head of Recruitment approval, while all system changes must be approved by the System Owner (Head of HRIS Support) or their nominated deputy via a change request in HEAT before implementation. Testing responsibilities fall to the HRIS Support Centre, with standard test items including verification that text displays correctly across all affected screens where it appears. The document specifies that affected departmental users must be informed of changes through channels such as monthly bulletins or email either before or after implementation, and that downstream processes including Quick Reference Guide (QRG) updates and updates to the Language Pack Common Design Document must be completed following any language pack modifications. Additionally, potentially affected reports must be assessed and tested as part of the change process to ensure accuracy and consistency across the system.

Email templates are held and managed directly within CorePersonnel, however Core uses external documents for letter templates. The letter templates are currently saved...
ss: CorePersonnel letter and email templates are used across departments and central teams to generate standardized correspondence with employees. This document covers the approval process, change management procedures, and technical steps for creating, editing, and maintaining both letter templates (stored externally and managed via mail merge) and email templates (held directly in CorePersonnel). Open this if you need to request a new template, modify an existing one, or understand who must approve changes before templates go live. It's also your resource for the testing requirements and communication steps needed when implementing template changes.
sl: This document provides guidance on managing letter and email templates within the Core|Personnel human resources information system, covering the complete change management process from initial requirements through implementation and communication. Letter templates are externally managed documents stored in a shared folder (O:\PS\HRIS\Core correspondence templates\v20\1 v20 Current templates), while email templates are held directly within CorePersonnel, with detailed instructions available in the "Maintain document and email templates in the Portal" guide. Change requests for letter or email templates typically originate from business requirements and are led by Business Analysts or HR Officers within the HRIS Support Centre, with all changes requiring customer sign-off and HR Policy Team approval before becoming live. The HRIS Analysis team classifies these as minor changes and bears responsibility for implementation, utilizing standardized navigation paths through Core|Personnel menus and adhering to specific procedures such as saving new versions with version numbers and archiving outdated templates. Thorough testing must be performed on amended or new documents across multiple PCs to prevent corruption of merge fields and fill-ins, with testing typically conducted by the HRIS Business Analyst, HRIS Process Team, or end users depending on usage scope. Before implementation, relevant teams including the HR Policy Team must be informed, the change must be logged in the Changes and update spreadsheet, training materials must be updated by the HRIS Process Team, and users are subsequently notified through the HRIS Bulletin and HR Newsletter. The document confirms that template changes have no impact on downstream systems, processes, or standard reports, and includes references to the Core configuration guide for additional technical background and data source information on available field items for different Template Types.

sl: This document is a Time Management Workbook designed to track and manage outstanding tasks related to time management processes across multiple departments. ss: Time Management in CoreTime|CoreRoster involves configuring and managing Balances—the settings that determine how annual leave is calculated for each appointment. Open this document when you need to understand the change management process for creating, modifying, or removing Balances, including required approvals, testing procedures, and downstream impacts on payroll, timesheets, and HR reports. You'll also find guidance on when a new Balance is actually necessary versus reusing existing configurations, plus links to detailed how-to procedures. Use this if you're raising a change request related to Time Management Balances or need to understand who to consult, approve, test, and communicate with during implementation.
sl: This document provides guidance for managing changes to Time Management Balances within the Core|WFM system, specifically in the CoreTime|CoreRoster module accessed via System Parameters > Balances. The document outlines the complete change management workflow, including required approvals from the System Owner (Head HR Systems) via change requests in OSM, consultation with HRSEG and CoreTime POG, and potential payroll approval requirements for timesheet-related changes. It describes the technical processes for adding, changing, and removing balances, with detailed references to the companion "HOW TO - Manage Balances in CoreTime" guide for step-by-step instructions. The document identifies key stakeholders responsible for testing (Functional Analyst team), communications (departmental users via HRIS bulletin, HR Systems support, and Business Change and Training), and downstream impacts on systems including ESS, MSS, and payroll, as well as three standard timesheet reports (TIMDEP01, TIMDEP02, TIMDEP03). It also details which downstream systems and reports may be impacted by calendar changes and who needs to be informed at each stage.
sl: This draft document from the Change Management function provides comprehensive guidance on managing calendar maintenance processes within the Core|WFM Time Management system, specifically covering the procedures, approvals, and implementation steps required for calendar-related changes. The document outlines the complete approved process for raising changes, including mandatory consultation with system owners and approval requirements through OSM change requests by the Head HR Systems or their nominated deputy before implementation. It describes technical procedures for processing changes in the system, such as adding, changing, or removing calendar entries, along with standard navigation paths within Core|WFM (for example, Core|Personnel > Reference > Reference A–C > Accident Codes and Core|Pay > Reference > Pay Groups) and standardized button names and terminology used throughout the interface. The document addresses testing responsibilities, designating the Functional Analyst team as normally responsible for validating changes in appropriate test environments, potentially across different user access roles and menu profiles depending on the nature of the change. The document includes a detailed suggested timetable for calendar maintenance activities spanning August through October, with specific tasks assigned to HR Systems and Departmental HR/Managers, such as updating Holiday Schemes with closure dates, loading term-time shift patterns, extending system and user-defined calendars, completing balance period ends, and managing manual adjustments for carried forward leave before the new leave year begins.

t: Time Management - Holiday Schemes (DRAFT)
f: DRAFT Time Management - Holiday Schemes Knowledge Article.docx
s: A request for change could come from any source and is most likely to be a business requirement due to changes in existing process or implementation of new processes. Alternatively it could be a fix or enhancement that has been provided by the supplier. Any changes to any area of the Portal must follow the Change Management process in force at the time of the change.
ss: Holiday Schemes in Core|WFM define closure dates—such as public holidays and departmental fixed closure days—that are treated as non-working days for employees linked to them through their Balance records. The system uses employee work schedules to automatically adjust leave entitlements when a closure date falls on a day the employee would normally work. Open this document when setting up or modifying holiday calendars, linking Holiday Schemes to Balance records, or troubleshooting how closure dates affect timesheet approvals and leave calculations. You'll also find the change management process required before implementing any Holiday Scheme modifications, including approval steps and downstream impacts on payroll and leave reporting.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing changes to Holiday Schemes within the Core|WFM Time Management system, covering the complete lifecycle from request through implementation and communication. It outlines the approved process for raising changes, which may originate from any source including business requirements or supplier-provided fixes, and stipulates that all Portal changes must follow the organization's Change Management process, with potential escalation to HRSEG and CoreTime POG for agreement. The document specifies that changes require approval from the System Owner (Head HR Systems) or their nominated deputy via a change request in HEAT before implementation, and may require additional payroll approval if Timesheets are affected. A Holiday Scheme is defined as a configurable list of closure dates—including public holidays and departmental fixed closure days—that mark non-working days for employees linked to the scheme via their Balance, with the system automatically adjusting entitlements based on employee work schedules. The document details that the Functional Analyst team typically conducts testing in suitable test environments across different user access roles, while multiple stakeholder groups must be informed through different channels: departmental users via HRIS bulletin ideally before changes, HR Systems support when changes are made, and Business Change and Training before implementation to enable guidance updates. It identifies downstream impacts including potential effects on Payroll for Timesheet changes, Employee Self-Service (ESS) and Manager Self-Service (MSS), and affected standard reports including TIMDEP01 (Timesheet approvals), TIMDEP02 (Annual Leave), and TIMDEP03 (Sickness absence). The document clarifies that a single Holiday Scheme can be linked to multiple Balances with varying FTE Hours, Long Service Schemes, leave years, and Base Entitlements, provided all linked Balances share the same mandatory holiday dates, and notes that Holiday Schemes should not be used with Accrual Balances.

ss: Length of Service schemes in PeopleXD Workforce Management control how employee leave entitlements are awarded based on years of service, and this document outlines the formal change management process required to add, modify, or remove these schemes. Use this guide when you need to adjust service-based leave thresholds, FTE hour allocations, or accrual rates—changes that affect all employees assigned to a particular length of service code. sl: This draft document provides a comprehensive guide for managing changes to Length of Service schemes within the PeopleXD Workforce Management system, specifically addressing how to add, modify, or remove Length of Service schemes that affect employee leave entitlements. The document outlines the approval process, requiring that changes be presented to HRSEG for agreement and potentially shared with the CoreTime POG before implementation, with final system approval needed from the System Owner or their deputy via change request in OSM. t: WFM – User Defined Calendar
s: WFM – User Defined Calendar
ss: User Defined Calendar configuration in WFM (Workforce Management) within CoreTime allows you to create and manage custom payroll periods beyond the standard weekly, fortnightly, and monthly options. Use this document when you need to enable the User Defined Calendar feature, configure new calendar periods, assign calendars to work groups or individual employees, or extend existing calendars to cover additional pay periods. This is essential for organizations with non-standard pay cycles or unique timesheet requirements that don't align with default system calendars. The document provides step-by-step instructions for system configuration, period generation, and calendar assignment through CoreTime's System Parameters.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring and maintaining User Defined Calendars within the WFM (Workforce Management) system, specifically in the CoreTime application used for payroll and timesheet management. The document outlines the technical steps required to enable User Defined Calendar functionality through System Params by navigating to Control Parameters, selecting General Parameters - 4, and enabling the TIMESHEETS - RUN MONTHLY advanced option. It details how to create custom calendar periods by accessing System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, where users must define a Code and Name, set the Data Entry Offset to 0, and then generate periods based on start and end dates, with specific guidance that weekly calendars require 52 periods per tax year (or 53 if the pay date falls on April 5), fortnightly calendars have 26 periods, and monthly calendars have 12 periods. The document explains two assignment methods: assigning User Defined Calendars to entire Work Groups through CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups by selecting the calendar from the Pay Frequency dropdown and enabling the User Defined Calendar Group checkbox, or assigning to individual employees by overriding Work Group settings in Person Maintenance. This document is intended for HRIS administrators and Change Management personnel responsible for implementing payroll calendar changes, as it addresses the configuration, extension, and assignment processes needed to ensure timesheets and payroll align with custom organizational pay periods rather than standard weekly, fortnightly, or monthly options.

t: 17. v28 Guides - Additional Validation User Guide V28 Customer v1.0
f: 17. v28 Guides - Additional Validation User Guide V28 Customer v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of Guide The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the Additional Validation functionality in Time and Attendance, and how this is used. This includes: • What is Additional Validation and when is it used? • Detailed guidance on how to configure each type of Additional Validation. Additional Validation Overview It is possible to configure and use 3 types of Additional Validation within the system.
ss: Additional Validation in CoreHR Time and Attendance v28 prevents employees from cashing out excessive annual leave by enforcing three configurable validation types: Max Daily Pay Code Limit (restricts hours on a single pay code per day), Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit (restricts total hours across multiple pay codes per day), and Holidays & Contracted Hours Check (ensures weekly leave doesn't exceed contracted hours). These validations can be applied across Timesheet Input, Time Exceptions, Leave Approval, Absence Details, and Approve/Sign Off screens with configurable warning or stop alerts. Open this guide when configuring pay code limits, setting up validation rules for your organization, or troubleshooting leave entry restrictions in Time and Attendance.
sl: This guide documents the Additional Validation functionality in CoreHR's Time and Attendance v28 system, which is designed to prevent improper cashing out of annual leave by implementing three types of validation rules. The first validation type, Max Daily Pay Code Limit, is a pay code-level setting that prevents users from entering hours or values exceeding a configured daily maximum on a single pay code (for example, restricting annual leave to a maximum of 8 hours per day). The second type, Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit, is a validation rule that restricts the total hours an employee can record across multiple specified pay codes in a single day. The third type, Holidays & Contracted Hours Check, ensures that when annual leave is recorded, the total hours for the week do not exceed the employee's contracted hours. These validations are applied across multiple screens in the system including Timesheet Input, Time Exceptions, Leave Approval, Absence Details, and Approve/Sign Off screens, with configurable alert levels (Warning or Stop) that determine whether users can proceed or are blocked from continuing. The guide provides detailed configuration instructions for each validation type, including pay code settings, advanced options, personalized pay code groups, rule creation, and assignment of validation rules to specific companies or work groups. This document is intended for system administrators and configuration specialists who manage time and attendance policies within CoreHR Limited's HR systems.

t: Configuring Organisations V28
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure an organisation. Items covered include: • How to add an Organisation. • How to edit an Organisation. • How to duplicate an Organisation. • How to delete an Organisation. An organisation may be made of one or more individual companies which operate independently of each other.
ss: Organisation configuration in CoreHR's Payroll module allows you to set up and manage individual company codes within your organisation, each with their own unique payroll settings, pay groups, and operational details. Open this guide when you need to add a new company, edit existing company information (such as address or contact details), duplicate a company with similar settings, or delete a company from the system. You'll use this process to establish the foundational structure for how multiple companies operate independently within your payroll system, including configuring pay periods, bank details, payroll calendars, and currency codes.
sl: This CoreHR Payroll v28 guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring organisations within the system, covering the complete lifecycle of company management including adding, editing, copying, and deleting company records. The document explains that organisation codes distinguish between multiple independent companies operating within an organisation, each with unique company codes that link directly to pay groups, and users must have access to a company to access its associated pay groups. To perform organisation configuration tasks, users navigate to Settings > Company Parameters > Organisations, where they can access the Organisations screen via the CorePortal Pay Settings – Organisations menu option, though access restrictions may apply based on user permissions. When adding a new company, users complete mandatory fields marked with red asterisks such as a company code (maximum 40 characters) and address, along with optional fields including registered number, contact details, phone/fax numbers, email address, currency code, payroll provider selection (set to CorePay or blank for non-international organisations), and country code. The document also details the editing process where users select a company from the code drop-down menu and modify specific fields, the copying function that streamlines creating similar companies by duplicating existing records and updating only necessary details, and the deletion process which requires reassigning active pay groups to different companies via CorePay > Settings > Codes > Pay Groups to prevent data loss. A critical note warns against editing company details during an active payroll run to avoid processing errors.

t: Configuring Pay Group Access V28
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to grant Pay Group Access. Items covered include: • How to grant user access to a pay group. • How to remove pay group access from a user. How is User Access Managed on Payroll?
ss: Pay Group Access controls which payroll data individual users can view and process in the CoreHR Payroll Dashboard—allowing you to restrict employees to specific pay groups rather than granting system-wide access. This document explains how to grant users access to one or more pay groups and how to revoke that access when it's no longer needed. Open this guide when you need to set up payroll administrator permissions, onboard new team members to specific pay groups, or manage temporary access (such as covering a colleague's absence). The configuration happens in Settings > Codes > Pay Groups Access and requires selecting the user, pay group, and input location.
sl: This document is a user guide for CoreHR Payroll V28 that explains how to configure and manage Pay Group Access, covering both granting and removing user access to pay groups within the system. The guide describes two foundational access management categories in CoreHR: Menu Profiles, which control access to system functionality like dashboards and screens, and Data Access, which controls access to actual data records including employees, pay groups, and salaries. Pay Group Access specifically restricts payroll administrators' visibility and processing capabilities to only those pay groups they are authorized to support, allowing flexible assignment where users can have access to all pay groups, a single pay group, or temporary access during colleague absences. To grant user access, administrators navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups Access, filter by username or pay group, click Add to create a new row, then select the required pay group, username, and Input Location from drop-down menus before saving. The removal process follows a similar path through Settings > Codes > Pay Groups Access, but uses the filter function to locate the user and pay group combination, then clicks the delete button to revoke access. The document also notes that the CorePortal Pay Settings - Pay Groups Access menu option must be enabled in order for users to view and edit the Pay Groups Access screen, though disabled users can still access the screen with a restricted message. This guide is primarily used by system administrators and payroll administrators who need to configure user permissions within the CoreHR Payroll Dashboard and the People Management Dashboard.

t: Configuring Pay Groups V28
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Pay Groups. Items covered include: • How to add a Pay Group. • How to edit a Pay Group. • How to duplicate a Pay Group. • How to delete a Pay Group. A pay group is used for grouping employees that have the same pay frequency.
ss: Pay Groups in CoreHR's payroll system are used to group employees with the same pay frequency so they can be processed together for payment. This guide covers how to add, edit, duplicate, and delete pay groups, along with configuring critical fields like pay frequency, wages/salary indicator, pay periods, maximum thresholds, and standard hours or days. Open this document when you need to set up a new pay group, modify existing pay group settings, or understand how to configure payroll-specific parameters like pay frequency (weekly, fortnightly, monthly) and period hours/days that affect employee payment calculations. You'll also find guidance on user access permissions for pay group configuration through the Settings menu.
sl: This document is a user guide for version 28 of CoreHR's payroll system that provides comprehensive instructions on configuring pay groups, which are organizational units that group employees who share the same pay frequency so they can be processed together for payment. The guide covers four main operational tasks: adding, editing, duplicating, and deleting pay groups, all of which are accessed through the Settings > Codes > Pay Groups menu path. To perform these tasks, users must have the CorePortal Pay Settings - Pay Groups menu option enabled in their system, which grants full view and edit access to the Pay Group screen; if disabled, users see an access restriction message. When adding a new pay group, users must complete mandatory fields including a unique code, description (maximum 30 characters), and critical configuration settings such as Pay Frequency Indicator (W, F, M, 4, or B), Wages/Salary Indicator, and various period fields that track tax years, input periods, and payroll cycles. The document details numerous additional fields used to establish payroll parameters, including Maximum Hours, Maximum Gross pay, Maximum Nett pay, Pay Period Hours, Pay Period Days, and Days in Year, along with formulas explaining how these fields work together to convert annual employee rates to hourly equivalents. Optional configuration fields include the Annual Allowance Indicator and Validation Bypass settings that allow administrators to customize pay group behavior for specific business requirements. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR configuration specialists who need to set up and maintain the foundational pay group structures required for processing employee payments in CoreHR's payroll module.

t: Configuring Payroll Calendars V28
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure Payroll Calendars for a company. Items covered include: • How to add a Payroll Calendar. • How to edit a Payroll Calendar. • How to duplicate a Payroll Calendar. • How to delete a Payroll Calendar. A payroll c alendar must be generated for each company within an organisation .
ss: Payroll calendars in CoreHR must be created and maintained for each company to track period end dates for weekly, fortnightly, and four-weekly pay cycles. This guide covers how to add, edit, duplicate, and delete payroll calendars, as well as how to amend dates and build calendars for new years—accessed through Settings > Company Parameters > Payroll Calendars. Open this document when you need to set up initial payroll calendar configurations, adjust calendar dates due to leap years or week 53/54 situations, or manage calendar access permissions for payroll users. The guide details the specific calendar fields (Week Number, Tax Period, Week End Date, fortnightly/4-weekly indicators, etc.) and explains the Build/Rebuild Year function for copying calendars across years.
sl: This document is a user guide for configuring payroll calendars in CoreHR Payroll v28, providing step-by-step instructions on how to add, edit, duplicate, and delete payroll calendars for companies within an organization. Additionally, it provides configuration guidance for user access to the Amend Contract Start Date function and covers contract amendments with and without salary impact, changes of hours, contract timeline and history tracking, and the process for ending individual contracts with consideration to Substantive Date implications. This document is essential for HR teams and administrators who need to understand the workflows, system screens, and business rules for managing the full contract lifecycle in the People Management system.

sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for accessing and navigating the HR Employee Record within the CoreHR People Management system version 27+. sl: This recruitment administration user guide for CoreHR Limited version 27+ provides comprehensive instructions for managing the entire recruitment process within the system's portal interface. You'll find mapping tables showing which Back Office forms have Portal replacements and which continue to operate in Back Office, plus new functionality available exclusively on Portal such as WFM configuration areas and employee appointment transfers. Open this guide when you're planning or executing a move to Portal-based Workforce Management, need to understand which processes are changing, or require setup instructions for admin and manager access.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for migrating both administrator and manager users from Back Office to Workforce Management (WFM) on CorePortal, covering the transition process for v28 and later versions. The document details how to access and use two distinct dashboards: the WFM Admin Dashboard for administrators and the WFM Manager Dashboard for managers, with section 2 and section 7 providing overviews of each respectively. It includes specific configuration tasks such as assigning WFM Admin users access to the dashboard (section 5.1), configuring access types (section 5.2), assigning admin users access to employees (section 5.3), and configuring the Employee Calendar Screen (section 5.4), along with similar configuration steps for managers in section 9. t: Payroll Reconciliation report
s: PeopleXD Payroll (UK): Reconciliation Report Description Run a reconciliation report. Fields included in the reconciliation report. Reconciliation report menu option.
ss: The PeopleXD Payroll Reconciliation Report consolidates UK payroll data into a single view, displaying income tax, National Insurance contributions, apprenticeship levy, and amounts due to HMRC that would otherwise be scattered across multiple reports. Use this report during end-of-period payroll reconciliation to verify all statutory deductions and employer payment submissions in one place. Open this when you need to reconcile payroll values across tax months and years, or when preparing documentation for HMRC compliance. The report requires the Final Controls - Reconciliation menu option to be enabled and is accessed through the Payroll Dashboard's Outputs section.
sl: The Payroll Reconciliation Report is a feature within PeopleXD Payroll (UK) that consolidates payroll data into a single comprehensive report, addressing the limitation of information available on standard P32 reports and enabling more efficient end-of-period reconciliation processes. To access this report, users must first enable the menu option "Final Controls - Reconciliation" (Menu ID: FINALREPORTS_MENU.RECONCILIATION) within CorePortal Pay. The report is generated by navigating to the Payroll Dashboard, selecting the Manage Payroll tab, choosing a Pay Group, accessing the Outputs section, selecting Reports, and then Reconciliation, where users populate required fields including Company, Pay Group, Year, and Tax Month before clicking Print to export a .csv file from the Report Centre. The reconciliation report outputs detailed payroll data organized into four main sections: Income Tax (boxes 1-5 covering PAYE, student loans, postgraduate loans, and payment dates), National Insurance Contributions (boxes 6-20 including gross NICs, statutory pay recoveries such as SSP, SMP, SPP, SAP, and SPBP, and related NIC compensation), Apprenticeship Levy calculations both by period and year-to-date (boxes 21-34 showing earnings, BIK values, leviable earnings, levy rates, and allowances), and the final amount due to HMRC per the Employer Payment Submission (boxes 35-39 summarizing net income tax, NIC, and levy due). This document is designed for UK payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to reconcile payroll submissions with HMRC requirements and verify the accuracy of tax, national insurance, and levy calculations across payroll periods.

ss: The People Management Portal User Guide covers the migration of HR processes from CoreHR's Back Office system to CorePortal, including employee lifecycle tasks like adding starters, processing leavers, managing contracts, and administering salaries. Open this guide when your organization is transitioning to People Management on CorePortal, or when you need to understand which back office functions have moved to portal and which still require back office access.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instruction on migrating People Management functions from CoreHR's Back Office system to its Portal interface (version 27+), covering both existing processes and newly available features. The document explains how to access People Management on Portal, navigate the People Management Dashboard, and understand which back office screens have been mapped to new portal screens while identifying forms that will continue to use the back office. Key existing processes detailed include adding new starters, processing leavers, managing employee contracts and salary administration, handling allowances and personal records, recording probation details, and managing work schedules, HR balances, and cost allocations. The guide introduces new functionality available exclusively in Portal, such as the Menu Profile Matrix, Employee Files, PayScale Restriction Matrix, Social Security Settings, Tasks Lists, Terms and Conditions, Payroll Instructional Forms, Wage Warning Setup, and Employee Transfers (in version 28). Implementation involves four sequential steps: reviewing portal functionality, assigning appropriate menu profiles (PORTALMIGRATION_PEOPLEMGT_VIEW and PORTALMIGRATION_PEOPLEMGT_ALL) to portal users, completing training on specific features, and configuring data access through either automated mapping by CoreHR or manual assignment of user permissions. The document is intended for HR administrators and people management professionals who need to transition their daily operations to the portal environment, while excluding Training, Health & Safety, and HESA modules from the current migration scope. Supporting resources include CoreInsight Personnel Reporting Views, standard insight reports, back office to portal mapping tables, and supplementary training guides referenced throughout the document.

ss: The Onboarding Checklists feature in CorePortal helps HR teams create, configure, and assign onboarding task lists to new employees in the CoreHR system. This guide covers how to build default and custom checklists, add specific checklist items (documents, policies, free text, UDFs), assign them to employee groups, and monitor completion status across your workforce. Use this guide when you need to set up the initial onboarding experience for new hires, track who has completed their onboarding tasks, or modify existing checklist templates. It's essential for HR administrators managing the employee onboarding process and wanting visibility into onboarding progress on the Employee HR Dashboard.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing the Onboarding Checklists feature within CorePortal for People Management v25, a CoreHR system. The document covers the complete lifecycle of onboarding checklists, including how to view, update, and create new checklists, with specific guidance on navigating the 'Onboarding Checklists' Widget and configuring the Default Checklist through four sequential steps: Details, Home Tab Details, Steps, and Criteria List. ss: Employee Files in CoreHR allows you to set up document types and control who can view, upload, and manage employee documents across the system. sl: This user guide provides detailed configuration instructions for the Files feature within CoreHR's People Management v27 system, specifically covering how to set up and manage employee document storage and access controls. The document explains how to manage Document Types through the Template Configuration Centre by navigating to Data Centre in People Management, searching for "Document Type," and accessing the Document Type screen where administrators can add, edit, and delete document type entries with fields such as Document Type (up to 13 alphanumeric characters), Description, and Active status settings. Access management is categorized into three user roles: Administrators can be granted either full access to all files or access restricted by specific Document Types, Employees can view and upload documents through Employee Self-Service if ESS options are enabled, and Managers can access and upload files for their team members through Manager Self-Service if MSS options are enabled. t: People Management v27 - HR Allowances - User Guide v1.0
f: People Management v27 - HR Allowances - User Guide v1.0.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how employee allowance records are managed on People Management. Guidance will be provided on the following topics: • Key concepts and terminology associated with allowances. • Creating an allowance. • Editing an existing allowance. • Ending an existing allowance. • Cancelling or deleting an allowance. • The impact of salary amendments on existing allowances.
ss: HR Allowances in People Management v27 covers how to manage permanent, recurring employee allowances that are processed with each payroll run—including creating, viewing, editing, ending, and deleting allowance records. The guide explains different allowance types (Value, Percentage, and Scaled), how they interact with payroll, and the impact of salary changes on existing allowances. Open this guide when you need to set up or modify recurring payments like shift differentials, night duty allowances, or percentage-based supplements for employee contracts in CoreHR. It's essential for HR staff responsible for maintaining accurate allowance records that feed into the payroll calculation process.
sl: This user guide for People Management v27 provides comprehensive guidance on managing employee allowance records within the CoreHR system, covering key concepts, creation, editing, ending, and deletion of allowances. The document explains the distinction between permanent or recurring allowances set up in People Management (which are calculated and included in each payroll run) and once-off allowance payments that are captured directly in Payroll rather than in the HR system. It describes four main allowance types: Value allowances (both Standard Value with fixed amounts and Variable Value with employee-specific amounts), Percentage allowances (calculated as a percentage of an employee's salary), and Scaled allowances (which operate based on points on a defined scale with date-effective functionality). Users will learn to navigate specific screens and processes including how to view allowances and their statuses, add new allowances through the Allowances Screen (with specific guidance for annualized allowances), edit existing allowances, end allowances with options to remove end dates, and cancel or delete allowances entirely. The guide also addresses the impact of salary amendments and pay multiplier changes on existing allowances, as well as configuration settings such as the Pay Group 'Annual Allowance Ind' field that affects how allowances are processed. HR professionals and payroll administrators responsible for employee compensation management in CoreHR will use this document to ensure allowances are properly configured and maintained throughout an employee's tenure.

sl: This user guide provides detailed guidance on configuring the Diversity Config feature within People Management v28, specifically accessible via the HR Admin Setup Settings tab on the People Management dashboard. To access the functionality, users navigate through the Data Centre tab, select Open at HR Admin Setup Settings, and click Diversity Config to open the configuration popup screen. The guide documents configurable sections including Personal Details (containing Gender, Gender Identity, Sexual Orientation, Date of Birth, NI Number, and Previous Surname fields), Diversity (containing Ethnic Origin, Nationality, National Identity, and Citizenship fields), Family Details, Notes, and Disability Details sections, each with individual field-level controls. This document is used by HR administrators and system configurators who need to customize diversity information visibility and editability for employees and managers accessing their profiles through the employee and manager portals.

t: People Management v28 - Changing and Amending End Dates - User Guide v1.0
f: People Management v28 - Changing and Amending End Dates - User Guide v1.0.pdf
s: The purpose of this guide is to provide instruction on how to change or amend an end date that has been applied to an employee’s contract. The examples provided in this document will specifically review how to change an end date that was applied when a person was made a leaver on CoreHR. However, the steps to amend/remove the date are the same to remove an end date applied to a contract via any other standard CoreHR process.
ss: Changing and amending end dates in CoreHR's People Management system allows you to modify or remove end dates that were applied to an employee's contract when they were marked as a leaver. Use this guide when you need to update a leaver's end date to a different date, or remove an end date entirely to restore an employee record to active status (typically to correct an error). These changes can only be made before the employee has been processed by Payroll, and the steps apply whether the end date was originally set through the leaver process or another standard CoreHR function.
sl: This user guide for People Management v28 provides detailed instructions on how to change or amend end dates that have been applied to employee contracts in the CoreHR system. The document covers two main processes: changing an end date for a leaver and removing an end date entirely, with both tasks accessed through the Command Centre > Employee screen by viewing the employee record and selecting the Amend End Date option in the Summary section. To change an end date, users must locate the employee's last contract (ensuring the Appointment Status shows Ended/Ending and an End Date is populated), select Amend End Date, enter the new date in DD-Mon-YYYY format on the Modify Post Appointment End Date screen, and click OK to save. To remove an end date, users follow a similar path but select Remove End Date instead, which returns the employee's record to Active status and prevents them from being processed as a leaver. Both processes have a critical restriction: they can only be performed if the employee has not yet been processed as a leaver by Payroll, which is a key limitation users must verify before attempting these amendments. The document is primarily intended for HR administrators and People Management users who need to correct leaver records or adjust employment end dates in error situations, and it clarifies that removing an end date should only be used to correct errors rather than to rehire employees.

Open this document when you need to build or modify your company's org chart in CoreHR, establish reporting relationships, or update structural elements like departments and cost centres. It covers everything from initial structure creation through hierarchy maintenance and activation.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and managing organizational structures within CoreHR's People Management v28 system, specifically designed for CoreHR administrators and HR personnel responsible for system setup and maintenance. The document covers the complete lifecycle of organizational structure management, including creating new structures, editing existing ones, and configuring the associated organizational hierarchy through the CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management menu path, where users access the Maintain Hierarchy Structure screen to view and manage all existing organizational structures. The guide details the configuration of structural levels and reference data items such as Company, Division, Management Unit, Department, Work Group, Cost Centre, Location, and custom User Fields 1–5, along with configuration options like the Hierarchy Indicator, Initial Value, Hide Indicator, and Display Mode settings that control how the structure appears and functions within the system. Users will learn how to create hierarchies by adding initial company or top-level entries, then progressively adding subordinate levels, as well as how to modify existing structures by adding, removing, or reordering levels to reflect organizational changes.
