t: XD Recruitment Candidate Anonymisation & CV Parsing - User Guide
f: XD Recruitment Candidate Anonymisation & CV Parsing - User Guide.pdf
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on the candidate anonymisation and CV parsing functionality in PeopleXD Recruitment. This includes: • How to configure this functionality • What data can be anonymised • Where data is anonymised • Viewing parsed CVs 1.2. What is Candidate Anonymisation?
ss: PeopleXD Recruitment's candidate anonymisation and CV parsing features let you hide personal information like names and contact details during specific recruitment stages, and automatically extract structured data from CVs including employment history, education, and skills. You'll use this guide to configure which applicant statuses trigger anonymisation, set up CV parsing in admin settings, and control what candidate information appears across the Applicant List and One View screens. Open this document when you need to enable or disable anonymisation for your recruitment workflow, configure which CV data should be redacted, or understand how parsed CV information is displayed to your recruitment team.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for implementing and managing candidate anonymisation and CV parsing functionality within PeopleXD Recruitment. The document covers four main areas: configuration steps for enabling anonymisation on specific applicant statuses through the Recruitment Dashboard's Toolbox and Applicant Status settings, CV parsing setup via the Administrator Dashboard's Admin Settings where users can toggle the enable_cv_parsing parameter and configure what information displays on the CV Profile Tab, the specific locations where anonymisation is applied including the Applicant List, Bulk Status Update, and Applicant One View screens (General Tab, CV Profile Tab, and Documents Tab), and how to view parsed CV data which includes Candidate Summary, Automated Summary, Employment History, Education History, and Skills sections. The guide addresses important implementation considerations such as supported CV file types, the point-in-time nature of the parsing process, and behavior changes when candidate status updates occur through the Interview Panel Widget. This resource is designed for PeopleXD Recruitment administrators and recruiters who need to configure anonymisation rules to hide personal information like names, addresses, and contact details during specific recruitment stages, and for users managing CV submissions in systems with XD Recruitment Premium licenses and the Volcanic-powered careers website.

t: Configuring the Data Migration Tool 1.0
s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to configure the data migration functionality on CoreHR. ss: The Data Migration Tool 1.0 configures bulk data upload and processing functionality within CoreHR, enabling administrators to set up dashboard tabs, widgets, and user access controls for migrating employee and HR data. This guide walks you through creating a Data Migration tab on the Administrator Dashboard, adding the three required widgets (Data Migration Options, Data Migration Templates, and Data Migration Update Facility), and assigning appropriate menu permissions to users who need to upload files and process updates. Open this document when you're setting up CoreHR for the first time, adding new data migration users, or troubleshooting access to the data migration features in your system.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for configuring the Data Migration Tool version 28 in CoreHR, specifically designed for system administrators responsible for setting up data migration functionality. The guide covers three main configuration areas: Dashboard Configuration, which explains how to add a Data Migration tab to the Administrator Dashboard and enable the three required widgets (Data Migration Options, Data Migration Templates, and Data Migration Update Facility); User Access configuration, which details how to assign appropriate menu profiles and permissions to users; and Menu Options, which lists all available V1 (previous) and V2 (enhanced) data migration menu options that control specific processes such as template downloads, uploads, processing, and update retrieval. The guide explains that a pre-configured menu profile called CorePortal_DataMigration_User is available by default, which includes all necessary permissions for users to complete data migration uploads and process updates through the single menu option "CoreHR - Data Migration." This document is essential for CoreHR administrators who need to properly configure the data migration tool to support bulk uploading of various employee data types including contracts, allowances, auto-enrolment history, benefits, contacts, and cost allocations.

sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and using the Recruitment Dashboard within the CoreHR system, specifically version 27, and is intended for recruitment administrators managing the baseline configuration and default menu profiles. s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how to use the Data Migration Update Facility widget. This includes: • An overview of the Data Migration Update Facility widget. • What records can be updated using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. • How to update data using the Data Migration Update Facility widget. • The dependency on Insight reports for employee and contract updates. • Cancelling an update that is in progress. •...
ss: The Data Migration Update Facility is a CoreHR widget that enables bulk updates to employee records, contract details, and reference data without manually updating each record individually. It allows you to update up to 10 personal details (such as home phone, bank details, and shift information), 12 contract elements (including job title, cost centre, and employee status), and 4 reference data items (like cost centre and pay code descriptions). Open this guide when you need to make batch changes across multiple employee or contract records in CoreHR, or when updating reference data like shift types and work groups. The guide includes step-by-step instructions for completing updates, cancelling in-progress changes, fixing errors, and detailed helper guides for each of the 26 update options available.
sl: This user guide for the Data Migration Update Facility v28 is designed for CoreHR system administrators and HR professionals who need to perform bulk updates across employee, contract, and reference data records within the CorePortal environment. The document covers the complete workflow for using the Data Migration Update Facility widget, including three main types of updates: 10 specific personal details on employee records (such as address details, bank details, contacts, expense code, home phone, input location, pay code group, probation details, shift details, and sickness category code), 12 contract elements (including category, cost centre, employee status, employee sub-status, FTE, job category, job title, location, project, reports to, sub-category, and work group), and 4 reference data items (cost centre description, pay code description, shift type, and work group description). The guide provides step-by-step instructions for completing updates through the Person/Contract Records updating process and Reference Data updating process, as well as procedures for cancelling updates in progress and fixing errors that are identified during the update. An extensive appendix contains 26 detailed helper guides covering each individual update option available in the facility, enabling users to understand field requirements and dependencies for specific data elements. The Data Migration Update Facility is positioned as an efficient alternative to updating individual employee, contract, or reference data items through standard CoreHR screens, allowing bulk modifications to be performed simultaneously across multiple records while maintaining data integrity through error-checking capabilities.

The GDPR Request Centre provides this data in both a CSV file and a machine-readable JSON file. JSON – JavaScript Object Notation is an open-standard file format that uses...
ss: The GDPR Request Centre in PeopleXD enables you to process two types of employee requests: Subject Access Requests (where employees can download their personal data in CSV or JSON format) and Right to be Forgotten requests (where employees request deletion of their data). Open this guide when you need to configure user access to the GDPR Request Centre through menu profiles and organisational roles, create and manage subject access requests, process deletion requests, or understand the control parameters that govern data retention and cleardown timelines. You'll also find step-by-step instructions for downloading completed request files and reporting on GDPR activity through Insight.
sl: This How To Guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing Subject Access Requests and Right to be Forgotten requests through the GDPR Request Centre, a system feature that enables employees to request copies of their personal data in CSV and JSON formats and to exercise their right to be forgotten under GDPR regulations. The document covers the complete configuration process, beginning with creating a Menu Profile with code "GDPR" in the Security module and assigning specific Menu Options (GDPR Requests and CorePortal – InsightArea GDPR) through Security > Menu Profiles, followed by assigning the profile to individual users via PeopleXD > Security > User Management. Users must also be assigned the standard "GDPR Organisational Role" at either Company or Department level (configured via the gdpr_org_group parameter in Administrator Dashboard > Admin Settings), then assigned to specific employees through People Management > Data Centre > Maintain Organisational Role by Person. The guide describes creating a Subject Access Request by navigating to Administration Dashboard > Admin > GDPR Requests, selecting Request Type as "Data Provision," identifying the data subject, and configuring filter settings for Ordinary personal information, Sensitive categories, and Financial data, with the request progressing through OPEN, PROCESSING, and CLOSED statuses. It explains how to download completed request files in multiple formats via the GDPR Documents screen accessed through the Ellipses button on the GDPR Request Centre. Additionally, the document addresses configurable parameters including the gdpr_statutory_years setting (defaulted to 7 years) that validates deletion requests based on employee leave dates, and the gdpr_cleardown_days parameter (defaulted to 30 days) that automatically removes query request history. This guide is primarily used by administrators and GDPR compliance officers who need to configure user access, process employee data requests, and manage right to be forgotten submissions while maintaining organizational compliance with GDPR regulations.

t: End-to-End Staff Request Approval Process  0.8
s: Professional, Admin, Support and Apprenticeships Associate Professorships Statutory Professorships (RSIV and ALC6) Fully externally funded? Central Panel approved for internal recruitment ? Proceed to recruit internally Proceed to recruit externally Recruitment successful?
ss: The end-to-end staff request approval process covers how to create, route, and approve new staff positions in the Core system across professional, admin, support, apprenticeship, research, and professorship roles. It outlines the required approval gateways—including divisional approval, Registrar's Recruitment Panel (RRP) review for new posts, and Rewards Team grading assessment—along with the distinction between internal and external recruitment paths. Use this guide when your department needs to request a new position, understand which approval panels have jurisdiction over your role type, or navigate the workflow steps in Core to move a staff request through the approval process. This document also clarifies when internal recruitment must be attempted first (with a minimum 2-week posting period) before proceeding to external recruitment.
sl: This document describes the end-to-end staff request approval process for various employment categories including professional, admin, support, apprenticeships, research staff, and statutory professorships within an academic institution. The process is managed primarily through the Core system, where staff requests are initiated with a completed Staff Request form and supporting New Recruitment Approval form, then routed through divisional approval workflows before proceeding to the appropriate central approval panel—either the Registrar's Recruitment Panel (RRP) for professional and admin roles, the PVC's Panel for research staff and associate professorships, or the Senior Appointments Panel (SAP) for statutory professorships. Key decision points in the workflow determine whether positions are refills requiring less approval, whether they are fully externally funded, and whether internal or external recruitment should proceed, with the document noting that internal advertisements must remain live for at least two weeks before external recruitment is considered. The process addresses specific system configurations including the DAPP (Staff request approver) role allocation at the divisional level in Core, grading approval requirements handled by the Rewards Team, and the need to record position type to distinguish between internal and external vacancies for tracking and reporting purposes. The document includes detailed governance structures such as the RRP composition (Chair: Registrar; Secretary: Shaka Obhiozele; six-member Senior Leadership Team with three attending meetings) and specifies divisional approval authorities ranging from Heads of Division to the Pro-Vice-Chancellor for GLAM departments. Additional guidance covers priority candidate considerations, business case requirements, and staff redeployment considerations to support recruitment decisions and reporting to committees such as PRAC and Personnel Committee on vacancy numbers, staff costs, and contractor usage across divisions.

t: Insert Asks and Prompts into Letter Templates
f: HOW TO - Insert Asks and Prompts into Letter Templates.docx
s: Contents Example: Navigation Prompts and reminders Picking out key areas on images Useful on busy screens or if item is not easily identifiable. Best done in Snag-it where possible as it is more flexible and the formatting is embedded into the image rather than sitting over the top. Ask fields The Ask field code prompts you to enter information and assigns your response to a bookmark.
ss: Letter templates in Microsoft Word use Ask and Fill-In fields to prompt users for information that populates into documents automatically. Ask fields store responses in bookmarks that can be referenced in multiple locations throughout a document, while Fill-In fields insert responses directly where the field appears. You'll open this guide when creating or editing template documents that need to request variable information from users—such as client names, report months, or personalized messages—either for single documents or mail merge operations. The document covers the step-by-step process for inserting these fields, configuring prompts and default responses, and understanding the field syntax and behavior.
sl: This document is a how-to guide that explains how to insert Ask and Prompt fields into Microsoft Word letter templates to create dynamic, interactive documents. The guide covers three main field types: Ask fields, Fill-In fields, and IF fields, providing step-by-step instructions for implementing each within both standard documents and mail merge workflows. For Ask fields, users navigate to the Insert tab, select Quick Parts and then Field, choose Ask from the Field names list, and enter a prompt question and bookmark name to store the response, with optional default responses and the ability to prompt once per merge using the \o switch. Fill-In fields follow a similar process through Insert > Quick Parts > Field, selecting Fill-in, and entering prompt text, but they display responses directly in place of the field rather than referencing a bookmark. For mail merge implementations, users access fields through the Mailings tab in the Write & Insert Fields group by clicking Rules and selecting either Ask or Fill-in, allowing responses to apply to all records when the "Ask once" or equivalent checkbox is selected. The document explains field syntax conventions such as { ASK Bookmark"Prompt" [Optional switches] } and { FILLIN ["Prompt"] [Optional switches] }, along with optional switches like \d for default responses and \o for single prompts during merges. This guide is used by document creators, business professionals, and mail merge administrators who need to create reusable letter templates that prompt for variable information while maintaining consistent formatting across multiple documents or merged records.

You'll also find steps for raising change requests and maintaining departmental letterhead configurations.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing document templates in Portal v2.0, covering the complete lifecycle of template creation, modification, and maintenance. The document is organized into four main sections: creating new mail merge document templates, updating existing templates, raising change requests, and resolving common template issues. For new template creation, the guide details the process of setting up merge fields by accessing Mailings > Start Mail Merge > Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard, selecting data sources from the Data Source folder with pipe ("|") delimiters, and configuring macros that automate functions such as pulling departmental headers and footers from C:\Coreapps\Letter_head.docx and displaying Fill-in prompts to end users. Template updates require editing the Word template, uploading amended versions to the Portal, making changes through the Portal interface, and archiving old versions while maintaining a Change-Update Requests log located at O:\PS\HRIS\Core correspondence templates. The troubleshooting section addresses specific formatting and functionality problems including department headers appearing on every page, spacing issues between rows and paragraphs, missing headers, and merge field and prompt display failures. t: Manage Email Templates v2.0
f: HOW TO - Manage Email Templates v2.0.docx
s: The University uses emails for communicating with job applicants. This document relates to the manual email sent to applicants from the Recruitment module about a specific vacancy. For guidance on automatic emails refer to: This guide covers the following process steps: Create a new email template From the Templates tab click on ACTIONS and choose Create Email Template 1.1.
ss: Email templates in the Recruitment module are used to communicate with job applicants about specific vacancies. This guide walks you through creating new email templates, editing existing ones, and deleting templates within the HR Admin setup. Open this document when you need to set up or modify recruitment communications, customize merge fields for applicant information, or manage your library of email templates. The process involves accessing the Document and Email templates section in People Management, configuring template details, and composing the email subject and body with available data fields.
sl: This document is a how-to guide for managing email templates within the University's Recruitment module, specifically for communications sent to job applicants during the recruitment process. The guide covers three core processes: creating a new email template, amending an existing template, and deleting a template, all accessed through the Core|Portal > People Management > Data Centre > HR Admin HR Setup Settings > Document and Email templates menu path. When creating a new email template, users must complete the Template Details section by entering a Template Name, selecting the "Called From" source (typically Employee Search or View Applicants), choosing a Template Group (Employee Search, View Applicants, Post Appointments, or Recruitment), and selecting a Data View Source that determines which merge fields are available for insertion. The Email Editor section allows users to enter a subject line and email body (limited to 2000 characters including spaces), with the ability to insert dynamic merge fields by positioning the cursor and selecting from the available field menu. To amend an existing template, users click the ellipses next to the template name and select "Edit" to make required changes before saving. To delete a template, users similarly click the ellipses and choose "Delete," then confirm the deletion with "YES." The document includes an important caveat that editing or deleting active templates that have already been used or sent has not been tested, and the implications of such actions are unknown, which system administrators should consider before making changes to templates in use.

t: Word tips Keep text together
s: Keep text together You can often improve the look of your document by keeping certain words and paragraphs together on the page or across page breaks. Also, you can use hyphenation to improve overall readability. Word automatically breaks the text at a space or a hyphen at the end of a line.
ss: Formatting text in Word to prevent awkward page breaks and improve document appearance covers techniques like nonbreaking spaces, nonbreaking hyphens, and paragraph control settings. Use this guide when you need to keep related words, hyphenated terms, or entire paragraphs from splitting across page lines, or when you want to eliminate widows and orphans (single lines stranded at page breaks). Open this document if you're finalizing a Word document and want to polish its layout and readability before sharing or printing.
sl: This document provides practical guidance on formatting text in Microsoft Word to improve document appearance and readability by keeping related content together across page breaks. The guide covers four main techniques: using nonbreaking spaces to keep two words together on a single line (inserted via Insert > Symbol > More Symbols > Special Characters tab, or using the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+Spacebar), and using nonbreaking hyphens to prevent hyphenated words from breaking across lines (accessed the same way or with Ctrl+Shift+Minus Sign). For paragraph-level formatting, the document explains how to keep an entire paragraph on the same page by right-clicking the paragraph, selecting Paragraph, navigating to the Line and Page Breaks tab, and checking the "Keep lines together" option. It also describes how to keep related consecutive paragraphs or subheadings with their following content together on the same page using the same right-click menu path and checkbox. The guide addresses specific formatting problems such as "widow" lines (the last line of a paragraph appearing alone at the top of a page) and "orphan" lines (the first line appearing alone at the bottom of a page), which can be prevented by enabling Widow/Orphan control in the same Pagination section of the Paragraph dialog box. This document is typically used by Word users who want to enhance document layout and professionalism by controlling how text flows across pages.

t: DRAFT_HOW TO - Fix Payroll Condenser Errors
f: DRAFT_HOW TO - Fix Payroll Condenser Errors.docx
s: The PAYDEP01 Payroll Costings Report is run each month after the final monthly payroll run. It returns the complete pay history for all active staff (casuals and employees) in a given payroll period, e.g. We share this data with departments so that they can check their monthly costings.
ss: Payroll Condenser errors occur when the automatic comparison between original PAYDEP01 payroll data and condensed payroll data reveals mismatches, which must be fixed before sharing monthly costings reports with departments. This guide walks you through identifying error records in the EmployeeCheck worksheet, preparing comparison data by copying original records next to condensed records in Excel, and manually fixing errors by checking for missing Appointment IDs and pay Elements. Open this document when you run the monthly PAYDEP01 Payroll Costings Report and the Final Check Figures worksheet shows discrepancies that need to be resolved.
sl: This document is a comprehensive guide for identifying and resolving errors that occur when using the Payroll Condenser tool, a macro-enabled Excel spreadsheet that processes payroll data for university departments. The document explains that the Payroll Condenser takes large datasets from the PAYDEP01 Payroll Costings Report (which can contain over 140,000 rows) and condenses them into single rows per Employee + Appointment ID + Pay Element combination by consolidating employer-paid costs such as National Insurance, apprentice levy, and pension contributions into their corresponding salary and allowance rows. Error identification begins by unhiding the EmployeeCheck worksheet and filtering the "Difference" columns to locate non-zero values that indicate mismatches between original and condensed data, with the filtered personnel numbers representing the error records requiring correction. The data preparation phase involves navigating to the Condensed worksheet to locate the error record, then copying all relevant rows from columns A (Tax Year) through AH (Total by Cost Centre) from the Original Data worksheet and pasting them below the condensed records with blank rows in between for clarity. The fixing process requires visual comparison of condensed versus original data to identify where the Payroll Condenser has skipped records, with particular attention to missing Appointment IDs and missing Elements that must be added to the condensed dataset to resolve the errors. This guide is primarily intended for payroll administrators and departmental staff who work with the Payroll Condenser tool monthly and need to validate that condensed payroll data accurately reflects the original payroll run before sharing costings information with departments.

s: reports Reports Some reports have pay codes hard-coded into calculations and conditions. Payroll should confirm whether a pay code needs to be added to any of the following reports. If the pay code is for an allowance administered by departments, you must add it to the ALLOWANCE_FLAG calculation in the following .RDL files: PERDEP01 Full Data Set PERDEP01 Full Data Set with Allowances PERDEP01 Casuals Only - Full Data Set with Allowances PERDEP20 Approved Allowance...
ss: Pay code maintenance in the Portal covers viewing, creating, and editing pay codes used in payroll processing, including allowances, deductions, and special codes for court orders. Use this guide when you need to search for existing pay codes, create new ones by copying templates or from scratch, or configure pay code details like formulas, rules, and general ledger mappings. You'll also learn how to set up specific pay code types such as percentage allowances, scaled deductions, student loans, and court/voluntary order codes. This document is essential for payroll administrators managing the complete lifecycle of pay codes in the Core Portal system.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for managing pay codes within the Portal's payroll system, covering both viewing and creating new pay codes along with their detailed configuration. The document guides users through accessing the Pay Code Library via Core | Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pay Codes and provides multiple search methods including search by pay code, search by description or partial description, and advanced filtering by payment type. Pay code details are managed through a Pay Code Wizard consisting of three main tabs—Pay Code Formula (for basic setup including analysis code, hours/value/days/units, and multiplier settings), Rules (for configuration such as taxability, National Insurance eligibility, and pensionability), and General Ledger (for finance-related settings like expense codes), with Court or Voluntary Order pay codes requiring an additional fourth tab called Payment Orders. The document explains how to create new pay codes either from scratch using the CREATE NEW PAY CODE button or more commonly by cloning existing pay codes using the Clone function, with users required to complete a New Pay Code Request spreadsheet before creation. Specific configuration details covered include setting multiplier values (ranging from 0 for non-payroll codes to 2 for double time), adding scaled deductions with thresholds, creating percentage-based allowances with calculation elements, and configuring student loan thresholds. The document also addresses the critical requirement that new pay codes must be added to specific hard-coded calculations in various .RDL report files such as PERDEP01, PERDEP20 for department-administered allowances, PAYLIN20 and PAYLIN21 for Linacre College, and PAYCTR40 for casual payroll hourly rate monitoring. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HRIS support staff who need to establish, maintain, and properly integrate pay codes throughout the organization's payroll and financial reporting systems.

t: Maintain Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal v1.3
f: HOW TO - Maintain Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal v1.3.docx
s: Contents On the Employee Self Service landing page the next Pay Day is displayed under ‘Important Dates’. This relies on Payroll calendars held in the Portal for each pay group paid through the Payroll module. In December each year new calendars must be created for the following year.
ss: Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal stores the payment schedule for each pay group, which displays the next pay day to employees on the Employee Self Service landing page. You'll need to create new calendars in December each year with all 12 monthly payment dates for the following year, since existing calendars cannot be overwritten. This guide walks you through creating, editing, and deleting payroll calendars in the Core Portal's Admin Settings, plus explains the annual maintenance schedule to keep pay date information current.
sl: This How To Guide provides instructions for maintaining payroll calendar dates in the Portal system, specifically addressing the annual process of creating, editing, and deleting pay calendars for different pay groups. The document describes three core procedures: creating a new calendar by accessing Core Portal > Employee Dashboard, navigating to Admin Settings via the Classic UI interface, and completing the Create CorePayroll Calendar Dates form with fields for Pay Group (20 or 21), Year, Pay Group Frequency (Monthly), and all 12 monthly Pay Dates from January through December. The guide addresses the specific scenario where existing calendars cannot be overwritten, requiring users to create entirely new calendars each December for the following year before the December pay date, then delete the previous year's calendars in January after the January pay date. It explains that until new calendars are created, the Next Pay Date section on the Employee Self Service landing page will display as blank, and that editing should only occur if a published pay date has been changed by the Payroll team. The document also covers viewing calendar details through a pop-up window and the editing process, which requires dates to be entered in dd/mm/yy format. This guide is intended for Portal administrators and Payroll teams responsible for maintaining accurate pay date information that displays under the Important Dates section on the Employee Self Service landing page, and it integrates with the Payroll module and ESS (Employee Self Service) systems.

Open this document whenever you're working with the Payroll Dashboard's Pension Scheme settings and have a Pension Scheme Template from Payroll to complete.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing pension schemes within a Portal v2.0 system, covering the complete lifecycle of pension scheme administration from viewing existing schemes to creating and editing them. The document guides users through accessing the Pension Schemes window via Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pension Scheme, where they can search pension schemes by code and view tiered (banded) contribution rates organized by salary tiers with employee (EE) and employer (ER) percentage fields and effective dates. For adding new pension schemes, the guide explains the process of duplicating existing schemes and then completing three pages of detailed configuration, starting with Page 1 fields such as Pension Code, Description, Company, Renewal Period (Tax Week), fixed and percentage-based deduction values for employees and employers, Reckonable Days, Social Welfare Deduction settings, Scheme Type (contributory or non-contributory), and employee pay codes for various deduction categories. The document also covers editing existing schemes to amend contribution rates for employees and employers, modify pay codes assigned to schemes, and update other details, as well as maintaining Voluntary Salary Cap (VSC) rates and managing auto-enrolment notifications and parameters including pension rules, earnings parameters, and state pension ages. Users of this document are typically payroll and pensions administrators who need to configure and maintain pension scheme data, and the guide references related reports (PERSUP14, PERSUP15, PAYPEN02) that require updating whenever pension rates change, as well as external configuration documentation for auto-enrolment events in HRISPRD.

sl: This document provides instructions for maintaining and updating the Casual Payment spreadsheet v2.0, a tool used by payroll teams to manage casual employee payments with current hourly rates and validation rules. The primary task covered is updating hourly rates on the submission spreadsheet, which requires unprotecting the workbook via File > Info > Protect Workbook Structure, unhiding the Hourly Rates sheet, and replacing the existing spinal point and hourly rate data while ensuring values are ordered from lowest to highest. t: Manage Expense Codes (DRAFT)
s: Expense Codes Background Expense Codes are used to summarise transactions into groups of expenses/costs and liabilities, so they can be posted GL in the form of Debits and Credits. The following points should be taken into consideration regarding Expense Codes: An Expense Code is not associated with an employee. Its possible to have a different expense Code for every element of pay an employee receives.
ss: Expense Codes in PeopleXD are 8-digit numeric codes used to categorize payroll transactions into groups of expenses, costs, and liabilities that post to the general ledger as debits and credits in your Financial Management System. This guide covers how to view existing codes, manually create new codes when requested by Payroll Operations, and set up data mapping to ensure PeopleXD expense codes match those in your FMS (particularly when converting between numeric and alphanumeric formats). Open this document when you need to add a new expense code to PeopleXD, configure GL costing for a new pay code or allowance, or troubleshoot code mismatches between your payroll and financial management systems.
sl: This How To Guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing Expense Codes within PeopleXD, a payroll and human resources system that interfaces with Financial Management Systems (FMS). The document explains that Expense Codes are 8-digit numeric fields used to summarize and categorize employee transactions into groups of expenses, costs, and liabilities for posting to the General Ledger as Debits and Credits, and that they work in conjunction with Cost Centres rather than being tied to individual employees. Users can view existing Expense Codes by navigating to People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Expense Codes, and create new codes through the same path or alternatively via Payroll Dashboard > Settings > General Ledger Costing > Expense GL Codes by clicking Add and entering the code number and description provided by the Payroll Operations Manager. The document addresses a common integration challenge where PeopleXD's numeric Expense Codes need to be mapped to alphanumeric GL/Account codes in the FMS using Data Talk mapping functionality, accessed through Payroll Dashboard > Settings > General Ledger Costings > General Rules & Settings and selecting the ORAEXP mapping purpose code for Expense Codes to Oracle. The guide includes steps for configuring the File Definitions screen (File Type R12GL) to ensure proper mapping between systems, and concludes with instructions for re-running the General Ledger process via Payroll Dashboard to verify that mapped codes are outputting correctly to the FMS. This document is primarily used by Payroll Operations Managers and system administrators who need to set up new Expense Codes in response to new pay codes or allowance requests.

t: Manage Grades and Rates in the Portal v1.0

ss: The Portal's Pay Rates and Pay Scales sections let you manage employee grades and their associated salary rates, scale points, and pension assignments. Use this guide when you need to create a new grade with annual salaries at different scale points, update existing rates, assign pension schemes, or configure payroll and general ledger output rules. Open it if you're responsible for maintaining grade structures, setting up pay scales for new roles, or making salary adjustments that affect payroll processing. This guide covers all Portal navigation paths and configuration steps needed to manage grades from creation through editing and removal.
sl: This How To Guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing pay grades and salary rates within the Portal system's payroll and people management modules. The document covers five main processes: viewing existing rates through Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Pay Rates > View Position Rates, viewing scale points via Core|Portal > People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Pay Scale Point, adding new pay scales (grades) through multiple configuration steps, editing existing pay scales and rates, and removing or closing grades from the system. When creating a new grade, users must navigate through sequential steps including setting up the pay scale with position code and description, configuring scale points with ascending numerical values and narratives, entering annual salary rates for each scale point, assigning pension schemes through the Auto Enrolment settings under Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters, and configuring General Ledger output rules via Maintain GL Parameters to control which grades appear in projects and GL files. The document specifically addresses common issues such as the inability to delete scale points once created (requiring values to be set to 0.01 instead), the random sort order when locating grades in GL parameters, and the need to check whether changes to standard grades should also apply to equivalent Linacre College Grades (ZC01S to ZC10S). Payroll administrators and HR personnel use this guide when implementing new salary structures, updating annual pay rates, managing pension assignments, and ensuring proper integration with general ledger and payroll reporting systems, with references to reports like PERDEP01 Staff in Post, PERDEP20 Monthly Changes, and PERDEP21 Monthly Data Input check that may require updates based on grade changes.

Open this document when you need to understand the consultation and approval requirements, change management steps, testing procedures, and downstream system impacts—such as updates needed in X5, Financials, and payroll reports—associated with grade or rate changes.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for managing grades and rates within the Portal system, covering the complete lifecycle of grade creation and modification processes. The document outlines that the Reward Team and HR Analytics Team are responsible for producing and confirming rates, and specifies the detailed information required to set up new grades—including grade code, description, scale points, scale narratives, bar points, yearly full-time rates, full-time hours, and effective dates—all confirmed through the Portal > People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Pay Scales screen. The approved process requires consultation with multiple teams including Payroll, Pensions, and the X5 system (used for research grant costing), with changes typically discussed and agreed through the HRSEG (Human Resources Systems Evaluation Group) or via expedited approval methods when urgency demands. Grade change requests must be formally documented in OSM (the change management system) and approved before QA testing, with the HRIS Functional Analysis Team responsible for the actual implementation of new grades and points. The document addresses specific scenarios such as removing scale points due to minimum wage compliance, which may necessitate moving existing employees to different grade points—a task typically performed by the HRIS Data Service Administrator in consultation with relevant departments. Additionally, the guide identifies downstream system impacts requiring notification to teams including the BFT Team and Financials FSM team regarding the GL to R12 interface, and emphasizes the importance of notifying the X5 team well in advance of rate changes, ideally during non-production testing phases.

ss: Payroll data loading in PeopleXD involves uploading employee rates, pay scales, and position rates through the Administrator and Payroll Dashboards using templated Excel files. This guide walks you through the required column formats and upload sequence for four file types: Pay Grade Scale Point (manual), Pay Scale Point (automated), Position Rate Details, and Employee New Rates of Pay, along with back-out procedures if needed. Open this document when you need to perform bulk payroll data uploads, update employee salary information across multiple records, or maintain pay grade structures and scale points in PeopleXD. It's essential reference material for HR teams preparing cleansed data files from Analytics for system loading.
sl: This document is a comprehensive guide for uploading payroll-related data files into the PeopleXD system using both manual and automated processes across the Administrator and Payroll Dashboards. The document outlines a mandatory four-step loading sequence that begins with manual creation of new grades via People Management > Data Center > Pay Scales, followed by loading a Pay Scale Point File through Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration > Load File (using pipe-delimited formatting), then loading a Position Rate Details File via Payroll Dashboard > Uploads > Load Position Rates of Pay, and finally loading an Employee New Rates of Pay file through the same Payroll Dashboard uploads area. Each section specifies the exact column headings and data requirements, such as Position Code, Description, Scale Points aligned with National Spine Points (NSP) and University of Oxford (UoO) naming conventions, rate sequence numbers, and effective dates in DDMMYYYY format. The document explains technical considerations including file format conversions (converting CSV to pipe-delimited files using Notepad++), the purpose of barrier points that prevent automatic salary increments, and toggle settings for active status. Back-out procedures are provided for each file type, allowing users to clear down loaded data using the Administrator Dashboard's 'Clear Down' option if no subsequent activity has occurred. This guide is primarily used by payroll administrators and data managers who work with cleansed and transformed data provided by the Analytics Team in Excel format to perform mass uploads of salary grades, scale points, position rates, and employee pay rates across the organization.

ss: Bank sort code uploads keep your Core payroll system's reference data current when financial institutions release updated sorting codes. This guide walks you through preparing the sort code file from the external sorting codes database, validating it through multiple formatting steps in Excel and Notepad++, uploading it via CorePortal's Data Migration tool, and verifying the data appears correctly in Core's Back-Office. Open this document when you receive a HEAT incident notification about new bank sort codes becoming available, or whenever you need to update the bank reference data in your Core system to ensure accurate employee payment processing.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive how-to guide for uploading bank sort codes into a Core system, covering the entire process from file preparation through post-upload verification. The process begins with receiving email notifications logged in HEAT, accessing www.sortingcodeselectronic.co.uk with credentials, and downloading the "Variable Length – delimited" file to the Bank Sort Codes folder at P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\Bank Sort Codes. The file preparation involves unzipping the downloaded file as codes.dat, running the "PERSUP09_Bank Sort Codes Reference Data" report in Discoverer, exporting to Excel, and using the SORT CODE MASTER.xlsm file to compare existing and new sort codes by running a macro in the "Instructions" tab. The document then details extensive data cleaning steps using Notepad++ to remove quotation marks and excess commas via Find & Replace functions, followed by verification in Excel to ensure data remains within columns A–F only. The upload itself is performed through CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration, selecting "Bank Reference" under "F: Reference level," with the system validating data every 10 minutes and reporting errors that must be corrected before migration can proceed. Finally, successful uploads are verified by navigating to Core Personnel > Reference > A-C > Bank Sort Codes and using Query Mode to confirm the migrated data matches the original upload file. This guide is typically used by HR administrators or support staff responsible for maintaining current bank reference data in the Core system.

The document addresses common data quality issues such as sort codes being misinterpreted as dates, requiring format changes from dd/mm/yyyy to ddmmyy and adding leading zeros through custom formatting (000000), as well as removing dashes from sort code values using Find and Replace. Users must also compare new sort codes against existing data using the Discoverer report "PERSUP09_Bank Sort Codes Reference Data" and conditional formatting to identify duplicates before uploading only non-duplicate entries. ss: Pay code maintenance in the Portal covers the complete lifecycle of managing allowances and deductions—from viewing existing pay codes to creating new ones and configuring their formulas, rules, and general ledger settings. Use this guide when you need to search for a specific pay code, set up a new allowance or deduction with calculation rules, or adjust whether a pay code is taxable, pensionable, or linked to court orders. Payroll administrators open this document whenever they're processing a New Pay Code Request or need to modify existing pay code configurations in Core|Portal's Payroll Dashboard. The guide walks through the Pay Code Wizard tabs and explains how to handle special scenarios like percentage allowances, scaled deductions, and court/voluntary order pay codes.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for maintaining pay codes within a portal-based payroll system, covering both viewing existing codes and creating or editing new ones. The guide walks users through accessing the Pay Code Library via Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, and explains three primary search methods: searching by specific pay code, by description or partial description, and using an Advanced Filter to filter by payment type. For viewing pay code details, users click the ellipses next to a code and select Edit to access the Pay Code Wizard, which contains three standard sections—Pay Code Formula (for basic setup), Rules (for configuration such as tax and pension treatment), and General Ledger (for finance-related settings like expense codes)—with Court Order and Voluntary Order pay codes requiring an additional Payment Orders section. When creating new pay codes, users must reference a New Pay Code Request spreadsheet and can either clone an existing code or create one from scratch by selecting Payment Type and Payment Subset Type; the cloning process preserves attributes from the original code but requires verification and updates. The Pay Code Formula section requires detailed configuration of mandatory fields including Analysis Code, Hours/Value/Days/Units designation, Multiplier values (ranging from -1 for deductions to 2 for double time), and conditional fields such as Standard Value, Scaled Deduction thresholds, Percentage calculations, or Student Loan thresholds depending on the pay code type. The document also addresses critical integration points, noting that payroll administrators must update specific RDL report files (PERDEP01, PERDEP20, PAYLIN20, PAYLIN21, and PAYCTR40) when new pay codes are created for allowances, Linacre College, or casual hourly rates. This guide is designed for payroll staff and HRIS Support personnel who regularly maintain pay code configurations and must follow the formal New Pay Code Request Template process before implementation.

t: Maintain Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal v1.2
f: HOW TO - Maintain Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal v1.2.docx
s: Contents On the Employee Self Service landing page the next Pay Day is displayed under ‘Important Dates’. This relies on Payroll calendars held in the Portal for each pay group paid through the Payroll module. In December each year new calendars must be created for the following year.
ss: Payroll Calendar Dates in the Portal determine the "Next Pay Day" displayed on the Employee Self Service landing page and must be maintained annually for each pay group. You'll use this guide to create new calendars each December or January for the upcoming year, edit existing calendars if pay dates change, and delete outdated calendars. Open this document when you need step-by-step instructions for managing payroll calendars through the Core Portal's Admin Settings, or when you're preparing the portal for a new calendar year.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing payroll calendar dates within the Portal system, specifically addressing the annual process of creating, updating, and removing pay calendars for different pay groups. The document explains that the Portal's Employee Self Service landing page displays the next pay day under "Important Dates," which depends on payroll calendars maintained for each pay group processed through the Payroll module. Since existing calendars cannot be overwritten, new calendars must be created each December for the following year, with the guide offering two implementation options depending on when December's pay day falls. To access the calendar maintenance functions, users must navigate through the Core Portal Employee Dashboard by first switching to the Classic UI via Account Settings, then selecting Admin Settings from the Quick Jump menu and locating the Payroll Calendar Parameters section under Core Portal Additional Parameters. The document details three primary tasks: creating new calendars by clicking "Create CorePayroll Calendar Dates" and entering pay group numbers (20 or 21), year, monthly frequency, and all 12 monthly pay dates in dd/mm/yy format; editing existing calendars to update dates that have been changed by Payroll; and deleting outdated calendars using the Delete button with confirmation. The recommended Option 1 approach suggests creating January-only calendars in December, then updating them with full-year dates in January before deleting the previous year's calendars, while Option 2 allows creating complete calendars immediately after December's pay day and removing old ones, though this leaves the Next Pay Date section temporarily blank.

sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing pay grades and salary rates within the Portal system, covering both viewing and configuring grade and rate information. The document details specific menu paths such as Core|Portal > People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data for accessing pay scales, scale points, and rates, as well as Core|Portal > Payroll Dashboard for viewing and adding position rates. ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in CoreHR let you create custom data fields at the Appointment, Person (employee), or Recruitment level to capture organization-specific information. Open this document when you need to build a new UDF from scratch—including setting up field labels, defining dropdown list values, choosing where the field appears in the system, and optionally restricting access to specific users. You'll also find instructions for editing or removing existing UDFs and how to grant access to secured fields. Use the accompanying Excel template to plan and test your UDF design before creating it in the CoreHR portal.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for creating, configuring, and managing User Defined Fields (UDFs) in CoreHR, which can be established at three levels: Appointment, Person (employee), or Recruitment. The process begins with completing an Excel template from the MASTER UDF Template v2 file located in P:\PROJECTS\HRIS Programme\12. Support\Reference Data\UDFs\, where users enter a unique 6-character Reference Code, a description (maximum 40 characters), select the Location type, define Field Items with labels, choose Data Types, and configure up to 12 list items if applicable. Once the template is validated through the Preview tab, users navigate to Core Portal > Data Centre > HR Admin Setup Settings > User Defined Objects to create the UDF in the system, then access the Data Labels screen via the Ellipses button to configure field properties including Active status, User Description, Data Type, and optional Format Mask for numeric fields. The document addresses critical configuration steps such as defining where the UDF appears by selecting Post Appointments for appointment-level UDFs, Employees for person-level UDFs, or E-Recruitment for recruitment UDFs, as well as creating the List of Values by clicking the Define List Items button and adding individual items with Active toggles. For UDFs requiring restricted access, users can enable Security Required and then grant access through Core Portal > Core Security > Set Up > System Users by selecting the appropriate account type (Portal or Back Office), entering the username, selecting User Defined Access, and toggling the Access Granted column for each authorized user. The document also covers editing and removing existing UDFs, cautioning that changes will affect all existing records and may cause errors, with detailed guidance available in the referenced Knowledge Article on User Defined Fields. Personnel Administrators, Recruitment Administrators, and system configuration specialists use this document when setting up custom fields to capture organization-specific data, and the UDFs created are subsequently reported across various reports including the PERDEP01 Staff in Post report.

You'll access these functions through People Management > Reference Data > Location Codes in the Core Portal. Open this guide if you're setting up a new department location, updating address information for payroll purposes, or deactivating a location that's no longer in use.
sl: This How To Guide provides step-by-step instructions for creating, editing, and removing location codes within the Core|Portal system, specifically accessed through People Management > Reference Data > Location Codes. The document guides users through creating new location codes by navigating to the ADD function and populating required fields including Location Code (sequential), Description (formatted as two-character department code followed by location description), and Area Code (beat bike number), with address details entered through the ellipses menu option after initial save. When editing existing location codes, users can modify the description field directly or access address details through the ellipses menu to update individual address fields, taking care not to populate Address Line 5 as it does not print on payslips. The document addresses the specific scenario of handling multiple location codes for the same department by requiring sequential numbering in the description field (e.g., AA1, AA2) to maintain clarity. For location code removal, rather than deleting entries that may exist on historic appointments, the system requires users to replace the description with "DO NOT USE" followed by the two-character department code in parentheses and to remove associated address details. This document is typically used by personnel administrators and data management staff who need to maintain accurate location information in the payroll and human resources system to ensure proper address assignment for employee records.

s: New functionality providing the ability to delete an employee’s appointment when processed in error either by way of replacing contract (transfer) or as a new additional contract. In addition, the ability to delete the latest appointment sequence if processed in error. The delete contract functionality can be used for the following process scenarios: Replacement Contract has been processed – Delete replacement and reinstate previous post To be eligible for deletion a new...
ss: Deleting contracts and amendments in PeopleXD People Management allows HR administrators to reverse employee appointments that were processed in error, including replacement contracts, additional contracts, and contract amendments. You can delete a contract only if the new post hasn't been paid yet, using the Delete Contract button found in the HR Employee Dashboard Contracts section. This guide covers step-by-step instructions for deleting contracts and amendments, eligibility requirements, configuration settings needed, and how deletions affect applicants and HR audit records. Open this document when you need to undo an incorrectly processed appointment and restore an employee's previous post or remove an erroneous contract amendment.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for HR administrators using the PeopleXD PeopleManagement system to delete employee contracts and appointments that were processed in error. The guide covers three primary deletion scenarios: removing replacement contracts while reinstating the previous post, deleting additional contracts that were incorrectly added, and removing the latest appointment sequence when a contract amendment was processed in error. To delete a contract, users navigate through the People Management menu to the Command Centre tab, access the Employee section, search for the relevant employee, and then locate the Contracts section on the HR Employee Dashboard where a Delete Contract button is available in the Summary section ellipsis menu. The system enforces specific eligibility requirements, such as that contracts can only be deleted if the new post has not yet been paid and the appointment has not already ended; if these conditions are not met, an error message prevents deletion. Configuration of the delete functionality requires enabling multiple menu options across both the People Management system (including PEOPLE_MANAGEMENT, HR ADMIN, EMPLOYEE_DASHBOARD, and DELETE_CONTRACT_AMENDMENT) and Web Services (including various DELETE_APPOINTMENTS and related API endpoints). The document also addresses important side effects and considerations, including how applicants linked to deleted replacement contracts remain associated with the vacancy but cannot reselect the post, and how deleted appointment details are recorded in the HR Audit Report with an audit type indicator showing "delete" for tracking and compliance purposes.

t: Maintain Continuous Service Eligibility Rules in the Portal
f: HOW TO - Maintain Continuous Service Eligibility Rules in the Portal.docx
s: PeopleXD holds rules which determine whether or not a given appointment is eligible to be counted towards an employee’s Continuous Service. Those rules must be aligned with the University’s policy around Continuous Service and should be updated whenever this policy changes. This guide covers the following process steps: Create a new rule Select “Continuous Service” from the drop-down list.
ss: Continuous Service eligibility rules in PeopleXD determine which appointments count toward an employee's service history, and these rules must stay aligned with your University's Continuous Service policy. This guide walks you through creating new eligibility rules, amending existing ones, and deleting rules that are no longer needed in the Core Portal's Organisation Rules section. You'll learn how to configure rule fields like sequence order, eligibility status, reference levels, break-in-service calculations, and activation status. Open this guide when you need to set up or modify the criteria that govern whether specific appointments, departments, pay scales, or employee statuses qualify for Continuous Service calculations.
sl: This How To guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing Continuous Service eligibility rules within PeopleXD, the system that determines which employee appointments count toward Continuous Service calculations in alignment with University policy. The document covers three core processes accessed through Core|Portal > People Management > HR Admin Setup and Settings > Organisation Rules > Eligible Service Rules: creating new rules, amending existing rules, and deleting rules. When creating a new rule, users select "Continuous Service" from a dropdown menu and configure multiple fields including Seq. (the sequence order in which rules are applied), Eligible (a checkbox indicating eligibility status), Reference1-3 (classification levels such as Company, Department, Employee Status, or Job Title), Code1-3 (corresponding alphanumeric codes), Break In Service (number of days between appointments), Break In Service Type (the starting day of the week for counting break periods), and Length of Service (whether to include or exclude break days). The document emphasizes that sequence numbers should be added to the bottom of the rule list unless specifically inserting mid-sequence, and that the Break In Service Type field allows administrators to specify which day of the week the break countdown begins, such as "From Sunday" or "From Monday." Amending existing rules requires locating the target rule by scrolling or filtering, then editing the necessary fields using the same field definitions provided in the creation process. Deleting rules involves selecting the target rule, clicking the ellipses (…) menu at the end of the row, and choosing Delete, with a critical warning that deletions cannot be undone.

t: Onboarding draft guidance and notes
s: The creation of an onboarding checklist was approved and prioritised by the Personnel POG in 2022. The checklist is accessed in the Social Hub via Employee Self Service. Social Hub Configuration widget In order to configure On and offboarding the Social Hub Configuration widget must be enabled.
ss: Onboarding checklists in Social Hub are configured through the Administrator Dashboard using custom pages, surveys, and staff grouping rules. This guidance covers how to set up the Social Hub Configuration widget, create checklist components (text pages, links, and surveys with various field types), and restrict access to tasks based on employee groups. You'd open this document when implementing or managing an employee onboarding program that uses the Social Hub Employee Self Service portal. It provides step-by-step instructions for administrators building the initial checklist structure and controlling who sees which onboarding tasks.
sl: This onboarding draft guidance document provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and building an onboarding checklist system within the Social Hub, which is accessed through Employee Self Service. The document covers the foundational setup requirement of enabling the Social Hub Configuration widget through Administrator Dashboard > Admin > Site Manager > Dashboard Configuration, and then details how to create individual checklist components including Custom Pages (with Text or Link types), Surveys, and various field configurations. For custom pages, administrators can upload .png cover images and add content up to 2500 characters, with the ability to insert hyperlinks for Link-type pages through the Edit Custom Page window. The Surveys section explains how to create new surveys by defining sections (configured as Rows or Columns) and adding fields with different answer option types such as Text Field, Text Area, Date Field, Number Field, Combo Field, Radio Group, and Slider Field, with some field types like Combo Field (Ref Data) linking to pre-existing reference data items. Additional configuration tasks include Landing Page Configuration to organize and restrict custom pages to specific staff groups, Staff Grouping to control which tasks are presented to individuals based on defined criteria, and Adding Items to the Checklist which involves Input items, UDF items, and surveys. The document also covers restricting access to tasks using Staff Groups and the final Activation step, with the entire system designed to support personnel onboarding workflows approved by the Personnel POG in 2022.

t: PeopleMgt_Delete Person within PeopleXD People Management
f: HOW TO - PeopleMgt_Delete Person within PeopleXD People Management.docx
s: The Access Group has released new functionality providing the ability to delete an employee/person record, which can be used where the employee record was added in error. There are limitations, which prevent a person record from being deleted, these are: An employee record cannot be deleted if their salary has been paid. In this instance, an error will be displayed stating, “This person record cannot be deleted as they have already been processed by payroll.
ss: Deleting employee or person records in PeopleXD People Management requires checking eligibility first, as records cannot be deleted if payroll has processed salary payments or if WFM timesheet transactions exist on the record. This guide walks you through the step-by-step process of deleting a person record from the Command Centre, scheduling the deletion (which occurs overnight), and undoing a scheduled deletion if needed before the job completes. You'll also learn how to remove WFM timesheet transactions that may be blocking deletion and how to report on pending deletions using the PERSUP17 HR Audit report. Open this document when you need to remove an employee record that was added in error or when you're troubleshooting why a person cannot be deleted from the system.
sl: This how-to guide documents the complete process for deleting employee or person records within the PeopleXD People Management system, specifically addressing scenarios where employee records have been added in error. The document covers the overall deletion workflow accessible through the People Management dashboard via the Command Centre tab, Employee section View button, and Actions menu where users select the Delete Person option, with confirmation required before the system schedules an overnight job to complete the deletion. The guide identifies two critical limitations that prevent person deletion: records of employees who have already been paid through payroll (generating an error message stating the person cannot be deleted as they have been processed by payroll) and records containing WFM timesheet transactions, which trigger an error message blocking deletion until those transactions are removed. To address the timesheet transaction barrier, the document provides detailed steps for accessing the WFM Admin Dashboard, selecting WFM Person Maintenance, querying the employee, navigating to the relevant week via the Timesheet option, and deleting the timesheet entries before attempting person deletion again. The guide also explains how to verify deletion eligibility using the PAYDEP02 Historic Pay Costing report and TIMDEP01 timesheet report, as well as how to undo a scheduled deletion before the overnight job completes by navigating to the employee record and selecting Undo Delete Person from the Actions menu. Additional configuration details specify that several Web Services menu options require enabling against the relevant Menu Profile, including MAIN_MENU.WS_PEOPLE, WS_PEOPLE_MENU.PATCH, and related employment history and roster update options. This document is primarily intended for HR administrators and system users in PeopleXD environments who need to manage erroneous employee records while understanding payroll and timesheet constraints.

ss: PeopleXD's Employee Offboarding feature on CorePortal allows HR administrators to configure the complete offboarding process, including checklists, custom pages, policy documents, and user access controls. This guide covers how to enable offboarding, set up checklist items and custom pages that can be restricted by staff criteria groups, configure the offboarding dashboard, and manage security permissions for employees, managers, and administrators. Open this document when you need to set up or modify offboarding workflows, define which tasks appear for departing employees based on their department or employment type, or configure who has access to the offboarding system. You'll also use it to establish the Leave Date threshold that triggers automatic task assignments and to report on offboarding activities through CoreInsight.
sl: This document is a configuration user guide for the Employee Offboarding feature within the PeopleXD People Management system, specifically for setting up and managing offboarding processes on CorePortal. The guide covers how to enable the Social Hub Configuration widget through the People Management Dashboard by quick jumping to Dashboard Configuration, selecting the People Management Dashboard, and adding the Social Hub Configuration widget to the applicable tab. It details the process of activating Employee Offboarding by navigating to the Social Hub Configuration widget, clicking the View button adjacent to the Activate label, and entering a mandatory Leave Date that determines which employees with departure dates on or after that date will be assigned to applicable offboarding checklists. The document explains how to configure multiple elements including Offboarding Checklists, Custom Pages, Policy Documents and Handbooks, and Documents Requested, with specific guidance on creating and maintaining checklist items that can be assigned a specified number of days before an employee's departure date and restricted by criteria groups to customize tasks for different employee segments. It addresses user access management through three default security menu profiles—Offboard_Admin, Offboard_MGR, and Offboard_EMP—as well as Web Service Modules for controlling who can access the offboarding dashboard and related functions. This guide is intended for HR administrators and system configurators who need to set up and customize the offboarding workflow, distinct from the companion "How to Use" user guide that provides training for end users accessing the Employee Offboarding dashboard.

s: Purpose of the Guide The purpose of this document is to provide guidance on how User Defined Fields (UDFs) are configured. This includes UDFs that are stored against: • Employees • Posts • Contracts This document will provide instruction on how to: • Create & edit UDFs. • Make UDF items available on People Management. • Make UDF items available to managers to view or update.
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in PeopleXD allow you to capture custom data specific to your organization that isn't available as standard fields—such as equipment assignments or company-specific attributes—and store this information against employees, posts, or contracts. This guide walks you through creating, editing, and managing UDFs through the People Management dashboard, including how to configure access so that managers and employees can view or update specific fields. Open this document when you need to set up new custom fields in PeopleXD, modify existing UDF configurations, or control which roles can access sensitive field data. It also covers optional security settings for UDFs containing particularly sensitive information.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the PeopleXD People Management system, which are custom data fields used to store organization-specific information not provided by standard system features. The document explains that UDFs can be created and attached to employees, posts, or contracts, and can utilize up to 12 standard field types including text, number, list, date, and text area fields, along with optional start and end dates. To configure UDFs, users access the Maintain User Defined Fields screen by navigating through the Data Centre widget, opening HR Admin Setup Settings, and searching for User Defined Objects under HR Configuration. The guide details the complete creation process in five steps: adding a new UDF code, configuring data labels, defining the user-defined type, optionally setting employee and manager access permissions, and optionally hiding from/to date fields. Additionally, the document covers updating existing UDFs through editing descriptions, modifying items, adding new items, updating advanced settings, making UDFs inactive, or deleting them entirely. Access controls are a key feature, allowing HR administrators to determine visibility and editing permissions for managers and employees, with the option to flag sensitive UDFs with additional security requirements that restrict access to authorized HR administrators only. All UDF data is fully reportable through XD Insight, enabling comprehensive analytics and reporting on custom field information across the People Management system.

t: Post Restructuring Tool
s: The Post restructuring functionality allows you transfer a group of employees from one part of the structure to another. The tool enables employees to be moved within different areas of the structure based on the following scenarios: Move an employee to another post Move an employee to another area within the structure ‘Move Department’ Move a Post and linked Employees to another Post Move a Post and linked Employees from one area within the Organisation to another area...
ss: The Post Restructuring Tool enables you to transfer employees and posts between different areas of your organizational structure within PeopleXD. Use this tool when you need to move individual employees to new posts, relocate entire departments to different areas, or reorganize multiple levels of your hierarchy at once. Open this guide when you're ready to create a restructuring profile, validate employee and post data, and process the transfer to make organizational changes effective on a specific date. Note that you must update your Organizational Hierarchy before using this tool, and certain record types (casual, contract, non-employee, and agency) require a separate process.
sl: The Post Restructuring Tool is a guide that enables users to transfer groups of employees between different parts of an organizational structure through a systematic process accessible via Personnel > Maintenance > Post Management > Organisational Hierarchy. The tool supports multiple restructuring scenarios, including moving individual employees to different posts or departments, relocating entire posts with their linked employees to new areas, and transferring complete departmental levels across the organization. To process a restructure, users must first create a new profile by entering a Profile Name and Effective Date, then specify transfer parameters by ticking "Organisational Structure" for both Transfer From and Transfer To fields, selecting "Update Existing Contract" as the Restructuring Type, and configuring the From Structure Details and To Structure Details sections with appropriate company and hierarchy information. After saving the profile, users can view the list of active employees and posts matching the source structure, select a Transfer Reason such as "Restructuring," and then validate all records using the Validate Records button, which highlights invalid records in red with error messages such as "Hierarchy details do not exist" or "Employee has a confirmed future appointment." The tool excludes CASUAL, CASTCH, NONEMP, and AGENCY records from processing, which require a separate procedure, and only processes commenced appointments. Once validation is complete, users click Process Transfer to finalize the restructure, and the system displays confirmation details including the new Post Number, Post Title, and processing date for each transferred record. This document is typically used by human resources and organizational management personnel who need to reorganize departmental structures and move employee assignments in response to institutional changes.

sl: This How To Guide provides comprehensive instructions for viewing and maintaining reference data across two system interfaces: the Portal and the back office. t: Clear Down Applications at the Applicant's Request
