s: This document explains the process for deleting a single applicant from the e-Recruitment system following an individual request from the applicant, normally via incident management. Other Related Documents HOW TO manage the bulk applicant clear down process.docx Deleting an applicant account from the applicant portal where no applications have been submitted Restrictions There is a limit to what we are able to clear down. Applications must be retained for a period of six...
ss: The e-Recruitment system allows you to delete individual applicant records when an applicant requests their data be removed, typically through an incident management request. The process involves checking that all vacancy applications have reached a final status (such as Rejected, Successful, or Withdrawn) and that at least six months have passed since the final status date—a retention requirement that applies to most vacancies. You'll update the applicant status to "Z-HRIS Support Centre Use Only," delete merged application packs, and then run the clear down process through the Applicant Clear Down function in Preview mode before executing the final update. Open this guide when you receive a data deletion request from an applicant and need step-by-step instructions for safely removing their records from the recruitment system.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for HRIS Support Centre staff to delete individual applicant records from the e-Recruitment system when requested by applicants, typically through incident management channels. The process involves four main phases: checking vacancies applied for through the Recruitment > Recruitment Enquiries > Applicant Detail menu path, updating applicant status through Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Vacancy Detail, clearing down records via Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Applicant Clear Down, and handling incomplete application statuses. A critical restriction applies throughout: applications must be retained for a minimum of six months after a final decision has been made on a vacancy (either an appointment confirmed or confirmed that no appointment will be made), which the document notes is mandatory regardless of the applicant's request. The process requires staff to verify all applicant statuses are in "final states" such as Rejected, Successful, Offer Refused, Withdrawn, or Standby before proceeding, with an exception for vacancies in the TSS system. The document explains that applicant statuses must be changed to "Z-HRIS Support Centre Use Only" and merged application packs must be deleted before running the cleardown process, which includes a Preview mode to verify correct applicants and vacancies before executing the Update mode to permanently remove records. If applicant statuses are incomplete or less than six months have passed since the final status date, the HRIS Support Centre must contact recruiting departments and either wait for status updates or schedule a reminder to revisit the vacancy after the six-month period has elapsed.

sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for maintaining and configuring online application forms within the portal 2.0 system, specifically for the University of Oxford's E-Recruitment Form. Users of this guide—typically recruitment administrators managing the University of Oxford's application forms—will also find guidance on testing changes by attaching forms to active vacancies and related documentation references stored in the HRIS Programme support folder.

ss: The bulk applicant clear-down process removes applicant records from your recruitment system after a specified date range, typically on an annual basis. This guide walks you through running the RECEUP01 control report in Discoverer, using the Applicant Clear Down function to delete records by applicant status, and performing validation checks to ensure the process completed successfully. Open this document when you need to perform an annual or periodic purge of old applicant data, or when coordinating with your Head of HRIS on clear-down timescales and post-deletion verification.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for executing the bulk applicant clear-down process, which systematically removes applicant records from the recruitment system based on applicant status and date ranges. The document covers five main process steps: preparation (creating folders and saving checklists), running the RECSUP01 Applicant Clear Down Control report in Discoverer with date parameters from 1 August to 31 July, clearing down applicants by status through the Recruitment > Recruitment Maintenance > Applicant Clear Down menu path, performing post-clear-down verification checks, and coordinating with CoreHR to remove merged PDF packs. The process requires users to set the Mode Indicator to "Preview" first to view applicants meeting selection criteria (by applicant status code in the Applicant Status field), then change it to "Update" to execute the actual clear-down, with the system generating confirmation reports for each status batch processed. Post-clear-down validation involves re-running the Discoverer report to confirm no records remain, sampling applicant records from the Applicant Detail per Vacancy tab, and checking vacancies in the Applicant Summary by Vacancy tab to verify the difference column values match actual remaining applicant counts. This document is primarily used by HRIS (Human Resources Information System) administrators and recruitment support staff who manage annual or periodic applicant record purges, requiring coordination with the Head of HRIS on timescales and final coordination with CoreHR for deletion of associated merged PDF files.

ss: The Pay Scale Band functionality in the Recruitment system automatically populates salary ranges on job vacancies based on selected pay grades. When a recruiter sets a pay scale on a vacancy (for example, "Grade 1"), the Grade and Salary field automatically displays the corresponding salary range (such as "£25,000 - £35,000"). This guide walks you through activating the Pay Scale Bands feature, creating and updating pay scale bands with minimum and maximum rates, and configuring how these salary ranges display on the eRecruitment website and job search results. Use this document if you need to set up or modify how candidate-facing vacancy postings show salary information linked to organizational pay grades.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing and displaying pay scale salary ranges within a recruitment system's vacancy postings. The document covers the complete configuration process, starting with activating the Pay Scale Bands feature by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Admin Settings and setting the parameter "cp_erc_auto_bands" to Y, which enables automatic population of Grade and Salary fields based on configured salary ranges. Users must have the menu options "Coreportal Recruitment - Pay Scale Bands Edit" and "Coreportal Recruitment - Pay Scale Bands View" assigned to access the Pay Scale Bands screen via Recruitment > Toolbox > Pay Scale Bands, where administrators can add new bands by selecting a pay scale code and entering minimum and maximum salary rates, amend existing bands by updating the Min Rate and Max Rate fields, or delete bands using the Remove function. The guide addresses the practical scenario of updating pay scales following a pay uplift by recommending the use of report PAYSUP02 to ensure non-discretionary salary ranges are accurately reflected. Configuration of the eRecruitment website involves accessing Recruitment > Toolbox > Recruitment Admin, selecting Appointments Version 4, and enabling the Pay Scale and Grade and Salary items for display on the Job Search results page with specified display orders, sort orders, and heading styles. Additionally, system administrators must configure Form Profiles by editing the Job Specification Section v4 within each active form profile, applying consistent settings such as including both Pay Scale and Grade and Salary items, setting appropriate order numbers, marking them as required fields, and applying the same heading style formatting across all eRecruitment-related pages. This document is essential for recruitment administrators, HR personnel, and system configuration teams who need to ensure that vacancy postings automatically display salary range information corresponding to selected pay grades.

t: Manually Update the Job Seekers Register

s: CoreHR have a piece of functionality called the Job Seekers Register (“JSR”), which can be used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who should be considered for redeployment within their companies. The JSR is, in essence, just a register – adding an employee’s contract to it does not automate any kind of employment processes. However, the existence of a central register of “job seekers” may support the Senior Appointments team’s with the Priority...
ss: The Job Seekers Register (JSR) in CoreHR is a manual register used to flag employees whose contracts are ending so they can be considered for redeployment and support through the Priority Candidate Support Scheme. Using the JSR Override field in CoreHR's back-office, you can manually add an employee's contract to the register by setting the override to "Yes," or remove them by changing it back to "Calculate." An overnight system process picks up these changes and updates the JSR flag accordingly. Open this guide when you need to add or remove specific employee contracts from the Job Seekers Register within CoreHR.
sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for manually managing the Job Seekers Register (JSR) functionality within CoreHR, a system used to identify employees whose contracts are ending and who may be considered for redeployment opportunities in support of the Priority Candidate Support Scheme (PCSS). The JSR itself is a central register rather than an automated employment process management tool, and while CoreHR offers both automatic rule-based and manual methods for populating it, this guide focuses exclusively on the manual approach using the JSR Override flag. To access the JSR functionality, users must navigate through the CoreHR back-office launched from CorePortal, then proceed to CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile, where they can search for an employee by name or personnel number and access their record. The Job Seekers Register screen displays the employee's current appointments with two critical fields: the JSR flag (a read-only system field that indicates whether a contract is registered) and the JSR Override field (a user-editable field with three options: Calculate, Yes, or No). To manually add an employee's contract to the JSR, users change the JSR Override field to "Yes," confirm the warning message, and save the changes, after which an overnight database job (PERS_JOB_SEEKERS_REGISTER_PROC.PROCESS_J) processes the update and the JSR flag becomes ticked the following day. Removing an employee from the JSR follows a similar process, requiring users to change the JSR Override field from "Yes" to "Calculate," confirm the change, and allow the overnight job to process the removal, resulting in the JSR flag being unticked. This guide is intended for Senior Appointments Team members and HR personnel responsible for manually managing contract redeployment candidate lists within their organization.

ss: The Job Seekers Register (JSR) in CoreHR is a manual register used to flag employees whose contracts are ending and who may be considered for redeployment within the organization. This guide covers how to manually add and remove employee contracts from the JSR using the JSR Override field in CorePersonnel, since the Senior Appointments Team uses manual rather than automatic registration. Open this document when you need to add an employee to the register by setting JSR Override to "Yes" or remove them by changing it back to "Calculate." The overnight database process will then update the JSR flag to reflect your changes.
sl: This how-to guide explains the Job Seekers Register (JSR) functionality within CoreHR, a system used to identify and track employees whose contracts are ending so they can be considered for redeployment opportunities through the Priority Candidate Support Scheme. The document describes two operational approaches to managing the JSR: an automatic process that uses configured system rules to identify eligible contracts based on criteria such as organisational hierarchy and appointment details, and a manual process using a JSR Override flag that allows users to directly add or remove employee contracts regardless of eligibility rules. The guide focuses on the manual process and provides step-by-step instructions for navigating to the Job Seekers Register screen via CorePersonnel > Employee Search > Person Profile within CoreHR's back-office, which is accessed through CorePortal. To add an employee's contract to the JSR, users locate the employee record, access the Job Seekers section from the Select Detail menu, and change the JSR Override field from its default "Calculate" setting to "Yes," then save the changes. The document explains that the JSR Override field has three possible values—Calculate (apply system eligibility rules), Yes (manually add the contract), or No (prevent addition)—and notes that the JSR flag itself is system-only and cannot be manually updated by users. An overnight database job (PERS_JOB_SEEKERS_REGISTER_PROC.PROCESS_J) processes the change and updates the JSR flag within one business day. Removing an employee's contract from the JSR follows a similar process, requiring users to change the JSR Override field back to "Calculate" and allowing the overnight job to remove the contract automatically. This guide is intended for Senior Appointments teams and HR personnel who need to manually manage the JSR outside of automated eligibility processes.

t: PeopleXD Recruitment- Applicant Management V1.3
s: Purpose of the Guide This document outlines how to use and manage the Applicant side of PeopleXD Recruitment. sl: This PeopleXD Recruitment Applicant Management user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing candidates throughout the recruitment lifecycle within the XD Recruitment system. s: This document details how to change the Terms and Conditions document that is accessed from the ‘Terms of Use’ link on the public Recruitment page and the terms and conditions link that can be accessed from the applicant account prior to submitting an application. Contents Uploading the new documents Select Company – 10 ‘University of Oxford’ and Form Profile ERECRUIT - ‘E-Recruitment Form’. Click on the Load Document button.
ss: The eRecruitment system allows you to upload and manage the Terms and Conditions and Submission Guidelines documents that appear on your public recruitment page and in applicant accounts. Use this guide when you need to update these legal or policy documents for new recruitment cycles, ensuring applicants see the most current terms before submitting applications. The process involves uploading two PDF documents through the Document Management screen in Personnel > Recruitment, then removing outdated versions. Follow these steps to keep your recruitment documentation current and compliant.
sl: This document provides instructions for updating the Terms and Conditions and Submission Guidelines documents that appear in the public-facing recruitment interface, specifically the 'Terms of Use' link on the Recruitment page and the terms and conditions link accessible from applicant accounts before submission. The process requires navigating to Personnel > Recruitment > Reference > General Document Management, where users must upload the same document twice using the Load Document button—once designated as 'Terms and Conditions' and once as 'Submission Guidelines' for the E-Recruitment Form profile associated with University of Oxford (Company 10). The upload procedure involves selecting a PDF file through the browser window that opens automatically, with the critical constraint that file names cannot exceed 44 characters and shorter file paths may be necessary. After successfully uploading both new documents, users must update the previous versions by changing their Document Type field to blank, while simultaneously assigning the appropriate Document Type labels ('Terms and Conditions' and 'Submission Guidelines') to the newly uploaded documents before saving. The document also covers the deletion process for obsolete versions, which involves highlighting each old version, clicking Delete, and confirming the deletion through warning and confirmation messages that appear sequentially. ss: Insight reports enable you to create custom reports on surveys built for the onboarding checklist within CorePortal. Use this guide to build new reports from scratch—selecting data fields and tables, adding filters and sort orders, creating calculations, and organizing multi-tab reports—as well as to edit existing reports by adjusting tabs, filters, sorts, and calculations. Open this document when you need to set up reporting on onboarding survey data or modify reports you've already created to change their structure, filters, or calculations.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for creating and editing Insight reports configured specifically for reporting on surveys created for the onboarding checklist. The creation section covers building standalone reports by navigating to CorePortal > Insight and using the ACTIONS > Create Report menu to select either Table or Pivot format, then adding columns by searching data fields (such as Person reference) and tables or views, with the requirement that at least one field from HR Person Master must be included when adding survey details. The guide details how to apply hard-coded filters and optional filters (parameters) through the Filters setting, with optional filters enabling end users to enter their own criteria via prompt text, as well as how to establish sort orders and create calculations within the Columns setting. The editing section explains how to access existing reports through either My Recent Reports (displayed as tiles) or All Reports (displayed in a list), then access Edit Mode through ACTIONS to modify tabs, filters, sorts, and calculations. Specific editing capabilities include renaming tabs and the overall report name (with the first tab name determining the report name), reordering tabs using numbered positioning, and editing or hiding existing calculations located in the Columns list. sl: This document is a comprehensive guide for rendering reports in Visual Studio within the HR Reporting system, covering both fundamental concepts and step-by-step processes across multiple environments. t: DRAFT_HOW TO - Manage Reports - Report Files

ss: Report files (.RDL) in Visual Studio contain the design and structure for HR reports that query the PeopleXD database. sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for managing report files (.RDL files) within Visual Studio for the HR Reporting system, specifically covering the essential tools and panes used to work with reports. t: Manage Reports - Access Permissions within HR Reporting
f: HOW TO - Manage Reports - Access Permissions within HR Reporting.docx
s: The SSRS reports developed by the Functional Analysis and HR Analytics teams are stored in the various HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA and LIVE), where end-users may execute them as necessary. Two levels of security apply to every report: PeopleXD’s database security and HR Reporting’s “folder-based” security. This how-to guide only addresses how to manage security within the HR Reporting environments.
ss: HR Reporting uses folder-based security in PeopleXD to control which SSRS reports users can access across DEV, TEST, QA, and LIVE environments. This guide covers managing access through Active Directory (AD) groups and the reporting folder hierarchy, including tasks like viewing and editing folder security, managing AD group membership, and creating or deleting AD groups. Open this document if you need to grant or restrict user access to specific report folders, troubleshoot why users can't see certain reports, or manage the AD groups that control report permissions. It's essential for HR administrators and IT teams who oversee who can view Payroll, Personnel, Pensions, and other departmental reports.
sl: This how-to guide explains how to manage access permissions for SSRS reports stored in the HR Reporting environments (DEV, TEST, QA, and LIVE) through folder-based security, providing context on the two-layer security model that applies to all reports: PeopleXD's database security and HR Reporting's folder-based security. The document describes the reporting folder hierarchy consisting of four levels—the Home folder (Level 0, which grants access to the reports server itself), Navigation folders (Level 1, which organize reports by broad categories such as "Payroll" or "Recruitment"), Subfolders (Level 2, which further subdivide Navigation folders into granular categories like "Current Reports" and "Monthly Reports"), and Report folders (Level 3, which contain the actual .RDL files)—with the understanding that security is not applied to individual .RDL files but rather at the folder level. The guide covers managing Active Directory (AD) groups, which are collections of CONNECT user accounts that control user access to specific folders throughout the hierarchy, with examples of AD groups including HRIS-RR-PAYMREP (Payroll managers), HRIS-RR-EDU_TEAM (Equality & Diversity team), and HRIS-RR-SUP_REP (HR Systems Support team). The processes section addresses key tasks including managing AD group membership, creating or deleting AD groups, managing reporting super-groups, viewing folder security, editing folder security, and handling folder security for subscription-based reports. This document is used by HR and reporting administrators who need to configure which users can access specific reports by assigning AD groups to folders at each level of the hierarchy, and it references related guides covering HR Reporting environments, change processes, parameters, shared data sources, shared datasets, troubleshooting, and Visual Studio basics.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive how-to guide for managing change requests and implementing modifications to SSRS reports and shared datasets within the OSM (Oracle Service Management) system, covering both changes to existing reports and requests for entirely new reports or datasets. t: Manage Reports - Parameters
s: Context A parameter is technically “a limit or boundary which defines the scope of a particular process or activity”. Within the context of HR Reporting, parameters are values a report user can set before running a report. These values limit the query the report sends to the database, and therefore limit the data the report will return from the database.
ss: Report parameters allow users to filter data before running a report by selecting specific values like department codes or personnel numbers from the PeopleXD database. This guide covers how to view, create, edit, and remove parameters across three locations: SQL code in the .RDL file, the Parameters folder in the Report Data pane, and the optional Parameters textbox that displays selected values at the top of a report. For viewing parameters, the guide details how to access the Dataset Properties window via the Datasets folder, inspect the Query pane for SQL code, and use the Report Parameter Properties window to configure the General, Available Values, and Default Values tabs. When parameters are displayed in the textbox, the document shows how to right-click and access the Expression window to view the VBA code that controls parameter display formatting. This document serves HR Reporting administrators, report developers, and business users who need to configure, troubleshoot, or understand how parameters function within report (.RDL) files in Visual Studio or similar reporting environments.

ss: Shared data sources in HR Reporting Visual Studio solutions define which PeopleXD database (UOXC, UOXP, UOXU, UOXZ) your reports connect to and provide the login credentials needed to access that database. This guide covers how to view, test, and amend shared data sources—including updating database connections, managing login credentials, and troubleshooting connection failures. Open this document when you need to configure data source connections in Visual Studio, reset expired HR Reporting passwords in the Oracle_DS_UserCredentials source, or verify that your reports are connecting to the correct PeopleXD database environment.
sl: This How To Guide explains how to manage shared data sources in HR Reporting Visual Studio solutions, which are connection profiles that define both the PeopleXD database being used and the login credentials required to access it. The document covers two primary shared data sources used across most reports: Oracle_DS_ServiceAccount, which connects using a service account to run SQL queries for shared datasets and report parameters, and Oracle_DS_UserCredentials, which uses individual user credentials to apply row-level security when retrieving report data. To view a data source, users navigate to the Solution Explorer pane in their Visual Studio solution, expand the Shared Data Sources folder, and double-click or right-click the desired data source to open the Shared Data Source Properties window and General screen. The document details how to check database connections by examining the "Connection String" field, which displays which PeopleXD database the solution connects to (such as UOXZ, UOXC, UOXU, or UOXP), and how to verify login credentials by clicking Build next to the Connection String field and using the Test Connection button to confirm database accessibility. For amending data sources, users access the same Solution Explorer path, open the Connection Properties window, and can update either the "Server name" field to change the database or the "User name" and "Password" fields to update credentials, with the ability to save passwords for the UserCredentials data source to streamline repeated report runs in the Preview pane. The guide also addresses common connection problems, such as invalid credentials, expired HR Reporting passwords requiring reset through the HR Systems Support team, or temporary database unavailability during system maintenance, and provides specific guidance for the ServiceAccount data source which uses the username "REPORT_POWERBI" and maintains "Save my password" settings across all solutions.

ss: Shared datasets are reusable SQL queries in HR Reporting that retrieve reference data from PeopleXD to populate report parameter drop-down lists, such as department or absence reason selections. sl: This How To guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing shared datasets in HR Reporting, which are SQL queries stored as .RSD files that can be reused across multiple report (.RDL) files to populate parameter drop-down lists with reference data from PeopleXD. t: Manage Reports - Troubleshoot Common Errors
f: HOW TO - Manage Reports - Troubleshoot Common Errors.docx
s: Context This document contains a list of error messages commonly encountered when writing reports in SQL Developer and rendering them in Visual Studio. Any new error messages encountered by report writers should ideally be captured in this document so that resolutions, when identified, may be added here.
ss: Report writers encounter SQL and Visual Studio errors when creating reports in SQL Developer and rendering them in Visual Studio, such as ORA-00904 (Invalid Identifier), ORA-00918 (Column ambiguously defined), ORA-00932 (inconsistent datatypes), and BC30203 (Identifier Expected). This document provides explanations and resolutions for these common error messages, including troubleshooting steps like checking for misspelled database views, removing duplicate column references, ensuring proper date formatting, and verifying VBA expressions in report parameters. Open this guide when you encounter error messages during report development or need to understand why your SQL queries or Visual Studio reports are failing to execute. It's also a resource for capturing and documenting new errors as your team encounters them.
sl: This troubleshooting guide provides a comprehensive reference for report writers encountering common errors when developing reports in SQL Developer and rendering them in Visual Studio. The document addresses multiple SQL-related errors including "Enter substitution variable," which occurs when ampersands appear in code and can be resolved by replacing them with "and" or using the SET DEFINE OFF command before the SELECT statement. The guide explains the ORA-00904 "Invalid Identifier" error, which arises from misspelled or non-existent item and view references, and provides specific guidance on proper view referencing across multi-layer queries such as Base Query and Main Display Layer structures. It covers the ORA-00918 "Column ambiguously defined" error that occurs when duplicate items are referenced in a single SELECT statement, offering solutions through either removing duplicates or applying aliases to differentiate them. The document also details the ORA-00932 datatype error that results from comparing dates not in proper Date format or using TRUNC() functions on non-date variables, as well as the ORA-01790 error that occurs when UNION statements have misaligned column ordering. For Visual Studio-specific issues, the guide addresses the BC30203 "Identifier Expected" error that appears during report preview and relates to missing .VALUE or .LABEL identifications in VBA expressions within the Parameters textbox. This guide is intended for report writers and developers actively creating and debugging reports in these systems, serving as both a reference document and a living resource for capturing new errors and their resolutions.

t: Add a Formatting Switch to a Field Code
f: HOW TO - Add a Formatting Switch to a Field Code.docx
s: Right-click the field, and then click Edit Field. Do one of the following: If Field properties and Field options are displayed, select the formatting options that you want. If only the field code is displayed, click Options, and then select the formatting options that you want.
ss: Field codes in documents can be formatted using three types of formatting switches: the Format switch (\*), Numeric format switch (\#), and Date-Time format switch (\@). The Format switch controls capitalization (Caps, FirstCap, Upper, Lower), number display (Arabic numerals, Roman numerals, ordinal text, alphabetic characters), and character formatting to preserve previous formatting when fields update. The Numeric format switch (\#) controls how numeric results display, such as currency formatting or decimal places. Open this document when you need to customize how field results appear in your document—whether you want to change text capitalization, convert numbers to words or Roman numerals, format currency values, or maintain specific formatting across field updates.
sl: This how-to guide explains how to add and use formatting switches in field codes within a document editing application, specifically addressing users who need to control how field results are displayed. The document describes the fundamental process of accessing formatting options by right-clicking a field and selecting Edit Field, then choosing formatting options either from the Field properties dialog or by clicking Options if only the field code is displayed. It covers three primary types of formatting switches: the Format switch (\*) for controlling capitalization and number display formats; the Numeric format switch (\#) for specifying how numeric results appear with currency symbols and decimal places; and the Date-Time format switch (\@) for date formatting. The Format switch section details multiple capitalization options (Caps, FirstCap, Upper, Lower) and number format options (Arabic, CardText, DollarText, Hex, OrdText, Ordinal, Roman, and alphabetic), each with specific examples showing how field codes like { FILLIN "Type your name:" \* Caps } or { PAGE \* Arabic } produce formatted results. The guide also explains character formatting switches including \*Charformat, which applies the formatting of the first letter of a field name to the entire result, and \*MERGEFORMAT, which preserves previously applied formatting when fields are updated. Additionally, the document describes how to construct numeric format switches using format items like 0 and # to control decimal places and display formatting, with examples such as { = SUM(ABOVE) \# $#,##0.00 } displaying currency values. This resource is designed for document creators and editors who need precise control over how dynamic field content appears in their documents without manually reformatting each time fields update.

t: Enable Personal Email Contact Type when Onboarding Applicants
f: HOW TO - Enable Personal Email Contact Type when Onboarding Applicants.docx
s: When an applicant is onboarded from the Recruitment module into People Management and becomes an employee the default Contact Type field for the applicant’s personal email to populate is ‘EMAIL – WORK’. A new parameter allows the organisation to select which ‘Contact Type’ field they wish to be populated as an alternative when a new starter (applicant) is pulled through, this does not rewrite when a later contract is appointed such as a new additional or transfer occurs....
ss: When applicants are onboarded from the Recruitment module into People Management, their personal email is automatically assigned a contact type field—by default set to 'EMAIL – WORK'. This guide shows how to use the cp_erc_pers_contact parameter in Administrator Dashboard > Admin Settings to change which contact type field (such as EMAIL-HOME) receives the personal email address for new starters. Open this document if you need to configure alternative email contact type assignments during applicant onboarding or if you want to understand how personal and work email addresses are categorized and viewed within employee records in People Management.
sl: This how-to guide explains how to configure which contact type field receives an applicant's personal email address when they transition from the Recruitment module to People Management as a new employee. By default, the system populates the personal email into the 'EMAIL – WORK' contact type field, but organizations can change this behavior using a system parameter. To enable an alternative contact type, users navigate to Administrator Dashboard > Admin Settings, search for the parameter code cp_erc_pers_contact (Applicant Email Contact Type for New Starter), click EDIT, and select their preferred Contact Type Code from the popup that appears. The configuration applies only to new starters transitioning from applicants and does not carry forward to subsequent employment changes such as new contracts, additional positions, or transfers. Employees' contact details including their assigned email addresses can be viewed in People Management by navigating to Employee Search > ACTIONS > Personal Profile > Contact Details. The guide identifies two primary contact types: EMAIL-HOME (Contact Type Code: PRHOEM) configured for applicants' personal email addresses, and EMAIL-WORK (Contact Type Code: EMAIL) for university email addresses populated nightly through an automated overnight interface that should never be manually updated. A complete reference list of all available contact types can be accessed through People Management > Data Centre > Reference Data > Contact Type.
