s: Core allows users to configure system events by specifying what occurrence or action will “trigger” an event and what action or output the event should produce. There are many different Event Categories, and within each Category, there are many different Event Types. This guide covers the category of Training Events, and takes you through the following processes: Creating a new event Open CoreHR and in the toolbar, go to CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration...
ss: Training event configuration in CoreHR allows you to set up automated notifications triggered by employee course actions like Request Date, Start Date, and Training Status changes. This guide walks you through creating new training events, editing existing ones, and deactivating events—including how to specify notification types (email, employee, organization role, or person), set timing conditions, and customize subject and message text. Open this document when you need to configure who receives training notifications, what triggers them, and what information they contain, or when you're troubleshooting existing training event setups in CoreHR's Event Management system.
sl: This guide explains how to manage Training Events within the Core system, which allows users to configure system events by specifying triggers and the actions or outputs those events should produce. The document covers three main processes: creating new training events, editing existing ones, and deactivating events, all accessed through the CoreHR > Event Management > Hr Event Configuration menu path where users select "Training – Employee Courses" from a dropdown to view available Training event types including "Request Date," "Start Date," and "Training Status." When creating a new event, users select an event type, click "Add New Notification," and specify a Notification Type (Email, Employee, Organisation Role, or Person) along with timing parameters for how many days before or after the event to trigger the notification. The guide addresses the specific scenario where events triggered by a PROVIDER_CODE require verification that the code exists in CorePersonnel > Training > Training Maintenance > Course Providers, with instructions for creating a new provider code if needed. Users must configure the notification subject and message text using the PERS_TRAINING_LOG_VIEW data source before activating the event by ticking the "Active Indicator" flag, with an alternative "Test Mode Indicator" available for testing notifications without sending emails. The document also explains how to edit existing events by navigating to the same menu path and selecting the event to modify its settings, subject, or message text, as well as how to deactivate events by unticking the "Active Indicator" flag. This guide is essential for CoreHR administrators and training coordinators who need to set up automated notifications for employee training course events within their organization.

t: Prepare Data for the Data Migration Tool v2.1 DRAFT Aug21
f: HOW TO - Prepare Data for the Data Migration Tool v2.1 DRAFT Aug21.docx
s: Your upload file must contain all of the columns shown on the template document even if they contain no data. The upload template will include a column for each possible data item so for a UDF, 12 fields can be added so there will be 12 columns in addition to the required fields. Once you have save your upload file as a .CSV, DO NOT SAVE again when exiting as the formatting you have just completed will change back to the defaults.
ss: Preparing data for upload to CorePortal's Data Migration tool requires formatting your file to match the provided template, including all required columns and proper date formatting before saving as a CSV file. You'll download the template and helper documents from CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration, then structure your data to match the specified fields and formats, paying special attention to date fields which vary by field type (such as UDF From/To dates versus other date fields). Before uploading, verify your file in Notepad++ to ensure formatting is preserved and no special characters exist. Use the Data Migration Options widget to load your file, then review and process records individually or in bulk to complete the migration.
sl: This document is a practical how-to guide for preparing and uploading data using the Data Migration Tool v2.1, with recent updates in August 2021 incorporating new Portal screens and processes. The guide covers the complete workflow for data migration, beginning with navigating to CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration to access the Data Migration Templates Widget, where users download both the template file and helper file relevant to their data type, such as UDF (User Defined Fields). Critical preparation steps include formatting all columns to match the template exactly, ensuring all columns from the template are present even if empty, formatting all data as text, and paying special attention to date fields, which require the DD-MMM-YYYY format and must include leading zeros (for example, 01 instead of 1), particularly since UDF Date From/To fields have different formatting requirements than other date fields. The upload process involves opening the prepared file within the template using the import wizard with delimited settings (either comma or pipe delimiters), copying and pasting data into the template file, saving as a .CSV file, and then verifying formatting in Notepad++ to check for special characters or errors before upload. Users then navigate back to CorePortal > Administrator Dashboard > Data Migration, use the Data Migration Options widget to click LOAD FILE, browse to select their file, and wait for upload completion confirmation. After upload, users can review records by clicking Edit on the file status line, optionally process individual records using the PROCESS RECORD button to test, or process all records at once using PROCESS ALL RECORDS, with the system displaying status updates of PROCESSING until completion shows as COMPLETE or FAILED. This document is essential for system administrators and data migration specialists who need to import data into the system while avoiding common formatting errors that cause validation failures.

t: Record a Macro
s: In MS Word go to the developer tab and click on Record Macro Insert a name for the macro (no spaces) and under ‘Assign Macro to’ click on Button A pop up window will appear. Find your new macro in the left hand box, highlight and click on Add. Press CTRL and F keys together to open the find and replace function.
ss: Recording macros in Microsoft Word automates repetitive find-and-replace tasks by capturing your actions and saving them as a reusable button in the ribbon. This process helps you save time when you need to perform the same text replacements across multiple documents without manually executing the steps each time. Open this guide when you want to set up a macro for a find-and-replace function you perform regularly, or when you need instructions on accessing the Developer tab and assigning macro commands to a button shortcut.
sl: This how-to guide provides instructions for creating and using a macro in Microsoft Word to automate the find and replace function. The document walks users through the initial setup by navigating to the Developer tab and selecting Record Macro, then naming the macro (without spaces) and assigning it to a Button through the assignment dialog box. Once the macro is created and the new macro is highlighted and added from the left-hand box, users are guided to open the Find and Replace function by pressing CTRL and F together, then accessing the Navigation box on the left side of the page to select the Replace option. The guide explains how to enter the specific text details that need to be replaced according to user requirements. After completing these steps, users must return to the Developer tab and click Stop Recording to finalize the macro. Upon completion, a shortcut button for the macro appears in the ribbon at the top of the Word window, allowing users to quickly execute the find and replace operation on any document by simply clicking the button rather than manually repeating the steps each time.

t: Setup an AD Account for Tableau
f: HOW TO - Setup an AD Account for Tableau.docx
s: Tableau is a data visualisation software that enables data to be transformed into interactive visualisations (called dashboards) and then shared with users. Within the University, access to Tableau dashboards is controlled by Active Directory (“AD”) groups. An AD group can be assigned to a published Tableau workbook and all the dashboards within the workbook.
ss: Setting up Active Directory accounts for Tableau users within the University requires creating AD accounts and assigning them to the appropriate AD groups that control access to Tableau dashboards and reports. This guide walks you through accessing BSP AD User Management, checking whether an AD account already exists, creating new AD accounts, assigning users to AD groups, and configuring account settings like expiration and unlock options. Open this document when you need to provision a new Tableau user, verify an existing account, or modify AD group assignments for dashboard access. You'll also find contact information for the Microsoft Platform Services Team and DRAM Business Intelligence team if you need to request creation of new Tableau AD groups.
sl: This guide provides comprehensive instructions for creating and managing Active Directory (AD) accounts for Tableau users within a university environment where access to Tableau dashboards is controlled through AD groups. The document explains how to access BSP AD User Management through CONNECT Remote Services by selecting the Administrative Tools icon and then BSP AD USER management, where users log in with credentials in the format bsp\sso (such as abcd1234). It covers the complete workflow for checking whether an AD account already exists by navigating to the BSP_Users > Common Users section, right-clicking to select Find, and searching by name to view results. The guide details the process for creating new AD accounts by right-clicking and selecting New > User, then entering the first name, last name, and user login name in sso format, followed by adding the email address in the General Tab. It includes instructions for assigning AD groups to accounts by clicking the Member Of tab, selecting Add, and entering the partial or full AD group name (such as "BIHRStaffDiversityData") before using Check Names to confirm and select available groups. The document also references account settings options for unlocking accounts and configuring account expiration dates, and identifies key contacts at the Microsoft Platform Services Team (Svetlana Kuznetsova) and DRAM Business Intelligence team (Matthew Noonan-Nagl) for requests to create new Tableau AD groups through HRIS Standard Incidents on OSM.

t: Troubleshoot Browser Issues
s: If a user is experiencing problems with a browser-based process, e.g. running reports or doing work in the Portal, there are some common troubleshooting techniques you can employ to try to resolve the issue. This document explains how to: run an incognito browsing session, clear browsing history, and disable extensions on all common PC browsers. Incognito browsing If a user is having problems with a process and you suspect their browser may be to blame, it is useful to...
ss: When browser-based processes like running reports or working in the Portal encounter problems, this guide walks you through three common troubleshooting techniques: using incognito browsing sessions, clearing browser history, and disabling extensions. The document covers step-by-step instructions for Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Internet Explorer, including keyboard shortcuts and menu navigation for each browser. Open this guide when a user reports issues with HR Reporting servers or other Portal functions and you need to systematically isolate whether cached data or browser extensions are causing the problem.
sl: This troubleshooting guide provides step-by-step instructions for resolving browser-related issues in common PC browsers including Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Microsoft Internet Explorer. The document addresses a specific problem discovered in April 2021 where users were unable to run reports on HR Reporting servers (referenced as OSM Problem Record #40002259), though the techniques described apply broadly to any browser-based process failures such as portal work or report generation. The guide outlines three primary troubleshooting methods: opening incognito or private browsing sessions (using keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+Shift+N for Chrome and Edge, or Ctrl+Shift+P for Firefox and Internet Explorer), clearing browser history and cached data through specific menu paths and search bar links (such as chrome://settings/clearBrowserData for Chrome or edge://settings/clearBrowserData for Edge), and disabling extensions via extensions management pages (chrome://extensions/ for Chrome or about:addons for Firefox). For each browser, the document provides detailed instructions on which cached items to clear—including browsing history, cookies, cached images and files, passwords, autofill data, and site settings—and specifies setting the time range to "All time" or "Everything" before clearing. The extension disabling section explains that users can isolate problematic extensions by re-enabling them one-by-one after clearing data, allowing them to identify which specific extension caused the original issue. This resource is primarily used by IT support staff and system administrators who assist end users experiencing functionality problems with browser-dependent applications and systems.

t: Use the External Users Widget
f: HOW TO - Use the External Users Widget.docx
s: The External Users widget is a widget within the CorePortal Security Dashboard. Enabling this widget will allow us to create Portal accounts for users who do not have an employee record in CoreHR. Specifically, it will allow us to provide members of the Access Group with Portal accounts, so that they can provide better support to the University with incidents, problems and projects.
ss: The External Users widget in CorePortal's Security Dashboard enables you to create Portal accounts for non-employees, such as Access Group members who need to support the University with incidents, problems, and projects. Use this guide when you need to set up, manage, or delete external user accounts, including configuring authentication types and assigning menu profiles to control their Portal access. Open this document if you're responsible for onboarding external support staff or maintaining existing external user accounts in CorePortal.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for managing the External Users widget within the CorePortal Security Dashboard, which enables organizations to create Portal accounts for non-employee users such as Access Group members who need to support university incidents, problems, and projects. The guide begins by explaining how to enable the External Users widget by navigating to CorePortal > Security > Menu Profiles, searching for the "COREPORTAL_SUPPORT" menu profile, and enabling four specific menu options: Create External, Delete External, External User Creation, and Get External. To create an external user, administrators navigate to CorePortal > Security > User Management, scroll to the External Users widget, click "Create External User," and complete all required fields while setting their own username and password, with a convention of prefixing Access Group usernames with "C##". The document details how to manage existing external users by locating them in the System Users widget (identifiable by their automatically-assigned "EXT" employee number prefix like EXT00000001), selecting "Manage Account," and configuring their authentication type to "LDAP - Active Directory Authentication" for SSO WebAuth access via the General tab's Security section. Additionally, administrators can assign or remove menu profiles to external users through the Menu Security tab by toggling the Active indicator on profile records, with blue indicators showing active profiles and white indicators showing inactive ones. Finally, the guide explains how to delete external users by selecting them in the External Users widget, choosing "Drop/Delete Account," and confirming the deletion, which removes both their username and EXT number from the database. This document is essential for CorePortal administrators and Access Group representatives who need to provision and maintain Portal accounts for external stakeholders without CoreHR employee records.

t: Access Group Time Calendar Maintenance Mar21 (1)
f: Access Group Time Calendar Maintenance Mar21 (1).docx
s: The following processes are part of the yearly administration that is required to keep the CoreTime system up to date. The administration of yearly time processes is the task for the CoreTime Administrator. This document outlines how to: Extend the CoreTime System Calendar Update Holiday Scheme details Extend a Balance Calendar Complete the Balance Period End How to Complete the Scenario Extend System Calendar The CoreTime System Calendar must be extended each year to...
ss: CoreTime administrators use this guide to complete four essential yearly maintenance tasks that keep the time and attendance system current and accurate. The document covers extending the system calendar to the next year, updating holiday scheme details with new public holidays, extending balance calendars for leave types like annual leave, and closing out balance periods to calculate new entitlements. Open this guide at the beginning of each year or when you need step-by-step instructions for any of these calendar administration tasks in CoreTime. Each section includes prerequisites, required data, detailed steps, and expected outcomes for successful completion.
sl: This document is a how-to guide for CoreTime Administrators that outlines the four essential yearly maintenance tasks required to keep the CoreTime system current and functioning properly. The document covers extending the CoreTime System Calendar by navigating to System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, where administrators add new calendar years with the correct start date (matching the T&A Company's start day), number of weeks, and then use the "Generate Period" function to automatically create all periods for that year. It also explains how to update Holiday Scheme details by accessing System Params > Holiday Schemes > Company Holiday Details to enter company and public holiday dates with associated pay codes for the upcoming year. The guide describes extending Balance Calendars, which manage entitlements like Annual Leave and Study Leave independently of the System Calendar, by navigating to System Params > Balances > Calendars and configuring period numbers, start dates, end dates, and carry-forward limits for each balance type. Finally, it addresses the Complete Balance Period End process, which closes balance calendars at year-end to calculate new entitlements, apply Length of Service adjustments, and process carried forward values. This document is intended for CoreTime Administrators who need an active CoreHR Back Office account and must ensure all prerequisites are met and required data is gathered before executing these critical year-end procedures.

t: Balance & HS MatrixVer2
s: Workbook with sheets: Bal & Hol Matrix by Dept, Balance Hol Matrix, 2025-2026, 2025-2026 Website, 2024-2025 Sheet: Bal & Hol Matrix by Dept Department in Balance | Balance Code | Balance Description | Holiday Scheme | Weekly FTE | Daily Hours | LOS Scheme | Full AL Ent Days Personal leave in days + Bank Holiday + Fixed Closure arrangement | Default weekly | Default Daily | Inc PH & FC | Inc PH & FC | Floating Excl PH & FC | Floating Excl PH & FC | Holiday Pattern (public...
ss: The Balance & HS Matrix workbook tracks annual leave entitlements, holiday schemes, and working hour configurations across departments in your workforce management system. Use this tool to view balance codes, leave accrual by department, full allocation entitlements (including personal leave, bank holidays, and fixed closures), and holiday patterns for planning purposes. Open this document when you need to verify an employee's leave balance, configure holiday schemes for different departments, or audit annual leave allocations for payroll and scheduling accuracy.
sl: This document is an Excel workbook designed to manage and track employee balance and holiday scheme information across multiple departments and fiscal years. The primary sheet, "Bal & Hol Matrix by Dept," contains structured data organized by department and includes key fields such as Department, Balance Code, Balance Description, Holiday Scheme, Weekly FTE, Daily Hours, and Leave of Absence (LOS) Scheme. The workbook tracks annual leave entitlements (Full AL Ent Days) and calculates personal leave allocations by combining personal leave days, bank holidays, and fixed closure arrangements, with separate columns for default weekly and daily calculations. It captures holiday pattern details with distinctions between calculations that include public holidays and fixed closures versus floating holidays that exclude them. The workbook contains multiple sheets covering different time periods (2025-2026 and 2024-2025) as well as a website-facing version, indicating it serves as both an internal reference tool and a source for external-facing information. This document is typically used by Workforce Management (WFM) teams, HR personnel, and departmental managers who need to maintain accurate leave balances, verify holiday scheme assignments, and ensure consistent application of entitlement rules across the organization.

t: Create a pay code group in WFM
f: HOW TO - Create a pay code group in WFM.docx
s: Contents Creating a Pay Code Group Click on ADD GROUP Enter a Group Code (max 6 characters) and Group Description (max 40 characters) Refer to existing Pay Code Groups to check the formatting for the code and description To add Pay Codes to the new group click on ADD Choose a pay code from the drop down list Repeat steps 6 and 7 for each pay code to be added to the group. Editing a Pay Code group Search for the group to be edited Add or delete pay codes as required...
ss: Pay code groups in WFM organize multiple pay codes into logical categories for easier management and access control. Open this guide when you need to create a new pay code group, assign specific pay codes to it, or edit an existing group by adding or removing pay codes. The process takes place in WFM Configuration Settings and requires you to define a group code and description, then populate it with the relevant pay codes from your system. Use this document if you're setting up payroll structures or managing employee compensation classifications in WFM.
sl: This how-to guide provides instructions for creating and managing pay code groups within a Workforce Management (WFM) system, specifically covering two main tasks: creating new pay code groups and editing existing ones. The document explains the creation process by detailing the menu navigation path: WFM Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Configuration Settings, followed by clicking on 'Pay Code Groups' and selecting ADD GROUP. When creating a new pay code group, users must enter a Group Code (limited to 6 characters maximum) and a Group Description (limited to 40 characters), with the guide recommending that users review existing pay code groups to understand proper formatting conventions before entering their own. After saving the initial group information, users can populate the group by clicking ADD and selecting individual pay codes from a dropdown list, repeating this process for each pay code they wish to include before saving again. The document also covers the editing functionality, which follows the same initial navigation path (WFM Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Configuration Settings > Pay Code Groups) but allows users to search for an existing group and modify its contents by adding or removing pay codes as needed. This guide is typically used by WFM administrators or configuration specialists who need to organize and categorize pay codes into logical groups for workforce management purposes, helping to streamline payroll processing and ensure consistent pay code application across the organization.

t: Create Shift Types in Portal
f: HOW TO - Create Shift Types in Portal.docx
s: The Shift Type configuration screen is available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard. The following menu profile should be assigned in order to gain access to the steps below. A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work.
ss: Shift types in the WFM Admin Dashboard determine the hours employees are contracted to work and are assigned to appointments through People Management > Work Schedule. This guide covers creating weekly shift patterns and rotating shifts in Portal, including how to generate unique shift type codes, define daily work patterns, and apply labels for easy identification and searching. Open this document when you need to set up new shift types for your department, copy existing shifts, or deactivate shifts that are no longer in use. You'll need the WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES menu profile to access the Shift Type configuration screen.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for HR Systems administrators on how to create and manage shift types within the Portal's WFM Admin Dashboard, accessible through the WFM_SHIFTS_TYPES menu profile. It explains that shift types determine contracted working hours and are built by assigning work patterns (measured in 3-minute intervals, up to 13 hours maximum) to each day of the week, with a "REST" pattern used for non-working days. The document covers two main shift creation processes: weekly shift patterns, which require generating a unique code using the Shift Type Code Generator and filling in required fields including Code, Name (limited to 40 characters), and an optional Label for grouping and searching, and rotating shifts, which follow specific naming conventions (RT<APP.ID><VERSION LETTER> or TT<APP.ID><VERSION LETTER>) and allow for multiple weekly pattern variations. For employees with flexible arrangements or varying patterns, the document explains that shift codes for weekly patterns are generated centrally while rotating shift codes are linked to employee appointments, and departmental HR can request new shift types via OSM service request. Additional operational tasks covered include copying existing shifts using the three breadcrumbs menu option and deactivating shifts that are no longer in use, though deactivated shifts retain any existing employee assignments and cannot be deleted. This guide is essential for HR Systems administrators who need to set up the foundational shift configuration that Departmental HR Administrators then use to assign shifts to employees through People Management > Work Schedule.

t: Create Work Groups in Portal
f: HOW TO - Create Work Groups in Portal.docx
s: The Work Group configuration screen is available via Portal on the WFM Admin Dashboard. The following menu profile should be assigned in order to gain access to the steps below. The following menu options and webservices should be activated in order for you to gain access to the steps above.
ss: Work Groups in the WFM (Workforce Management) system organize employees by department and configure their timesheet, holiday, and scheduling settings within the Portal admin dashboard. You'll use this guide to create new Work Groups for standard departments or pilot departments using the Time and Absence system, each with specific holiday schemes and shift configurations. Open this document when you need to set up departmental configurations, copy existing Work Group settings to new departments, or manage Work Group status by marking them inactive or deleting them. You must have the WFM_WORKGROUP_CONFIG_ACCESS menu profile assigned to complete these tasks.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for creating and managing work groups in the Portal's WFM Admin Dashboard, which requires the WFM_WORKGROUP_CONFIG_ACCESS menu profile for access. The document covers five main processes: setting up work groups for standard non-pilot departments, setting up work groups for Time and Absence pilot departments, copying existing work groups, marking work groups as inactive, and deleting work groups. For standard departments, users navigate to WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Group and create entries with specific required fields including a numeric 6-digit Work Group Code, a description prefixed with the Department Code, Company (1 University of Oxford), Holiday Scheme (HS001), Shift Type (37.5HRS A-R Standard MON-FRI), Timesheet (Test Timesheets), Pay Frequency (Monthly User Defined Calendar), with Calculate Default Hours set to NO and both Generate Timesheets and Calculate Clockings enabled. For Time and Absence pilot departments, the process is similar but requires selecting from multiple Holiday Scheme options (NDM1, UAS, PHYSIC, ACDEP1, or ITSERV depending on department type), using REST as the Shift Type, Live Timesheets instead of Test, and activating additional toggles for 'Allow Generation of Default Clocks' and 'User Defined Calendar Group' in the General Parameters section. The document also explains how to copy a work group using the Breadcrumbs feature, mark work groups as inactive (which hides them from dropdown lists unless the Active Indicator filter is toggled), and delete work groups only when no employees or managers are assigned. This guide is intended for WFM administrators responsible for workforce management configuration and department setup at the University of Oxford.

t: HR Systems - WFM_Configuring Work Groups for CoreTime v1.0
f: HR Systems - WFM_Configuring Work Groups for CoreTime v1.0.docx
s: Configuring Work Groups for CoreTime These steps are followed by HR Systems when configuring new or existing work groups for use with CoreTime Creating a New Work Group Login to CoreHR Back Office Navigate to CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Parameters > Work Groups Enter the Work Group Number as the next consecutive number available (6 digits) – run PERDEP16 to get a list of current workgroups Enter the Work Group Name based on the information submitted by the department in...
ss: HR Systems staff use this guide to create new work groups in CoreTime and configure existing ones for payroll and timekeeping operations. The document walks through setting up work group parameters in CoreHR Back Office, including assigning holiday schemes, defining shift types, enabling timesheet generation, and configuring pay frequency and clocking rules. Open this guide when you need to establish a work group for a department, integrate it with CoreTime's payroll interface, or adjust work group settings for accurate time and attendance tracking.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for HR Systems personnel to configure new and existing work groups within the CoreTime workforce management system. The guide covers two main processes: creating a new work group and configuring an existing work group for CoreTime use, both accessed through the CoreHR Back Office by navigating to CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Parameters > Work Groups. When creating a new work group, users must enter a 6-digit Work Group Number (obtained by running the PERDEP16 report), assign a unique Work Group Name prefixed with a two-character department code, select University of Oxford as the Company, and save the record using the yellow disc button. Configuration of a work group for CoreTime involves multiple detailed settings across several parameter sections, including selecting an appropriate Holiday Scheme and setting the Default Shift Type to 'REST'. The Payroll Interface section requires enabling 'Live Timesheets' and checking the 'Generate Timesheets' box, while the Pay Frequency section must be set to 'Monthly UDC' with all other fields left blank. Additional configuration steps involve accessing General Parameters – 2 to enable checkboxes for 'Calculate Clockings', 'Allow Generation of Default Clocks', and 'User Defined Calendar Group', followed by navigating to the Group Codes section to assign 'Manager' as the Personalised Pay Code Group. This document is essential for HR Systems administrators responsible for setting up and maintaining CoreTime work group configurations to ensure proper timekeeping, payroll integration, and departmental organization within the University of Oxford's HR infrastructure.

t: HR Systems - WFM_Creating Shift Types v1.0
f: HR Systems - WFM_Creating Shift Types v1.0.docx
s: A shift type determines the hours an employee is contracted to work. Departmental HR Administrators assign the appropriate shift types to appointments via People Management > Work Schedule, but can only assign shift types that have been created by HR Systems. Shift Types and Daily Work Patterns Shift Types are formed by assigning a work pattern to each day of the week.
ss: Creating shift types in CoreTime/CoreRoster is an HR Systems function that establishes the work hour patterns employees are contracted to work—patterns that departmental HR administrators then assign to employee appointments in People Management. This guide walks you through setting up both weekly shift patterns and rotating or term-time shifts using the CoreHR Back Office, including how to generate unique shift codes, define daily work patterns, and enter shift descriptions. Open this document when you need to create a new shift type in the system, have received a request from departmental HR via OSM, or need to set up rotating and flexible scheduling arrangements.
sl: This guide provides HR Systems administrators with step-by-step instructions for creating new shift types in the CoreHR Back Office system, which define the contracted working hours for employees. Shift types are constructed by assigning work patterns (measured in 3-minute intervals, with a maximum of 13 hours per day) to each day of the week, using the 'REST' pattern for non-working days, and are accessed via CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Parameters > Shift Types. The document addresses two primary scenarios: Part A covers weekly shift patterns where employees follow the same schedule each week, and Part B covers rotating and term-time-only shifts where patterns vary by week or are linked to specific employee appointments. Departmental HR Administrators request new shift types through OSM and provide a Shift Code Generator output; HR Systems then enters the unique shift code in the 'Type' field, creates a concise description (maximum 40 characters) in the name field following specified naming conventions (such as "PT 10Hr Week Mon-Fri 2Hrs"), and selects daily work patterns using the lookup function before saving via the yellow disk icon. The naming conventions differ by shift type: weekly patterns begin with FT or PT to indicate full-time or part-time status, rotating shifts use the format RT<APP.ID><VERSION LETTER>, and term-time-only shifts use TT<APP.ID><VERSION LETTER>. The document also references a SQL query ("Core Time Shift Type Reference Data List.sql") available in the Functional Analyst SQL Library that HR Systems can run to verify all shift types created in the system and validate testing data.

t: Maintain calendars in WFM (Year end admin) v1.0
f: HOW TO - Maintain calendars in WFM (Year end admin) v1.0.docx
s: The following processes are part of the yearly administration required to keep the Core|Time system up to date. Contents Extend System Calendar The Core|Time System Calendar must be extended each year to cover the next calendar year. Before extending the System Calendar check and make note of the following items (per T&A Company): Start day of the Company (e.g.
ss: Maintaining calendars in Core|Time requires annual administration tasks to keep the system current and accurate. This guide covers extending the System Calendar and Balance Calendar to cover future years, configuring company holiday schemes, and completing the balance period end process to calculate new entitlements and process carried-forward leave. Use this document at year-end when you need to roll over calendars, set up new balance periods, and close out the previous year's entitlements in WFM. It also includes steps to recalculate balances across all employees after the rollover is complete.
sl: This document is a year-end administration guide for maintaining calendars and balance periods within the Core|Time workforce management system to ensure accurate timekeeping and leave tracking. The guide covers four primary processes: extending the System Calendar by navigating to System Params > Calendars > System Calendar to add new yearly calendar periods with proper start dates and week counts; extending Company Holiday Schemes through a separate Portal Guide; extending Balance Calendars via System Params > Balances > Calendars by adding balance period entries with start and end dates plus carried forward limits; and completing the Balance Period End process through CoreTime > Period End > Balance Period End to calculate new entitlements and apply length of service adjustments. The document addresses critical requirements for preventing gaps in calendar coverage, ensuring start dates align with the company's configured start day (such as Monday), and managing carried forward leave balances with specified maximum day or hour limits. Year-end administrators must verify that the System Calendar is current, Balance Calendars exist in CoreHR, and period end dates have passed before running the period end process, then use the WFM Admin Dashboard > Balance Maintenance screen to recalculate all rolled-over balances across all employees to ensure full entitlement visibility. This guide is primarily used by HR and workforce management administrators during the annual cycle to maintain system accuracy and prevent entitlement errors.

t: Maintain Pay Codes for WFM in the Portal v1.0
f: HOW TO - Maintain Pay Codes for WFM in the Portal v1.0.docx
s: All time (hours & minutes) needs to be recorded against a valid Pay Code. Pay Codes originate in CorePay, but require specific configuration within Core Time to function properly with Timesheets and/or Leave/Absence. For full guidance on configuring pay codes for WFM refer to the Pay Codes guide Time & Pay Codes Pay codes only need to be activated in Time Management if they are required for leave & absence or timesheets.
ss: Pay codes in WFM (Workforce Management) require configuration within Core Time to properly record all employee time—whether for leave and absence or timesheets—and then transfer that data to payroll. This guide explains the two main pay code categories (Leave & Absence and Timesheets), their subcategories, and the specific settings and parameters needed to set up or amend each type. Use this document when you're creating new pay codes in the WFM Admin Dashboard, need to determine which existing pay code to mirror for a new code, or want to understand how to configure codes for employee requests, absences, or timesheet work. The guide includes practical examples like adding unpaid study leave, new casual pay codes, and balance-linked employee request codes.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to understanding and configuring pay codes within the WFM/Time Management system, which are essential for recording all time entries in hours and minutes. Pay codes originate in CorePay but must be specifically configured in Core Time to function properly with Timesheets and Leave/Absence functionality, accessible through WFM Admin Dashboard > Settings > Reference Data > Pay Codes. The document categorizes pay codes into two main types—Leave & Absence codes (which record time away from work) and Timesheet codes (which record hours worked and trigger payment)—with further subcategories including Employee Request codes, Absence-Basic and Absence-Advanced codes, Paid as Claimed Work codes, Paid as Claimed Holiday codes, and Employee Work codes, each with distinct behaviors and parameters. The guide addresses the configuration process by detailing specific steps such as creating reason code groups linked to pay codes via WFM Admin Dashboard > Settings > Configuration Settings > Pay Code Groups, managing sensitive absence settings on the Leave Request Settings screen, and adding codes to relevant Working Time Group columns through CoreTime/Core Roster > System Params > Reference Q-Z > Working Time Parameters. The document includes three practical examples—adding a new absence type (Green Day), adding a new Casual Pay Code (Casual Catering Assistant), and adding an Employee Request balance-linked code—that illustrate how to determine which existing pay code settings to mirror based on intended code behavior. This resource is intended for WFM administrators and HR personnel responsible for maintaining and updating pay code configurations to support organizational policies and payroll accuracy.

t: Maintain Pay Codes for WFM v1.1
f: HOW TO - Maintain Pay Codes for WFM v1.1.docx
s: Pay Codes drive PeopleXD Time functionality as all time (hours & minutes) needs to be recorded against a Pay Code. Pay Codes originate in CorePay, but require specific configuration within Time to function properly with Timesheets or Leave/Absence. Time & Pay Codes Pay codes only need to be activated in Time Management if they are relevant to the leave & absence or timesheet processes.
ss: Pay codes in PeopleXD Time drive all time recording functionality—whether for leave and absence or timesheets—and require specific configuration within the system to work properly with employee requests, timesheets, and payroll processing. This guide helps HR Systems staff set up and maintain new or amended pay codes by classifying them into types (such as Employee Request codes, Absence codes, or Paid as Claimed Work codes) and walking through the configuration steps in CoreTime. Open this document when you need to create a new absence type, casual pay code, or other pay code variant, or when you're troubleshooting why a pay code isn't functioning as expected in Time Management.
sl: This document serves as a configuration guide for HR Systems administrators who need to set up and maintain pay and absence codes within the PeopleXD Time (Workforce Management) module, which integrates with the CorePay system. The document explains that pay codes are essential to PeopleXD Time functionality since all recorded time must be assigned to a pay code, and these codes originate in CorePay but require specific configuration within Time to work properly with timesheets and leave/absence processes. Pay codes are accessed and configured through CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Pay Codes, and are categorized into two main types—Leave & Absence codes (which record time away from work) and Timesheet codes (which record hours worked)—with multiple subcategories including Employee Request (balance-linked), Absence-Basic, Absence-Advanced, Paid as Claimed Work, and Employee Work codes. The document provides detailed step-by-step configuration processes, including adding codes to Working Time Groups via CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Reference Q-Z > Working Time Parameters > Working Time Group 029, linking codes to Pay Code Groups through CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Reference K-P > Personalised Pay Code Groups, and creating or assigning reason codes through CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Params > Reference Q-Z > Reason Codes/Reason Code Groups. Three practical examples walk through real-world scenarios: adding a new absence type (Green Day), adding a new casual pay code (Casual Catering Assistant), and adding an employee request balance-linked code, each illustrating how to determine appropriate settings based on intended code behavior. The document also addresses configuration considerations such as managing sensitive absences by controlling the "Display on Co-Worker's roster" setting on General Parameters 1 and determining which Working Time Group columns and Pay Code Groupings are relevant for each code type.

t: Override Workgroup Holiday Scheme at employee level within the Portal (DRAFT)
f: HOW TO - Override Workgroup Holiday Scheme at employee level within the Portal (DRAFT).docx
s: The Workgroup Override allows the user to override certain workgroup settings at an employee level. Currently the only override setting being utilised is the Holiday Scheme. The Holiday Scheme calculates when an employee is allowed to book leave and this is derived from the workgroup as default.
ss: Override Holiday Scheme settings at the employee level within PeopleXD's WFM Admin portal when multiple employees share the same workgroup but have different holiday terms. This guide walks through adding, editing, and deleting Holiday Scheme overrides for individual employees through the Person Maintenance section, allowing you to customize leave eligibility rules beyond the default workgroup settings. Open this document if you need to set up or manage holiday entitlements that differ from an employee's assigned workgroup, or if you need to remove an existing holiday scheme override.
sl: This guide provides instructions for overriding workgroup Holiday Scheme settings at the individual employee level within the PeopleXD portal, specifically addressing situations where multiple employees share the same workgroup but have different holiday terms and leave booking requirements. The document covers three main processes: adding or editing a Holiday Scheme override, deleting an existing override, and maintaining and tracking overrides, though the latter section notes that specific procedures are still to be determined. To access these functions, users must have the menu options 'WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Work Group Override' and 'WFM Admin > Person Maintenance > Add/Update Work Group Override' enabled in their system. The add or edit process requires users to log into PeopleXD, navigate to WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Person Maintenance, locate the employee by selecting the correct Appointment ID if multiple appointments exist, access the Work Group Override tab, and use the ellipses menu to edit the Holiday Scheme field, which displays both the default Work Group Value and any existing Person Override Value. The deletion process follows the same navigation steps but concludes by selecting 'Delete Override' from the ellipses menu and confirming the deletion through a prompt. This guide is intended for WFM (Workforce Management) administrators who need to customize holiday leave policies for individual employees while maintaining standard workgroup configurations for others.

t: Solution Design Document for Oxford v1.0

The broad in-scope processes are as follows: Occupational Absence Leave Management Leave Management (Accruals) Online Timesheet Claims Pilot Departments Throughout the Discovery process, the following departments have been confirmed as pilot groups:...
ss: Oxford University's Workforce Management implementation covers occupational absence recording, leave management, and online timesheet claims across five pilot departments using the People XD system. This solution design document details all necessary configuration steps including reference data setup (pay codes, calendars, work patterns, holiday schemes), person-level configuration, timesheet generation processes, and portal dashboard settings for both employees and managers. Open this document when setting up or troubleshooting the Workforce Management module at Oxford, configuring employee absence and leave functionality, or implementing changes to timesheet approval workflows. It's essential for system administrators, implementation teams, and anyone managing the CoreTime system configuration for occupational absence and leave management.
sl: This Solution Design Document details the configuration requirements for implementing the Workforce Management module of People XD from the Access Software Suite across five pilot departments at the University of Oxford, specifically covering Occupational Absence Recording, Leave Management, Leave Management with Accruals, and Online Timesheet Claims functionality. The document encompasses extensive reference data configuration including Company Details, System Calendar and User Defined Calendar setup (with the System Calendar accessible via CoreTime/Roster > System Params > Calendar), Pay Codes for both Occupational Absence and Online Timesheet Claims, Reason Codes, Work Patterns, Shift Types, Work Groups, Holiday Schemes, and Balance configurations for entitlements, accruals, and pro rata calculations. Person-level configuration is addressed through Person Overrides, Personalised Pay Code Groups, Shift Type assignments, Balance Entitlements, Absence Categories, Menu Profiles for both managers and employees, and CoreTime System User setup. The document describes critical operational processes including timesheet generation with both Test Mode and LIVE Mode options, approval workflows, sign-off procedures in the Portal, and functionality to ignore unconfirmed or unsigned-off hours. Portal configuration is detailed for both Employee and Manager Dashboards, with Employee Dashboards featuring Book Leave, Balance, and Timesheet functionality, and Manager Dashboards including Home, Timesheet, and Delegation tabs. The pilot implementation targets five departments (Classics, BDI-NDM, Oxford Ludwig Institute NDM, Physics Lab Demonstrators, and Human Resources), with full-time and part-time term-time employees receiving Occupational Absence and Leave Management capabilities, while variable hours and casual employees receive Leave Management with Accruals and Online Timesheet Claims functionality.

t: Transfer Timesheets to Payroll in WFM v1.1
f: HOW TO - Transfer Timesheets to Payroll in WFM v1.1.docx
s: This process is followed by the Payroll Officer managing the casual payroll and should be completed once the casual payroll deadline has passed, so that departments have had the opportunity to resolve any unapproved timesheets and/or add claims on behalf of workers. This process will transfer the hours to CorePay (creating CorePay timesheets) and progress the CoreTime period to the next month. Before creating the timesheets, it is possible to review errors by retrieving...
ss: The Payroll Officer uses this process to transfer casual worker hours from CoreTime to CorePay after the payroll deadline has passed, creating CorePay timesheets and advancing the period to the next month. Before finalizing the transfer, you review errors and controls in test mode within CoreTime's Period End section to identify any unapproved or unsigned timesheets that departments need to resolve. The process includes checking for five types of warnings—ranging from unapproved codes to historical hours—and reviewing control totals showing total hours, pay code breakdowns, and worker counts. Once errors are reviewed and controls verified, you switch to final mode to create timesheets, which simultaneously transfers all hours to CorePay and closes the current period.
sl: This document provides a step-by-step guide for Payroll Officers to transfer casual payroll hours from CoreTime to CorePay after the payroll deadline has passed, enabling the progression of the CoreTime period to the next month. The process is executed through the CoreTime > Period End > Generate Timesheets menu path, where users input company information (University of Oxford), calendar code (Calendar Code 'A' for New Monthly), and specify work groups using the Work Group From and Work Group To fields with list-of-values selection. The document describes a two-phase approach: Part 1 uses Test mode to review and validate data without affecting CorePay, allowing Payroll Officers to identify errors and warnings before finalizing the transfer, while Part 2 executes the actual transfer in Final mode by changing the Mode field setting and clicking the Create Timesheets button. Five specific error/warning types are detailed in the document, including unapproved codes (Type 1), unconfirmed hours (Type 2), unconfirmed absence codes for non-payable work groups (Type 3), and historical hours issues (Types 4 and 5), with explanations of when these errors require department intervention and when they will be resolved in future periods. Throughout both phases, users access the Controls button to review the Controls Totals window, which displays total hours across workers and pay codes, the breakdown by pay code, and the number of workers whose hours are being transferred to CorePay. The document emphasizes that Test mode should only be used for review purposes and that the Ignore Unconfirmed checkbox must be selected before retrieving hours in both phases, with the system automatically processing all work groups when Final mode is activated.

t: Upload complex shifts in WFM v1.1
f: HOW TO - Upload complex shifts in WFM v1.1.docx
s: Follow these steps to create complex shift types (e.g. Term-time only patterns that span a 52 week period) or to upload multiple shift types in bulk when on-boarding new departments with a large number of new part-time shifts. For individual shifts which repeat weekly, please see the separate guidance on Creating Shift Types Contents Knowledge Article: WFM_Time Management Knowledge Article Other Related documents HOW TO - Prepare data for data migration Part Time Shift...
ss: Uploading complex shifts in WFM v1.1 covers how to create and bulk upload complex shift patterns—such as term-time only shifts spanning 52 weeks or multiple part-time shifts—using the Rotating Shift Pattern Builder or Multiple Shift Generator tools. This guide walks you through preparing shift data files, validating them for errors, and loading them into the system via the PeopleXD Data Migration tool. Open this document when onboarding new departments with large numbers of shifts or when you need to set up non-standard shift patterns that don't repeat on a simple weekly cycle. You'll also find naming conventions and file formatting requirements (CSV with pipe separators) needed to successfully process your shift uploads.
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance for creating and uploading complex shift types in WFM v1.1, specifically for scenarios involving term-time only patterns spanning 52 weeks or bulk onboarding of multiple part-time shifts for new departments. The document covers two main processes: handling complex shift types using the Rotating shift pattern builder spreadsheet and uploading multiple shifts using the Multiple shift generator tool, with both requiring completion of the Shift Type Code and Shift Type Description fields in the Data worksheet tab. Key data preparation steps include validating that all days in the sequence have entries (even if marked as Non-Working Day), reviewing error-check columns (J for complex shifts, BV to BZ for multiple shifts), ensuring shift type descriptions do not exceed 40 characters, and using the Part Time Shift Type Descriptions Calculator to generate descriptions by copying hours, totals, and Shift Ref columns. Before uploading, users must remove formulas by copying and pasting as values, verify that shift codes do not already exist in the system using the Core Time Shift Type Reference Data List.sql query from the Functional Analyst SQL Library, delete duplicate shifts, remove example records (Joe Bloggs), and eliminate blank rows. The actual upload process involves navigating to Administrator dashboard > Data Migration > Data Migration Options, configuring the list separator to pipe (|) in Control Panel > Clock and Region settings, saving the file as CSV in Notepad++, and uploading via the Load File button, where the system scans for errors before processing. This document is designed for HR administrators and departmental personnel managing workforce scheduling who need to handle non-standard shift patterns or migrate large volumes of new shift data into the system.

ss: WFM Company and Calendar Configuration covers how to set up and manage company profiles within the Workforce Management system, including creating new companies, configuring calendar periods, and establishing parameters for timesheets, absences, clocking, and rostering. Open this guide when you need to add a new company to WFM, configure calendar years and periods, or adjust settings that control how timesheet data is processed, who can enter data, and how absences and hours are calculated. It walks you through the three-step setup wizard and explains all configuration tabs available after initial setup, from Absence Parameters to Contract Hours to Auto Advance Periods scheduling.
sl: This document is a how-to guide for configuring workforce management companies and calendars in a WFM system that has recently been migrated from a back office into a portal environment. The guide walks users through accessing the Company and Calendar Configuration screen via the WFM Admin Dashboard, then selecting Company and Calendar Config, and covers the process of adding new companies by completing mandatory fields, enabling the Active toggle, and working through a three-step system calendar wizard that configures calendar years, periods, and company parameters such as Late Pay Code and Unapproved Absence Pay Code. The document addresses the Auto Advance Periods functionality, which automatically moves system calendars forward when they fall into the past, and includes configuration for this feature with options like scheduling the advance, enabling historical balance recalculation, and managing user-defined calendar periods. The guide provides detailed explanations of multiple configuration tabs including Summary Tab (which defines company name, start day, dates, status codes, and timesheet templates), Company Calendar Years Tab, Company Calendar Periods Tab, Rostering Tab, Generate Timesheets Tab, and specialized tabs for Absence Parameters, Late Parameters, Clocking Parameters, Flexitime, Banked Hours Parameters, and others. Additional configuration areas covered include file locations, sign-off rules, trigger point groups, night premiums, agency parameters, contract hours, and advanced options. This document is designed for WFM administrators and configuration specialists who need to set up and manage company-level configurations, calendar structures, and operational parameters that govern how employee time and attendance data is processed, calculated, and approved within the WFM system.

t: WFM_Complete Balance Period End and Balance Recalculate in the Portal
f: HOW TO - WFM_Complete Balance Period End and Balance Recalculate in the Portal.docx
s: At the end of the balance/holiday year the Balance Calendars must be closed to: Calculate new entitlements Apply Length of Service Adjustments Process carried forward valued
ss: The WFM (Workforce Management) Balance Period End and Balance Recalculation process in PeopleXD closes out leave and balance calendars at the end of each holiday year to calculate new entitlements, apply Length of Service Adjustments, and process carried forward values. You'll use this guide when you need to complete the Balance Period End function in the WFM Admin Dashboard and then force a Balance Recalculation to update employee balances for the new period. The process requires the WFM_BALANCE_PERIOD_END menu profile and should be performed after HR teams have reviewed outstanding leave balances and determined carry-over amounts. Open this document if you're responsible for rolling over leave balances and entitlements in your organization's annual holiday year cycle.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for HR administrators responsible for closing balance and holiday years in the WFM (Workforce Management) Portal system, specifically detailing the processes needed at year-end to calculate new entitlements, apply Length of Service Adjustments, and process carried-forward values. The guide requires users to have the WFM_BALANCE_PERIOD_END menu profile assigned via Security > User Management and provides two configuration approaches: either using pre-configured PeopleXD menu profiles (WFM_BALANCE_ADMIN, WFM_BALANCE_PERIOD_END, WFM_ADVANCE_PERIOD) or enabling individual menu options and web services separately within existing HR Systems profiles. The document outlines specific prerequisites including ensuring the System Calendar and Balance Calendar are current and extended to future periods, verifying Entitlements Length of Service values are up to date, and confirming that relevant reports (such as TIMDEP02 Leave Balance History per Employee) have been run to capture outstanding leave balances before rollover begins. The Complete Balance Period End process involves navigating to WFM Admin Dashboard > Balance Maintenance, selecting the relevant balance, accessing the Balance Period End tab, ensuring the filter returns ALL records, and clicking Run Period End to close the current balance period. Following the period end completion, an overnight automated process calculates employee balances; however, administrators may need to manually force a Balance Recalculation by navigating to the Balance Recalculation tab, selecting the From Period, choosing whether to recalculate Balance Values, Booked Values, or Both, and clicking Recalculate. The University of Oxford configuration is noted as requiring zero days carry-over by default, with any agreed carry-over to be manually input by HR teams in the new holiday year, and this process must be repeated for each balance rolled to the next period.

ss: The WFM User Defined Calendar feature in CoreTime allows you to create custom pay periods beyond the standard weekly, fortnightly, and monthly options. This document walks you through configuring and enabling the calendar in system parameters, extending it to cover future periods, and assigning it to work groups or individual employees. Open this guide when you need to set up a non-standard pay frequency schedule or adjust calendar periods for your organization's specific payroll requirements.
sl: This how-to guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring, enabling, extending, and assigning User Defined Calendars (UDC) within the WFM system, specifically in the CoreTime module. The document covers the initial configuration process, which involves accessing System Params > Reference A - C > Control Parameters to enable the User Defined Calendar Entry by adding a row with "TIMESHEETS - RUN MONTHLY," followed by navigating to System Params > Calendars > System Calendar to create calendar codes, set data entry offsets, and generate periods. For users needing to extend an existing calendar, the guide explains how to access the calendar code in System Params > Calendars > System Calendar, enter start and end dates, and use the Tab key to auto-generate periods, while noting the standard period counts (52 for weekly, 26 for fortnightly, and 12 for monthly calendars). The assignment process is detailed in two scenarios: assigning to entire Work Groups through CoreTime > System Params > Work Groups by selecting the UDC from the Pay Frequency dropdown on General Parameters - 1 and enabling the User Defined Calendar Group checkbox on General Parameters - 2, or assigning to individual employees by accessing CoreTime > Pers. Data > Person Maintenance and selecting the UDC from the Pay Frequency dropdown under Work Group Override 2. This guide is intended for WFM administrators and payroll configuration specialists who need to implement customized pay period calendars across employee populations or manage exceptions to standard weekly, fortnightly, and monthly pay frequencies.

ss: Reason Codes and Reason Code Groups in WFM allow HR Self-service users to record detailed absence information by categorizing absences like sickness into organized groups. Open this document when you need to set up or maintain absence categorization in your WFM system, or when managing which reason codes are available for HR users to select during absence recording.
sl: This document is a how-to guide for workforce management administrators who need to create, modify, and organize absence reason codes within their system. The guide covers the complete lifecycle of reason code management, beginning with background information explaining that Absence Reason Codes (such as Sickness Absence) are linked to Reason Code Groups to allow HR Self-service users to provide detailed information about absences being recorded. The document provides step-by-step instructions for four main tasks: adding new reason codes through the WFM Admin Dashboard > Reference Data > Reason Code and Groups menu where administrators enter an alphanumeric code (maximum 6 characters), description, and type; amending existing codes by directly overwriting fields or using toggles to activate or deactivate codes; linking reason codes to Reason Code Groups by selecting a group code (such as SICK) from a dropdown and adding available codes to that group; and removing codes from groups using the DELETE function with confirmation. The guide references specific menu profile configuration requirement (723413661) that must be enabled before users can access the Reason Code and Groups functionality. This document is primarily used by WFM administrators and HR configuration teams who manage the structure and organization of absence categorization within their workforce management system to support self-service absence recording by HR users.

Enter a name for the scheme, following...
ss: Maintaining accrual and entitlement balances in CoreTime/CoreRoster for tracking employee leave—such as annual leave, long service leave, and holiday schemes—requires configuring multiple system parameters. This guide walks you through creating Long Service Schemes, setting up accrual balances with parameters like affecting codes and accrual calendars, and configuring entitlement balances with pro rata settings. Use this document when you need to establish or modify how employee leave accruals are calculated, when leave is awarded based on length of service, or when setting up new leave schemes in the WFM system. It's essential for HR and payroll administrators managing leave policies across different employee groups.
sl: This document is a comprehensive how-to guide for configuring and maintaining balance schemes within a workforce management system, specifically covering accrual balances and entitlement balances. The guide walks users through creating Long Service Schemes by navigating to CoreTime/CoreRoster > System Parameters > Balances > Length of Service Increments, where administrators define service code increments with "From Months," "To Months," and "Percentage" fields to determine when employees receive additional annual leave based on tenure. Users then create Accrual Balances through the Parameters submenu, configuring critical settings such as Display Format (Decimal), entitlement behavior (ALLOW vs. STOP), and whether to use personal or universal leave calendars with specific start and end date configurations. The document details configuration of multiple submenus including Affecting Codes (which links holiday pay codes and deducts taken leave from accrued balances), Advanced Parameters (requiring position history population from CoreHR and appointment-based settings), and the Accrual Calendar (which sets percentage accrual rates with minimum and maximum hour thresholds). Additionally, it covers Entitlement Balances configuration, including Holiday Scheme creation, Length of Service settings, pro rata calculations, and the Balance Calendar setup with specific date ranges. This guide is designed for workforce management system administrators and HR configuration specialists who need to establish or maintain leave balance systems that track employee entitlements, apply service-based increments, and manage holiday accrual across either personal or universal leave year structures.

t: WFM_Maintain Bank Holiday Schemes in the Portal
f: HOW TO - WFM_Maintain Bank Holiday Schemes in the Portal.docx
s: A Holiday Scheme is a list of closure dates, such as public/bank holidays and departmental fixed closure days. These dates will be treated as non-working days for anyone linked to the Holiday Scheme (via their Balance). The system using employee work schedules to determine if the employee would normally work on the closure day and adjusts their entitlement accordingly.
ss: Bank Holiday Schemes in the WFM module define closure dates—such as public holidays and departmental fixed closure days—that are treated as non-working days for employees linked to the scheme through their Balance. This guide walks you through creating new Holiday Schemes in PeopleXD's WFM Admin Dashboard and extending existing schemes by adding additional closure dates with the appropriate pay codes (160 for public holidays, 3990 for fixed closure days). You'll need the WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG menu profile assigned to your user account to complete these tasks. Open this guide when you need to set up holiday entitlements or update closure dates for your organization's leave management.
sl: This how-to guide provides instructions for creating and maintaining bank holiday schemes within the WFM (Workforce Management) portal, which define closure dates that are treated as non-working days for employees linked to the scheme through their Balance records. The document explains that Holiday Schemes contain lists of public/bank holidays and departmental fixed closure days, and the system uses employee work schedules to determine whether employees would normally work on closure days and adjusts their entitlements accordingly, though Holiday Schemes should not be used with Accrual Balances. Users must have the menu profile WFM_BANK_HOLIDAY_CONFIG assigned through Security > User Management to complete these functions. To create a new Holiday Scheme, users navigate to PeopleXD > WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Configuration Settings > Bank Holiday Schemes, click the "Add New Scheme" button, enter a unique code and description (maximum 40 characters), and then add individual closure dates on the General Settings tab by selecting the Holiday Date field and assigning the appropriate pay code—either "160 – PUBLIC HOLIDAY" for bank holidays or "3990 – FIXED CLOSURE DAY" for departmental closures—while setting Hours to "Calculate" and Apply Hours to "ALL." To extend an existing Holiday Scheme with additional closure dates, users follow a similar process by locating the scheme in Bank Holiday Schemes, selecting View from the ellipses menu, and adding new closure dates with the same field requirements. This guide is designed for WFM administrators responsible for configuring and maintaining holiday schedules across the organization's workforce management system.

t: WFM_Maintain Work Patterns in the Portal v1.0
f: HOW TO - WFM_Maintain Work Patterns in the Portal v1.0.docx
s: What are Work Patterns Work Patterns define a daily work schedule. They identify the different work durations that exist within the organisation and capture the expected working hours for an employee. Selected work patterns are then used to configure an employee’s shift type.
ss: Work Patterns define daily work schedules in the WFM (Workforce Management) system and identify the different work durations and expected working hours for employees across your organisation. This guide covers how to create, copy, and configure work patterns in the Portal, including setting default hours, start/end times, pay codes, breaks, and other parameters through the WFM Admin Dashboard. Open this document when you need to set up new shift schedules, modify existing work patterns, or configure how standard hours and overtime are calculated for different employee roles. It's essential for WFM administrators who manage shift types and need to establish the foundational scheduling templates used throughout the system.
sl: This guide document explains how to maintain and configure Work Patterns within the WFM (Workforce Management) Portal, covering the complete lifecycle of work pattern management for administrators. Work Patterns define daily work schedules and capture expected working hours for employees, serving as a foundational element linked throughout the system and used to configure employee shift types. Administrators access the Work Patterns screen via WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Work Patterns, where they can view all created patterns, search by criteria such as Default Pay Code or Active status, and see key fields including Pattern Code, Description, Default Pay Code, Default Hours, Start Time, End Time, and Label. The document provides step-by-step instructions for adding new work patterns by completing mandatory fields (Pattern Code, Description, Default Pay Code, Extra Hours Worked, Default Hours, Default Start Time, Default End Time, and Earliest Start Time) and then configuring additional details through tabs, as well as copying existing patterns through the 3-dot menu. Configuration occurs primarily through the General Parameters screen, which allows customization of default start and end times, default hours, overtime overrides, and toggles for features such as Fill Basic Hours, Rest Pattern, Split Default Hours, Roster Calculation, and Standard Calculation, along with assignment of Default Pay Code and Extra Hours Worked pay codes. The document also identifies several configuration areas—including Standard Hours, Breaks, Absence, Overtime, Flexitime Settings, Alternate Patterns, Premiums, Rostering, Roster Allowances, Alternate Premium Patterns, Bonus Payments, Work Pattern Mapping, Miscellaneous Settings, and NCHD Settings—that have been enabled in the Portal migration but are not currently utilized. This guide serves administrators responsible for organizational workforce management who need to create, copy, and configure work patterns to meet their specific business requirements.

ss: WFM yearly extension and period-end activities in CoreTime and the WFM Admin Dashboard cover extending multiple calendars (System, User Defined, Balance, and Accrual), configuring holiday schemes, and managing entitlements for the upcoming year. Use this guide when you need to prepare your WFM system for a new calendar year, close out current balance periods, and ensure all leave accrual and entitlement balances are properly configured and calculated. It walks you through specific steps in Back Office CoreTime and the Portal WFM Admin Dashboard to extend calendars, update holiday schemes, configure length of service increments, and run balance period-end and recalculation processes. Open this document at year-end or when implementing new annual leave, accrual, or entitlement periods in your organization.
sl: This comprehensive how-to guide details the complete year-end extension and period closure process for a workforce management (WFM) system, specifically covering all calendar, balance, and entitlement configurations required to support ongoing payroll and leave management operations. The document walks users through extending the System Calendar via Back Office Core Time > System Params > Calendars > System Calendar by adding new yearly entries with start dates, week counts, and auto-generating weekly periods, as well as extending User Defined Calendars and Balance Calendars to establish new period date ranges for leave accrual tracking. It provides step-by-step instructions for configuring multiple interconnected calendar types—including Accrual Calendars (which define accrual percentages for hours worked), Balance Calendars (which define leave year start and end dates), and Holiday Schemes accessed through Portal WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Configuration Settings > Bank Holiday Schemes—to ensure accurate leave and entitlement calculations across different balance types. The guide specifically addresses the distinction between accrual balances (which do not interact with holiday schemes) and entitlement balances (which do), with detailed field-level instructions for entering periods, elements, FTE hours, and length of service scheme selections in Back Office Core Time > System Params > Balances > Entitlements per Balance. Users must complete the Balance Period End process via Portal WFM Admin Dashboard > Balance Maintenance to close out the current period, calculate new entitlements, and apply length of service adjustments before triggering a Balance Recalculation to update employee balances system-wide. This document is essential for WFM administrators and finance teams managing annual leave cycles, public holidays, and employee entitlements who need to prepare their system for a new fiscal or calendar year.

sl: This How To Guide provides instructions for overriding the Holiday Scheme setting at the individual employee level within the Back Office system, addressing scenarios where multiple employees within the same workgroup have different holiday entitlements.
