t: Job Seekers Register
s:
# Job Seekers Register User Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR system users how to use the **Job Seekers Register** feature in PeopleXD's People Management system. After reading it, users will understand:

## What the Feature Does
The Job Seekers Register automatically identifies and tracks employees whose fixed-term contracts are ending soon, so the organisation can consider them for other open positions within the company before their employment ends. This helps with internal redeployment and ensures employees nearing the end of their funded positions have opportunities for continued employment.

## What Users Will Learn to Do

1. **Configure the system** — Set up two key configuration areas:
   - Define numeric parameters that control which employees qualify for the register based on their continuous service length and how soon their funding expires
   - Set up eligibility rules to determine who can be included

2. **Manage the register** — Add employees to the Job Seekers Register and understand how the system handles:
   - Funding expiry dates
   - Continuous service requirements
   - Automatic updates to the register

3. **Access reporting** — Use views and reports to monitor the Job Seekers Register data

The guide emphasises that the system works automatically based on configured rules around employees' funding expiry dates and service history, minimising manual administration while ensuring eligible employees are properly flagged for redeployment opportunities.
ss: The Job Seekers Register in People XD automatically identifies employees nearing the end of their contract funding and considers them for internal redeployment opportunities based on their continuous service and eligibility criteria. You'll use this guide to configure numeric parameters that set minimum continuous service requirements and funding expiry thresholds, then define service rules that determine which employees qualify for the register. Open this document when setting up or managing your organization's redeployment process, or when you need to understand how employees are automatically added to the Job Seekers Register based on their funding expiry dates and service history.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing the Job Seekers Register feature within People Management, which automatically identifies and links employees approaching the end of their contracts to the company's Job Seekers or Redeployment Register based on their funding expiry dates and continuous service eligibility. The configuration process involves two main steps: first, setting numeric client parameters through the People Management Dashboard by navigating to Data Centre > HR Admin Setup Settings > System Parameters – Advanced > Client Parameters to define JSR Continuous Service Eligibility (minimum months of service required) and JSR Funding Expiry Eligibility (maximum months before an employee's funding expiry date stored on their Post Appointment Cost Allocation), and second, configuring Eligible Service Rules through the same dashboard path to establish which employee categories qualify for inclusion on the register. The document details how to add service rules by assigning sequence numbers, toggling the Eligible indicator to include or exclude specific employee groups, and using up to three references (such as Company, Department, Cost Centre, Location, Employee Status, Job Title, and various user codes) combined with corresponding codes to create nuanced eligibility criteria. Key operational processes covered include adding employees to the Job Seekers Register, managing funding expiry dates, tracking continuous service, and implementing automatic register updates, all of which ensure that employees nearing contract completion are considered for redeployment opportunities. The guide emphasizes that the system strictly processes employees based on the Funding Expiry date recorded on their Post Appointment Cost Allocations, meaning employees without Cost Allocations will not be included in the JSR calculation. HR administrators and people management professionals responsible for workforce planning and employee redeployment use this guide to configure and maintain the register, with reporting capabilities available through designated views to monitor register membership and eligibility status.

ss: The Key Information section in XD People Management allows HR administrators to view and update essential employee details within the Employee Profile. This covers personal information such as names, social security numbers, retirement dates, service history, work permits, and contract details, all accessible via the Command Centre employee search. HR teams use this screen to maintain accurate employee records and override system-calculated continuous service dates when needed. You'd open this guide when you need to update employee personal data, manage service dates for payroll or leave calculations, or understand which fields can be configured in your People Management system.
sl: This user guide provides detailed guidance on the Key Information section of the Employee Profile within XD People Management, a system used by HR administrators to access and amend employee personal details. To access the Key Information screen, users navigate to the Command Centre, search for an employee on the Employees screen, click the View button to open their record, and then select the Key Information tab. The document describes four main sections for managing employee information: the General section captures employee names, social security numbers (PPS/NI/Social Security Number), and retirement dates with fields supporting up to 40 alphanumeric characters for name fields; the Service Details section displays and allows override of employee service dates including Recent Start Date, Date First Joined, TUPE Date, Override Start Date, Override End Date, and calculates Continuous Service Duration and Total Length of Service. All data updates follow the same process of entering or modifying information in the required fields and clicking the Save button at the end of the screen. The document also references that field visibility and mandatory status are controlled by HR Admin Field Options configuration, meaning organisations can customize which sections and fields appear based on their specific use of People Management, with further configuration guidance available in a separate Configuring HR Admin Field Options user guide and a Continuous Service user guide for detailed information on service calculations.

t: Leavers
s:
# Leavers User Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to process an employee as a leaver in the PeopleXD HR system. After reading it, you'll be able to:

**Main Process:**
- Make an employee a leaver by accessing the employee record, clicking Actions, and selecting "Process As Leaver"
- Complete the required leaver information including the leaving date, leaving code (reason for leaving), leaving destination, and location after leaving
- Add optional comments about the end of employment

**Key Details You'll Learn:**

The guide explains the purpose of the leaver process: to make an employee's record dormant on the system from a specified leave date, end their salary record and all contract-related details as of that date, and enable Payroll to process them for a P45 (final tax document).

**Additional Actions:**
- Record notice periods by capturing either the employee's resignation date or the employer's notification date
- Review a "Leaving Summary" that shows all contract elements being ended, including cost allocations, allowances, deductions, annual leave balances, and pension scheme assignments
- Preview appointment and org structure details for the contract being ended (read-only view for review purposes)
- Save the leaver record

**Important Limitation:**
The guide clarifies when NOT to use this process — specifically, it should not be used when a contract is being replaced by another contract or when an employee has multiple active contracts and only one is ending. Alternative procedures exist for those situations.
ss: The People Management Leavers process enables HR teams to mark an employee as a leaver, which dormantly ends their employee record, salary, and all contract details as of a specified leaving date. Use this guide when you need to process employee departures, end all active contracts at once, record resignation or employer notification dates, and prepare leaver information for Payroll to issue a P45. The process handles key details like leaving date, reason for leaving, and documents cost allocations, allowances, deductions, and pension scheme assignments that will be affected. Open this document when an employee is permanently leaving the organisation and you need step-by-step instructions on how to complete the leaver process in the system.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing employee departures within the Access People Management system, specifically covering the process of converting an active employee record into a leaver status. The document details the core leaver process initiated through the employee record widget by clicking the Actions button and selecting Process As Leaver in the Contracts tab, which opens a screen where users must enter a mandatory Leaving Date and can optionally record the Leaving Code, Leaving Destination, Location After Leaving, and Comments (up to 80 characters). The guide explains that the End All Contracts field is enabled by default to terminate all active contracts, and users can access additional functions through the Actions menu to record Notice Periods (for Employee Resignation or Employer Notification dates), view the Leaving Summary screen (which displays affected Cost Allocations, Allowances, Deductions, Annual Leave Balance, and Pension Scheme Assignments), and preview read-only Appointment Details and Org Structure information for review purposes only. Once saved, the system immediately reflects the employee's status change throughout the application, either as Ended (if the leave date is in the past) or Ending (if the leave date is today or in the future), with the Dormant label appearing on employee records with past leave dates and the Leaving label appearing for future dates. The document also covers how to review and amend leaver details after the initial process, including the ability to modify the Leaving Code, Leaving Destination, Location after Leaving, and Comments, though the Leaving Date itself cannot be edited on the review screen. This guide is essential for HR personnel and payroll administrators who need to properly process employee departures to ensure employee records become dormant, contracts are ended, and the system can generate P45 documentation through the Payroll integration.

t: Maintain the Organisational Hierarchy
s:
# Summary: Maintain the Organisational Hierarchy

This guide teaches users how to manage and update an organisation's structure within the PeopleXD HR system. 

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Access the hierarchy management screen** through two routes: the Post Management widget on the People Management dashboard, or via the Data Centre widget
- **View and navigate the organisational structure** by expanding and collapsing different business units to see the full hierarchy, or using the "Expand All/Collapse All" function to display the entire structure at once
- **Search for specific business units** by name or code, with the system automatically displaying the full hierarchy path where that unit is located
- **Add new business units** to the hierarchy by selecting a parent business unit, searching for available child business units to add, and enabling them with a toggle before saving
- **Delete business units** from the hierarchy (specific deletion steps are referenced in the table of contents but not detailed in the provided text)
- **Edit existing hierarchies** to keep the organisational structure current and accurate

The guide focuses on the practical steps needed to maintain and modify how the organisation's departments and business units are structured and related to each other in the system.
ss: Organisational hierarchies in PeopleXD can be created, edited, and maintained through the Structure Setup screen in People Management. This guide covers how to expand or collapse business units, search for specific departments, add new business units to your hierarchy, and delete units that no longer have associated posts or appointments. Use this when you need to set up or modify your company's reporting structure, department levels, or management chains. You'll need the appropriate menu permissions in People Management and CorePortal to access and make changes to your organisational structure.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for maintaining organisational hierarchies within the PeopleXD system, specifically covering how to edit existing hierarchies, add new business units, and delete business units from a structure. The Structure Setup screen can be accessed through two pathways: via the Post Management widget on the People Management dashboard, or through the Data Centre widget by selecting View All and then Structure Setup, where users can click Hierarchy on the relevant row to begin maintenance. The guide details specific interface interactions including expanding and collapsing business units using arrows or the Expand All/Collapse All buttons, and using the Search function to locate specific business units by name or code, which automatically expands the hierarchy to display the complete path. Adding a business unit requires clicking the three dot menu, selecting Add, searching for the desired unit(s), enabling the Add to the Hierarchy toggle, and clicking Save, with the option to include already-linked items via a filter. Deleting a business unit involves accessing the three dot menu, selecting Delete, and confirming the action, though this operation is only possible when no active or dormant posts or appointments exist within that hierarchy, and automatically removes all hierarchy levels below the deleted unit. The document is designed for People Management system administrators and users responsible for organisational structure configuration, and references specific system menu options and web services (including Get hierarchy businessunits, Delete hierarchy businessunits, and Update hierarchy businessunits) required to access and perform these maintenance functions.

t: Managing Post Profiles
s:
# Summary: Managing Post Profiles Guide

This guide teaches users how to manage post profiles within the PeopleXD HR system. After reading it, users will be able to:

**Core Tasks:**
- Access and navigate to post profiles in the system
- Search and filter post profiles to find specific records
- View comprehensive post profile details, including organisational structure, post details, cost allocations, pension schemes, full-time equivalent (FTE) information, linked appointments, and terms and conditions
- Create new post profiles from scratch
- Edit existing post profiles while understanding what restrictions or impacts apply to current appointments and contracts
- Deactivate posts by making them dormant and reactivate them when needed

**Financial and Administrative Management:**
- Add, edit, and delete cost centre allocations to posts
- Manage pension schemes assigned to posts—including adding new schemes, ending existing ones, and deleting schemes
- Handle important date considerations when making cost allocation changes

**Staffing and Capacity:**
- Update and transfer FTE (full-time equivalent) allocations across posts
- Manage user-defined fields (custom data fields) on post profiles by adding, editing, and deleting them

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for all these post profile management functions within the People Management module of PeopleXD.
ss: Post profiles in PeopleXD form the foundation for every employee contract and appointment, storing predefined information like job title, department, and pay scale that gets inherited when creating new starters, promotions, or rehiring employees. This guide covers how to create, edit, and maintain post profile records through the Post Management widget, including managing cost centre allocations, pension schemes, and FTE (full-time equivalent) details. Open this guide when you need to set up new posts, update existing post information, make posts dormant, or manage the organizational structure and terms and conditions associated with posts. HR administrators use this process to maintain an accurate, up-to-date list of available posts that managers and recruitment teams reference during staffing and recruitment workflows.
sl: This user guide for the XD People Management system provides comprehensive instructions on creating and managing Post Profile records in PeopleXD, which serve as the foundation for all employee Post Appointments and Contracts. The document covers accessing Post Profiles through the Post Management widget on the People Management dashboard, where users can filter and view detailed Post Profile information including Organisational Structure, Post Details, Cost Allocations, Pension Schemes, FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) Maintenance, Appointments, and Terms and Conditions. The guide details specific procedures for adding new Post Profiles, editing existing ones, making posts dormant or reactivating them, with particular attention to restrictions that may impact existing Post Appointments and Contracts. It includes dedicated sections on managing Post Cost Centre Allocations (adding, editing, and deleting with date considerations), managing Post Pension Schemes (adding, ending, or deleting schemes), and maintaining FTE through update and transfer functions. The document also explains how to manage Post User Defined Fields (UDFs) by adding, editing, or deleting them, and provides instructions for viewing Post Appointments linked to profiles. This resource is primarily used by HR administrators who need to maintain an up-to-date list of available posts for creating new starters, awarding promotions, managing rehires, and supporting Staff Requests and Recruitment processes, ensuring that employee contracts inherit predefined information such as Post Title, Department, and Pay Scale.

t: Managing Salaries
s:
# Summary: Managing Salaries User Guide

This guide teaches users how to access, view, and manage employee salary records within the PeopleXD People Management HR system.

**Key topics covered include:**

- **Salary Record Fundamentals** — Understanding how salary records are created and structured. Users learn that salary records are linked to employee contracts or post appointments rather than directly to employee records, and that employees with multiple active contracts will have multiple corresponding salary records.

- **Viewing Salary Information** — How to locate and access an employee's salary data within the People Management system.

- **Understanding the Current Salary Screen** — A detailed breakdown of the salary screen interface, including how to interpret different sections such as:
  - Contract and Pay Group information
  - Current salary options and timelines
  - Allowances
  - Increment history

- **Handling Different Salary Scenarios** — How the salary screen appears and functions in various employment situations, including when contracts are appointed but not yet started, ended, future-ended, or when salary amendments are pending or future-dated.

- **Creating and Modifying Salaries** — Step-by-step instructions for creating salary amendments, including ad hoc adjustments and how to amend outstanding salary records.

- **Access Permissions** — Understanding the difference between HR access and salary access within the system.

After reading this guide, users will be able to navigate salary records, interpret salary information, and make necessary salary amendments in the system.
ss: Salary records in People Management are created and linked to employee contracts, and this guide explains how to view, understand, and amend them. It covers key salary concepts like pay scales, grades, rates, and multipliers, as well as how salary information flows from contract creation through to payment. Use this guide when you need to access an employee's current salary details, understand salary record components like the Current Salary screen, or create salary amendments for changes like pay increases or pro-rata adjustments. You'll also learn about different salary scenarios such as future-dated amendments, outstanding amendments, and how salaries display for contracts at various stages (appointed, commenced, or ended).
sl: This user guide for XD People Management provides a comprehensive overview of how employee salary records are accessed, viewed, and managed within the system, covering key concepts, terminology, and practical procedures that HR administrators need to understand. Salary records are created against an employee's Contract or Post Appointment—not independently—and become viewable on the employee's record only when the contract has been 'Commenced'; if an employee has multiple active contracts, they will have corresponding multiple salary records. The document explains the 'Current Salary' screen and its components, including fields for Contract, Pay Group, Current Salary Options, Timeline, Allowances, and Increment History, along with how the salary screen displays differently depending on various contract scenarios such as appointments not yet commenced, ended contracts, future-ended contracts, outstanding salary amendments, and future-dated amendments. Key elements of salary records include Rate Type (either Pay Scale or Personal rate structures), Pay Scale/Grade/Position Code, Point on the pay scale, Amount/Rate of Pay, Rate basis (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, or Annual), and Multiplier (typically aligned to employee FTE for pro-rata calculation). The guide details two main tasks: creating ad hoc salary amendments and amending outstanding salaries, providing step-by-step processes for these modifications. This document is designed for HR administrators who need to manage employee compensation within the People Management system and serves as a reference for understanding how salary data is structured, where to locate it, and how to make necessary salary-related changes while respecting the sensitive data access controls that apply to salary information in CoreHR.

t: New Contract
s:
# Summary of "New Contract" User Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to create and manage new contracts for existing employees in the PeopleXD People Management system. 

**What you'll learn:**

The guide covers two main scenarios for awarding new contracts:

1. **Replacement Contracts** — when an employee's current contract ends and is immediately replaced with a new one (such as during a promotion). When you create a replacement contract, all associated items tied to the old contract automatically end, including cost allocations, pension assignments, salary, deductions, allowances, and annual leave.

2. **Additional Contracts** — when an employee receives a new contract that runs alongside their existing contract(s), without ending the current one.

**What you'll be able to do:**

After reading this guide, you'll be able to:
- Navigate to an employee's record and access their contracts
- Initiate the replacement contract process
- Select which contract to replace
- Begin configuring the new contract by selecting the appropriate organizational post
- Handle specific tasks like copying allowances and pension information from old contracts to new ones
- Configure replacement contracts with correct start and end dates (whether they're for past, present, or future scenarios)
- Set up required menu options for the new contract

The guide distinguishes this process from New Hire and Rehire procedures, which are covered separately.
ss: Creating a new contract in People Management allows you to either replace an existing employee contract with a new one (such as during a promotion) or add an additional contract while keeping the current one active. The replacement contract process involves selecting the contract to replace, then completing a multi-step wizard to define the organizational structure, contract information, salary details, and optionally copying over allowances and pension assignments from the old contract. You would use this guide when you need to generate a new Contract ID or Appointment ID for an existing employee, ensuring all related items like cost allocations, deductions, and leave entitlements are properly transitioned. This is distinct from new hire or rehire processes and requires specific menu profile and pension menu options to be configured.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for awarding new contracts to existing employees in the People Management system, specifically covering two distinct scenarios: replacement contracts where a current contract is ended and replaced with a new one (such as during a promotion), and additional contracts where a new contract runs concurrently with existing contracts. The replacement contract process involves navigating through Command Centre > Employees, selecting the employee record, accessing the Contracts tab, and clicking Replace Contract, then proceeding through a multi-step wizard that includes selecting the Post in Step 1 Organisational Structure, entering contract details in Step 2 Contract Information (where the effective date cannot be earlier than the start date of the contract being replaced or its latest amendment), and configuring salary information in Step 3 Salary Information with fields such as Scale, Point on Scale, Multiplier, and Amount to be paid. The guide addresses the critical distinction that when a contract is replaced, all attached items including Cost Allocations, Pension Scheme Assignments, Salary, Deductions, Allowances, and Annual Leave are automatically ended, and it includes specialized functionality for copying allowances from the replaced appointment to maintain continuity. Additional sections detail specific features such as copying pensions and handling contracts with different authorization statuses (Auto Authorised, Auto Commenced, or Authorised Post Appointment posts), with varying requirements for post-wizard actions depending on the post type selected. This document is designed for HR administrators and People Management system users who need to process contract changes for existing employees and understand the menu options and permissions required to complete these operations.

t: New Hire contracts
s:
# Summary: New Hire Contracts User Guide

This guide teaches HR users how to set up new employees in the PeopleXD People Management system. After reading it, users will be able to:

**Main Setup Processes:**
- Set up new hires using three different post profile/appointment types: Auto-Authorised Post Profiles, Auto-Commenced Post Profiles, and Planned & Authorised Post Appointments
- Navigate the New Employee Wizard to search for and select the appropriate post for a new employee
- Check for duplicate employee records before creating a new hire entry
- Complete the authorization and commencement of appointments through the system

**Key Capabilities:**
- Search for posts using various criteria (post number, post title, or organizational hierarchy filters)
- Review posts that meet specific search criteria
- Complete the full workflow from initial setup through appointment commencement
- Copy existing new starter records to set up similar employees more efficiently

**Important Limitations:**
- The guide does not cover how to create or manage Post Profiles themselves (users are referred to a separate guide for that)
- There are restrictions on copying new starters for non-auto post types

Overall, this is a practical step-by-step manual for completing the initial onboarding process for new employees within the People Management system, covering the various pathways depending on the type of post being used.
ss: New Hire Contracts covers the process of setting up new employees in People Management, including Auto-Authorised, Auto-Commenced, and Planned & Authorised appointment types. It walks you through the New Employee Wizard workflow, which includes searching for the appropriate post profile, checking for duplicate employee records, and capturing essential personal information like name, date of birth, contact details, and address. Open this guide when you're onboarding a new hire and need step-by-step instructions for creating their employee record and contract in the system. You'll also find guidance on copying existing starter records and managing different post profile appointment scenarios.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance on setting up new hires in the People Management system, covering multiple appointment pathways including Auto-Authorised Post Profiles, Auto-Commenced Post Profiles, and Planned & Authorised Post Appointments. The document details the step-by-step New Employee Wizard process, which begins by clicking the New Starter button on the Command Centre widget and searching for the required Post Profile using either the Search Posts function (by Post Number or Post Title) or the Post Filter button (to filter by organisational hierarchy data). The Duplicate Employee Check screen helps prevent duplicate records by allowing users to search existing employees using Forename, Surname, or PPS/NI Numbers before creating a new starter record. The setup process includes completing the Person Information step, which captures mandatory employee details across multiple fields including Title, Forename, Surname, Gender, Date of Birth, Nationality, Email Address, Phone, Mobile, and address information configured by country within the CoreHR system. The guide also covers subsequent steps such as the Commence Appointment screen and processes for Non-Auto Post Profiles, which require additional authorization and planning stages through the Plan Appointment and Authorise Appointment screens. HR professionals and recruitment administrators typically use this document when onboarding new employees to ensure proper contract creation and system setup according to their organisation's post profile configuration.

t: Notice Periods
s:
# Summary: Notice Periods Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure and manage employee and employer notice periods within the PeopleXD HR system.

## What you'll learn:

**Understanding Notice Periods**
- Definition: A notice period is the length of time given to an employee before employment can be terminated, or the time an employee must give before leaving their role
- Purpose: To allow both employers and employees to plan for the end of the working relationship and minimize business disruption

**Configuration Methods**
The guide covers three main ways to set up and manage notice periods in PeopleXD:
1. Notice Period Rules Configuration
2. Terms & Conditions setup
3. Employee Record management

**System Access and Controls**
- Which menu options in PeopleXD control access to notice period functionality
- What web services are available for creating, deleting, getting, and updating notice period data
- How to configure notice period rules as new organizational defaults
- Access permissions for different user roles (view-only vs. update permissions)

**Operational Use**
- How notice periods are displayed and used during the employee leaving/leaver process
- How to maintain notice period information on individual employee records
- System configuration options, including whether notice periods display by default on the "Process as Leaver" screen

The guide is designed as a practical reference for HR administrators who need to set up, configure, and maintain notice period functionality in their PeopleXD system.
ss: Notice Periods in PeopleXD allows you to configure and manage both employee and employer notice periods based on length of service, helping to minimize business disruption when staff leave. You can set up notice period rules by company and pay scale, specifying different notice requirements (in days, weeks, months, or years) for employees at different tenure levels. This document covers how to configure these rules through the Notice Period Rules screen, assign them via Terms & Conditions or employee records, and manage them during the leaving process. Open this guide when you need to set up notice period rules, understand how notice periods display on the leaver process, or manage notice period settings for your organization.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance on configuring and managing employee and employer notice periods within the PeopleXD system, covering three main implementation approaches: Notice Period Rules Configuration, Terms & Conditions setup, and Employee Record management. The document explains that notice periods represent the length of time required for either party to terminate an employment contract, serving to minimize business disruption and allow both employers and employees to plan for workforce transitions. Configuration is controlled through specific menu options in the People Management system—including Employer Notice Period Rules (ORGANISATIONAL_CONFIGURATION_MENU.EMPLOYER_NOTICE_PERIOD_RULES) and notice period view/update functions on the Employee Dashboard—as well as five web services for creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting notice period data. The guide details how to access the Notice Period Rules screen via the Data Centre and HR Admin Setup Settings, where administrators can configure rules based on company code, pay scale, length of service in years, and notice period type (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years). A system parameter (cp_notice_period_hide) in Admin Settings allows organizations to control whether notice periods display on the Process as Leaver screen, with an option to hide this field if not required by the organization. The document is designed for HR administrators and system configurators who need to set up, maintain, and troubleshoot notice period functionality during the employee departure process.

t: Offboarding Configuration
s:
# Offboarding Configuration Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators and system configurators how to set up and configure the Employee Offboarding feature in the PeopleXD (CorePortal) HR system.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Core Setup:**
- Enable the Employee Offboarding feature in the system
- Access and navigate the Offboarding Configuration widget

**Offboarding Checklists:**
- Create and maintain offboarding checklist items with different types
- Set up which checklist items appear for different employees or circumstances
- Restrict who can see or access specific checklist items

**Custom Content:**
- Add custom pages to the offboarding process with different page types
- Control access to custom pages through restrictions

**Required Documentation:**
- Configure policy documents and handbooks to be reviewed during offboarding
- Set up which documents employees must return or provide

**Reporting & Visibility:**
- Configure the Employee Offboarding dashboard (landing page) that employees and managers use
- Set up staff grouping and criteria groups for organizing offboarding tasks

**User Permissions:**
- Manage user access levels for three main user types (administrators, managers, and employees)
- Configure security profiles and web service modules to control who can perform what actions

The guide is designed for system administrators and HR configuration staff, and complements a separate user guide that covers how end users interact with the offboarding system.
ss: XD Offboarding on CorePortal allows HR administrators to configure the entire employee departure process, including checklists, custom pages, policy documents, and dashboard settings. Use this guide when setting up offboarding for the first time, creating task checklists triggered by employee leave dates, or establishing different offboarding workflows for various staff groups and organizational criteria. The document covers enabling the offboarding feature, defining checklist items and custom pages, managing user access for employees and managers, and configuring the offboarding dashboard. Open this if you need to configure which tasks, documents, and pages appear for departing employees in your CorePortal system.
sl: This document is a configuration user guide for the Employee Offboarding feature on CorePortal, providing step-by-step instructions for system administrators and HR personnel to set up and customize all offboarding workflows and processes. The guide covers enabling the Social Hub Configuration widget through the People Management Dashboard by searching for "social" in the available Tab Widgets section and selecting it to appear on designated dashboard tabs such as the Data Centre tab. To activate Employee Offboarding, users navigate to the Social Hub Configuration widget, click the View button adjacent to the Activate label, and click the Enable button on the Offboarding section, after which they must enter a mandatory Leave Date that determines which employees with that leave date or later are assigned to applicable offboarding checklists. The document details configuration of multiple offboarding components including Offboarding Checklists (where checklist items can be assigned X days before an employee's Date Left and restricted by criteria groups for different organizational segments), Custom Pages with various page types, Policy Documents and Handbooks, and Documents Requested sections. It also addresses the Employee Offboarding Dashboard landing page configuration, Staff Grouping through criteria group creation, and User Access management through three default security menu profiles: Offboard_Admin, Offboard_MGR, and Offboard_EMP, along with associated web service modules. This configuration guide is designed for HR administrators, managers, and system integrators who need to customize the offboarding experience before end users access the feature through the companion "How to Use" user guide.

t: Onboarding
s:
# PeopleXD Onboarding Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the PeopleXD HR system's onboarding module to manage and complete new employee onboarding processes.

**Key areas covered include:**

**Onboarding Basics**
- The distinction between employee onboarding (for new hires) and cross-boarding (for internal moves)
- How to access and navigate the Social Hub Dashboard, which serves as the central hub for onboarding activities

**Social Hub Dashboard Features**
- The information header that displays key employee details
- Checklists that track onboarding tasks, including what's outstanding and what's been completed
- Different onboarding scenarios and rules for checklist items
- Social activity features for team interaction
- Content pages for sharing information

**Available Pages and Content Types**
- System pages including New Starters listings, team area management, employee directory, quizzes, events, and FAQs
- Custom content pages that can include text, videos, maps, links, and images

**Notifications and Progress Tracking**
- How to receive and manage notification emails (weekly and daily summaries)
- Monitoring employee onboarding progress through the system

Overall, this guide enables HR professionals and managers to set up comprehensive onboarding workflows, track new employee progress through structured checklists, communicate information effectively, and ensure all onboarding tasks are completed systematically.
ss: The XD Onboarding platform in People Management supports guided onboarding for new joiners and existing employees moving to new roles, teams, or contracts. It uses the Social Hub dashboard to organize onboarding tasks through configurable checklists, pages (including New Starters, Employee Directory, and quizzes), and notifications to track employee progress. Open this guide if you need to understand how to use onboarding checklists, navigate the Social Hub dashboard, or monitor new starter and cross-boarding progress as a manager or HR administrator. The guide explains the difference between new starter onboarding and cross-boarding, plus how to access and complete onboarding tasks before or after an employee's start date.
sl: This user guide provides a comprehensive overview of the Employee Onboarding functionality within People Management, covering both new starter onboarding and cross-boarding processes for existing employees. The document explains how to access and navigate the Social Hub Dashboard, which serves as the central hub for onboarding activities, including an Information Header, Checklists section with Tasks Outstanding Lists and Completed Items, Social Activity features, and Content Pages. The guide details various system pages available within onboarding such as New Starters, My Team Area, Employee Directory, Quiz, Events, and FAQ, as well as custom pages that can display Text, Video, Map, Link, and Image content. It describes the checklist functionality in detail, including how to manage checklist items, understand onboarding scenarios, and work with item restrictions and considerations that affect task completion. The document also covers notification systems through Weekly and Daily Summary Emails, methods for tracking employee onboarding progress as a manager or HR administrator, and procedures for importing pre-V27 onboarding checklists during system upgrades. This guide is intended for employees, managers, and HR administrators who need to understand how to use the onboarding platform, though it explicitly notes that configuration setup guidance is covered in a separate Employee Onboarding v28 configuration user guide.

ss: PeopleXD Onboarding Configuration covers the setup and customization of employee onboarding workflows within the PeopleXD system, including enabling the onboarding feature, creating and managing checklists with various item types, and building custom pages with content like links, videos, maps, and images. It also explains how to configure system pages such as employee directory, quizzes, events, and FAQs, as well as set up team-specific onboarding content. sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for configuring the Employee Onboarding feature within PeopleXD, Access Group's onboarding system, detailing how to set up and manage all aspects of the onboarding process. t: Organisational Role Delegation
s:
# Summary: Organisational Role Delegation Guide

This guide teaches managers how to use the Organisational Role Delegation feature in the PeopleXD HR system to temporarily reassign their managerial responsibilities to colleagues.

**What you'll learn:**

- **Understanding delegation**: What organisational role (org role) delegation is and why it's useful — primarily for covering periods when a manager is unavailable (such as during leave or absence)

- **Eligibility and permissions**: Who is allowed to delegate roles, who can receive delegated roles, and which roles can and cannot be delegated (HR determines which roles are eligible for delegation)

- **What delegated managers can access**: What visibility and permissions a colleague receives when a role is delegated to them

- **How to delegate**: Step-by-step instructions for using the Delegation widget on the Manager Dashboard to:
  - Delegate an org role to a colleague
  - Choose which roles to delegate, to whom, and for how long
  - Update or delete existing delegations
  - Search for and report on delegations already in place

- **System configuration**: How HR administrators can set up the delegation feature, including which org roles should be available for delegation, configuring the widget and dashboard, and managing user access permissions

- **Important considerations**: Key points managers and administrators need to know about how the delegation process works and what happens when roles are delegated
ss: Organisational Role Delegation in PeopleXD allows managers to temporarily reassign their approval responsibilities to colleagues through the Manager Dashboard, covering periods when they're unavailable such as during leave. Managers control which org roles get delegated, to whom, for how long, and the reason, while HR determines which roles are eligible for delegation—for example, annual leave approvals but not salary approvals. Open this document if you need to delegate manager responsibilities to a colleague, configure which roles can be delegated in your system, or understand what visibility and access a delegated manager receives during the delegation period. This guide covers the delegation process, configuration setup, and important considerations like when delegation isn't suitable (such as permanent role changes).
sl: This user guide from Access Group explains how managers can use the Delegation widget on the Manager Dashboard within XD People Management to temporarily reassign their organisational role (org role) responsibilities to colleague managers during periods of unavailability such as leave. The document covers who is eligible to delegate roles (managers only), who can receive delegated roles (other managers with the same defined org role, typically set through the "reports to manager" relationship), and which org roles HR can configure as delegable through the flagging process described in section 3.1. The guide walks users through the complete delegation workflow including locating the Delegation widget, executing delegations via section 2.2, updating existing delegations in section 2.4, and deleting delegations in section 2.5, while also explaining how delegated managers are automatically assigned roles in People Management and receive outstanding approvals in the Notification Centre. Importantly, the document clarifies that delegation is a temporary solution unsuitable for permanent role changes such as employee departures or internal role transfers, which instead require manual HR reassignment or Manager Rollup processing. The guide also addresses configuration requirements in section 3, including setting org role delegation parameters, configuring the delegation widget and dashboard display, and managing user access permissions for both managers using the delegation feature and delegated users receiving temporary role assignments. This document is primarily used by HR administrators and managers who need to understand the system's delegation capabilities, configure which org roles support delegation, and manage temporary approval responsibilities.

t: Organisational Roles Configuration
s:
# Summary of "Organisational Roles Configuration" Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage organisational roles in the PeopleXD HR system.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Configuration Skills:**
- How to create new organisational role types and edit existing ones
- How to deactivate organisational roles when they're no longer needed
- How to assign organisational roles to individual employees

**Understanding Organisational Roles:**
The guide explains that organisational roles are used to identify employees with specific responsibilities in the organisation. These roles enable employees to:
- Receive alerts and notifications relevant to their position
- Complete approvals for various processes (such as salary approvals)
- Receive and update work tasks

The system comes with three default roles (HR Salary Approver, Payroll Salary Approver, and Reports To), but is highly customizable so you can create additional roles tailored to your organisation's needs.

**Where Roles Are Used:**
The guide also provides an overview of different areas throughout PeopleXD where organisational roles are applied in practice — for example, sending notifications to specific role holders like IT Managers for new starters, or controlling which employee records managers can see in their team views.

Importantly, employees can hold multiple organisational roles simultaneously to allow them to engage in a variety of different tasks and responsibilities across the system.
ss: Organisational Roles in PeopleXD identify employees with specific managerial or approval responsibilities, such as HR Salary Approvers or IT Managers, enabling them to receive alerts, complete approvals, and manage tasks across the system. This guide covers how to create and edit org role types in the Reference Data section, assign roles to individual employees, and configure advanced options like delegation and manager rollup. Open this document when you need to set up new approval roles, assign existing roles to staff members, or understand how org roles control access to features like the Manager Dashboard and salary approval workflows.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and managing Organisational Roles within the PeopleXD People Management system, covering both the creation of role types and their assignment to employees. Organisational Roles are used to identify employees with specific managerial or approval responsibilities, with default roles including HR Salary Approver, Payroll Salary Approver, and Reports To, though the system is highly configurable to support custom roles tailored to organisational needs. To configure Org Role Types, users navigate to the People Management dashboard, select the Data Centre tab, click Reference Data, and search for Organisational Role Types to access the Maintain Organisational Role Types screen, where they define roles using fields such as Role Type (maximum 6 alphanumeric characters), Description (maximum 40 characters), and an Active toggle to enable role availability. Creating new Org Roles involves clicking Add on the Maintain Organisational Role Types screen, entering required details including the Role Type and Description, enabling the Active field, and clicking Save, while existing roles can be edited or deactivated as needed. Assigned Org Roles enable employees to receive alerts and notifications, complete approvals, and receive and update tasks, with the system supporting multiple role assignments per employee through screens such as Assign Access and Maintain Organisational Roles by Person. The document also references advanced configuration options including Delegation, Manager Rollup +1, and Menu Profile Matrix, which are covered in separate user guides, as well as feature-specific implementations where Org Roles control access and task workflows such as sending notifications to IT Managers or approving expense items. This guide is primarily used by system administrators and People Management professionals responsible for establishing organisational role structures and assigning them to employees within their organisations.

t: Organisational Structure Configuration
s:
# Summary: Organisational Structure Configuration Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage an organisational structure within the PeopleXD HR system. Here's what you'll learn to do:

## Core Setup Tasks
- **Access and create** organisational structures from the correct location in the system
- **Build the structure framework** by adding levels that define how your organisation is hierarchically arranged
- **Configure structure settings** including hierarchy indicators, initial values, hide indicators, and display modes
- **Activate** your completed organisational structure to make it operational

## Managing Existing Structures
- **Edit existing structures** by adding, removing, or reordering levels as your organisation evolves

## Reference Data Configuration
The guide covers how to define and configure the standard organisational components that form the building blocks of your structure:
- Company, Division, Management Unit, Department, Work Group, Cost Centre, and Location
- Custom User Fields (1–5) for organisation-specific needs

## Hierarchy Setup and Maintenance
- **Create and link hierarchies** that show reporting lines and organisational relationships
- **Build hierarchies** by adding a company/initial level and then adding subsequent levels beneath it
- **Manage hierarchy elements** including removing levels and handling shared hierarchy elements (where entities can belong to multiple parts of the structure)

## Display and Customisation
- **Control how the hierarchy displays** by setting default collapse/expand preferences and other display options

Overall, this guide enables HR administrators to design a complete organisational structure that accurately reflects their company's layout and reporting relationships within the PeopleXD system.
ss: Organisational Structure configuration in CoreHR lets you set up and manage your company's hierarchical framework, including levels like Company, Division, Management Unit, Department, and Work Group. This guide walks you through creating new structures from scratch, editing existing ones, defining reference data items, and linking them to your organisational hierarchy. Open this document when you need to establish how your organisation is structured in the system, add or remove hierarchy levels, or configure how the hierarchy displays and functions. You'll access these settings through CoreHR's back-office application under CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring and managing organisational structures and hierarchies within the CoreHR back-office application, specifically for people management purposes. The document covers the complete lifecycle of organisational structure management, including creating new structures from scratch, editing existing ones, and maintaining the associated reference data and hierarchies. To access the organisational structure configuration, users navigate to CorePersonnel > Maintenance > Post Management and select Organisational Hierarchy, which opens the Maintain Hierarchy Structure screen where all existing structures are listed and can be filtered by Structure Code. The creation process involves multiple defined steps: creating the structure itself, adding levels to it, defining reference data items, and configuring settings such as hierarchy indicators, initial values, hide indicators, and display modes before activating the structure. For existing structures, the guide explains how to add new levels, remove levels, or reorder levels as organisational needs change. The reference data configuration section details eight specific data types used within organisational structures—Company, Division, Management Unit, Department, Work Group, Cost Centre, Location, and User Fields 1-5—each with their own configuration guidance. The document also covers hierarchy linking and maintenance, including how to create hierarchies, add companies or initial levels, add subsequent levels, remove levels, and manage shared hierarchy elements. Additional configuration options such as default collapse/expand settings for hierarchy display are included, along with menu navigation paths for accessing various organisational components. This guide is designed for system administrators and configuration specialists responsible for setting up and maintaining organisational structures in CoreHR implementations.

s:
# Payroll Instructional Forms Guide — Summary

This guide teaches HR users how to use the Payroll Instructional Forms feature in the PeopleXD system to communicate pay-affecting employee information directly to the Payroll team.

## What You'll Learn to Do:

**Core Skills:**
- Create custom payroll instruction forms tailored to your organization's needs
- Add new HR task list items designated as Payroll Instructional Forms
- Assign these tasks to specific organizational roles
- View and action tasks through the Pay Portal
- Generate reports on payroll instructional forms

**System Navigation:**
- Access and use the Pay Portal interface
- Locate and complete HR form tasks
- Review the history of instructional forms that have been submitted

**Form Configuration (for administrators):**
- Build custom forms from scratch
- Organize forms into logical sections
- Add individual fields to forms
- Control who can access specific forms
- Designate task owners responsible for completing forms

## What Payroll Instructional Forms Cover:

The guide explains that these forms are used to communicate various pay-affecting changes including: holiday balance adjustments, student loan deductions, tax code changes, overtime hours, bonuses and ad-hoc payments, pension changes, pay awards, employee joiners/movers/leavers, cost allocation changes, and manual payment adjustments.

Essentially, this is a guide for setting up and using an automated communication system between HR and Payroll to ensure employee pay records are updated accurately with all relevant information.
ss: Payroll Instructional Forms in People Management enable HR to capture and automatically communicate pay-affecting information directly to Payroll for joiner, mover, and leaver processes—such as holiday balances, student loans, tax code changes, bonuses, and pension updates. This guide covers how to complete forms via the HR Task List, access them through Pay Portal, and configure custom forms with specific fields and access restrictions for different organizational roles. Open this document when you need to submit payroll instructions as part of employee lifecycle events or when setting up new payroll communication workflows in your system.
sl: This user guide for XD People Management explains how to use Payroll Instructional Forms to capture and automatically share pay-affecting information from HR to the Payroll team during joiner, mover, and leaver processes. The document covers the complete workflow including how to create custom forms, add them as HR Task List items, restrict form access, nominate task owners, and confirm tasks on the Payroll Dashboard. Users access Payroll Instructional Forms through the People Management Dashboard by navigating to the Command Centre widget, selecting Outstanding Processes, and choosing the appropriate employee tab (such as Leavers) to start the form and enter relevant payroll information. The forms communicate critical pay-affecting details such as holiday balance adjustments, student loan payments, PAYE/tax code changes, overtime hours, ad hoc payments, pension changes, pay awards, and cost allocation modifications. Once completed in the HR Task List, these forms become visible in Pay Portal where Payroll Administrators can review them and make necessary adjustments using the Time Sheet Adjustment screen before processing employee payroll records. Configuration of custom forms involves creating the form structure, adding sections and fields, and establishing access controls and task ownership to ensure proper routing to designated payroll personnel. This guide is primarily used by HR professionals and payroll administrators who need to systematize communication of pay-related changes within the People Management system.

t: Payscale Configuration
s:
# Payscale Configuration Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to configure and manage pay scales in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What pay scales are**: Pay scales (also called grades or positions) determine employee pay based on factors like job role, experience, length of service, and responsibility level.

- **The three components of a pay scale system**:
  - Pay Scales (the grade or position level an employee is assigned to)
  - Pay Scale Points (the different levels or steps within a pay scale)
  - Pay Scale Rates (the actual pay amount for each point on a scale)

**What you'll be able to do:**

- Navigate to where pay scales are configured in PeopleXD (under People Management > Payroll)
- Create and maintain pay scales
- Create and maintain pay scale points
- View and maintain pay scale rates (the actual pay values)
- Set up and manage pay scale restrictions (rules that control which combinations of scales, points, and rates are allowed)
- Turn pay scale restrictions on or off
- Understand user access permissions for pay scale configuration

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for each of these tasks, allowing HR administrators to set up a complete pay scale structure in the system.
ss: PeopleXD pay scales define employee compensation by combining a pay grade, scale point, and associated pay rate—typically organized by job role, experience, and responsibility level. This guide walks you through setting up and maintaining pay scales in both the People Management and Payroll modules, including how to configure scale points, rates, and restriction rules. Open this document if you need to create new pay grades, adjust pay scale points and rates, or establish pay scale restrictions for your organization. HR and Payroll administrators use this guide when implementing or updating compensation structures in PeopleXD.
sl: This document is a user guide for configuring pay scales within the PeopleXD system, specifically designed to help HR and Payroll administrators set up and manage employee compensation structures. The guide explains that pay scales consist of three interconnected components—the pay scale itself (also called grade or position), pay scale points (the levels available within a scale), and pay scale rates (the actual pay amount for each point)—which together determine an employee's compensation based on factors such as job role, experience, and responsibility. Pay scales can be configured through two different dashboards depending on organizational setup: in People Management by navigating to the Data Centre tab and selecting Reference Data, or in Payroll by accessing the Settings tab and using options such as Position Reference, Scale Point Profile, and Add Position Rates. The configuration process involves creating pay scales by clicking Add on the appropriate screen and filling in required fields including Code, Description, currency selection, minimum and maximum Nett Pay thresholds, position group assignments, allowance codes, and annual leave entitlement levels, with the system flagging employees who fall outside defined pay ranges through gross-to-nett exception messages. The document also covers pay scale restrictions, which can be configured and activated to control how pay scales are applied, including steps to edit and deactivate restriction rules. This guide is essential for HR and Payroll administrators who need to establish or modify compensation structures, and it particularly addresses the distinction between standard pay scales and personal rates assigned directly to individual employee records.

t: Pension by Appointment
s:
# Summary: Pension by Appointment User Guide

This guide teaches HR users how to manage employee pension schemes using the "Pension by Appointment" approach in the PeopleXD CoreHR system — a method where pension schemes are linked to individual employee contracts rather than to employee records themselves.

The guide covers the following practical tasks:

**Setting up pension schemes:**
- How to add pension schemes to post profile records (job positions)
- How to end or delete post pension schemes

**Managing assignments:**
- How to assign a pension scheme to an employee's contract
- How to amend or change an existing pension scheme assignment
- How to end a pension scheme assignment (either when a contract ends or independently)
- How to delete a pension scheme assignment

**Key concept explained:**
The guide distinguishes between two different pension management approaches available in the system. "Pension by Appointment" allows organizations to assign different pension schemes to different contracts held by the same employee, and these assignments are independent of whether an employee changes or adds contracts. This contrasts with "Pension by Person," where pension is managed at the employee level in Payroll and is unaffected by contract changes.

The guide also notes the payslip impact of using the Pension by Appointment option, though specific details on this impact are not included in the extracted text provided.
ss: The Pension by Appointment feature in CoreHR allows organizations to assign pension schemes directly to employee contracts rather than at the person level. This guide covers how to link pension schemes to post profiles, assign them to employee contracts, amend existing assignments, and end assignments when contracts end. Use this document if your organization manages pension administration by contract appointment and you need step-by-step instructions for setting up or modifying pension scheme assignments in People Management. Open this guide when you need to understand how contract-level pension changes differ from person-level pension management or when troubleshooting pension scheme visibility and assignment issues.
sl: This user guide provides detailed instructions for managing pension schemes in CoreHR's People Management module when organizations use the "Pension by Appointment" configuration, which assigns pension schemes at the contract level rather than at the person level. The document covers the complete workflow for pension scheme management, including linking schemes to Post Profile records via Post Profile Maintenance (option 11 in the Select Option list), assigning schemes to individual employee contracts, amending existing assignments, and ending or deleting assignments when contracts end. A key distinction explained is that Pension by Appointment allows different pension schemes to be assigned to different contracts for the same employee, with automatic termination of pension scheme assignments when a contract ends, unlike the alternative "Pension by Person" approach which manages pensions independently of contracts through Payroll. The guide walks users through specific tasks such as adding a Post Pension Scheme by looking up the scheme code and setting a Start Date via the Pension Schemes window, ending schemes by entering an End Date, and deleting schemes using the delete button. This document is intended for HR administrators and People Management users responsible for contract-level pension administration who need to understand how pension scheme assignments interact with employee contracts and post profiles in the CoreHR system.

s:
# Summary of Personnel Number Generation Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure the PeopleXD CoreHR system to manage how employee personnel numbers are created or assigned when setting up new employees.

## What You'll Learn

**Two Personnel Number Generation Options:**

1. **Automatic Generation** — The system automatically creates a personnel number for each new hire based on configurable rules. Numbers can be customized to match your organization's requirements, including adding prefixes, suffixes, and controlling the number length.

2. **Manual Generation** — Personnel numbers must be manually entered into the system for each new hire, with no automatic format validation.

The system can be configured to use either option exclusively, or both options can be active simultaneously, allowing users to choose which method to use when creating each new employee record.

## Configuration Steps

The guide walks through:
- Where to access personnel number configuration settings in the system (via the Data Centre widget and HR Admin Setup)
- How to define and activate generation rules for automatic numbering
- How to set the system parameter to either automatic or manual mode
- How to use the Create New Employee Wizard with your chosen method
- Additional technical considerations including valid format indicators and modulus generation routines

By following this guide, users will be able to set up personnel number generation according to their organization's employee numbering policies and requirements.
ss: Personnel Number Generation in CoreHR allows you to configure how employee numbers are created when new hires are set up in the system. You can choose between automatic generation (where the system assigns numbers based on customizable rules with prefixes, suffixes, and length requirements) or manual entry (where HR staff enter numbers directly). Open this guide when you need to set up or modify employee numbering rules, access the Personnel Numbering Maintenance screen in HR Admin Setup, or decide whether your organization should use automated or manual number assignment. The guide covers how to define format rules, activate them, and configure the system parameter to match your organization's employee numbering requirements.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring personnel number generation in CoreHR within the People Management module, specifically addressing how organizations can automate or manually manage the creation of employee numbers during new hire setup. The document outlines two primary configuration options: Default Automatic, which automatically generates employee numbers according to organizational format requirements using a defined prefix, suffix, and length; and Default Manual, which requires manual entry of personnel numbers with no format validation applied. To access and configure these settings, users navigate through the Data Centre widget to HR Admin Setup Settings and search for Personnel Numbering Maintenance, which displays two default rows for both automatic and manual options. For automatic generation configuration, administrators define rules on the right-hand side of the Personnel Numbering Maintenance screen by specifying parameters including Prefix (up to 4 alphanumeric characters), Length (the numeric portion between prefix and suffix), Start Range, End Range, Last Number (which can be manually overridden to control the next generated number), and Suffix (up to 4 alphanumeric characters), with a total character limit of 10 characters across all components. The configuration process involves three sequential steps: defining the rule with the desired format parameters, activating the rule by selecting the Active checkbox and clicking Save, and setting the system parameter to either Automatic or Manual mode depending on organizational preference. This document is primarily used by HR administrators and system configurators who need to establish personnel numbering conventions in CoreHR during initial implementation or when modifying existing number generation rules to match changing organizational requirements.

t: Post Restructuring
s:
# Post Restructuring Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Post Restructuring functionality in PeopleXD to reorganise the company's structure—either consolidating business units or creating new ones.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**What a Restructuring Profile is:** A container holding all details needed for an organisational move, including the old and new post structure, effective date, and affected employees. Multiple profiles can be created and edited until processed, after which they're locked.

**The complete post-restructuring process**, which involves 12 sequential steps:

1. Remove any confirmed future appointments and outstanding salary approvals that would interfere with the restructuring
2. Add new reference data (new departments, sections, or posts) to the system
3. Link new reference data items to the organisational hierarchy tree
4. Grant system users access to any newly created departments
5. Create the required restructuring profile(s)—one profile per unique employee movement
6. View affected employees and run validation checks
7. Identify and fix any errors found during validation
8. Generate a report showing the changes
9. Process the transfer to apply changes
10. Request PeopleXD to synchronise system tables
11. Run the report again and save it locally
12. Perform spot checks on employees to verify the restructuring worked correctly

**Important constraints:** Users learn that restructuring only updates the post hierarchy (department, section, etc.), creates a new sequence in the appointment record without changing the employee ID, doesn't affect salary or allowances, must be tested on UAT before running on Live, and only processes the most recent active appointment.
ss: Post Restructuring in PeopleXD allows you to change your organisation's structure by moving employees between departments, sections, or business units through the creation of Restructure Profiles. This functionality updates employee appointments with new post hierarchies while preserving their salary and allowances, and requires careful preparation including removal of future appointments, addition of new reference data, and hierarchy linking before validation and processing. Use this guide when you need to regroup existing business units, create additional business units, or make large-scale organisational changes, and follow the step-by-step procedure to validate movements, fix errors, process transfers, and perform post-restructure spot checks. The process must be tested on UAT and signed off before running on your Live system.
sl: This user guide explains how to use the Post Restructuring functionality in PeopleXD People Management to modify an organization's structure by regrouping business units or creating additional units, with the process controlled through the POST MANAGEMENT MENU-POST RESTRUCTURING option in CorePersonnel. A Restructuring Profile contains the details for organizational movements including old and new post structures, effective dates, and affected employees, and multiple profiles can be created for different movements (for example, one profile if an entire section moves together, or two profiles if the section splits between different departments). The document provides a twelve-step procedure beginning with removing any Confirmed Future appointments and outstanding Salary Approvals, followed by adding new reference data (such as Departments), linking new hierarchy items to the Hierarchy Tree, ensuring system users have access to new departments, and creating Restructure Profiles that establish the rules for validation. Users must run validation checks on affected employees, fix any errors (typically caused by missing hierarchy links), generate reports, process the transfer, and contact PeopleXD to synchronize tables to complete the restructure. The guide emphasizes critical prerequisites including conducting the restructure on UAT and obtaining sign-off before running on Live, noting that Post Restructuring updates employee appointments with new post hierarchies while preserving salary and allowances, and that spot checks should be performed after processing to confirm no changes to pay rates or allowances. This document is primarily used by back office users and system administrators responsible for managing organizational restructuring in the PeopleXD system.

t: Probation Dates
s:
# Summary: Probation Dates User Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to manage and record probation information for employees in the PeopleXD HR system (CoreHR). 

**Key learning outcomes:**

After reading this guide, users will understand how to:

- **Record probation expiry dates** — the planned end date of an employee's probation period (e.g., 6 months after hire)
- **Capture probation review dates** — track up to two review points during the probation period
- **Document probation extensions** — record when probation periods are extended

**Two methods are covered:**

1. **Direct input** — HR administrators can manually enter probation details directly onto an employee's contract record
2. **Automated setup via Terms and Conditions Profiles** — administrators can create standard probation periods (e.g., 6 months) that automatically calculate the expiry date based on the contract start date and can be reused across multiple posts and contracts

**Important context:**

The guide explains that probation information is stored at the contract level (not the employee/person level), meaning different probation periods can be recorded for different contracts an employee may hold, such as initial hiring contracts, promotion contracts, or rehire contracts.
ss: Probation Dates in CoreHR allows you to record and manage employee probation expiry dates, review dates, and extensions at the contract level for new hires, promotions, and rehires. You can enter probation details directly on an employee's contract record or use Terms and Conditions Profiles to automatically calculate expiry dates based on a default probation period. Open this guide when you need to set up probation timelines for a new employee, track probation review points, record a probation extension, or configure default probation periods across multiple contracts using Terms and Conditions templates.
sl: This document is a user guide for the People Management system that explains how to manage and assign probation dates and related details to employee contracts in CoreHR. The guide covers two main processes: directly updating probation details on individual contracts through the Command Centre > Employee screen and the Probation Details tab, and automatically calculating probation expiry dates using Terms and Conditions Profiles linked to Post Profiles. When using the direct update method, HR administrators can populate several fields including Probation Expiry Date, Review Date 1, Review Date 2, Probation Extension Date, Extension Reason, and Extension Completion Date, all of which are optional and can be entered via calendar or in dd/mm/yyyy format. For the Terms and Conditions approach, administrators navigate to Data Centre, access Terms and Conditions Setup, and configure a Probation Period Type (Days, Months, or Years) and corresponding number, which the system then uses alongside the contract start date to automatically calculate the expiration date—for example, a 6-month probation period starting 1st January 2017 would automatically calculate to 30th June 2017. The document emphasizes that probation details are captured at the contract level rather than the person level, allowing organizations to track probation for various contract types including initial new hire, promoted, additional, and rehire contracts. This guide is intended for HR administrators responsible for setting up and maintaining employee probation information in the People Management system.
