t: Rehires
s:
# Rehires Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators how to rehire former employees who are no longer active in the PeopleXD system. Here's what you'll learn:

## Key Capabilities

**Understanding Rehires:**
- You can only rehire employees whose previous employment was already recorded in the system and who are currently marked as "dormant" (inactive)
- When you rehire someone, their existing HR record is reactivated rather than creating a new one
- Their personal information can be updated to reflect any changes since they last worked
- Once rehired and their contract is commenced, they become available to payroll with a new salary

## Step-by-Step Process

The guide walks through the complete **4-step Rehire Person Wizard**:

1. **Person Info** — Review and update the employee's personal details, which may have changed since their previous employment

2. **Organisational Structure** — Select the post (job position) for the new contract, with options for auto-authorised posts or authorised appointments with sequence numbers

3. **Contract Information** — Set up contract details with restrictions (such as the effective date cannot be earlier than their previous leave date)

4. **Commencement** — Finalize and commence the appointment

## Additional Topics

The guide also covers how to identify potential rehires through duplicate employee checks and validation rules for pay group assignments.
ss: The rehire process in People Management allows HR administrators to reactivate dormant employee records and set up new contracts for previously employed staff. You'll use the 4-step Rehire Person Wizard to update personal details, select an organizational post, enter contract information, and configure salary details—with some fields automatically populated based on the post selected. Open this guide when you need to bring back a former employee whose previous employment was recorded in CoreHR, or when you need step-by-step instructions for commencing appointments and validating pay group assignments during rehiring.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for rehiring dormant employees within the CoreHR People Management system, covering the complete rehire process from employee search through contract commencement. The document explains that employees must exist on CoreHR in a dormant status to be rehired, and walks through the four-step Rehire Person Wizard accessed via the Actions button on an employee record after searching by Social Security Number (PPS or NI Number) for accuracy. Step 1 prompts administrators to review and update personal details that may have changed since the employee's last period of employment, Step 2 requires selecting an appropriate Post from the dropdown list based on HR access permissions and optionally choosing a Sequence number for Authorised Post Appointments, and Step 3 involves setting the Effective Date (which cannot be earlier than the previous Leave Date) and completing mandatory contract fields that may auto-populate based on the Post selection. Step 4 captures salary information including Scale, Point on Scale, Multiplier, and payment amount, with the employee's previous pay group being retained unless changed in Payroll. The guide distinguishes between Auto Commenced Posts, which automatically commence upon wizard completion, and Auto Authorised or Authorised Post Appointments, which require a separate manual commencement step to make the employee and contract available to the payroll team. Additionally, the document covers rehire validation processes including duplicate employee checks and pay group validation, while noting that rehired employees will maintain a complete employment history reflecting all periods of service with the organisation.

t: Salary Approval Configuration
s:
# Summary: Salary Approval Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to set up and manage salary approval processes in the PeopleXD CorePortal system. After reading it, users will understand how to configure two different types of salary approval workflows:

**Standard Salary Approvals** — This approach involves setting up organizational role types and assigning them to employees. Users will learn how to define approval roles (such as managers or supervisors), establish approval groups, determine the sequence in which approvals must occur, and assign these roles to specific employees within the organization. The guide covers role naming conventions, active/inactive status management, and how to grant access to both salary approvers and system administrators.

**Workflow-Based Salary Approvals** — This is a more flexible approach using custom workflow processes. Users will learn why workflow-based approvals are needed, how to configure workflow processes, how to link organizational role types to workflows, and how to assign employee groups to specific approval workflows. This section also covers how to exclude certain employee groups from particular workflows when needed.

**Additional Coverage** — The guide includes information about user access and menu permissions for both salary approvers and administrators, as well as upgrade considerations for organizations transitioning from existing configurations or managing legacy contact types.

In essence, this guide enables HR administrators to establish and manage the rules and processes that determine how salary changes and approvals flow through their organization in the CorePortal system.
ss: Salary Approval Configuration in CorePortal allows you to set up and manage two distinct approval types: Standard Salary Approvals and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals. This guide covers how to enable the approval process through system parameters, define organisational roles (such as HR Salary Approver and Payroll Salary Approver), assign approval sequences, and control user access to the salary approval functions. Open this document if you need to configure which managers approve salary records before they reach Payroll, set up approval hierarchies by department or pay group, or manage who has access to the salary approver menu in CoreHR.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for configuring salary approval processes within the CoreHR system, specifically focusing on implementation in CorePortal rather than the CoreHR back office. It covers two distinct salary approval approaches: Standard Salary Approvals and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals, though only one can be active at a time on the system. For Standard Salary Approvals, administrators must first enable the "Use HR Salary Approval Process" parameter through the Data Centre widget and HR Admin Setup Settings, then configure the "HR Salary Approval Type" and "Payroll Salary Approval Type" parameters to specify organizational levels such as Department or Pay Group where approvals will be routed. The guide explains how to set up Organisational Role Types (such as HR Salary Approver and Payroll Salary Approver) through the Reference Data screen, including the option to create custom roles or multiple approval tiers. For Workflow-Based Salary Approvals, the document describes how to configure workflow processes and assign or exclude employee groups to those workflows. The document is intended for system administrators responsible for configuring salary approval workflows and for salary approvers who need menu access guidance, addressing configuration scenarios that help resolve salary routing and approval assignment challenges in the people management system.

t: Salary Approvals
s:
# Salary Approvals Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Salary Approvals feature in the PeopleXD HR system (CoreHR). After reading it, you will understand:

**What Salary Approvals Are:**
- A control mechanism that requires all new salary and allowance records to go through a formal approval process before they can be used by the Payroll system
- Salary records move through different approval statuses: "Pending" (initial state, not available to payroll), "In Approval" (approved by some but not all approvers, still not available to payroll), and "Approved" or "Future" (fully approved and ready for payroll processing)

**Two Approval Methods:**
The system offers two different approaches to managing salary approvals—Standard Salary Approvals and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals.

**How to Navigate and Use the System:**
- Understanding the Salary Approvals screen and its different views (your pending approvals, all outstanding items, rejected items, and historical approval records)
- Viewing the salary request details and employee information
- How to approve or reject outstanding salary and allowance requests
- How different payroll scenarios and employee payroll setup configurations affect approvals
- How to track approval status on the Current Salary screen
- How to delete pending salary records when needed

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for managers and administrators who need to review, approve, or manage salary and allowance changes within the system.
ss: The Salary Approvals feature in CoreHR controls how new salary and allowance records are created and managed by requiring them to pass through multiple levels of approval before becoming available to Payroll for processing. Salaries move through statuses of "Pending," "In Approval," "Approved," or "Rejected" depending on where they are in the approval workflow. This guide covers two configuration options: Standard Salary Approvals (typically a 2-level HR and Payroll approval structure) and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals (a customizable process). Open this document if you need to understand how to review, approve, or reject salary amendments in CoreHR's XD Portal, or if you're responsible for managing salary approvals at any level in your organization.
sl: This user guide for CoreHR's Salary Approvals feature provides a comprehensive overview of how salary and allowance records are created, reviewed, and managed through a controlled approval process. The document covers two distinct configuration options: Standard Salary Approvals, which typically uses a two-level approval structure with HR approval (often at department level) followed by Payroll approval (typically at pay group level), and Workflow-Based Salary Approvals, which allows organizations to define customized approval processes. The guide explains key screens and functionality including the Salary Approvals Screen with sections for "My Approval Items," "All Outstanding Items," "All Rejected Items," and "All Approval Items," as well as the Salary Request Screen used for standard approvals and controls for approving or rejecting outstanding salaries. Users encounter four distinct salary statuses throughout the process: "Pending" for newly created records not yet available to payroll, "In Approval" for records undergoing multi-level review, "Approved" or "Future" (for future-dated salaries) when all approval levels are complete and the record is available to payroll, and "Rejected" for records that fail approval at any stage. The document addresses practical scenarios including how employee payroll setup impacts approvals, how to view approval status on the Current Salary Screen, and how to delete pending salary records. This guide is designed for HR managers, payroll approvers, and system administrators who need to implement salary governance controls and ensure that all compensation changes receive appropriate oversight before being processed by the payroll system.

t: Salary Increment Configuration
s:
# Summary of "Salary Increment Configuration" Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to set up and configure the salary increment process in the PeopleXD CoreHR system.

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**System Parameters Configuration:**
- How to enable the HR-controlled increment process, which activates the automatic daily increment system
- How to set the "Increment Days" parameter, which determines how far in advance the system searches for upcoming salary increment due dates (for example, setting it to 30 days means the system will identify and process all increments due within the next 30 days)
- How to control whether salary amendments created by the increment process require approval through the standard salary approval workflows, or whether they should bypass approvals and be automatically approved for immediate payroll processing

**User Access Permissions:**
- How to configure which users can view the history of salary increments
- How to grant permissions for users to amend increment details

**System Setup:**
- How to access the necessary HR Admin setup screens and locate the relevant system parameters
- How to run the increment process job

The guide provides practical, step-by-step instructions for configuring these features to support an organization's salary increment workflows, with options to automate the process or require approval depending on business requirements.
ss: Salary increment configuration in CoreHR involves setting up system parameters, user access permissions, and automated daily processes to manage employee salary increases. Key configuration tasks include enabling the HR-controlled increment process, defining how many days forward the system should look for increment due dates, and deciding whether salary amendments require approval or process automatically to payroll. You'd open this guide when setting up CoreHR for the first time, configuring who can view or edit increment details, or troubleshooting why the daily increment job isn't running as expected. The document covers essential parameters like the "RUN_HR_RUN_INCREMENTS" job that automatically processes increments each day at 3am and controls approval workflows for salary amendments.
sl: This document is a configuration user guide for setting up the salary increment feature within CoreHR, a people management system, and is intended for system administrators and HR professionals responsible for implementing increment processes. The guide covers the essential configuration steps accessible through the Data Centre tab via HR Admin Setup Settings and System Parameters - Advanced screen, where administrators must enable the "Use HR Controlled Increment Process" parameter to activate daily salary increment processing. Key configurable parameters include "Increment Days," which determines how far forward the system searches for upcoming increment due dates to process salary amendments, and "Bypass Salary Increment Approvals," which controls whether automatically generated salary amendments require approval through the standard Salary Approval process or are approved automatically and sent directly to Payroll. The document specifies that certain parameters, namely "Use Increment Workflow Approval Process" and "HR Increment Questionnaire," are not recommended for enabling and do not align with the standard increment workflow. User access is controlled through specific menu options: "People Management Increment History View" permits users to view increment history on the Current Salary screen, while "People Management Increment History Edit" allows users to modify increment details including the Place Increment On Hold indicator, Increment Due Date, and associated comments. The underlying automated process runs through a daily database job named "RUN_HR_RUN_INCREMENTS," which executes by default at 3am each day and processes all eligible salary increments in a single daily run. This guide helps administrators resolve configuration questions and understand which settings control approval workflows, automation levels, and user permissions related to salary increment management in CoreHR.

t: Salary Increments
s:
# Salary Increments Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage salary increments in the PeopleXD HR system, specifically for employees on pay scales.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide explains the automatic increment process, which automatically creates a new salary record that moves an employee to the next point on their pay scale, eliminating the need to manually create salary amendments for regular annual or periodic increases. This can apply to all employees on a common date or to individual employees based on dates specific to their employment (such as 12 months from their start date).

**Key concepts covered:**

- **How increments work** — The system runs daily to identify employees whose increment due date is approaching (typically within a set number of days, like 30 days in advance) and automatically generates the appropriate salary amendment
- **Pay scale requirements** — Increments only apply to employees with "Pay Scale" salaries; they cannot be automatically created for "Personal" rate salaries
- **Increment attributes** — Key terms like "Increment Due Date" (when the increment should be applied) and the "Increment System Job" (the daily automated process)

**Practical tasks you'll be able to perform:**

- View, add, and delete increment due dates
- Generate incremented salary amendments through the daily increment process
- Identify which salaries have been incremented
- Manage increment hold indicators
- Process salary approvals related to increments
- Review increment history records
ss: Salary Increments on XD People Management automates the process of moving employees to the next point on their pay scale, eliminating the need to manually create salary amendments for regular annual or periodic increases. Use this guide when you need to view, add, or delete increment due dates, understand how the daily increment system job works, or manage increment holds and approvals. The increment process applies only to employees on pay scale salaries (not personal rate salaries) and can be triggered on organization-wide dates or employee-specific dates like work anniversaries. Open this document if you're managing employee salary progression, setting up automatic increment processing, or configuring increment rules in CoreHR.
sl: This user guide from Access Group provides comprehensive guidance on managing salary increments within the XD People Management system, specifically designed for HR professionals and payroll administrators who handle employee compensation. The document explains the increment process, which automatically creates new salary records that move employees to the next point on their pay scale, applicable only to employees with "Pay Scale" salaries rather than "Personal" rate salaries, and eliminates the need for manual salary amendment creation. Key processes covered include managing the Increment Due Date field on the Current Salary screen, the daily Increment System Job that automatically reviews all employees' Increment Due Dates and generates new salary records based on pay scale point increment rules defined in CoreHR, and the use of the On Hold Indicator to prevent processing when necessary. The document details pay scale point configuration elements such as progression rules, the next available point, length of time on point, bar points, and age restrictions, with reference to the separate Configuring Pay Scale Reference Data guide for detailed setup instructions. The salary increment process can operate independently from or with an increment-specific approval workflow, meaning increments can be created automatically without approval or with controlled approval requirements, with the On Hold Indicator providing additional control when large groups of employees increment on the same date. Users will also find guidance on viewing, adding, and deleting Increment Due Dates, understanding the daily increment generation process, identifying incremented salaries, and accessing increment history records.

t: Social Security Settings
s:
# Summary: Social Security Settings Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure and use the Social Security Settings feature in the PeopleXD HR system to manage social security number validation across multiple countries.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
The guide explains that Social Security Settings allows organizations to set up validation rules for employee social security numbers, with built-in support for:
- PPS Numbers (Republic of Ireland)
- NI Numbers (United Kingdom)

**Configuration Capabilities:**
After reading this guide, you'll understand how to:
- Set a default social security number type and validation rule for your organization
- Create exceptions for groups of employees in different jurisdictions that require different validation rules or no validation at all
- Customize field labels to match different countries' social security terminology
- Apply different validation requirements based on employee location or contract details

**Practical Example:**
The guide illustrates how to configure a system that uses NI Number validation by default for UK employees, applies PPS Number validation for employees based in Ireland (identified by their contract location), and allows unrestricted number formats for employees in other countries—with appropriate labels displayed for each group.

**Technical Setup:**
You'll also learn where to access the Social Security Settings feature in the system (via the Data Centre widget and HR Admin Setup), how to configure global settings and exceptions, and what additional parameters need to be enabled to activate the feature.
ss: CoreHR's Social Security Settings feature enables you to configure validation rules for employee social security numbers across different countries and jurisdictions, including PPS Numbers for Ireland and NI Numbers for the UK. You use this feature to set a global default validation rule and then create exceptions for specific employee groups based on organizational structure or pay group, allowing different validation standards for different locations. Open this document when you need to set up or modify how your system validates social security numbers during employee setup, or when your organization has employees in multiple countries requiring different number formats and validation routines. The configuration happens in HR Admin Setup Settings within CoreHR, where you define global settings and exception rules to match your organization's specific requirements.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance on configuring the Social Security Settings feature within CoreHR's People Management system, which enables organizations to capture and validate social security details for employees across multiple countries. The document covers how to access Social Security Settings through the Data Centre widget via HR Admin Setup Settings, then search for and select the Social Security Settings option. The core functionality allows administrators to configure Global Settings that establish a default validation routine for social security numbers—either PPS Number for the Republic of Ireland, NI Number for the United Kingdom, or None for organizations with employees in other jurisdictions—with each option including a customizable label of up to 20 alphanumeric characters. The document also explains how to configure Social Security Exceptions using the Social Security based on Organisational Structure section, which allows administrators to identify groups of employees who require different validation routines based on their organizational level or pay group, such as employees in specific departments, locations, or cost centres. The guide provides practical configuration examples demonstrating how an organization might set NI Number as the default while creating exceptions for Ireland-based employees requiring PPS Number validation and USA-based employees requiring Social Security Number validation. This document is intended for HR administrators and system configuration specialists who need to set up social security validation rules tailored to their organization's specific multi-country workforce requirements, and it references that a specific parameter must be enabled to switch on the Social Security Settings feature, with additional menu options available for implementation.

t: Successful Applicants
s:
# Successful Applicants Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators how to process successful job applicants through the PeopleXD People Management system after they've accepted job offers in the Recruitment module.

## What You'll Learn

**Main Processes Covered:**
- How to access the list of successful applicants waiting to be processed
- How to set up contracts for three types of hires:
  - **New starters** – brand new employees joining the company
  - **New contracts for existing employees** – both replacement contracts (changing roles) and additional contracts (taking on extra positions)
  - **Rehires** – former employees being brought back

**Key Functionality:**
- Navigating to and viewing the Successful Applicants screen, which displays applicants ready for processing
- Understanding which applicants appear on your screen based on your HR access permissions (you'll only see applicants linked to contracts/posts you have access to)
- Reading applicant summary information including their name, applicant number, personnel number, vacancy details, intended start date, and post
- Completing the contract creation process for each applicant type
- Processing the "Commence Appointment" step for new starters
- Managing applicant details on employee records once hired

The guide is designed for HR administrators who use both the Recruitment and People Management modules and need to finalize employment contracts for candidates who have accepted job offers.
ss: The Successful Applicants feature in People Management handles contract creation for candidates accepted through the Recruitment module, covering new hires, new contracts for existing employees (replacement or additional), and rehires. HR administrators use this tool to process applicants who have received and accepted job offers, including linking applicants to employee records, reviewing offer details, and commencing appointments. Open this guide when you need to set up contracts for newly hired or rehired staff, add additional contracts to current employees, or manage applicant records after the recruitment offer stage is complete.
sl: This user guide provides instructions for HR administrators on using the Successful Applicants feature within the People Management system, which is integral to the recruitment process and handles contract creation for new hires, existing employees receiving new or replacement contracts, and rehired staff. The document explains how to access the Successful Applicants screen through the Command Centre widget and the View button for Applicants, which displays a filtered list of applicants based on the HR user's designated access permissions to specific contracts and posts. The Successful Applicants screen presents summary-level details for each applicant including name, applicant number, personnel number (for existing employees), vacancy ID and name, start date, post, and action type, with applicants categorized as either "New Starter" (brand-new or dormant employees) or "New Appointment" (existing active employees available for new contracts). For each applicant, HR administrators can perform several key actions: viewing the contract offer details in read-only format through a 3-step Applicant Offer Screen, linking new starters to existing employee records via the Employee Link dropdown or to other applicant records using the Applicant Link functionality, or declining job offers to remove applicants from the screen when they reject the position. The guide covers specific processes including the Commence Appointment workflow for new starters, the creation and management of new contracts (both replacement and additional contracts for existing employees), and the rehiring of former staff, with all processing dependent on applicants first being linked to job offers in the Recruitment module and flagged as having accepted those offers.

t: Task List Configuration
s:
# Task List Configuration Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage HR Process Task Lists in the PeopleXD HR system.

## What You'll Learn:

**Core Concepts:**
- What HR Process Task Lists are and their purpose in the system

**Creating and Managing Task Lists:**
- How to access the HR Task Lists screen
- How to create a new task list from scratch
- How to add individual task list items to your configuration

**Configurable Task Steps:**

The guide covers all the different types of HR-related information steps you can include in a task list, such as:
- **Employment & Access:** User access assignments, leaver access, probation details, terms and conditions (general, pay, and balances)
- **Personal Information:** Contacts, next of kin, dependents, diversity information (disability and background)
- **Financial & Payroll:** Bank details, allowances, cost allocations, tax details, payroll legislative options
- **Professional Development:** Qualifications, professional bodies, CPD (Continuing Professional Development) information, languages
- **Administrative:** Badge details, files/documents, user-defined information, and specific user-defined fields

**Ongoing Management:**
- How to update existing task lists
- How to assign ownership of task list steps to specific people

In essence, this guide enables HR administrators to configure customized checklists of employee information and HR processes that need to be completed for various HR workflows.
ss: HR Process Task Lists in CoreHR guide users through mandatory steps required during New Starter, New Contract, Additional Contract, Rehire, and Leaver processes. This guide covers how to set up task lists, configure the specific steps (such as Allowances, Bank Details, Tax Details, Probation Details, and Terms and Conditions), assign step owners, and manage access permissions. Open this document when you need to create or modify task lists to ensure employees and contractors complete all required information at the right time in their employment journey.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for configuring and using HR Process Task Lists within the CoreHR system, specifically for People Management functions. The guide covers the complete setup process including how to access the HR Task Lists screen, create new task lists, and add individual task list items that direct users through mandatory steps during employee lifecycle events such as new starter, rehire, new contract, additional contract, or leaver processes. It details 24 specific task list steps and screens that can be configured, including Allowances, Bank Details, Badge Details, Cost Allocations, Qualifications, Terms and Conditions (General, Pay, and Balances), Tax Details, Diversity information, CPD Information, and access-related steps such as Assign User Access and Assign Leaver Access. The document explains how to update task lists, nominate step owners, restrict access to specific task list steps, configure notifications, and manage task list completion through both the setup interface and the Outstanding Processes screen. It also addresses contract-related task list management with menu options for viewing, updating, and completing task lists. This guide is intended for HR administrators and system configurators who need to establish standardized workflows and ensure that critical employee data fields are completed during hiring, contract changes, and separation processes.

t: Terms & Conditions
s:
# PeopleXD Terms & Conditions User Guide — Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage Terms and Conditions (T&C) Profiles in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide covers the complete lifecycle of T&C Profiles:

- **Understanding T&C Profiles**: What they are (reusable templates of contracted terms and conditions), what contract elements they contain (probation expiry dates, notice periods, increment dates, allowances, and leave balances), and how they work within the system.

- **Creating and managing profiles**: How to create new T&C Profiles from scratch, set up profile rules to determine when profiles apply based on criteria like employee status or location, configure general settings, pay components, and balance information. The guide also covers how to duplicate existing profiles, update them, and delete them when no longer needed.

- **Assigning T&Cs to contracts**: How to link T&C Profiles to Post Profiles (job templates), assign specific allowances and balances to posts, and apply T&C Profiles to individual employee contracts. This includes handling different contract types such as auto-authorised contracts, auto-commenced contracts, standard contracts, and restructured contracts.

After reading this guide, users will be able to set up standardised terms and conditions templates and apply them consistently across posts and employee contracts in the system.
ss: Terms and Conditions (T&C) Profiles in PeopleXD are templates that define contracted terms such as probation expiry, notice periods, allowances, and leave balances for employee contracts. You'll use this guide to create new T&C Profiles, assign them to Post Profiles based on rules like location or department, and then apply them to individual employee contracts through HR Process Task Lists. Open this document when you need to set up standardized contract terms, link those terms to job posts, or apply specific terms to new employee contracts during onboarding. It covers the complete workflow from creating and configuring T&C Profiles to updating them at both post and contract level.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing Terms and Conditions (T&C) Profiles within the XD People Management system on CoreHR, covering the creation, updating, and assignment of these profile templates to employee contracts. T&C Profiles are configurable templates that define contracted terms including probation expiry dates, notice periods, increment due dates, allowances, and balance information, which can be applied to both Post Profiles and individual employee contracts. The document explains the step-by-step process for viewing T&C Profiles by navigating to the Data Centre and searching for "Terms and Conditions Setup" in People Management, where users can access the Terms and Conditions Setup screen to search, edit, copy, or delete existing profiles. Users can create new profiles on the Edit Template screen by entering a Template code (up to 6 alphanumeric characters), Template Description (up to 100 characters), and defining Profile Rules based on contract elements such as Company, Management Unit, Department, Cost Centre, Location, Category, Sub Category, Job Title, and Post Type to determine when a profile applies. The guide covers the critical workflow of first linking a T&C Profile to a Post Profile via CoreHR, then assigning Post T&Cs to employee contracts through HR Process Task Lists, with the note that T&Cs cannot be assigned directly to contracts without using task lists. This document is designed for HR administrators and people management professionals who need to configure standardized terms and conditions for posts and contracts, establish assignment rules based on organizational attributes, and manage the full lifecycle of T&C profiles within their organization.

t: Terms & Conditions Configuration
s:
# Summary: Terms & Conditions Configuration Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure the PeopleXD HR system to use Terms and Conditions Profiles. After reading it, users will understand how to:

**Set Up Access and Permissions:**
- Grant system access to the Terms and Conditions setup functionality through the appropriate menu options in People Management
- Enable user access to manage Terms and Conditions Profiles

**Configure Task Lists:**
- Access and set up HR Task Lists to include Terms and Conditions options
- Enable task lists to appear when completing new hire, contract replacement, or rehire processes
- Add specific Terms and Conditions task list steps to employee workflows, including:
  - Terms and Conditions General (required as a foundation step)
  - Terms and Conditions Balances (requires the General step to also be used)
  - Terms and Conditions Pay (requires the General step to also be used)

**Manage Employee-Level Access:**
- Control how employees access their Terms and Conditions information
- Manage related functions like allowances and balances

The guide is a configuration manual focused on system administration and setup rather than end-user operations. It assumes the user has the ability to manage menu options and access controls within the CoreHR system, and that the actual Terms and Conditions profiles themselves are set up separately using a different guide.
ss: Setting up Terms and Conditions in CoreHR involves configuring profiles, task lists, and user access permissions across the People Management system. This guide covers how to grant staff access to create and manage Terms and Conditions Profiles, configure which T&C tasks appear during new hire and contract processes, and control visibility of T&C information on employee records. Open this document when you need to establish menu option permissions for Terms and Conditions functionality or set up task list steps for General, Balances, and Pay options in your HR workflows. It's essential for HR administrators managing access controls and process configuration in PeopleXD People Management.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive guidance on configuring CoreHR's Terms and Conditions Profiles functionality, covering access management, task list setup, and employee-facing configurations within the People Management system. The document details how to grant access to the Terms and Conditions Setup option through the Data Centre > People Management screen menu option, which provides full access to create and update Terms and Conditions Profiles. It explains task list configuration by describing how to access HR Task Lists via the Data Centre > Settings screen using the People Management Hr Task Lists menu option, and how to enable task lists on employee records through the People Management Hr Process Update menu option, which triggers the task list popup upon completion of new hire, contract replacement, or rehire wizards. The guide specifies three optional task list steps that can be configured—Terms and Conditions General, Terms and Conditions Balances, and Terms and Conditions Pay—with the requirement that the General option must be included if either Balances or Pay options are used, and notes that these options must be configured across all relevant contract process types (New Starter, New Contract, Re-hire). Access to individual task list T&C options is controlled through specific menu options: People Management General Terms Conditions, People Management Balance Terms Conditions, and People Management Pay Terms Conditions, with additional menu options required for the Add Allowances button (People Management Add Allowances) and Add Balance button (People Management Add Balances). The document also covers how employees access Terms and Conditions on their employee records, which is controlled by the same menu options used for task list access, though this view is read-only and does not allow updates. This guide is primarily used by system administrators and HR configuration specialists who need to set up and control access to Terms and Conditions functionality within the CoreHR People Management module.

t: User Data Access
s:
# Summary: User Data Access Guide

This guide teaches HR system administrators how to manage and control user access to employee data within the PeopleXD HR system.

Specifically, users will learn how to:

**Understand Access Fundamentals:**
- How user access works in the system overall
- How access is controlled based on organisational structure (departments, teams, hierarchies)
- How access is controlled based on pay groups

**Configure User Access:**
- Where access permissions are granted to individual users
- How to grant HR-related access so users can view and manage employee records, employment contracts, and posts/positions
- How to grant pay-related access so users can view and manage salary and allowance information
- How to assign default menu profiles to users so they see the appropriate options for their role

**Apply Additional Data Controls:**

**Post Profile Access:**
- What additional security configuration is needed for post profile data access within CoreHR

The guide also includes a detailed appendix with screenshots and visual references showing where these access controls appear on various HR screens (employee records, contracts, posts, salary information, etc.), making it a practical reference for administrators implementing these settings.
ss: User Data Access covers how to manage employee, contract, and salary information access in the PeopleXD People Management system. It explains how to grant users both menu profiles (system functionality access) and data access (actual employee records, posts, and salary information) based on organisational structure levels such as company, department, or management unit. Open this guide when you need to set up or modify what data a user can see in People Management, assign HR or pay access permissions, or understand how access controls work across different organisational levels. This is essential for HR administrators and payroll managers configuring user permissions in the system.
sl: This user guide explains how to manage and configure user access to employee, contract, and salary data within the People Management system on PeopleXD. The document covers two distinct categories of access that users require: Menu Profiles (which provide access to system functionality like dashboards, screens, buttons, and widgets aligned to user roles such as PEOPLE_MGT_EMPLOYEE_ADMIN) and Data Access (which controls access to specific records including Employees, Posts, and Salaries). User data access is structured around the Organisational Structure defined in PeopleXD, allowing administrators to grant access at various hierarchy levels such as the entire Company, specific Departments, or particular Management Units. The guide details specific configuration processes including Granting HR Access for Employees, Contracts, and Posts (covered in section 3.2), Granting Pay Access for Salaries & Allowances (section 3.3), and Assigning Default Menu Profiles (section 3.4), with additional sections addressing Substantive Contract Access and Confirmed Future Contracts. The document is intended for HR administrators and payroll administrators responsible for configuring user permissions in People Management, and it includes an extensive appendix with specific screen names such as the Employee Screen, Employee Record Contract List, Contracts Screen, Command Centre Widget, and Advanced Employee Setup screens. This guide helps resolve access configuration issues by providing clear procedures for determining where access is granted and how to properly configure data visibility across different user roles and organisational levels.

# Summary: User Defined Field Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR system administrators how to configure and manage User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What UDFs are:** Custom fields that can be added to the HR system to capture organization-specific information beyond standard HR data fields
- **How to access UDF configuration:** Where in the system to find and use the UDF configuration tools
- **How to create new UDFs:** A step-by-step process covering adding UDF codes, configuring data labels, defining field types, and setting optional access controls and date parameters
- **How to update and maintain existing UDFs:** How to edit UDF descriptions, modify existing items, add new items, adjust advanced settings, deactivate UDFs, or delete them completely
- **How to control who sees UDFs:** How different user types (HR administrators, managers, and employees) can access and view UDF data, including how to set reporting and dashboard visibility
- **How to implement security restrictions:** How to configure additional security settings when UDFs contain sensitive information that should only be accessible to certain users

The guide provides practical, hands-on instructions for managing the entire lifecycle of custom fields within the HR system.
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in PeopleXD allow you to store custom data specific to your organization against employees, posts, or contracts—such as equipment assignments or other non-standard information. This guide walks you through creating, editing, and managing UDFs through the People Management dashboard, including how to configure access for HR administrators, managers, and employees. You'll open this document when you need to set up custom fields for your organization, modify existing UDFs, or control who can view and update sensitive custom data.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the XD People Management system, which are custom data fields used to capture organization-specific information not provided by standard system functionality. The document covers the complete lifecycle of UDF management, including how to create UDFs by following five steps: adding a new UDF code, configuring data labels, defining the user defined type, optionally setting employee and manager access permissions, and optionally hiding date fields. Users can also update existing UDFs through the Maintain User Defined Fields screen by editing descriptions, modifying existing items, adding new items, and updating advanced settings, as well as making UDFs inactive or deleting them entirely. UDFs can be created and attached to employees, posts, or contracts, and can be configured using up to 12 standard field types including text, number, list, date, and text area elements with optional start and end date fields. Access to UDF configuration occurs through the People Management dashboard by navigating to HR Admin Setup Settings via the Data Centre widget, then searching for User Defined Objects under HR Configuration. The document addresses access control scenarios for different user types—HR administrators have standard access to all UDFs, while managers and employees can be granted view or update permissions on a per-UDF basis, and sensitive UDFs can be flagged with a security required flag to restrict HR administrator access. All UDF data is reportable through XD Insight, making this guide essential for HR administrators and configuration specialists who need to customize the People Management system to capture organization-specific employee, post, or contract data.

# Summary of "User Defined Field Data" Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators, employees, and managers how to work with User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the PeopleXD HR system.

**What UDFs are:**
User Defined Fields are custom data fields that store information not covered by the system's standard features. They're organisation-specific and vary between companies. For example, a company might use a UDF to record what equipment has been issued to each employee.

**What you'll learn to do:**

1. **Access UDFs** — Navigate to the User Defined Data screen from an employee's HR record to view any existing custom fields

2. **Search for UDFs** — Use keyword searches to find specific UDFs and switch between different employee contracts to view contract-specific custom data

3. **Add UDFs** — Create new user-defined data entries for employees, including understanding the difference between "Person UDFs" (employee-level data) and "Contract UDFs" (specific to an employment contract)

4. **Edit UDFs** — Update existing custom field data that's already been recorded

5. **Delete UDFs** — Remove custom field entries when no longer needed

The guide also covers access controls, such as UDF Assignment Groups that may restrict who can see or add certain types of custom fields, and security settings that may require special permissions to access sensitive custom data.
ss: User Defined Fields (UDFs) in CoreHR allow you to store custom data on employee records for information that isn't available as standard in PeopleXD—such as company-specific equipment assignments or organizational details. This guide walks you through accessing the User Defined Data screen from an employee's HR record, searching for existing UDFs, and performing key tasks like adding new UDFs, editing existing ones, and deleting records. You'll learn the difference between Person UDFs (linked to the employee record) and Contract UDFs (linked to a specific employment contract), plus how security settings and assignment groups control access. Open this guide when you need to capture or manage custom employee information that's specific to your organization.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for managing User Defined Fields (UDFs) in the CoreHR system within the PeopleXD People Management module. UDFs are custom data fields that allow organizations to store information not provided as standard system fields, such as company-specific equipment assigned to employees, and the guide explains how HR administrators, employees, and managers can work with these fields. Users access the User Defined Data screen by navigating to the Command Centre > Employees screen, searching for an employee, clicking View to open their HR record, and then selecting the User Defined Data option on the left side of the screen. The document details the complete workflow for adding new UDFs by clicking Add, selecting a UDF Type from a dropdown list, inputting required data, and saving the record to the employee's profile. A critical distinction covered is the difference between Person UDFs (associated directly with the employee record and not linked to any contract) and Contract UDFs (linked to specific contract records, requiring the correct contract to be selected first). The guide also addresses search functionality using keyword searches by UDF name and contract selection via a dropdown menu, while noting that access to specific UDFs may be controlled through UDF Assignment Groups or Security Required indicators. Additional configuration considerations mentioned include mandatory fields, variable input types based on UDF Type configuration, and the ability to view, edit, and delete existing UDF records through the interface buttons provided on the User Defined Data screen.

# Wage Warning Setup Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure wage warning validations in the PeopleXD HR system. 

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Understand wage warnings**: Learn what wage warnings are and how they function within the system, including where wage warning validation is available.

- **Configure three types of wage rates**:
  - **Minimum Wage**: Add, edit, delete, and activate minimum wage rates with sample rates provided
  - **Living Wage**: Add, edit, delete, and activate living wage rates with sample rates provided
  - **Apprentice Wage**: Identify apprentice contracts, then add, edit, delete, and activate apprentice wage rates with sample rates provided

- **Access the wage warning setup area**: Know where to navigate in the system to configure these settings.

- **Enable wage warnings**: Switch on wage warning parameters for each of the three wage types (minimum wage, living wage, and apprentice wage warnings).

- **Understand validation application**: Learn how the system applies wage validation checks and key points to note about the validation process.

- **Complete additional configuration**: Set up menu options and customize warning message text as needed.

In essence, this is a practical setup guide for HR administrators who need to configure the system to automatically flag or warn when employee wages fall below specified minimum, living, or apprentice wage thresholds.
ss: The Wage Warnings feature on PeopleXD validates employee salaries against minimum wage, living wage, and apprentice wage thresholds to alert users when contracted rates may be too low. Configuration involves setting up and activating wage rates for each tax year, identifying apprentice contracts, and enabling validation parameters for the different wage types. This guide covers where wage warning validation displays in the system, how the calculation works based on employee date of birth, contracted hours, and country-specific rates, and the complete setup steps required to activate these compliance checks. Open this document when you need to configure wage rates on PeopleXD or troubleshoot why wage warnings are or aren't appearing during employee contract setup.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation on the Wage Warnings feature in PeopleXD, a People Management system, explaining how to configure and apply wage validation across minimum wage, living wage, and apprentice wage rates. The document covers detailed setup procedures including how to access the Wage Warning Setup area, add and manage rates for each wage type (minimum, living, and apprentice), edit existing rates, and delete rates as needed, with sample rates provided for reference in sections 2.2 through 2.4. Wage Warnings function by validating employee salaries against configured rates based on the employee's date of birth, contracted hours and weeks (or FTE Weeks per Year), contract type, pay group country for multi-country setups, and the effective dates of the rates defined in the system. The validation applies specifically to New Hire and Rehire screens, where users receive alerts if a salary falls below the applicable threshold, helping prevent inadvertent underpayment of employees. Additional configuration is required to enable the feature, including switching on parameters for each warning type (Living Wage Warning, Minimum Wage Warning, Apprentice Wage Warning), setting up menu options, configuring warning message text, and establishing FTE Weeks per Year settings. This guide is intended for payroll and HR administrators who configure People Management systems and need to ensure wage compliance within their organization.

# Summary of "Auto Enrolment in Ireland User Guide"

This guide teaches PeopleXD Payroll users how to manage automatic pension enrolment for employees in Ireland.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What auto enrolment is** — the basics of who gets automatically enrolled in pensions and how contributions work
- **Key compliance requirements** — important deadlines and payment rules you must follow, including three critical rules: using NAERSA to determine eligibility, following AEPN instructions precisely, and understanding how pension pots transfer between providers
- **Employee rights** — what options employees have, including the right to opt out or pause contributions
- **The two-step payroll process** — the new steps you need to add to your regular payroll procedures to handle auto enrolment:
  1. Retrieving AEPN instructions (which tell you what pension actions to take for each employee)
  2. Submitting contribution files to the pension provider
- **Technical implementation** — how to use the six APIs (automated interfaces) provided by PeopleXD to communicate with the pension system and exchange the necessary information

The guide is designed for payroll professionals who need to integrate auto enrolment processes into their existing PeopleXD payroll operations and ensure compliance with Irish pension regulations.
ss: Auto Enrolment in Ireland is a statutory pension process you manage through PeopleXD Payroll, involving eligibility assessments, contribution submissions, and regulatory compliance with Irish pension rules. This guide walks you through the two core steps required: retrieving AEPN (Auto Enrolment Pension Notification) instructions from the authorities and submitting employee contribution files to the pension provider. Open this document when you need to understand how auto enrolment eligibility rules work, when and how to submit contributions, or how to handle employee opt-outs and contribution pauses. It's essential if you're managing payroll for Irish employees subject to automatic pension enrolment requirements.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for PeopleXD Payroll that explains how to implement and manage Auto Enrolment in Ireland. The guide covers the foundational concepts of Auto Enrolment, including who is automatically enrolled, how contributions work, key deadlines, payment rules, and employee rights such as opting out and pausing contributions. It describes two critical new steps that users must add to their payroll process: retrieving AEPN (Auto EnrolmentPN) instructions and submitting contribution files, detailing when and how to perform each step. The document explains the rules governing Auto Enrolment, specifically that NAERSA determines eligibility, AEPN instructions must be followed exactly, and pension pots follow members across employers. It covers technical aspects including the six APIs users will interact with for Auto Enrolment communication, system requirements, and the specific differences between Auto Enrolment and regular payroll processing. The guide provides practical procedures such as how to retrieve AEPNs from CSV files, print NAERSA exception reports, cleardown AEPN records, and view AEPN details on employee pension records. This document is designed for payroll professionals and administrators in Ireland using Access Group's PeopleXD system who need to configure and execute Auto Enrolment processes.

# Benefit Management Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage employee benefits within the PeopleXD HR system, with a primary focus on vehicle-related benefits (known as BIK — Benefit in Kind).

## Key Areas Covered:

**Understanding Benefit Management Options**
The guide explains different approaches to handling benefits, including returning benefits via the P11D form, payrolling benefits through a Car Administration Centre, or managing payrolling benefits manually.

**Setting Up Payrolling Benefits**
Users will learn how to configure the system to process vehicle benefits through payroll. This includes setting up RTI (Real Time Information) parameters, creating BIK pay codes, selecting which vehicle benefit codes to use, and recording vehicle registration dates. Configuration can be done either through the portal interface or back office system.

**Using the Car Administration Centre**
The guide covers how to use the dedicated Car Administration Centre tool to manage company vehicles, including adding new vehicles to the system, editing existing vehicle details, removing vehicles, and managing P46/P11D tax form information. It also explains how employees can view their primary car information through the Employee Self-Service (ESS) portal widget.

**Vehicle Administration**
Users learn how to add vehicles and vehicle types to the system through the back office when not using the Car Administration Centre.

**Year-End Administration**
The guide covers important end-of-year tasks, including configuring BIK rates for company cars, setting cash equivalent rates, managing van benefit charges, and calculating vehicle and fuel cash equivalent values under Optional Remuneration Arrangements.
ss: Benefit Management in PeopleXD Expense/Payroll covers how to set up and process benefits in kind (BIK), particularly company vehicles, for payroll purposes. This guide walks you through configuring BIK pay codes, managing vehicle details in the Car Administration Centre, and handling year-end tasks like P11D returns and Real Time Information (RTI) submissions. Open this document if you need to add employee vehicles to the payroll system, calculate taxable benefit charges, or prepare tax compliance documentation. It's essential for payroll administrators managing company car schemes and other payrolled benefits.
sl: This Benefit Management User Guide for PeopleXD Expense/Payroll provides comprehensive instructions for managing employee benefits within the system, specifically focusing on payrolled benefits and Benefits in Kind (BIK) administration. # Summary

This guide explains how to set up and use the PeopleXD HR system to include National Insurance (NI) savings from salary sacrifice schemes as a pension top-up in budget forecasts.

**What you'll learn:**

- **The purpose**: How to configure the system so that when employees use salary sacrifice for pension contributions, the employer's NI savings are automatically added to the pension top-up amount shown in budget forecasts.

- **Configuration steps**: You need to set up three things in CorePay:
  1. Identify which pay codes are salary sacrifice pay codes and link them to the relevant pension scheme
  2. Assign a specific pay code for recording salary sacrifice savings
  3. Set the percentage of the NI saving that will be passed to employees as an employer top-up (with 100% as the default)

- **How it works**: Once configured, when the system calculates pension figures in forecasts, it automatically includes the employer's NI saving. For example, if an employee sacrifices salary for a pension, the employer saves money on NI contributions (because the sacrificed amount reduces the payroll on which NI is calculated). This saving is then added to the employer's pension contribution and shown in the forecast total.

- **Practical example**: The guide includes a worked example showing how a £17.25 employer NI saving is calculated and combined with the standard employer pension contribution to give a total employer pension contribution figure.

This feature was introduced in an earlier version but updated in v26 to work with budget forecasting reports.
ss: Salary sacrifice National Insurance savings can now be included as a pension top-up in CoreBudget forecasts. The configuration process in CorePay requires setting up a salary sacrifice pay code, assigning it to a pension scheme, and defining a salary sacrifice savings contribution percentage that determines how much of the employer NI saving is passed to employees. Once configured, pension figures in budget forecasts automatically include the calculated NI savings from salary sacrifice arrangements. Open this guide if you need to set up or understand how salary sacrifice NI savings are reflected in your pension budget projections.
sl: This document is a user guide for CoreBudget that explains how to include salary sacrifice National Insurance savings as a pension top-up in budget forecasts, a feature introduced in version 26 of the Access Group's CoreHR system. The guide covers configuration requirements in CorePay across two main reference areas: Pay Code settings where users must identify salary sacrifice pay codes and assign them to a Salary Sacrifice Pension Scheme, and Pension Scheme settings where users must designate a Salary Sacrifice Savings pay code and configure a Salary Sacrifice Savings Contribution percentage to determine what portion of the employer NI saving is passed on as an employer top-up. Once configured, the pension forecasts in CoreBudget automatically include the employer National Insurance savings generated from salary sacrifice arrangements, calculated as a percentage of the difference between basic salary and gross pay after deductions. The document provides a detailed worked example showing how an employee earning £5,000 basic salary with NI category A would generate a £17.25 employer NI saving (calculated at 13.8% rate) that is added to the employer pension contribution of £225, resulting in a total employer pension contribution of £242.25. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and budget forecasters who need to understand how salary sacrifice benefits affect pension contribution calculations and forecasting within the CoreBudget module.

# Summary: Salary Sacrifice NI Saving as Pension Top Up in Budget Forecast

This guide explains how to configure and use the PeopleXD HR system to include National Insurance (NI) savings from salary sacrifice arrangements as pension top-ups in budget forecasts.

**What you'll learn:**

The guide covers the setup process needed to enable the system to automatically calculate and include employer NI savings as additional pension contributions when forecasting pension costs.

**Key configuration steps:**

1. **Pay Code setup** — Identify which pay codes are salary sacrifice arrangements and link them to the appropriate pension scheme
2. **Pension Scheme setup** — Assign a specific pay code where the NI savings will be recorded and set the percentage of NI savings to be passed on as an employer top-up contribution

**How it works:**

Once configured, when the system calculates pension forecasts, it automatically includes the NI saving generated from salary sacrifice arrangements as an additional employer contribution. For example, if an employee sacrifices £125 in salary for pension, the employer saves NI on that amount (e.g., £17.25 at 13.8% NI rate), and this saving is added to the employer's pension contribution figure in the budget forecast.

This feature was introduced to allow Core Budget to report on NI savings that were already being calculated in the payroll system, providing more accurate pension cost forecasting.
ss: The CoreBudget system now includes salary sacrifice National Insurance savings as a pension top-up in budget forecasts. You'll use this guide to configure salary sacrifice pay codes, assign pension schemes, and set contribution percentages in CorePay's Reference section so that employer NI savings are properly calculated and reported alongside employee pension contributions. Open this document when setting up or updating budget forecasts that need to account for the combined value of employer pension contributions plus NI savings generated through salary sacrifice arrangements. This functionality was introduced in v24 and extended to CoreBudget reporting in v26.
sl: This user guide documents the changes made to CoreBudget to enable the inclusion of salary sacrifice National Insurance (NI) savings as a pension top-up in budget forecasts. The document covers configuration processes conducted in CorePay across two main areas: the Reference > Pay Code section where salary sacrifice pay codes must be identified and linked to their corresponding Salary Sacrifice Pension Scheme, and the Reference > Pension Scheme section where a Salary Sacrifice Savings pay code and a Salary Sacrifice Savings Contribution % must be assigned to determine what percentage of the NI saving is passed on as an employer top-up. Once configuration is complete, the pension figure calculated in the forecast automatically includes the NI saving from the salary sacrifice, with the employer NI saving calculated at 13.8% for NI category A earnings above the secondary threshold. This guide is used by budget planners and payroll administrators who need to configure and forecast pension contributions that incorporate salary sacrifice NI savings as employer top-ups. A sample scenario illustrates how an employee's basic salary of £5,000 with a 2.5% employee salary sacrifice pension contribution generates an employer NI saving of £17.25, resulting in an overall employer pension contribution of £242.25 when combined with the standard 4.5% employer pension contribution.

1. **Non-vehicle benefits** — general benefits that don't involve company cars
2. **Vehicle benefits** — with instructions for two different scenarios:
   - When vehicles are already registered in the Car Admin Centre
   - When the Car Admin Centre is not being used

**Supporting resources:** The guide provides sample CSV files and file format specifications for each benefit type, showing the correct structure and data fields required to ensure successful uploads.

**Troubleshooting:** Instructions on how to handle upload errors, including a common issue where blank lines at the end of CSV files cause failures, with step-by-step guidance on fixing this problem.

sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for loading Benefit in Kind (BIK) details into the Payroll system through the Portal, specifically covering the process of uploading benefits for payroll purposes. # Summary: Minimum Wage Exception Report User Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the **Minimum Wage Exception Report** feature in the PeopleXD HR Payroll system to identify and monitor employees whose calculated hourly rates fall below statutory minimum wage requirements.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Understand the report's purpose**: The Minimum Wage Exception Report generates in both PDF and CSV formats and identifies employees whose hourly rate is below the statutory minimum wage rate applicable to their age group.

- **Set up the necessary prerequisites**: Configure the system to use the report by:
  - Establishing National Minimum Wage (NMW), National Living Wage (NLW), and Apprenticeship Rates rules in People Management
  - Configuring which Pay Codes should be included in minimum wage calculations
  - Setting up Periodic Employee Hours on the Pay Group

- **Configure Pay Codes**: Enable the Minimum Wage/Living Wage Check indicator on relevant pay codes so they're included when calculating employee earnings.

- **Configure Pay Groups**: Set up periodic employee hours on pay groups to support the minimum wage validation.

- **Generate the report**: Create and run the Minimum Wage Exception Report (Pay305mw) to identify compliance issues.

- **Handle special scenarios**: Manage minimum wage checks for starter and leaver employees mid-payroll period.

The guide notes that while the minimum and living wage checks work across multiple countries, the Apprenticeship Rates Check applies specifically to UK payrolls.
ss: The Minimum Wage Exception Report in Payroll identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below statutory minimum wage thresholds (National Minimum Wage, National Living Wage, or Apprenticeship Rates) based on their age. Open this guide when you need to configure pay codes and pay groups to enable minimum wage checks, or when you're ready to generate the exception report to flag compliance issues. The report outputs in both PDF and CSV formats and applies to payrolls in any country, though apprenticeship rate checks are UK-only. Payroll administrators and compliance professionals typically use this document to understand how to identify and resolve instances where employee hourly rates fall below statutory requirements, with the report also supporting scenarios involving starter and leaver mid-period wage adjustments.

# Summary: RTI Stability Improvements Guide

This guide explains the updates to Real Time Information (RTI) functionality in CorePay v26. Users will learn about four key improvements that have been made to enhance system stability and prevent data submission errors:

1. **Enhanced Excel Reports** — The Excel file exported from the RTI screen for FPS (Full Payment Submission) files now includes additional data fields: RTI Employee Number and National Insurance Number (NINO).

2. **Improved Exception Reporting** — The RTI exception report has been expanded to catch and flag critical errors before file transfer, including:
   - Missing employee dates of birth
   - Invalid characters in employee initials
   - Address lines exceeding 35 characters
   
   When these issues are flagged, users must correct the employee data and regenerate the FPS file before attempting transfer.

3. **Transfer Safeguards** — The RTI Transfer function now includes a protective mechanism that prevents users from submitting FPS files that contain critical errors identified by the exception report. Users receive warning messages for affected pay groups, and the system requires RTI validation to be completed before any additional payroll processing can occur.

4. **EPS File Generation for Prior Years** — Users can now generate an Employer Payment Summary (EPS) file for previous tax years, which automatically returns the full year-end position as required by HMRC.

**Important note:** These improvements require no new system configuration to implement.
ss: Real Time Information (RTI) filing in CorePay has been enhanced with stability improvements that catch and prevent common submission errors to HMRC. The updates include an improved exception report that flags critical issues like missing employee dates of birth, invalid characters in name fields, and oversized address lines—stopping you from attempting to transfer faulty FPS files. An enhanced Excel export from the RTI screen now includes RTI employee number and NINO values, and you can now generate EPS files for prior tax years. Open this guide if you're processing RTI returns in CorePay v26 and need to understand the new validation rules and error prevention features that apply to your payroll submission workflow.
sl: This document outlines the stability improvements made to Real Time Information (RTI) functionality in CorePay version 26, specifically focusing on enhancements to the RTI system used for UK payroll compliance with HMRC. The document describes four key changes to RTI processes: first, the Excel report generated from the RTI Screen for FPS file type now outputs additional values including 'RTI EMPNO' and 'NINO' fields; second, the RTI Exception Report has been enhanced to flag specific critical errors such as missing employee date of birth, invalid characters in the 'initial' field, or address lines 1-5 exceeding 35 characters, requiring users to correct these issues before regenerating the FPS file and attempting transfer; third, the RTI Transfer function now prevents users from transferring FPS files that contain critical errors identified by the exception report and displays warning messages for affected pay groups, while also ensuring the RTI Validation indicator is set after every complete update to enforce proper RTI return submission; and fourth, users now have the ability to generate an EPS (Employer Payment Summary) file for a prior tax year as a Tax Month 12 return reflecting the full position at year-end. These improvements require no new configuration and aim to reduce RTI file transfer failures by catching and flagging data quality issues before submission to HMRC. The document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals using CorePay who manage RTI submissions and year-end payroll processes.

# Summary: Absence Cut Off User Guide

This guide teaches payroll administrators how to use the **Absence Cut Off feature** in PeopleXD Payroll, which gives them control over whether absence data from the Workforce Management (WFM) system is included when running payroll validation.

**What you'll learn:**

- **What the feature does**: The Absence Cut Off feature allows payroll administrators to run Payroll Validation either with or without pulling through absences that have been recorded in WFM, giving them more control over payroll figures and reports.

- **How to enable it**: Step-by-step instructions for turning on the feature by navigating to Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, searching for the setting `cp_manual_absence_run`, and updating its value to 'Y'. (Note: This feature requires Access Engineering to enable a feature flag in your system first.)

- **How to use it on the Payroll Dashboard**: Understanding the visual indicators in the 'Mode' column that show whether WFM absences are currently set to be included (Green) or excluded (Red), and how to use the 3-dot menu to toggle between "Disable WFM Absence" and "Enable WFM Absence" for specific pay groups.

- **How it works in single processing**: When running individual validation runs, users see a new screen with a toggle that matches the pay group's current WFM absence setting, allowing them to choose whether to include or exclude absences for that specific validation.
ss: The Absence Cut Off feature in PeopleXD Payroll allows you to run Payroll Validation without automatically pulling through absences recorded in WFM, giving payroll administrators greater control over payroll processing. You enable this feature through Admin Settings, then manage it via the Payroll Dashboard where a "WFM ABSENCE" indicator shows whether absences are currently included (green) or excluded (red) in validations. Open this guide when you need to configure the feature, understand how to toggle absence inclusion on the dashboard, or learn how to control which absences feed into your payroll during single validation runs.
sl: This user guide for PeopleXD Payroll documents the Absence Cut Off feature, which allows payroll administrators to control whether absences imported from Workforce Management (WFM) are included when running Payroll Validation. The feature addresses a common client need to have more control over payroll figures and reporting by preventing automatic inclusion of WFM absences during the validation process. To enable Absence Cut Off, administrators navigate to Administrator Dashboard > Site Manager > Admin Settings, search for the configuration parameter cp_manual_absence_run, and update its value to 'Y', though this requires the feature flag payroll-absence-validation to be activated by Access Engineering in both UAT and LIVE environments. The Payroll Dashboard displays a 'Mode' column indicator showing 'WFM ABSENCE' status in either Green (absences included in last validation run) or Red (absences excluded in last validation run), with a 3-dot menu offering options to toggle between 'Disable WFM Absence' and 'Enable WFM Absence' for each pay group. When the feature is enabled, users see a new toggle screen during single validation runs that automatically matches the pay group's WFM absence setting but allows manual override for individual validations. The document clarifies through its FAQ section that the feature is not date-driven but rather controlled by when administrators run the absence process, that administrators can re-enable absences after disabling them, and that it only affects WFM-sourced absences rather than those manually input by payroll staff. Access to the Absence Cut Off screens requires the menu option WS_PAYROLL_MENU.PATCH_PAYGROUP_PARAMETER in the Web Services system.
