sl: This document is a user guide for the Assembly Points feature within the Access Group's Workforce Management (WFM) system, specifically designed for administrators who need to create and manage emergency assembly points for their organization. The guide explains how to access the Assembly Points screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard by navigating to WFM Configuration and selecting the Assembly Points tile, and outlines the specific fields users will encounter including Assembly Point Code (up to 6 alphanumeric characters), Assembly Point Description (up to 40 characters), Label (up to 40 characters), and Active status. The document details two primary processes: adding new assembly points by clicking Add, entering a code and description, optionally adding label information, and clicking OK; and assigning assembly points to employees either through Person Maintenance by accessing the Emergency Details tab or through People Management > Employees > Key Information, with the important restriction that only Active Assembly Points are available for employee assignment. The guide addresses menu security configuration by specifying that administrators must enable two menu options—Assembly (CONFIG_SET_MENU.ASSEMBLY_POINTS in CorePortal) and Get assemblypointspeople (WS_ROSTER_MENU.GET_ASSEMBLYPOINTSPEOPLE in Web Services)—through Security > Menu Profiles to grant user access to the Assembly Points functionality. Additional features include search and filter capabilities on the Assembly Points screen, allowing administrators to locate specific assembly points by code, description, or label, and to filter by active or inactive status, with the ability to view assigned employees through the three-dot menu option on each assembly point.

t: Additional Validation
s:
# Summary of "Additional Validation" Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure three types of validation rules in the PeopleXD Time and Attendance system. These validations are designed to prevent employees from incorrectly cashing out annual leave.

The three validation types covered are:

1. **Max Daily Pay Code Limit** — Restricts the maximum number of hours of annual leave an employee can record on a single pay code in one day. This is configured as a pay code setting.

2. **Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit** — Sets a maximum total number of hours that can be recorded across multiple pay codes on any given day. This is configured as a validation rule and requires setting up personalized pay code groups and assigning rules to companies or work groups.

3. **Holidays & Contracted Hours Check** — Ensures that when annual leave is recorded, the total weekly hours don't exceed what the employee is contracted to work. This is also configured as a validation rule.

For each validation type, the guide provides detailed configuration instructions, including how to set up pay codes, create validation rules, configure settings, and assign the rules to the appropriate companies or work groups within the system. Users will understand the purpose of each validation, when to use them, and step-by-step instructions for implementing each one.
ss: Additional Validation in CoreHR Time and Attendance enables you to set limits on pay codes and hours to prevent excessive annual leave cashouts. This guide covers three validation types: Max Daily Pay Code Limit (restricts hours per pay code per day), Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit (restricts total hours across multiple pay codes), and Holidays & Contracted Hours Check (ensures weekly leave doesn't exceed contracted hours). Open this document when you need to configure validation rules in your Time and Attendance system, set up pay code limits, or understand how validation alerts work across timesheet input, leave approval, and sign-off screens.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Additional Validation functionality within CoreHR's Time and Attendance system (Version 28), specifically designed to prevent the cashing out of annual leave for employees. The guide covers three types of additional validation that can be configured: Max Daily Pay Code Limit (a pay code setting), Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit (a validation rule), and Holidays & Contracted Hours Check (a validation rule), each with distinct purposes and configuration requirements. Max Daily Pay Code Limit prevents employees from recording more than a configurable number of hours on a single pay code per day and can be applied to value pay codes (such as meal allowances), unit pay codes (such as on-call allowances), or hours pay codes (such as annual leave), with validation alerts configured to display either warnings or stops across screens including Timesheet Input, Time Exceptions, Leave Approval, Absence Input, and Sign Off/Approve. Max Overall Daily Pay Code Limit restricts the total hours an employee can record across multiple pay codes in a single day, requiring configuration of Maximum Daily Hours and creation of personalized pay code groups. The Holidays & Contracted Hours Check validation rule ensures that when annual leave hours are recorded, the total weekly hours do not exceed the employee's contracted hours. The document provides detailed configuration guidance for each validation type, including step-by-step instructions for pay code setup, advanced options configuration, rule creation, and assignment of validation rules to company or work groups. This guide is intended for HR administrators and system managers who need to implement these validation controls within their Time and Attendance processes to maintain compliance with leave policies.

t: Advanced Period
s:
# Summary: Advanced Period Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to use the Advanced Period feature in the PeopleXD Workforce Management (WFM) system to manage Time and Attendance calendar periods.

## What You'll Learn

**Main Function:**
After reading this guide, you'll be able to advance calendar periods for your company's Time and Attendance system through the Portal interface (a feature that was previously only available in the Back Office).

**Key Capabilities:**
- Navigate to and set up the Advance Period screen via the System Users option in the Back Office
- Choose between two access levels when advancing periods:
  - **Home Company access** — advance calendars for only your home company and its associated user-defined calendars
  - **All Companies access** — advance calendars for all companies you have access to and their associated calendars
- Select specific calendars and move them to the next period
- View exceptions related to the current open period, including:
  - Unconfirmed Hours
  - Unapproved Leave Requests
  - Unapproved Pay Codes
- Check for transferred hours and access information related to advance period actions
- Understand warning prompts that appear when existing exceptions are detected before advancing a period

The guide also covers the specific menu options and system configuration required to enable this functionality on the Administrator Dashboard.
ss: The Advance Period feature in Workforce Management (WFM) allows administrators to move Time and Attendance calendar periods forward on Portal, either for their home company or across all companies depending on access level. Before advancing a period, the system displays exceptions such as unconfirmed hours, unapproved leave requests, and unapproved pay codes that may affect the transition. Open this guide if you need to configure administrator access to advance periods, understand how to navigate the Advance Period screen, or troubleshoot calendar period transitions in your organization.
sl: This configuration guide explains how to use and set up the Advance Period feature in Access's Workforce Management system (WFM V28), which allows administrators to progress Time and Attendance calendar periods for both company and user-defined calendars through the Portal interface. The document provides step-by-step instructions for navigating to the Back Office, selecting the System Users option, and choosing either "Home" or "All Companies" access levels under the Generate Timesheets tab to determine which calendars an administrator can advance. Once configured, users can select a specific calendar from those displayed on Portal and click "Update Period" to move to the next period, with the system providing a warning if exceptions exist before proceeding. The Advance Period screen displays three types of exceptions at the bottom: Unconfirmed Hours, Unapproved Leave Requests, and Unapproved Pay Code Exist, which relate to employees in the selected calendar for the current open period. The guide also covers the Transfer Access functionality, which shows hours that have been transferred via the Form Transfer Access, with visibility controlled through specific menu options in the Shifts module. Configuration requires enabling several menu options including Companies Calendars (Shifts > Get companies calendars), Update Company Calendar (Shifts > Update companies calendars period), Company Exceptions (Shifts > Get companies exceptions), and related Transfer Access options, all accessible from the Administrator Dashboard. The document notes that balance recalculation is no longer performed as part of the advance period process, distinguishing this version from previous functionality.

t: Approve Hours
s:
# Approve Hours Guide Summary

This guide teaches administrators and managers how to use the Approve Hours screen in the PeopleXD HR system to review, approve, and sign off on employee working hours.

**What you'll learn:**

- **How to access the Approve Hours screen** — Administrators navigate through the WFM Admin Dashboard while managers use the WFM Dashboard

- **How to view employee hours** — You can filter the display to show specific work groups, departments, and individual employees, or view all employees you have access to

- **How to filter hours by category** — You can choose to display all hours, hours requiring approval, exceptional hours, hours needing sign-off, or already signed-off hours

- **How to approve or reject individual days** — Including the ability to add comments and reasons for your decisions

- **How to perform group approvals or rejections** — Process multiple entries at once rather than one at a time

- **How to undo approvals/rejections** — Reverse decisions if needed

- **How to view supporting information** — Access weekly work schedules and full timesheets to inform your approval decisions

- **How to use filters effectively** — Manage the display to focus on the hours you need to process

- **How to configure system settings** — Set up whether cost centres, projects, positions, and comments are required or displayed during the approval process, and configure organizational roles and groups
ss: The Approve Hours Screen in Workforce Management allows administrators and managers to view, approve, and sign off on employee hours recorded in the system. You can filter and display hours by various criteria including work groups, departments, employees, pay codes, cost centres, projects, and attendance status types (such as hours requiring approval, exceptions, or pending sign-off). Open this guide when you need to understand how to access the approval interface, approve or reject individual or grouped hours, add comments or reasons for decisions, and manage configuration settings for your approval workflow. This document covers the transition of the Approve Hours functionality from Back Office to Portal, making it essential for anyone managing employee timesheets and attendance approvals.
sl: This user guide document explains the Approve Hours Screen, a Workforce Management feature that has been migrated from the Back Office system to Portal, enabling administrators to complete approval tasks within the Portal interface. The Approve Hours Screen displays employee attendance records organized by pay code and period, with default columns showing person number, name, appointment, pay code details, period information, day, and total hours, while additional columns such as cost centre and projects can be configured. Users can access the screen by navigating to either the WFM Admin Dashboard (for administrators) or WFM Dashboard (for managers) and selecting Approve Hours, with access controlled through menu profiles. The document describes specific screen actions including how to approve or reject individual days, add or view comments, add reasons for decisions, view weekly work schedules, and view timesheets, along with capabilities for group approval/rejection and undoing approvals. The Approve Hours Screen supports filtering by multiple attendance status types—including All Hours, Require Approval, Exceptions, Approved, Rejected, Pending Sign-Off, Signed-Off, and Requires Re-Code—allowing managers to focus on specific categories of attendance. Additional filtering options enable users to narrow results by departments, work groups, specific persons, cost centres, pay codes, locations, project codes, and team areas, with the ability to save filter configurations for repeated use. Configuration settings allow administrators to control whether cost centre, project, position, and scale point fields are displayed and updated, and to require comments when approving or rejecting hours, along with options for setting organizational roles and groups.

t: Badge Assignment
s:
# Badge Assignment Guide Summary

This user guide teaches HR administrators how to manage employee badges in the PeopleXD HR system's Workforce Management (WFM) module. Badges are used to enable automatic tracking of employee clockings via devices.

## What you'll learn to do:

**Manual Badge Management:**
- Access the Badge Details screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard and WFM Person Maintenance
- Add new badges for employees
- Edit existing badge information
- Delete badges
- View all badges assigned to an individual employee, including their status and issue dates

**Badge Rules and Constraints:**
- Understand that each badge number can only be assigned to one person
- Recognize that employees can have multiple badges assigned but only one can be active at any given time
- Know that active badges must have a valid issue date and cannot have an expiry date earlier than the issue date

**Additional Features:**
- Use the Badge Enquiry function to view badge details for employees within your area of responsibility
- Manage Clocking Distribution Groups (groups that receive clocking data)
- Enable Auto Assignment to automatically assign badges

**Bulk Operations:**
- Create multiple badges at once using the Bulk Creation feature and Data Migration Tool in the Administrator Dashboard

The guide also includes troubleshooting for common errors related to badge allocation and status conflicts.
ss: Badge assignment in Workforce Management allows administrators to create and manage employee badges for automatic clocking tracking via WFM devices. You can manually add, edit, or delete badges for individual employees through the Badge Details screen in the WFM Admin Dashboard, or create badges in bulk using the Data Migration tool. Open this guide when you need to issue a new badge to an employee, update badge information, troubleshoot badge allocation errors, or understand the rules around badge validity (such as the requirement that each employee can only have one active badge at a time). This document covers the complete badge lifecycle including version tracking, expiry dates, and how to manage visitor or contractor badges.
sl: This Badge Assignment User Guide from Access Limited's Workforce Management system provides comprehensive instructions for administrators on creating and managing employee badges used for automatic tracking of clockings via devices. The document describes how to access the Badge Details Screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard by navigating to WFM Person Maintenance, searching for an employee, and selecting the Badge Details tab, which contains three separate tabs: Individual Information, Badge Enquiry, and Clocking Distribution Groups. The Individual Information tab is where administrators perform manual badge management tasks, including adding badges by entering the Badge Number, Issue Date, and Version before clicking OK and activating the Valid toggle, editing existing badges through the 3-dot menu, and deleting badges with confirmation. Key fields in the badge system include Badge (a unique numeric field ranging from 1 to 12 digits that cannot be reused), Version Number (to track reissues such as when a card is broken), Issue Date, Expiry Date (optional, for noting when a badge was deactivated), and Description (optional, to designate visitor or contractor badges). The document addresses critical constraints and error scenarios, including that badge numbers cannot be assigned to multiple staff members once issued, only one badge per user can have an active status at any given time, and the expiry date cannot be earlier than the issue date. Additionally, the guide covers bulk creation of badges through the Data Migration Tool in the Administrator Dashboard and includes a Frequently Asked Questions section that resolves common errors such as duplicate badge number allocation and multiple active badges assigned to a single user.

t: Balance
s:
# Summary: Balance Configuration Guide

This guide teaches HR administrators how to configure and manage the **Balance** feature in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system. 

After reading this guide, users will understand and be able to:

**Main Tasks:**
- Access and use the Balance Configuration Summary Screen
- Copy existing balances
- View employees associated with balances
- Add new balances to the system
- Configure balance entitlements and pro-rata (proportional) entitlements
- Set up length of service increments
- Create and manage balance bonuses
- Establish balance rules

**Configuration Details:**
- Configure calendar parameters that govern how balances operate
- Set up balance calendars (the periods over which balances apply)
- Add and extend balance calendar periods
- Set up and manage accrual calendars (schedules for how balances accrue or build up)
- Add and extend accrual periods
- Configure "affecting codes" (pay codes or transactions that impact balance calculations)
- Define length of service rules for different employee tenure levels
- Set up FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) exceptions to handle part-time or variable hour workers

This is essentially a technical configuration manual for setting up how the system tracks, calculates, and manages employee balances (such as holiday, leave, or other benefits).
ss: The Balances Configuration Guide covers how to set up and manage balance elements, pay codes, and balance parameters in Workforce Management. It walks you through configuring balance entitlements, accrual calendars, bank holiday entitlements, and rules for leave or time-off tracking across your workforce. Open this guide when you need to establish how balances accrue, transfer between periods, or apply to different employee groups, or when setting up new balance types in your system.
sl: This document is a comprehensive configuration guide for the Balances module within Access Group's Workforce Management system, designed to help administrators set up and manage employee balance tracking. The guide covers fundamental terminology including Balance Elements, Pay Codes, Balance Parameters, and Balance Calendars, and then walks through accessing the Balance Configuration Summary Screen where users can perform core actions such as Add Balance, Balance Entitlements, Pro-Rata Entitlements, Length of Service Increments, Balance Bonus, Balance Rules, and Standard Hours configuration. The detailed configuration section explains how to set up Calendar Parameters, Balance Calendars, and Accrual Calendars by adding periods and extending existing calendars, as well as managing Affecting Codes, Length of Service rules, and FTE Exceptions. Users will find step-by-step instructions for configuring Entitlements Per Balance (including New Year Leave Entitlements, Accrual Entitlements, and Carried Forward Entitlements), Accrual Pay Codes, Bank Holiday Entitlements, and advanced settings such as Linked Balances, Balance Comparisons, and Transfers with historical tracking. The guide also addresses specialized configuration scenarios including Carried Forward Rules, Override In Period Limits, and Decay Setup, making it suitable for HR administrators, payroll managers, and Workforce Management system configurators who need to establish and maintain balance policies for their organizations.

t: Balance Maintenance
s:
# Balance Maintenance User Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators how to use the Balance Maintenance screen in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system to manage employee balance-related tasks.

**What you'll learn to do:**

1. **Access the Balance Maintenance Screen** — navigate to it from the WFM Admin Dashboard

2. **Recalculate Balances** — reprocess balance calculations and identify errors when they occur

3. **Activate Balances** — enable balances within the system and use associated actions as needed

4. **Run Period End processes** — execute end-of-period balance procedures, view threshold settings, and troubleshoot errors that arise during this process

5. **Manage Carried Forward Entitlements** — handle entitlements that roll over from one period to the next

**Key features of the Balance Maintenance Screen:**

The screen displays all balances in your system with information including the balance code, name, current period, whether it's flexitime, and balance type. The guide explains how to work with each of these balance management functions and provides step-by-step instructions for completing common administrative tasks related to employee leave, time off, and other balance types.
ss: Balance Maintenance in PeopleXD Workforce Management allows administrators to manage employee leave and entitlement balances through recalculation, activation, period end processing, and carried forward entitlements. Open this guide when you need to recalculate balances for individual employees or groups, activate balances in the system, run period end procedures, or manage how unused entitlements carry forward. The document provides step-by-step instructions for each task, including how to access the Balance Maintenance screen from the WFM Admin Dashboard and what to do if errors occur during processing.
sl: This user guide for the PeopleXD Workforce Management system explains the Balance Maintenance screen, which enables administrators to perform daily balance-related tasks within the WFM Admin Dashboard. The document covers four main processes: Balance Recalculation, Balance Activation, Balance Period End, and Carried Forward Entitlement, with each section detailing specific steps and workflows. The Balance Maintenance screen displays all system balances organized by fields such as Code, Name, Current Period, Balance Type, and counts of Active and Inactive employees assigned to each balance, with access to detailed employee lists available through a View Employees option in the 3-dot menu. The Balance Recalculation process allows administrators to recalculate balances for individual employees or groups based on their access level (Structure Code Access, System User Access, or Team Area Access), with options to recalculate based on Balance Values, Booked Values, or both, and includes a progress indicator showing completion percentage. The guide includes an Errors button that displays any issues encountered during recalculation that must be resolved before proceeding. Additional features covered include Balance Activation with an Actions button, Balance Period End with a View Thresholds button for monitoring threshold limits, and Carried Forward Entitlement settings, with all processes accessible through the Balance Maintenance screen's View option from the relevant balance's 3-dot menu.

t: Bank Holiday Schemes
s:
# Bank Holiday Schemes User Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage bank holiday schemes within the PeopleXD HR system's Workforce Management module.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Understanding Bank Holiday Rules:**
- Understand the key considerations for bank holiday schemes, including "Check Midnight" settings, hour-for-hour premium rules, Time Off in Lieu (TOIL) rules, and how work patterns interact with bank holiday pay codes

**Managing Bank Holiday Schemes:**
- Access and navigate the Bank Holiday Schemes summary screen
- Create new bank holiday schemes or copy existing ones
- Assign bank holiday schemes either to entire work groups or to individual employees

**Configuring Bank Holiday Settings:**
- Configure general settings for standard public holidays
- Set up hour-for-hour premium arrangements
- Configure "Scheduled to Rest" scenarios for employees not expected to work
- Configure "Scheduled to Work" scenarios for employees expected to work on bank holidays
- Set up bonus hours provisions
- Create and manage pay code rules and assign work groups to those rules

**Practical Application:**
- Work through real-world examples and scenarios showing how hour-for-hour premium rules apply in different situations (such as employees working as rostered, arriving early/late, taking extended breaks, or not showing up for scheduled shifts)

The guide provides step-by-step instructions and practical examples to help HR users correctly implement bank holiday policies within their organization.
ss: Bank Holiday Schemes in Workforce Management lets you configure how bank holidays are handled for employees and work groups, including premium pay rules, time off in lieu (TOIL), and bonus hours calculations. Use this guide to set up and assign bank holiday schemes, understand how midnight checks and hour-for-hour premium rules work, and configure pay codes specific to bank holidays. Open this document when you need to establish bank holiday policies, troubleshoot why an employee's bank holiday pay was calculated a certain way, or review detailed scenarios covering shifts that span midnight, no-shows, or employees working outside their roster.
sl: This document is a comprehensive user guide for the Bank Holiday Schemes feature within Access Group's Workforce Management system, detailing how to configure and manage bank holiday pay rules and employee entitlements. The guide covers the core processes of accessing the Bank Holiday Schemes Summary Screen, copying and adding bank holiday schemes, and assigning schemes either to entire work groups or to individual employees through the assignment functionality. The configuration section explains how to set up General Settings for standard public holidays and hour-for-hour premium rules, alongside specialized settings for Scheduled to Rest, Scheduled to Work, Bonus Hours, and Pay Code Rules, with specific instructions on adding pay code rules and assigning work groups to those rules. The document addresses critical bank holiday rule considerations including the Check Midnight feature for overnight shifts, Hour for Hour Premium Rules for calculating additional pay when employees work bank holidays, Time Off in Lieu (TOIL) Rules for granting compensatory time off, and Work Pattern Bank Holiday Pay Code configuration. Extensive worked examples throughout the guide demonstrate real-world scenarios for both Hour for Hour Premium and TOIL arrangements, covering situations such as employees rostered to work versus not rostered, early/late clock times relative to thresholds and grace periods, no-shows, and various overnight shift patterns that cross midnight. The document also includes guidance on accessing the Bank Holiday Entitlements screen to view employee entitlements, making it essential reading for payroll administrators, HR managers, and workforce scheduling professionals who need to correctly implement bank holiday compensation policies within their organization.

# Summary: Bulk Leave Approval Guide

This guide teaches managers and administrators how to use the Bulk Leave Approval feature in the PeopleXD HR system to efficiently process multiple employee leave requests in one place.

- **Accessing the tool** — How to navigate to the Bulk Leave Approval screen from either the WFM Admin Dashboard or Workforce Management Dashboard

  - View employee leave balances to inform approval decisions

  - Read and add comments on requests

- **Common questions** — A FAQ section addressing frequent user queries

ss: The Bulk Leave Approval screen in Workforce Management enables managers and administrators to review and process multiple employee leave requests in a single location, rather than handling them individually through notifications. You can filter requests by work group, department, employee, pay code, and request status, then approve or reject them using dropdown menus while viewing employee leave balances and attached supporting documents. sl: This user guide for Bulk Leave Approval, part of the Workforce Management system, provides managers and administrators with comprehensive instructions on approving multiple employee leave requests efficiently through a centralized interface rather than relying on individual notifications. The document explains how to access the Bulk Leave Approval screen via either the WFM Admin Dashboard or the Workforce Management Dashboard by navigating to the menu option on the left-hand side, with a note that users require an MSS account in BackOffice to view all reportees. The interface displays detailed information for each leave request including employee name, appointment, pay code, dates, duration, half-day indicators (AM/PM), request date, approval status, reason, unrostered hours indicator, document receipt status, document upload counts, comment counts, and overall status—with features like balance overlays and a 3-dot menu for accessing co-workers' absence information. The document addresses specific functionality such as approving or rejecting individual or bulk leave requests, managing comments and attached documents, viewing co-workers' calendars and leave absences, and configuring menu options and advanced settings through Coreportal parameters. t: Calculate Hours
s:
# Summary of "Calculate Hours" Guide

This guide explains how to use the **Calculate Hours screen** in the PeopleXD HR system, a feature that was recently moved from the back office to the Portal interface.

## What Users Will Learn:

**Screen Overview and Key Features:**
- The Calculate Hours screen displays a summary of the most recent calculation run, showing how many employees have been processed, how many are still pending, any errors that occurred, and the overall status (Complete, In Process, or Scheduled)

**Available Toggles/Options:**
- Run calculations for a single selected employee
- Run future calculations for selected employees (with configurable dates)
- Run real-time calculations for selected employees

**Access Levels and Permissions:**
The guide covers three different user scenarios for accessing the Calculate Hours function based on their system permissions:
1. System Users with "Generate Timesheets" permission — can access work groups at company or multi-company level
2. HR Admin Access users
3. Team Area Access users

Each access level determines which employees and work groups a user can run calculations for.

**Additional Configuration:**
- Calculation at the individual employee level
- How to view calculation history
- How to unlock days that have been locked
- Security settings and permissions configuration

The guide is essentially a configuration and user manual for managing hour calculations across employees in the PeopleXD HR system.
ss: The Calculate Hours screen in PeopleXD WFM allows users to process and review employee hours through future or real-time calculations. This configuration guide covers how to set up access for different user types (Generate Timesheet users, HR Admin users, and Team Area users), manage calculation runs across employees or work groups, and configure the necessary menu options and security settings. Open this document when you need to understand how the Calculate Hours feature works, set up user permissions for hour calculations, or configure the system menus required to run employee hour processing in your WFM system.
sl: This configuration guide explains the Calculate Hours screen within WFM v28, a tool that was previously available only in the back office but has now been moved to Portal, allowing users to calculate both future and real-time hours for selected employees. The document details three different calculation scenarios based on user permissions: System Users linked to the Generate Timesheets option who can access work groups by home company or all companies; HR Admin Access users who receive a filtered employee list; and Team Area Access users whose calculations run based on the team area structure. The configuration requires setting up multiple menu options through the Core Portal and Shifts modules, including Core Portal Calculate Hours, Get Hours Calculation, Create Hours Calculation, Calculation Errors, Create Hours Calculation (unlock days), Get Workgroups, Get Companies, and Companies Transfer Access.

s:
# Employee Calendars Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use the Employee Calendars feature within PeopleXD Workforce Management system.

**What you will learn:**

1. **Accessing the Employee Calendar Screen** — How to navigate to and open the calendar view, which varies depending on your user role (employee, manager, or administrator). Employees can access it through widgets like "My Calendar," "My Request," or "Work Week." Managers access it via team-related widgets or the Workforce Management Dashboard, while administrators use the WFM Admin Dashboard.

2. **Reading the Calendar Display** — How to interpret the 12-month work schedule view that shows an employee's scheduled work and color-coded status indicators (codes) representing different types of actions or statuses.

3. **Managing Absences** — How to view existing absences for an employee and how to add new absence records to the calendar.

4. **Using Team Calendar View** — How to access a broader view showing multiple team members' calendars.

5. **Understanding Edit and Delete Controls** — How permissions work for modifying or removing calendar entries based on user role.

6. **Working with Historical Data** — How to roll back weeks and view historical hours information.

7. **Handling Leaver Records** — How to locate and view employees who have left the organization.

8. **Configuration and Permissions** — How to set up pay codes, configure different access levels for administrators, managers, and employees, and link manager input to employee pay code groups.
ss: Employee Calendars in PeopleXD Workforce Management displays a 12-month work schedule for individual employees, showing configured pay codes, absences, and actions requiring approval or rejection. Use this guide to learn how to access the calendar screen for employees, managers, and administrators, manage absences and approvals, and configure pay code settings and user permissions. Open this document when you need to view or manage employee schedules, approve or reject hours and absences, or set up calendar configurations and access controls for different user roles.
sl: This user guide documents the Employee Calendars feature within PeopleXD Workforce Management, a system used by Access Group for scheduling and absence management. The guide explains how to access and navigate the Employee Calendar Screen, which displays a employee's 12-month work schedule with colour-coded work codes and pending actions requiring approval or rejection, accessible through different dashboards depending on user role: employees access it via the My Calendar widget on the Employee Dashboard, managers via the My Team widget or Workforce Management Dashboard, and administrators via the WFM Admin Dashboard. Key functionality described includes the Actions button which enables processes such as Person Absences, Add Absence, and Team Calendar viewing, along with controls for edit and delete permissions, the ability to roll back weeks and view historical hours, and filtering options to display leaver or unprocessed leaver employees. The screen provides filtering capabilities by pay code, work schedule, training assignments, and events, with options to view different time periods using year and month dropdowns. Users can approve or reject hours directly on the calendar grid by hovering over highlighted dates, or access the detailed Approvals screen by clicking the Edit button. The guide also covers the Employee Calendar Configuration Screen, which includes Pay Code Settings and role-specific access levels for administrators, managers, and employees, as well as menu profile imports and linking manager input to employee pay code groups.

t: Entering Timesheets
s:
# Summary: Entering Timesheets User Guide

This guide teaches users how to enter, manage, and submit timesheets in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system. 

**Key topics covered:**

- **Accessing the system** — How to open the Timesheet Input screen
- **Understanding the interface** — A detailed breakdown of seven sections on the timesheet screen, including person information, calendar navigation, colour codes, pay codes, balances, summaries, and clocking information
- **Basic timesheet operations** — How to add new timesheet entries, update existing entries, delete entries, add reason codes, and add comments to entries
- **Recording employee hours** — How to add, edit, and delete individual clockings (time records), plus how to copy previous week's data and add comments to clockings
- **Submitting claims** — How employees submit timesheet claims, add comments to claims, recall submitted claims, enter retrospective claims, and view submission summaries before final acknowledgement
- **Configuration options** — Basic menu settings for widget access and employee menu permissions

After completing this guide, users will be able to successfully record employee time, manage timesheet data, and submit timesheets and claims through the PeopleXD system.
ss: Entering timesheets in PeopleXD Workforce Management allows employees to record their hours, leave, overtime, and attendance data through the Employee Dashboard. This guide covers how to access the Timesheet Input screen, create and edit timesheet entries, manage employee clockings, and submit timesheet claims. Open this document if you need step-by-step instructions on recording hours, adding reason codes or comments to entries, copying previous week data, or submitting attendance claims for approval. It's essential for any employee using PeopleXD who needs to log their time or manage their timesheet submissions.
sl: This user guide for PeopleXD Workforce Management explains how employees access and use the Timesheet Input screen to record, edit, and submit timesheet and attendance data from the Employee Dashboard. Employees can reach the Timesheet Input screen through three pathways: selecting "View Timesheets" from the Calendar Widget's 3-dot menu, choosing "Timesheet Input" via the Actions button on the Work Week Widget, or clicking the "Input Time" button on the Timesheet Claims Widget. The document provides detailed coverage of the seven sections that comprise the Timesheet Input screen, including Person Information (which displays employee name, photo, and optional fields such as Department, Cost Centre, Job Title, Location, Organisation, and Work Group), Calendar and Navigation controls, Colour Codes, Pay Code Section, Balances Section, Summary Section, and Clocking Section. The guide walks users through core timesheet management tasks including adding new timesheet entries, updating existing entries, deleting entries, adding reason codes and comments, managing employee clockings (adding, editing, and deleting), and copying previous week data. It also addresses Employee Timesheet Claims processes, including how to submit claims, recall claims, enter retrospective claims, review submission summaries, and provide acknowledgement before final submission. The document is designed specifically for employees in organisations using PeopleXD who need to record hours worked, annual leave, overtime, and other attendance data on a weekly basis, with configuration options that allow organisations to customise which fields and features are available.

t: Exception Management
s:
# Exception Management Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage time and attendance exceptions within the PeopleXD HR system's clocking environment.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
- How to access the Exception Management screen through the Time Exceptions Widget on the Manager Dashboard or Workforce Management Dashboard
- How to view exceptions at a glance, including those requiring action and those that are auto-approved

**Managing Exceptions:**
- How to view and work with exceptions across three different tabs:
  - **Action Required Tab** – for exceptions needing your decision
  - **Auto Approved Tab** – for exceptions that have been automatically approved
  - **All Exceptions Tab** – for viewing all exceptions
- How to recode exceptions (reassign them to different pay codes)
- How to approve or reject exceptions that require your decision

**Configuration:**
- How to set up Exception Management to suit your organization's needs, including:
  - Accessing the Time Exceptions Configuration Screen
  - Configuring access based on organizational role/group or transactional rostered team area
  - Creating personalized pay code groups for recoding exceptions
  - Setting options like whether to include historical exceptions in your view

**Dashboard Setup:**
- How to configure and position the Time Exceptions Widget on different dashboard tabs for quick access

The guide also notes important technical considerations around how decimal values are converted to hours and minutes for display.
ss: Exception Management in Workforce Management handles time-based exceptions that occur in a clocking environment, allowing managers to review, approve, reject, or recode exceptions from a single screen. You would use this guide to learn how to access the Time Exceptions Widget on your Manager Dashboard, navigate the Exception Management screen's tabs (Action Required, Auto Approved, and All Exceptions), and take actions like approving exceptions or recoding them to different pay codes. Open this document if you need to understand how to configure exception management access based on your organization role or team area, or if you need step-by-step instructions for managing employee time exceptions within your payroll period.
sl: This Exception Management User Guide provides comprehensive documentation for managing time and attendance exceptions within a workforce management system accessed through the Time Exceptions Widget on the Manager Dashboard or Workforce Management Dashboard. The document covers the core Exceptions screen, which displays a centralized listing of exceptions with supporting information including employee details, roster and clock times, dates, pay codes, calculated hours, and required actions, all filterable by search, period selection (Current, Historical, or Both), and week navigation. Users can take actions on exceptions through three distinct tabs—the Action Required tab for exceptions needing attention, the Auto Approved tab for pre-approved exceptions, and the All Exceptions tab—with specific capabilities to recode exceptions by selecting alternative pay codes from pre-determined lists and to approve or reject exceptions with optional comment fields. The guide details configuration setup accessed via the Time Exceptions Configuration Screen, including Employee Information settings and a toggle for Include Historical Exceptions, along with two access configuration options: Option 1 based on Organisation Role/Group and Option 2 based on Transactional Rostered Team Area. Additionally, the document explains Recode Options using Personalised Pay Code Groups and provides instructions for adding Exception Recode Groups, while noting that decimal values are automatically converted to hours and minutes for display, though Monetary and Unit Values cannot be managed through this screen due to conversion issues. This guide is designed for managers and workforce administrators who need to monitor, approve, reject, and recode employee time exceptions in a clocking environment.

t: External Absence Interface
s:
# External Absence Interface Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to use PeopleXD's External Absence Interface to import absence, shift, and work pattern data from external systems into the Workforce Management (WFM) module.

**Key capabilities covered:**

- **Loading absence data** — importing employee absences from third-party systems into WFM for reporting purposes and to enable calculation of statutory and occupational absence payments in PeopleXD Payroll

- **Loading shift and schedule data** — importing work schedules and shift information for employees who have absences recorded, ensuring proper scheduling coordination

- **File format and structure** — understanding the required filename conventions, file types, and data layout for three types of files:
  - Absence files
  - Shift files  
  - Pattern/schedule files

- **Validation rules** — learning the critical constraints and validation assumptions that apply when loading each type of data, including how these interfaces can work together (integrated) or separately (non-integrated)

- **Data mapping** — understanding how columns in external files map to fields in the WFM system

- **File loading process** — how to upload files, load information into the system, handle manual loads, and review error logs when issues occur

- **System configuration** — setting up the necessary configuration in PeopleHub and the interface itself to enable the data imports

The guide is designed to support customers with varied requirements for importing absence and scheduling data from their existing systems into PeopleXD.
ss: The External Absence Interface enables you to load absence data, shift types, and work patterns from third-party systems into Workforce Management (WFM) to support reporting, absence payment calculations in PeopleXD Payroll, and accurate timesheet processing. The interface accepts absence data in CSV format (.dat files) with specific file naming conventions and supports multiple data formats including daily records or date-range entries, with built-in validation checks for employee existence, mandatory fields, date formats, and pay code validity. You would use this document when setting up integration between an external HR or payroll system and WFM, or when configuring how absence and shift information flows into your system for statutory and occupational absence payment calculations.
sl: This user guide documents the External Absence Interface for Workforce Management, a system designed to import absence data, shift information, and work patterns from third-party external vendors to satisfy varied customer requirements such as absence reporting, statutory and occupational absence payment calculations in PeopleXD Payroll, and ensuring correct work schedules align with recorded absences. The document describes three main integration interfaces: the Absence Interface, which accepts CSV files with a .dat extension using a defined filename convention (default prefix 'ABS_') and contains employee number, appointment ID, absence type, pay code, and date fields; the Shift Interface that loads associated shift types with validation for filename, file layout, and critical constraints; and the Pattern Interface for daily work patterns, which operates non-integrated or integrated with the absence interface depending on configuration. The guide provides comprehensive validation rules that flag individual record errors while continuing processing, including checks for employee existence, mandatory field completion, correct date and time formats, record type (Insert, Update, or Delete), and pay code validity, with all issues logged to an error table for user intervention. End users implementing this interface—particularly Workforce Management administrators managing absence data loads and payroll integrations—will use the Configuration sections covering PeopleHub Configuration and Interface Configuration settings, along with the File Load, Load Information, and Manual Load & Error Log functionality to manage data imports. The document has been updated as recently as September 2024 with modifications to the Absence File Layout section, specifically adding M/O (Mandatory/Optional) designation values.

t: Flexitime Calculation
s:
# FlexiTime Calculation Guide — Summary

This guide teaches users how to set up and manage a flexitime system in the PeopleXD HR platform. After reading it, users will understand how to:

**System Setup (5 configuration steps):**
1. **Create Pay Codes** — Set up four mandatory pay codes that track flexitime activity: Positive Flexitime (when employees work over their default hours), Negative Flexitime (when they work under), Coretime Infringement (for absences during required core hours), and Flexi Leave (for taking time off based on accumulated flexitime). Users learn which codes should be payroll-related and how to configure their balance effects.

2. **Configure Control Parameters** — Enable the necessary flexitime calculation settings and assign the pay codes created in Step 1 to the appropriate system fields. Users also learn how to specify what pay code should be used when an employee is absent for an entire day, and whether to flag core time infringements on full-day absences.

3. **Define Work Patterns** — Create flexitime rules for different types of workers and days, which the system applies to clock in/out times to calculate flexitime balances.

4. **Set Up Shift Types** — Configure shift categories for the flexitime system.

5. **Assign to Employees** — Link employees to the appropriate flexitime configuration.

**System Operations:**
- How flexitime is calculated and tracked
- How to view flexitime balances
- How to generate and read flexitime transaction reports

The guide essentially covers the complete workflow for implementing and administering a flexible working hours system within PeopleXD.
ss: Flexitime Calculation in Workforce Management (WFM) covers how to set up and configure flexible working hour rules for your organisation. This guide walks you through five essential setup steps: creating mandatory pay codes (Positive Flexitime, Negative Flexitime, Coretime Infringement, and Flexi Leave), configuring control parameters, defining work patterns with core time and flexible time bands, assigning shift types, and enrolling employees in the flexitime system. Open this document when you're implementing flexitime for the first time, updating work practices, or need to understand how flexitime balances and calculations are generated. You'll also find information on viewing flexitime transaction reports and managing employee flexitime balances.
sl: This user guide explains the reference data and configuration required to set up and operate the Flexitime system within Access Limited's Workforce Management platform. The document covers five essential setup steps: creating four mandatory pay codes (Positive Flexitime, Negative Flexitime, Coretime Infringement, and Flexi Leave), configuring Control Parameters by enabling package calculation settings and assigning pay codes to appropriate fields, establishing Work Patterns that define flexi rules and time ranges (Lapsed, Core Time, and Normal), setting up Shift Types, and assigning the flexitime configuration to employees. The guide details specific configuration steps such as accessing the System Params Menu to create flexi work patterns, filling in General Details fields like Pattern Code, Default Hours (in decimal format), Default Start and End Times, and FlexiTime Hours selections with sequence numbers and time band types. It addresses common scenarios including how full-day absences are handled (typically as negative flexitime unless a different pay code is specified via the Day Absence Code field), how to control whether Coretime Infringements appear on days of absence, and how to set up Business Absences on the Flexitime 2 section of Control Parameters. The document also covers the Calculation of Flexitime, Balance reporting, and Transaction Reports, making it essential for administrators configuring flexitime for the first time or when organizational work practices change.

t: Generate Timesheets
s:
# Summary of "Generate Timesheets" User Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the PeopleXD HR system's timesheet generation functionality within the Workforce Management (WFM) module. 

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Retrieve hours** from the system and understand the process for pulling timesheet data
- **Transfer hours** between systems or to payroll
- **Navigate key screens** used in timesheet management, including screens for viewing employees to be transferred, payroll hours, and historical records
- **Handle errors and warnings** that may occur during the retrieve hours process, such as issues with employees not on payroll
- **Sign off and approve timesheets**, including approving, rejecting, or deleting hours
- **Add and view comments** on timesheets for communication purposes
- **Use supervisor enquiry functions** to review employee timesheet data
- **Configure the system** for timesheet generation, including setting up supervisor enquiry screens, contact type configurations, and handling special scenarios like timesheets for employees leaving the organization

The guide provides both procedural instructions for performing these tasks and technical configuration information for system administrators setting up the timesheet functionality.
ss: Generating timesheets in WFM V28 involves converting Time & Attendance data into Payroll Hours through a two-step process: retrieving hours based on configured payroll rules, then transferring those hours to PeopleXD Payroll. Open this guide when you need to access the Generate Timesheets feature from the WFM Admin Dashboard or Workforce Management Dashboard in Portal, view payroll hour details before transfer, or troubleshoot errors during timesheet processing. The guide covers how to retrieve hours for specific calendars, transfer converted data to payroll, approve or reject hours, and handle common processing errors.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Generate Timesheets feature in Access Group's Workforce Management (WFM) V28 system, providing instructions on retrieving and transferring payroll hours through the Portal interface. The guide covers two main processes: retrieving hours, which converts Time & Attendance timesheets into Payroll Hours based on configured payroll rules, and transferring hours, which sends Payroll Hours to PeopleXD Payroll or creates interface files. Users access these functions by navigating to either the Workforce Management Dashboard or the WFM Admin Dashboard and selecting Generate Timesheets, where they can view Time & Attendance calendars, monitor process stages and statuses, and manage company-specific hours. The document addresses error handling and resolution, including a table of process errors, configuration for warnings related to employees not on payroll, and guidance on signing off hours. It also describes multiple functional screens including the Employees to be Transferred Screen, Payroll Hours Screen, View History Screen, Supervisor Enquiry Screens, and View Timesheets screen, which allows users to approve, reject, add comments, or delete hours. The guide includes detailed configuration sections covering general setup, menu options, contact type configuration for Supervisor Enquiry, and special handling for leavers and employees not on payroll. This resource is primarily used by payroll administrators and supervisors who need to generate timesheets within the PeopleXD Portal environment for streamlined payroll integration.

t: Generate Timesheets Parallel Run
s:
# Summary of "Generate Timesheets Parallel Run" Guide

This configuration guide teaches users how to set up and use the **Parallel Run feature** in PeopleXD's Generate Timesheets system within the Workforce Management module.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Concept:**
The guide explains how to use Parallel Run mode, which allows you to test and validate the new Portal version of Generate Timesheets by running it alongside your existing back office system. This lets you compare results between the two systems before fully switching over to the Portal version.

**Key Capabilities:**

- **Access and setup** — How to navigate to the Parallel Run feature, access menus, and enable the functionality through the system dashboard
- **Step-by-step process** — An 8-step workflow covering:
  - Accessing the Generate Timesheets screen
  - Running the process in back office
  - Viewing timesheet periods and company displays
  - Transferring hours between systems
  - Reviewing transfer details to identify discrepancies
  - Completing the parallel run and generating reports

- **Comparison and verification** — How to review parallel tables and reporting tools to spot any differences or errors that occurred when hours were transferred between the old back office system and the new Portal system

**Who Should Use It:**
Particularly valuable for organizations migrating from the back office timesheet feature to the Portal version, especially those processing large volumes of hours, as it provides a safety check before going live with the new system.
ss: The Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility in Workforce Management (WFM) allows you to test and validate the migration of timesheet processing from back office to Portal before going live. Use this guide when you need to compare parallel runs against existing back office Live Runs, verify that hours are transferring correctly without errors, and review employee and payroll data before final migration. This is especially important for organizations with large volumes of hours being transferred or those moving from the previous back office feature to the Portal version. The parallel mode lets you run validation checks per WFM company while keeping results in backup tables for analysis, with no impact to live operations.
sl: This configuration guide explains how to set up and use the Generate Timesheets Parallel Run facility within the Workforce Management system, which allows users to validate the migration of timesheet processing from the back office to the Portal environment. The document covers the complete parallel run process through nine sequential steps, beginning with the Generate Timesheets Screen on Portal and progressing through running Generate Timesheets in Back Office, reviewing Portal Screen Periods, displaying company information, transferring hours, reviewing transferred details, completing the parallel run, and finally conducting parallel run reporting. Parallel Run enables users to compare results between the new Portal version and existing back office Live Runs, verify migration accuracy, and identify any discrepancies in hour transfers before committing to live production operation, making it particularly valuable for sites processing large volumes of hours. The system provides significant operational benefits including employee and hours summary views before payroll transfer, continuous user feedback with estimated processing duration and completion notifications, visibility of blocker exceptions, and background task-driven processing that conserves administrative resources. Key features of Parallel Mode include per-company enablement for organizations with multiple WFM companies, validation of previously migrated calendars and periods without impacting live mode or marking employees as leavers, and storage of parallel run details in backup tables for comprehensive analysis and review. This guide is intended for payroll and workforce management administrators who are transitioning from the back office Generate Timesheets feature to the Portal version and need to ensure data integrity and accuracy throughout the migration process.

t: Geofence Clocking
s:
# Geofence Clocking Guide Summary

This guide teaches HR administrators and managers how to set up and manage geofence clocking in the PeopleXD Native Mobile App. Geofencing allows employees to clock in and out based on their physical location rather than manual entry.

**Key topics covered include:**

- **What geofencing is** — an explanation of the technology and its purpose in time tracking

- **Setting up geofences** — how to create and configure geographic boundaries for clocking locations, including how to access the admin screen and create new geofences

- **Managing geofences** — how to edit existing geofences, deactivate them, and assign criteria groups to control who can use specific geofences and under what conditions

- **Assigning employees** — how to assign groups of employees to geofences based on criteria, and how to view which employees are assigned to each geofence

- **Managing overrides** — how to handle exceptions to geofencing rules

- **Manager views** — what managers can see including time exceptions flagged by the system, exceptions shown on a map, and integration with workforce management dashboards

- **Employee experience** — what employees see in the mobile app when clocking in/out with geofencing, including location permissions, historical clocking records, and any restrictions or messages

- **Administrative access** — how to assign geofence clocking permissions to specific admin users and update admin profiles

The guide also includes a checklist for implementation and guidance on restriction levels that can be applied to geofences.
ss: Geofencing Clocking uses location-based virtual boundaries to control when employees can clock in and out via the PeopleXD Native App. Administrators configure geofences by defining a specific location's coordinates and radius (typically 80+ metres) through the WFM Admin Dashboard, then assign criteria groups and manage which employees can clock in within that perimeter. This guide covers the complete setup process, how managers view time exceptions and clocking data, and how employees interact with geofence restrictions on their mobile devices. Open this document if you're setting up location-based clocking controls, managing geofence configurations, or need to understand how geofencing affects employee clocking behavior.
sl: This document is a configuration guide for the Geofence Clocking feature within Access Group's PeopleXD Native App, designed to help administrators set up and manage location-based employee clocking. Geofencing establishes a virtual boundary around a specific location by defining latitude and longitude coordinates along with a required radius in meters, allowing employees to clock in and out only when their device is within the designated perimeter. The guide covers the complete setup process, including how to access the Mobile App Clocking – Geofence Admin Screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard by navigating to WFM Configuration, creating geofences, managing overrides, and assigning criteria groups to geofences. Administrators can edit geofences, view assigned employees, deactivate geofences, and manage restriction levels, while the system also provides manager views through the Time Exceptions Widget in the Manager Dashboard and the Workforce Management - Time Exceptions Screen for monitoring clocking issues. The document addresses practical implementation details such as location accuracy factors (GPS chip quality, cellular network, Wi-Fi, battery saving mode, and weather interference), recommending a minimum geofence radius of 80 meters to account for these variables. This guide is intended for system administrators configuring geofences and managers monitoring employee clockings, though it explicitly notes that geofence clocking applies only to the Native App and not to Portal or mobile web app clocking. The document also outlines employee functionality, including how users clock in and out, grant device location access, view historical clockings, and receive system messages related to geofence restrictions.

t: Grosvenor Clockings
s:
# Summary of "Grosvenor Clockings" Guide

This guide teaches users how to integrate Grosvenor's clocking system with the PeopleXD (XD) HR platform.

After reading this guide, users will understand:

**Core Integration Capabilities:**
- How to manage employee badges within the system
- How to synchronize clock times and attendance data between Grosvenor and the XD platform
- How data flows from Grosvenor into XD
- How to access employee data from XD and send it to clocking terminals
- How to configure terminal groups and endpoints

**Technical Setup:**
- How the authentication system works (OAuth 2 Client Credentials authentication using Client ID and Client Secret)
- How to set up and configure the web service application within XD
- What success and error codes indicate during integration processes

**Operational Features:**
- How to use badge numbers and person numbers in the system
- How to batch load clock data into XD
- How to use the admin screen for managing the integration
- How to synchronize distribution groups (both initial synchronization and ongoing distribution)
- How badge information is synchronized incrementally between systems
- Badge details and formatting requirements

The guide provides both high-level overview information and technical implementation details needed to set up and manage the Grosvenor clocking integration with PeopleXD.
ss: Grosvenor Clocking Integration connects your Grosvenor clocking system with the PeopleXD (XD) platform to automate employee badge management, clock times, and transaction flow between systems. This guide covers web service configuration, authentication setup using OAuth 2 Client Credentials, and how to enable specific clocking endpoints in your XD environment. Open this document when you need to set up the integration between Grosvenor and XD, configure web service privileges, or troubleshoot clocking data transfers using the provided success and error codes.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Grosvenor Clocking Integration, which describes how to integrate Grosvenor's employee clocking system with the XD workforce management platform. The guide covers five primary functional areas: Employee Badge Management, Clock Times Management, transaction flow from Grosvenor to XD, accessing and pushing employee data between systems, and Badge Web Service configuration including terminal groups and endpoints. The document explains that authentication uses OAuth 2 Client Credentials, requiring a Client ID and Client Secret obtained from the tenant's administration, with an access token required for each API request to endpoints at https://api.corehr.com. Configuration involves connecting to XD Web Services through the Web Service Application Setup screen, where administrators must add an application, enable specific web services (including /v1/clocking/batch/clocks POST, /v1/clocking/groups GET, /v1/clocking/badge GET, and /v1/image/user/:person GET), and unmask credentials to provide to the integrator. The system returns standard HTTP success and error codes—Code 200 for successful acceptance, Code 400 for transient issues where Grosvenor will retry, and Code 500 for sustained errors that halt delivery temporarily. Key operational considerations include pre-assigning badge numbers to personnel, agreeing on data formats in advance with the XP Project Team, validating integration through user acceptance testing and parallel runs, and reviewing transferred details via employee timesheets or Manager Team Scheduler to identify errors visible on the Clocking Admin Screen. This guide is primarily for system administrators and integration specialists responsible for configuring and maintaining the Grosvenor-to-XD clocking synchronization.

t: Leave Outage Periods
s:
# Summary: Leave Outage Periods Guide

This configuration guide teaches users how to set up and manage **Leave Outage Periods** in the PeopleXD HR system — a feature that blocks employees from requesting certain types of leave during specified dates.

## What you'll learn:

**Core Concept:** You can create "Outage Schemes" that prevent staff from submitting leave requests during blackout periods (such as Christmas or other company-defined dates). For example, if you want to stop annual leave requests over the Christmas period, you can pre-configure a date range, and any leave falling within or overlapping those dates will be automatically blocked when employees try to submit requests.

**Key Points:**
- Leave requests can only be blocked at the submission stage for employees; managers can still manually record leave for employees during outage periods
- Outage schemes can be applied at three levels: company-wide, work group, or individual employee — with employee-level settings overriding work group settings, which override company-level settings
- Multiple outage schemes can be created to cover different scenarios

**Practical Tasks:**
- How to create new outage schemes with specific names and date ranges
- How to maintain (edit) and delete existing outage scheme details
- How to assign outage schemes at the company, work group, and employee levels
- How to enable the outage configuration widget in the system
- Language and technical considerations for the system

The guide also includes real-world examples and important technical considerations for implementation.
ss: Leave outage periods in PeopleXD Workforce Management prevent employees from submitting leave requests during blocked date ranges, such as over the Christmas period. This configuration guide covers how to create outage schemes, define the specific dates and leave types to block, and assign schemes at company, work group, or employee level—with employee-level settings overriding lower-level configurations. Open this document when you need to set up or manage blackout periods for leave requests, configure which leave types are affected, or enable the outage widget on your dashboard.
sl: This document is a configuration guide for the Leave Outage Period functionality in PeopleXD Workforce Management, explaining how to set up and manage systems that block employees from requesting specific leave types during designated periods. The guide covers the complete process of creating outage schemes by navigating to relevant menu areas, entering an Outage Scheme name, selecting an associated Pay Code Group (which contains the leave types to be blocked), and then maintaining outage scheme details by specifying Date From, Date To, and Reason fields that define when leave requests will be restricted. The document describes how to assign these schemes at three hierarchical levels—Company Level via System Parameters > Reference A-C > Company Parameters, Work Group Level, and Employee Level—where employee-level settings override work group settings, which in turn override company-level settings, allowing for granular control over leave blocking policies. Additional configuration tasks include enabling the Balance Outages widget on dashboards by accessing Dashboard Configuration, searching for the widget, and selecting the appropriate Menu Profile for administrator access. The document addresses the specific problem it solves: preventing employees from submitting leave requests that fall within or span defined date ranges (such as the Christmas period), while noting that managers retain the ability to record leave for employees even during outage periods. The guide also references underlying system components including Pay Code Groupings maintained through Oracle Forms and Reference K-P, as well as important considerations about how the system stores multiple date ranges per scheme and displays reason messages to employees when they attempt to submit blocked requests.

t: Leave Requests and Absences
s:
# Summary: Leave Requests and Absences Guide

This guide teaches users how to manage leave and absences within the PeopleXD HR system. Here's what you'll learn:

## Key Topics Covered:

**Understanding the Basics**
- What leave requests and absences are, including different types of leave available
- How leave requests move through an approval workflow
- The difference between leave requests and absences
- How leave balances work in the system

**Managing Leave Balances**
- How to access and view your leave balance information
- How to assign new leave balances to employees
- How to make balance adjustments when needed
- How to view what employees are entitled to
- How to recalculate balances, edit balance settings, and deactivate balances when necessary

**For Employees (Self Service)**
- How to check your available leave balances
- How to view your own leave requests and absences
- How to view leave and absences on a calendar or by work week
- How to see when your co-workers are on leave or absent
- How to submit a new leave request
- How to upload supporting documents with your request
- How to edit or cancel leave requests you've already submitted

**For Managers (Self Service)**

# Summary: Irish Civil Service Annual Leave Carryover User Guide

This guide explains how to set up and use the Irish Civil Service Annual Leave Carryover feature in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system.

## What You'll Learn

**Legislative Background:**
- The rules introduced in January 2024 under the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 and the Workplace Relations Act 2015
- How Irish Civil Service annual leave is now managed in terms of carryover provisions

**Key Concepts:**
- Annual leave is divided into two types: statutory and non-statutory
- Statutory leave cannot normally be carried over (except in exceptional circumstances, handled manually)
- Non-statutory leave that isn't used must be carried over to the following year and must be used within that year
- This carryover can repeat annually for unused non-statutory leave

**The Priority Order for Taking Leave:**
When employees take time off, leave is deducted in this specific order:
1. Carried-over statutory leave (exceptional circumstances only)
2. Carried-over non-statutory leave from the previous year
3. Statutory leave earned in the current year
4. Non-statutory leave earned in the current year

**Configuration Skills:**
- How to enable the Irish Civil Service Leave Carry Over Rules in the system's Balance Configuration
- How to set rounding rules for statutory days for part-time employees
- Where to access and grant permissions for this functionality

The guide includes practical examples demonstrating how the legislation works in practice.
ss: Annual Leave Carryover in PeopleXD Workforce Management handles the Irish Civil Service legislation for managing unused leave, which distinguishes between statutory and non-statutory annual leave that can be carried over year to year. Open this guide when you need to configure carryover rules for Irish Civil Service employees, set up rounding options for part-time staff, or understand the order in which different types of leave are consumed. The document provides step-by-step configuration instructions within the Balance Configuration screens and includes a worked example of how the carryover rules apply in practice.
sl: This user guide explains how to configure and implement Irish Civil Service Annual Leave Carryover legislation in PeopleXD Workforce Management, a system used by Irish Civil Service organizations to manage employee leave. The document provides a comprehensive overview of the legislation introduced in January 2024 under Part 3 of the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997 (as amended) and the Workplace Relations Act 2015, which distinguishes between statutory and non-statutory annual leave with different carryover rules for each category. The configuration process involves accessing the Balance Configuration tile from the WFM Admin Dashboard, locating the Irish Civil Service Carry Over tab within the Balance Configuration screens, and enabling the feature through the "Use Irish Civil Service Leave Carry Over Rules" toggle, which then displays all balance periods for that balance. The guide covers specific configuration fields including the Statutory Days Rounding Rules for Part-Time Employees section, where administrators can select rounding types (Up to the nearest, Down to the nearest, or Nearest) applied to either days or hours, and input the corresponding rounding day and hour values to optimize the split between statutory and non-statutory leave. Within the Balance Calendar Periods section, users must enter the Irish Civil Service Statutory Days (defaulting to 20 days) and Irish Civil Service Statutory Hours (defaulting to 160 hours) for each period, allowing the system to properly track and manage the carryover of unused non-statutory leave from year to year while ensuring statutory leave is taken in the correct prescribed order. This document is intended for PeopleXD administrators responsible for configuring leave management systems in Irish Civil Service organizations and serves as both a reference guide and step-by-step configuration manual for implementing compliant annual leave carryover processes.
