# Summary of "Operational Demand for Roster" User Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the Operational Demand feature within the PeopleXD HR system's Workforce Management Rostering module.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Configuration and Setup:**
- Access and enable the Operational Demand Configuration Screen
- Create and configure grid templates to visualize demand data
- Apply conditional formatting to grid templates for better visual clarity
- Display events on grids and assign grid templates to specific teams
- Create formulas to calculate operational demand metrics
- Set up team mappings to link teams to demand data
- Create blended lines (combined data views from multiple sources)

**Data Management:**
- View and export operational demand grids to analyze workforce requirements
- Delete formulas, team mappings, and blended lines when no longer needed
- Access and manage menu options, including importing capabilities

**Reporting and Access Control:**
- Generate insight reports based on operational demand data
- Manage different access levels for administrators versus managers within the system

In essence, the guide covers how to configure the system to display, calculate, and track operational (staffing) demand requirements, then visualize and report on this data to support workforce planning and scheduling decisions.
ss: Operational Demand is a Workforce Management feature in PeopleXD that lets administrators configure and display data grids on the roster details screen to help managers plan staffing requirements. The feature involves setting up grid templates, formulas, team mappings, and blended lines in the WFM Admin Dashboard, then assigning these grids to specific teams. Managers can then view the operational demand data directly when working on rosters for the following weeks. Open this guide when you need to import data, create grid templates, assign them to teams, or enable the feature for your roster users.
sl: This user guide document contains comprehensive instructions for implementing and managing Operational Demand, an enhancement to People XD's Workforce Management Rostering feature that enables administrators to configure and display data grids to assist managers with staffing requirements. The document covers four main configuration components: Grid Templates (which display imported and calculated data), Formulas (used in calculations), Team Mappings (assigning grids to teams), and Blended Lines (combining data sources), each with detailed creation and deletion procedures. Key processes include accessing the Operational Demand Configuration screen through the WFM Admin Dashboard via WFM Configuration menu, creating new grid templates with unique Template Code and Template Description fields, and enabling the feature through the Roster General Settings tile by toggling the Operational Demand Grid option. The guide addresses configuration tasks such as conditional formatting for grid display, assigning grid templates to specific teams, exporting operational demand grids, and viewing grids on the roster details screen. Administrative setup requires importing menu options for menu security-driven access, while managers subsequently use the configured grids within the roster details interface to view staffing data for upcoming weeks. The document also includes sections on Insight Reporting integration and differentiated access levels for both administrators and managers, making it essential reading for workforce management teams implementing this rostering enhancement within the People XD system.

t: Publish Roster Less Contract Hours
s:
# Summary: Publish Roster Less Contract Hours Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the **Publish Roster Less Contract Hours** feature in the PeopleXD Roster system.

## What the Feature Does

The feature prevents you from publishing a weekly roster if any employees are scheduled to work fewer hours than their contracted hours. When you attempt to publish a roster, the system automatically checks all employees and compares their total rostered hours (across all team areas they work in) against their contracted hours.

## Key Functionality

- **Warning System**: If an employee in their home team area is rostered for less than their contracted hours, a warning message appears before publication is allowed
- **Drill-Down Capability**: You can view and investigate individual employees who are causing the warning
- **Overall Roster Total Column**: A new column displays each employee's total rostered hours across all team areas they work in, making it easy to spot those who are under-rostered or approaching overtime rates when working across multiple teams

## What You'll Learn

The guide covers:
- How the feature works and when to use it
- Step-by-step instructions for publishing a roster and handling contract hour warnings (with a worked example)
- How to configure the feature in admin settings, including enabling/disabling it and setting up the relevant display columns
- How to set up validation rules

After reading, you'll be able to configure this safety check and navigate the warning system when publishing rosters.
ss: The Publish Roster Less Contract Hours feature in Roster prevents publishing a weekly schedule if any employees are rostered for fewer hours than their contracted hours. When you attempt to publish a Team Area, the system checks all employees assigned to that area and displays a warning if anyone falls short of their contract hours, even if they're scheduled across multiple Team Areas. You'll open this guide when setting up or troubleshooting roster validation rules, configuring admin settings to enable the feature (via the cp_publish_val_contract parameter), or learning how to use the Overall Rostered Hours column to review employee scheduling compliance.
sl: This user guide for Roster V28 provides comprehensive documentation of the Publish Roster Less Contract Hours feature, which prevents roster publication when any employees are rostered for fewer hours than their contracted hours. The feature operates by checking employees when their Home Team Area is published and considers all hours worked across all Team Areas in the calculation. When a discrepancy is detected, a Roster V Contract Hours warning message appears on screen, allowing users to drill into affected employees by navigating through Quick Jump to Roster Details, clicking Actions, selecting Publish Week, and then reviewing the Roster V Contract Hours warning screen that lists all non-compliant employees. The system enables further investigation and adjustment via the Roster Details screen, which displays automatically filtered to show only employees causing the warning, and provides an Overall Roster Total column that sums hours across all Team Areas to help identify overtime and under-rostering situations. Configuration requires three key admin settings: the cp_publish_val_contract parameter (set to 'Y' to activate validation), accessed via Site Manager Admin Settings with keyword search 'when publishing the roster'; the cp_roster_show_col_total parameter (set to 'Y' to display the hours column), found by searching 'display total hours'; and the cp_roster_detcol parameter to specify which Roster Details Tab displays the Overall Rostered Hours values by entering 'OVERALL_ROSTER_TOTAL'. This document is designed for roster administrators and managers in Access Group systems who need to configure and manage the contract hours validation feature to ensure compliant scheduling practices.

t: Roster Absences
s:
# Roster Absences Guide Summary

This guide teaches users how to manage and configure absences within the PeopleXD HR system's Roster module. Here's what you'll learn:

## Main Topics Covered:

**Understanding Roster Absences:**
- How absences work within the Roster system, including how they're calculated based on work patterns and day duration
- The concept that all balances in Roster are tracked in hours rather than days, since schedules can vary

**Unrostered Bookings (Absences Before Schedules Are Created):**
- How to use Unrostered Bookings to record leave and absences before employee schedules have been finalized
- The complete leave request workflow: how employees submit requests and how managers receive and handle them
- How to view contract hours at different levels (employee, work group, and company level)
- Different types of absences you can record: absences on work days, absences on rest days, absences with specific start and end times, and part-day absences

**Absence Calculation Methods:**
- Two different part-day absence calculation methods: standard calculation and retail calculation
- How absence duration is calculated based on scheduled pattern times

**System Configuration:**
- How to enable and configure Unrostered Bookings functionality in your system
- How to set up absence work patterns
- How to configure absence start and end times

The guide is essential for any Roster environment since schedules may not exist when leave requests are submitted.
ss: Roster Absences covers how to manage employee time off in the WFM Roster system, particularly for absences booked before employee schedules are created. It explains the Unrostered Bookings feature, which allows employees to request leave on rest days and unrostered dates, and includes configuration steps for enabling this functionality. Open this guide when setting up absence management in Roster, processing leave requests from employees, or configuring how part-day and full-day absences are calculated based on employee contract hours.
sl: This user guide documents the roster absences functionality within the Access Group's WFM Roster system, specifically covering how to manage employee absences and leaves both on scheduled work days and on unrostered rest days. The document explains the Unrostered Bookings feature, which allows employees and managers to submit leave requests and record absences before employee schedules are created, addressing a key operational need since rosters may not exist when leave is requested. It describes two main processes for handling unrostered bookings: the Leave Request Process (where employees use the My Requests widget to submit requests through steps including selecting leave type, entering start and end dates, adding reasons and comments, then clicking Submit) and the Absence Detail Screen Process for direct absence entry. The guide covers critical configuration tasks administrators must perform, including switching on Unrostered Bookings functionality, allowing the feature through permission settings, creating absence work patterns, and setting absence start and end times, with specific sections for viewing contract hours at employee, work group, and company levels. Important considerations outlined include that unrostered bookings only apply when all days between start and end dates are rest days, that balances are tracked in hours rather than days due to varying daily durations in Roster, and that part-day absences cannot be submitted by employees for unrostered days since work times are unknown. The document also addresses scenarios requiring manual recalculation, such as when contract hours change midway through an absence, and explains different calculation methods available for part-day absences in both standard and retail environments.

t: Roster Attributes
s:
# Summary of "Roster Attributes" Guide

This guide teaches Team Managers how to use the Roster Attributes feature in PeopleXD's HR system to manage and organize employee scheduling information.

## What You'll Learn

**Understanding Attributes:**
- What attributes are (labels applied to an employee's work pattern that identify the job or task they're scheduled to complete)
- Examples of attributes include job roles like "Cashier," "Floor," "Security," or "Training"

**Assigning Attributes:**
- How to assign attributes to employees at multiple levels: individual employee level, single roster entries, multiple roster entries at once, and within a weekly view
- How employees can have default attributes assigned that carry through their schedules

**Viewing and Reporting:**
- How to view assigned attributes in the Roster Details screen
- How to filter roster views by attributes to find specific employees or job assignments
- How to generate reports based on attribute data
- How attributes can be overridden on a day-by-day basis if needed

**Setting Up Attributes (Configuration):**
- How to activate the Roster Attributes feature in your system
- How to create new custom attributes and organize them into attribute groups
- How to assign attribute groups to specific team areas or individual employees

In essence, this guide covers both the practical day-to-day use of attributes for roster management and the initial setup required to establish which attributes are available in your system.
ss: Roster Attribute is a labeling system in Roster that allows Team Managers to assign job or task designations (such as 'Cashier', 'Floor', 'Security', or 'Training') to employees for their scheduled patterns. You can assign attributes at the employee level as a default, override them daily, view them in Roster Details, and filter rosters by attribute to track which employees are scheduled for specific jobs. Open this document if you need to assign attributes to employee patterns, create new attribute types, set up attribute groups by team area, or generate reports based on assigned attributes. This guide covers the full functionality including assignment methods (employee level, single roster, or bulk), configuration steps, and how employees can view their assigned attributes through CorePortal.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Roster Attributes functionality in the Access Roster system (version 28), designed primarily for Team Managers who maintain and publish employee rosters. The document covers the complete lifecycle of roster attributes, including how to assign them to employees, view them in the Roster Details screen, filter views by attribute, generate reports, and configure the system with new attributes and attribute groups. An attribute is a user-defined label applied to an employee's work pattern to identify the specific task or job they are scheduled to complete, such as 'Cashier', 'Floor', 'Security', or 'Training', and can be set at a default level or overridden on a daily basis through the Roster Details screen. The guide walks users through multiple assignment methods: Employee Level (setting a default attribute in Person Attributes), Roster One, Roster Many, and Weekly View, as well as explains how to configure attributes in the system by creating new attributes and attribute groups and assigning them to team areas or individual employees. Key system restrictions noted include that each employee can only have one attribute assigned per pattern, attributes cannot be used with AutoRoster or Uncovered Shifts functionality in Phase 1, and Demand Rules based on attributes are not yet available. The document also indicates that employees can view their assigned attributes daily through the Calendar feature in their CorePortal ESS instance, providing visibility into their scheduled job tasks.

t: Roster Before Period is Published
s:
# Summary: Roster Before Period is Published

This user guide teaches HR roster managers how to use and configure the "Roster Before Period is Published" feature in PeopleXD's Roster system.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
The guide explains a validation control that prevents employees assigned to Recommended Teams from being scheduled to work in other Team Areas until their own Home Team Area roster has been published first. This ensures employees are rostered to their primary team before being used to fill gaps elsewhere.

**Key Topics Covered:**

- **Configuration**: How to turn this indicator on or off in the system
- **How It Works**: When the indicator is active, the system validates that an employee's Home Team Area has been published before allowing them to be scheduled in other Team Areas. When inactive, employees can be scheduled to other teams regardless of whether their home team roster is published
- **Where It Applies**: The indicator applies to four key rostering processes:
  - AutoRoster (automated scheduling)
  - Uncovered Shifts (filling unfilled shift slots)
  - Publish Available Shifts (opening shifts to employees)
  - Shift Swaps (employee shift exchanges)
- **Managing Recommended Teams**: How to add and configure recommended teams
- **Visual Indicators**: The ability to see which Team Areas have or haven't been published

This guide is designed for HR staff responsible for creating, maintaining, and publishing employee rosters, helping them control the order in which different team rosters are finalized and prevent premature allocation of staff across teams.
ss: The "Roster Before Period is Published" indicator prevents employees assigned to Recommended Teams from being scheduled to other team areas before their own Home Team Area roster has been published. This functionality applies during AutoRoster, Uncovered Shifts, Publish Available Shifts, and Shift Swaps processes to ensure teams maintain adequate staffing. Open this document if you manage rosters in Access Group's Roster system and need to understand how to configure this validation check or learn how it protects home team scheduling priorities across multiple team areas.
sl: This user guide for Roster v28 explains the "Roster Before Period is Published" functionality, which is a configuration indicator designed to prevent employees from being rostered to other teams before their own home team area has been published. The document is intended for users who maintain and publish employee rosters and covers configuration steps, including how to enable the indicator through Roster Links > Open General Settings > Published recommended teams indicator, as well as its application across AutoRoster, Uncovered Shifts, Publish Available Shifts, and Shift Swaps processes. When switched on, the indicator validates that an employee's home team area for a specific day or week has been published before those employees can be used by recommended teams to fill staffing shortages; when switched off, employees from recommended teams can be rostered before their home team area is published, which may leave the home team understaffed. The guide uses a detailed scenario involving three store team areas (Shoes, Suits, and Bags) to illustrate how the absence of this validation can result in one team's employees being completely depleted by other teams' staffing needs, leaving the home team unable to fulfill its own roster demand. The document also addresses important configuration notes and explains when and how the indicator is applied across different rostering workflows, including specific sections on adding recommended teams and publishing available shifts through different selection methods.

t: Roster Calculation Retail Calc
s:
# Summary of "Roster Calculation Retail Calc" Guide

This guide explains how to use the **Roster Calculation (Retail Calc)** feature in the PeopleXD HR system — a lightweight alternative calculation method designed for workforce management.

## What You'll Learn

**Core Functionality:**
- How the Retail Calc system works to calculate employee hours and attendance
- How it handles multiple work patterns (useful for employees whose schedules frequently change)
- How it processes employee clock-in/clock-out data (clockings)

**Absence and Break Management:**
- How to manage employee absences within the system, including scenarios where employees clock in during full-day or part-day absences
- How the system handles both paid and unpaid breaks, with multiple worked examples showing different break scenarios

**System Configuration:**
- How to set up Work Groups and Work Patterns for employees
- How to configure break tolerances and other control parameters
- How to configure employee records to use this calculation method

**Key Information:**
- The limitations of what this calculation can and cannot do
- Step-by-step scenarios with real examples (8 different break scenarios covering both paid and unpaid situations)
- Frequently asked questions

## Who It's For

The guide is intended for users managing rosters and attendance in retail or similar environments where employee schedules vary frequently. A prerequisite is that employees must already be assigned to a Team Area/Roster before the calculation can be used.
ss: Roster Calculation (Retail Calc) is a simplified attendance calculation engine for WFM Roster in PeopleXD that automatically computes employee hours, breaks, and exceptions based on clock times and work patterns. Unlike traditional roster solutions requiring extensive pattern configuration, this "lite" calculation needs only a handful of patterns, reducing setup complexity and data migration efforts. Use this guide when configuring or troubleshooting how the system handles multiple daily patterns, break deductions, paid/unpaid breaks, and absence scenarios. Open this document if you need to understand the calculation logic, set up work groups and patterns, or resolve issues with how hours are being calculated for roster-based employees.
sl: This user guide for the Roster Calculation (Retail Calc) solution provides an overview of a lightweight attendance calculation system designed for Access Group's WFM Roster module, specifically created to accommodate clients with frequently changing work patterns. The document covers how the calculation functions, its limitations, and the required configuration settings needed to implement it, including sections on Work Groups, Work Patterns, Break Tolerance, Control Parameters, and Employee Records. The system works by checking employee clock-ins and clock-outs, generating default hours for the day, creating exceptions for late arrivals or early departures, and intelligently handling multiple work patterns assigned to a single employee—either combining adjoining patterns (where the end time of one pattern matches the start time of the next) or requiring separate clockings for non-adjoining patterns. The calculation manages breaks by tracking total break duration against scheduled breaks, applying grace periods based on the number of daily breaks, and raising exceptions when employees exceed specified break times, with optional break untaken pay codes available when breaks are not claimed. The Retail Calc solution significantly reduces implementation complexity compared to traditional roster solutions by requiring only a handful of work patterns rather than extensive reference data, resulting in faster project completion, reduced data migration, and lower ongoing maintenance burden. The guide is intended for WFM administrators and implementation teams who need to configure and understand this simplified calculation method, and it includes detailed scenarios demonstrating both paid and unpaid break handling to illustrate how the system operates in practice.

t: Roster Details Roll Up
s:
# Summary of "Roster Details Roll Up" User Guide

This guide explains how to use and configure the **Roster Details Roll Up feature** in the PeopleXD CoreHR system.

## What You'll Learn:

**The Problem It Solves:**
When employees are rostered with different variables (such as different team areas, shift types, or qualifications) within a single week, they appear on multiple rows in the Roster Details - Week view screen. This makes it difficult to see all employees at once.

**The Solution:**
The Roll Up feature consolidates an employee's multiple roster rows into a single row per shift, making the roster easier to view and allowing more employees to be displayed on screen simultaneously.

**Key Functionality:**

1. **Roll Up Mode Display Options** — When Roll Up mode is enabled, you can choose to display one "Extra Display Item" alongside shift times in the roster box. Your options are:
   - None
   - Qualification
   - Team Area
   - Attribute

2. **Group By Feature** — The Group By function works with Team Area, Qualification, and Attribute fields and groups them per shift (rather than by employee or day level).

**What You Can Do:**
After reading this guide, you'll understand what Roster Details Roll Up does, see practical examples of how it transforms the roster view, and learn how to configure and enable this feature at the global level in your system.
ss: The Roster Details Roll Up feature in CoreHR consolidates multiple employee roster rows into a single row per employee on the Roster Details - Week view screen, making it easier to review more staff at once when employees are rostered across different qualifications, team areas, or shift types. By default, each variation splits an employee into separate rows, but activating Roll Up mode merges these into one. When Roll Up is enabled, you can select an Extra Display Item (Qualification, Team Area, or Attribute) to show alongside shift times, and use Group By functionality to organize employees by Team Area, Cost Centre, Location, Department, and other criteria. Open this guide when you need to configure or use the Roll Up feature to improve roster visibility and screening efficiency.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation on the Roster Details Roll Up feature within CoreHR's Roster V28 system, explaining how it functions and how to configure it for use. The feature consolidates an employee's roster rows into a single row per shift on the Roster Details - Week view screen, which by default displays multiple rows when employees are rostered across different variables such as team areas, shift types, and qualifications. When Roll Up mode is enabled, these multiple rows are merged into one, allowing managers and administrators to view more employees on screen simultaneously, which improves review efficiency. During Roll Up mode, users can select an Extra Display Item—either Qualification, Team Area, Attribute, or None—to display alongside shift start and end times in the roster box, since individual team areas or qualifications cannot apply to the entire merged row. The Roster Details screen retains Group By functionality while in Roll Up mode, allowing grouping by Team Area, Cost Centre, Project, Expense, Location, Work Group, Department, Job Title, Position, Category, or Appointment, though Qualification grouping is disabled in this mode and requires turning off Roll Up mode to access. The configuration process involves enabling the feature at a global level and then allows individual managers to toggle Roll Up mode on or off and define Extra Display Items through button clicks and dropdown selections on the Roster Details screen. This document is intended for managers and HR administrators who manage employee rosters in CoreHR and need to optimize their roster visibility and organization.

t: Roster Details
s:
# Summary of "Roster Details" User Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the **Roster Details screen** in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system. After reading it, users will understand how to:

**View and Understand Roster Information:**
- Access and navigate the Roster Details screen
- View roster details, employee information, and additional roster data
- Monitor cost versus budget information
- Identify and respond to roster alerts

**Perform Roster Management Actions:**
- Make changes to rosters, both for individual employees and across multiple staff members (global updates)
- Calculate planned and actual schedules
- Refresh weekly roster information
- Publish rosters to make them official
- Send roster updates to relevant parties
- Generate and review roster reports
- Switch between displaying values and hours in roster views
- Display or hide graphical representations of roster data

**Manage Individual Employee Roster Information:**
- Change an employee's roster assignment
- Process shift swaps between employees
- Record and manage employee absences
- Check and update employee availability for shifts
- View and manage employee qualifications
- Manage employee attributes
- Assign employees to team areas
- Track shift changes
- Review employee clockings (time tracking records)
- Input timesheet data

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for all these functions within the PeopleXD system's workforce management module.
ss: Roster Details in PeopleXD Workforce Management lets you view, plan, and manage employee shift schedules for your team areas in week or day view formats. Use this screen to access roster information filtered by team area and time period, review employee work patterns and break schedules, and complete scheduling tasks like publishing rosters and managing shift changes. Open this guide when you need to understand how to navigate the Roster Details screen, view roster data in different formats, or learn which actions you can perform directly from the roster—such as updating shifts, managing absences, or publishing weekly schedules. This is your reference for all roster-related workflows in PeopleXD WFM.
sl: This user guide documents the Roster Details screen within PeopleXD Workforce Management, which is the primary interface for accessing, reviewing, and completing roster tasks for team scheduling. Users access the Roster Details screen by navigating to the Workforce Management dashboard and selecting the Roster Details tab, where they can view rosters for Team Areas assigned to their remit in either Week view (showing daily columns with employee work patterns) or Day view (showing time slots with shift and break schedules). The screen provides filtering options including Group By (to organize employees by criteria such as Work Group), Team Area (to select which team's roster to display), and Period (to select roster periods or navigate between weeks), with additional customization available through the Roster Settings filter icon. Key sections of the screen include View Roster Details, Employee Details, Additional Information, Cost v Budget, and Roster Alerts, each providing different aspects of roster data and analysis. The Actions section enables broad roster management tasks such as Change Roster & Global Update, Calculate Planned/Calculate Actual, Refresh This Week, Publish Week, Send Update, Details Summary, Roster Reports, and display toggle options. Person Actions allow individual employee-level modifications including Change Roster, Shift Swap, Absences, Roster Availability, Qualifications, Attributes, Team Areas, Shift Changes, Clockings, and Timesheet Input. This document serves roster managers, team leaders, and workforce planners who need to plan and schedule employee shifts to align business demand with resource supply while maintaining compliance and operational efficiency.

t: Roster Employee Self Serve
s:
# Roster Employee Self Serve Guide Summary

This PeopleXD HR system guide teaches employees how to manage their work schedules and shifts through the self-service portal. After reading it, users will be able to:

**Roster Availability Management**
- Access and use the Roster Availability screen to indicate when they are and are not available to work
- Submit their availability for scheduling purposes
- Understand the cycle availability process
- Know how their availability submissions are approved

**Shift Swapping**
- Submit requests to swap shifts with colleagues
- Accept shift swap offers from other employees
- Understand the manager approval process required for shift swaps to be finalized
- Know their access rights and permissions for swapping shifts

**Uncovered Shifts**
- View and accept shifts that have been published but not yet assigned to anyone
- Reject shifts they don't want to work
- Access their history of uncovered shift activity
- Understand how the uncovered shifts widget is configured

**Co-Worker Visibility**
- View their co-workers' rosters and leave schedules
- Access information about colleague absences and associated pay codes
- Understand configuration options for this feature

The guide covers both employee and manager access levels, explaining what different user types can do within each feature of the roster self-service system.
ss: The Roster Employee Self-Serve functionality in PeopleXD Workforce Management enables employees to manage their schedules through the Employee Dashboard by submitting roster availability, swapping shifts with colleagues, accepting or rejecting uncovered shifts, and viewing co-worker rosters and leave. This guide covers the configuration and processes for four key self-service widgets: Work Week, Calendar, Shift Swaps, and the Unscheduled Shift Widget. Open this document if you need to understand how employees submit availability that may vary week-to-week, how shift swap requests and approvals work, or how to set up the approval workflows for these self-service actions. Use it as a reference when configuring employee self-service features in PeopleXD or troubleshooting how employees interact with roster management tools.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive documentation for the Roster Employee Self-Serve functionality within PeopleXD Workforce Management, a system by Access Group designed to enable employees to manage scheduling and availability tasks through the Employee Dashboard. The document covers four core self-service processes available to employees: submitting roster availability, accepting or rejecting uncovered shifts, submitting and accepting shift swap requests, and viewing coworkers' rosters and leave information. Roster Availability functionality allows employees to submit their working availability on a weekly basis via the Calendar Widget or Work Week Widget (accessed through the 3-dot menu or Actions menu respectively), with submissions optionally routed through a manager approval process before updating the employee's roster contract. The Shift Swap process enables employees to initiate shift exchanges with colleagues, with subsequent manager approval required before shifts can be reassigned. The Uncovered Shifts Widget allows employees to accept or reject shifts published by the organization through an Unscheduled Shift Widget, with configuration options and historical tracking of decisions available. Additionally, employees can view coworkers' rosters and leave information through a dedicated section that may require back office configuration of absence pay codes. This guide is intended for both employees using the self-service portal and managers administering the system, providing step-by-step guidance on accessing screens, submitting requests, and understanding approval workflows.

t: Roster Event Diary
s:
# Roster Event Diary Guide Summary

This guide teaches administrators how to use the Event Diary functionality in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system to create and manage organizational events.

## Key Learning Outcomes

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Event Management:**
- Access the Event Diary through the WFM Admin Dashboard
- Add new events to the system (such as company days, fire drills, training sessions, or Christmas events)
- Edit existing events
- Delete events

**Event Configuration:**
- Enter event details including title and description
- Set start and end dates for events
- Configure events as all-day events or specify exact start and end times

**Viewing Events:**
- View events through multiple system locations: Roster Details, Team Calendar, Employee Calendar, Team Scheduler, and Leave Requests
- Understand how events appear to different user roles (administrators and managers)

**Access Control:**
- Understand different permission levels for administrators versus managers
- Recognize how managers can view planned events to assess impacts on staffing and rostering requirements

The guide is intended primarily for system administrators who manage events at an organizational level, while acknowledging that managers can view these events to help plan their team's workload and attendance.

s:
# Summary: Roster Generate Demand Opening Times Guide

This guide teaches managers and administrators how to use the "Generate Demand for Opening Times" feature in the PeopleXD Roster system (v28).

## What You'll Learn

**Main Purpose:** The guide explains how to configure and use functionality that automatically restricts staffing demand generation to only occur during your company's operational hours, preventing the system from creating rosters for times when the store is closed.

**Key Problems It Solves:**
- Without this feature, if store opening hours change year-to-year (for example, shifting from 10:00-18:00 to 11:00-18:00), the system would still generate staffing demand for the old hours based on previous year's data, resulting in unnecessary staff scheduled outside actual opening times
- It ensures demand generation accounts for changes in operational hours and closure days (like holidays) that vary year-to-year

**What You Can Do After Reading:**
1. Enable or disable the functionality for your needs
2. Set and configure opening times in the Base Requirements section
3. Activate "Operational Times" for your system
4. Generate demand that respects your store's opening and closing times across different interface types
5. Review reports showing the generated demand data

The guide provides step-by-step configuration instructions, explains the process flow, and includes reporting capabilities so you can verify the demand has been generated correctly within your operational hours.
ss: The Roster system's Generate Demand for Opening Times functionality prevents staffing demand from being scheduled outside your store's operational hours by automatically restricting generated demand to match current opening and closing times. This configuration guide covers enabling the feature through the Interface Types screen, setting opening hours in Base Requirements for each team area, and ensuring demand generation accounts for year-on-year changes in operational hours or closure days. Use this document when configuring Roster to align predicted staffing demand with your actual store operating times, or when your store hours have changed and you need to prevent employees from being rostered during closed periods.
sl: This configuration guide is designed for Managers and Administrators using the Roster system to generate expected demands and outlines the complete functionality and setup required for the "Generate Demand for Opening Times" feature. The document covers enabling and disabling the functionality, accessing relevant screens, generating demand values, and producing reports related to staffing demand generation. The core functionality ensures that when demand is generated for a period, the system restricts demand generation to times within the company's operational hours for selected Interface Types, and automatically accounts for year-on-year changes to opening hours and closure days such as holidays. Configuration requires three main steps: setting opening times in Base Requirements by navigating to Roster Links and specifying Opening Time and Closing Time for each day via the Opening Hours tab, switching on the Operational Times toggle for each Interface Type on the Interface Types screen, and optionally customizing the four configurable organizational variable field labels (such as Entrance, Elevator, Escalator, and Changing Rooms) through the Language Pack in Site Manager. The document illustrates a scenario where without this functionality enabled, if a store's hours changed from 10:00–18:00 to 11:00–18:00, the system would incorrectly generate demand for the 10:00–11:00 slot using the previous year's trending data, potentially rostering employees outside actual opening times. When properly configured, the "Generate Values" process runs to calculate predicted demand values for the current period based on the previous year's actual values, with the restriction that generated data falls only within the designated store opening and closing hours.

# Roster General Configuration - Guide Summary

- Organizing your roster dashboard

ss: PeopleXD Roster General Configuration covers the complete setup and configuration of the rostering module within PeopleXD, including roster calculation types (Standard, Retail, Demand-Based), team area structures, and key parameters that control how schedules are created and managed. # Summary: Roster Team Area Delegation Guide

This guide teaches users how to use the PeopleXD HR system to temporarily delegate team area access to colleagues.

## What You'll Learn:

**Core Functionality:**
- How to temporarily reassign team area access to other users within a specified date range, with start and end dates
- How delegated access works during the active delegation period
- The difference between two delegation types:
  - **Employee Delegation**: When you delegate your own team area access to a colleague
  - **Manager Delegation**: When you delegate another user's team area access on their behalf

**System Configuration:**
- How to set up and enable team area delegation in the system
- How to configure delegation levels within team areas
- How to set up the delegation widget and dashboard

**Practical Tasks:**
- How to delegate team area access to colleagues
- How to edit an existing delegation
- How to delete a delegation

## Important Notes:
The guide clarifies that team area delegation only grants access to specific team areas—it does not automatically assign security menu profiles or access to processes and screens. Users who need access to organisational roles must set those up separately. Access is based on the system date, meaning delegated users can only view team areas when the delegation is active on that date.
ss: Team Area Delegation in Workforce Management lets users temporarily reassign their team area access to colleagues for a specified date range, enabling managers to complete approval actions during absences. The feature supports two delegation types: Employee Delegation (users delegate their own access) and Manager Delegation (managers delegate another user's access on their behalf). You'd open this guide when configuring team area delegation in CoreHR, setting up delegation levels within your organizational hierarchy, or learning how to create, edit, and delete delegations for your team. This document covers the complete setup process, including widget configuration, enabling the feature in CorePortal, and step-by-step delegation procedures for both employees and managers.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Team Area Delegation feature in Access Limited Distribution's Workforce Management v28 system, providing comprehensive guidance on how users can reassign team area access within specified date ranges. The document covers three main areas: an overview of team area delegation functionality, configuration steps including enabling the feature through the CorePortal menu option "CorePortal – Team area Delegation" and setting delegation levels via Roster Links, and detailed delegation processes for both Employee Delegation (where users delegate their own access) and Manager Delegation (where managers delegate another user's access on their behalf). The system allows delegated access to be temporary with defined from and to dates, during which assigned users can view and access team areas only if they have access on the system date, and access expires after the to date with no historical record remaining. Team Area Levels determine which users are visible for delegation based on organizational hierarchy, with delegation levels set to either level 3 (showing all users across parent and sub-stores) or level 2 (showing only users within the immediate store and sub-stores). # Summary: Roster Validation Rules User Guide

This guide explains the validation rules available in the PeopleXD Workforce Management system's Roster module. It teaches users how to set up and understand different types of checks that automatically flag potential issues when creating or modifying staff rosters.

The guide covers three main categories of validation rules:

**Roster Rules** — These are 12 different checks that monitor compliance and staffing levels:
- **Compliance checks** that ensure employees aren't breaching their contract hours, working time limits (per EU Working Time Directive), or required daily rest periods
- **Staffing level checks** that identify when shifts are understaffed or overstaffed compared to demand
- **Schedule checks** that flag employees working outside their contracted start/end times
- **Absence tracking** that displays employees with planned time off during the roster period
- **Employee preference checks** that highlight whether employees are working their preferred, undesired, or desired shift patterns (for those using self-rostering)

**Auto Rostering Rules** — Guidelines for how the system automatically assigns staff to shifts

**Uncovered Shifts** — Rules for identifying gaps when shifts don't have enough staff assigned

After reading this guide, users will understand what each validation rule does, how it works, what information it pulls from the system, and how to use these rules to ensure rosters comply with employment law, contracts, and staffing requirements.
ss: Roster Validation Rules in PeopleXD Workforce Management covers 26 different validation checks that automatically flag compliance and staffing issues when rosters are created or modified. These rules monitor employee contract compliance (hours, start/end times, work permits), Working Time Directive violations (weekly limits, daily rest requirements), staffing levels (understaffed/overstaffed shifts), and employee preferences from the self-rostering portal. Open this document when setting up roster validation to understand what each rule checks for, or when troubleshooting why specific validation warnings appear in your roster.
sl: This document is a user guide for the Roster Validation Rules feature within PeopleXD Workforce Management, explaining the various validation rules that can be configured to monitor roster compliance and quality. The guide focuses specifically on three categories of validation rules: Roster Rules, Auto Rostering Rules, and Uncovered Shifts, with each rule applying when the roster is open and changes are made. The Roster Rules section details 26 individual validation codes that check for compliance issues such as Contract Hours breaches (checked against the Contract History tab in People Management), Working Time Directive violations including daily rest hours and maximum weekly hours (pulled from the Working Time Directive Scheme attached to employees), staffing levels (comparing roster demand against actual assignments), and employee availability constraints like contract start/end times from the Roster Contract Details and Availability Profile. Additional rules monitor employee preferences and patterns entered through ESS Employee Self Rostering functionality, including preferred and undesired work patterns, as well as practical roster management metrics such as overstaffing, understaffing, planned absences, and cost versus budget comparisons at the Team Area level. The guide also addresses compliance-related validations such as work permit expiry dates from Personnel records, consecutive working days limits, and minimum/maximum contract hour thresholds. This document is primarily used by roster administrators, workforce managers, and payroll teams who need to configure and understand which validation rules to enable for their specific organizational requirements and compliance obligations.

# Staffing Demand Guide Summary

This PeopleXD HR system guide teaches users how to configure and manage staffing demand settings in the Workforce Management module. After reading, users will be able to:

**Add explanatory context to staffing requirements** — Users can attach narrative notes (up to 200 characters) to staffing rules to document the reasoning behind specific demands.

**Understand how staffing demand is calculated** — The guide explains how to access a detailed breakdown of demand calculations after the "Generate Demand" process runs, helping users see exactly how staffing numbers were determined.

**Import and apply data flexibly** — Users learn how to import data that includes start times and durations, with options to either apply values uniformly across all 15-minute intervals in that period, or distribute values proportionally across the timeframe.

**Set maximum staffing limits** — Users can configure rules that specify the maximum number of staff to schedule in any given time slot, preventing over-rostering.

**Create tiered staffing requirements** — Rather than having a single staffing level, users can set up ranges where different staffing numbers apply based on conditions (for example, in a restaurant: 1-5 covers requires 1 server, 6-20 covers requires 3 servers, 21-50 covers requires 4 servers). This provides more nuanced scheduling than a simple one-to-one relationship between demand and staff.

The guide provides step-by-step instructions for each feature, showing users where to find options within the system and how to complete each task.
ss: Staffing Demand in PeopleXD Workforce Management lets you configure how staff requirements are calculated and applied across your roster. You can add narratives to staffing rules, set minimum and maximum staff numbers, import demand data with start times and durations, and create flexible staffing ranges (for example, 1–5 customers require 1 staff member, while 6–20 customers require 3). Open this guide when you need to set up or adjust staffing requirement rules, configure data imports, or understand how demand calculations work in your WFM system.
sl: This user guide for PeopleXD Workforce Management documents the Staffing Demand features available within the system, which help workforce managers configure and calculate staffing requirements. The document covers how to add and view narrative fields on the Staff Requirements screen by navigating to Workforce Management Dashboard > Staff Requirements, selecting a group, and using the View/Add Narrative option with a maximum character limit of 200 characters. It explains the Staffing Demand Calculation feature accessible through the Generate Demand screen, where users can view detailed calculation explanations by selecting a team and date range, then expanding the 3-dot menu to select View Explanation. The guide details how to configure data imports with start time and duration functionality through WFM Admin Dashboard > WFM Configuration > Interface Types, where the Use Duration toggle and Spread Across Duration toggle control whether imported values apply uniformly to each 15-minute time slot or are divided across the duration period. It also describes the Maximum Number of Staff feature, configured by navigating to Staff Requirements and entering values in the Maximum Value column, which caps rostering numbers for cost control or facility constraints. Additionally, the document covers Staffing Demand Ranges, which replace one-to-one staffing calculations with flexible interval-based relationships, allowing managers to specify that different staff quantities are needed for different value ranges (for example, 1-5 covers require 1 server, 6-20 covers require 3 servers). This guide is intended for workforce managers and administrators who configure staffing requirements and need to understand how to set up narratives, calculate demands, import data with specific time parameters, apply staffing caps, and implement range-based staffing rules.

s:
# Summary

This guide provides step-by-step installation and configuration instructions for integrating PeopleXD with Access People Planner. After reading it, users will be able to:

**Set up the core integration connection:**
- Configure Access Workspace Administrator settings, including creating or identifying an organisation and setting up an XD External subscription with the correct menu endpoint URL and tenant ID
- Retrieve and note the public and private API keys needed for the integration

**Connect the systems via Hubble:**
- Add a Hubble Workspace client with the organisation ID and API keys, which will automatically map matching email addresses between PeopleXD and Access Workspace users
- Configure a Hubble People Planner client with the required organisation ID, namespace, and authentication keys from People Planner DevOps

**Enable features and access:**
- Request that a member of the WFM Product Team enable the required LaunchDarkly feature flag (`wfm-timesheets-phase2`)
- Grant users access to People Planner functionality by activating the People Planner Dashboard in their menu profiles within PeopleXD
- Set up fall-back work and rest patterns in PeopleXD to support shift information returned from People Planner

The guide also includes a routing mechanism at the start: users with PeopleXD V3 or later can skip ahead to step 4, while those using earlier versions should follow from step 2 onwards.
ss: Setting up the integration between PeopleXD (PXD) and Access People Planner requires configuration across multiple systems including Access Workspace Administrator, Hubble, LaunchDarkly, and PeopleXD itself. This document guides you through enabling the PeopleXD to Access People Planner interface, from creating organisations and subscriptions in Access Workspace to activating the People Planner Dashboard in PeopleXD and configuring fall-back work patterns. Open this document when you're implementing the PeopleXD and Access People Planner integration for the first time, or when setting up workforce management timesheet functionality between these systems.
sl: This document provides comprehensive installation and setup instructions for integrating PeopleXD (PXD) with Access People Planner (APP), guiding users through a multi-step configuration process that accommodates different integration methods. The setup begins in Access Workspace Administrator, where users must create or identify an organisation, add an XD External subscription with specific endpoint URLs and tenant IDs, and retrieve public and private API keys for later use. In Hubble's Integrations Tab under Workspace, users add a client with the organisation ID and API keys, which triggers a job to match email addresses between PeopleXD and Access Workspace users and create mappings; the document recommends waiting approximately 30 minutes for this process to complete before proceeding. The Hubble People Planner setup requires selecting a tenant, adding a client with organisation ID, and configuring namespace and key credentials (specifically the key name PxdPublisherSasPolicy) sourced from People Planner DevOps. Within PeopleXD itself, administrators must navigate to Security > Menu Profiles to locate and activate the People Planner Dashboard functionality for relevant user profiles, and configure fall-back work and rest patterns in the People Planner > Mapping > Fall-Back Patterns menu to support shift information. The document also notes that the feature flag wfm-timesheets-phase2 must be enabled by the WFM Product Team until Timesheet Phase 2 releases to production, and concludes with a final synchronisation step where consultants click 'Sync XD Employees' after validating all configuration data. This guide is intended for system administrators and implementation consultants who are configuring the integration between these two workforce management systems.

# Summary of the SEPA User Guide

This guide teaches users how to configure and implement the New SEPA Method in the PeopleXD HR and Expense system. SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) is updating to a new international standard called ISO 20022, which is becoming mandatory across Europe from October/November 2025 to improve payment processing efficiency.

After reading this guide, users will be able to:

- **Enable the New SEPA Method** at both the system level and individual company level within PeopleXD
- **Configure Local Instrument Codes** required for SEPA compliance
- **Map address data correctly** in the new structured format required by ISO 20022, including both employee and employer addresses
- **Prepare and clean address data** to meet the new structured address requirements
- **Understand changes to SEPA XML bank files** and how they affect payment processing
- **Configure bank-specific SEPA file format settings** to ensure payments are compliant with individual bank requirements
- **Validate SEPA payment files** to confirm they meet both the new standard and specific bank implementations
- **Prepare their organization** for the mandatory deadline with readiness checks and timelines

The guide focuses on the practical configuration steps needed in PeopleXD Expense to support the new SEPA standard before the mandatory switchover date.
ss: SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) ISO 20022 is a European payment standard that PeopleXD Expense must be configured to support, with mandatory adoption of the new messaging format by October 2025 and structured address requirements by November 2026. This guide walks you through enabling the New SEPA Method at system and company level, mapping employee and employer address data to meet structured requirements, and configuring bank-specific SEPA XML file settings. Open this document if you need to prepare your PeopleXD system for SEPA compliance, cleanse your address data for payment processing, or understand the configuration steps required before the October 2025 deadline.
sl: This user guide provides comprehensive instructions for configuring PeopleXD Expense to implement the New SEPA Method in compliance with ISO 20022 schema changes mandated by the European Payments Council. The document covers enabling the New SEPA Method at both System Level and Company Level, configuring the Local Instrument Code field, and performing data mapping for SEPA XML Bank Files to support structured address requirements for employee and employer information. It addresses key configuration tasks including switching on SEPA functionality in PeopleXD, mapping SEPA address data according to bank-specific formats, and validating payment files across different banking institutions to ensure compliance with their particular implementations. The guide clarifies the regulatory timeline, explaining that ISO 20022 messaging adoption became mandatory in October 2025, while the structured address requirement was delayed to November 2026, though many banks recommend early adoption to avoid future system changes. Employers and finance teams using PeopleXD Expense will use this document to prepare their systems for SEPA payment processing changes, including cleansing and validating address data, determining which address format their bank requires, and aligning their implementation with bank-specific requirements. The document emphasizes the importance of consulting directly with banks regarding their ISO 20022 support plans and structured address preferences before proceeding with system configuration.

t: Configuring Single Pension Scheme
s:
# Summary of "Configuring Single Pension Scheme" Guide

This guide teaches users how to set up and configure a Single Pension Scheme (SPS) within the PeopleXD HR system. After reading this guide, users will be able to:

**Core Configuration Tasks:**
- Configure system parameters needed for the pension scheme to operate
- Set up banking operational parameters specific to SPS
- Establish all necessary reference data that the pension scheme depends on

**Reference Data Setup:**
- Create and configure pension schemes within the system
- Input and maintain social welfare rates
- Set up pension-specific reference data
- Configure actuarial rates used for pension calculations
- Assign actuarial table references to link calculation tables to the scheme
- Define and maintain pension salary types (the salary components that feed into pension calculations)
- Establish pension types available within the scheme

**Additional Coverage:**
The guide includes a detailed appendix on Uniformed Accrual SPS, which covers specific configuration for schemes using uniform accrual methodology, including pension scheme setup, pension types, benefit statements, and retirement age settings.

Overall, this is a step-by-step technical configuration guide that enables HR administrators to fully set up a single pension scheme from the ground up in PeopleXD, specifying all the parameters, rates, data structures, and pension types needed for the system to calculate and manage employee pensions.
ss: Configuring a Single Pension Scheme (SPS) in PeopleXD Pension involves setting up system parameters, banking operational settings, and reference data such as pension schemes, social welfare rates, actuarial tables, and salary types. This guide clarifies which configuration steps are completed by the PeopleXD implementation team and which must be completed by your organization's pensions department after handover. You would use this document when preparing your environment for SPS deployment or when establishing the pensionable elements and operational controls specific to your organization. It covers both standard SPS configuration and specialized setups like Uniformed Accrual schemes.
sl: This configuration guide for PeopleXD Pension's Single Pension Scheme (SPS) is designed for pension department staff who need to complete local environment setup after the PeopleXD implementation team delivers the software and default configuration. The document outlines which configuration steps PeopleXD completes during implementation and which steps require client action, covering main configuration options and current processes requiring attention. Key configuration areas addressed include System Parameters (which control data presentation in Defined Benefit pension schemes and are set during implementation with no required client action), SPS Banking Operational Parameters (which specify how many years forward pension estimates can be generated without banking previous years, defaulting to 2 years), and extensive Reference Data sections covering Pension Schemes, Social Welfare Rates, Pension Reference Data, Pension Actuarial Rates, Actuarial Table References, Pension Salary Types, and Pension Types. The guide also includes an appendix on Uniformed Accrual SPS that addresses Pension Schemes, Pension Types, Benefit Statements, and Retirement Age configuration. This document serves as a handover guide from the implementation team to clients, clarifying that while PeopleXD handles core system parameter setup, clients must define pensionable elements and complete configuration specific to their local environment such as establishing scheme structures suited to SPS requirements.

t: SSP calculating at incorrect rate
s:
Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a government-mandated payment that offers financial support to employees unable to work due to illness. SSP is calculated based on a standard 5-day workweek, but issues may arise if the system incorrectly divides it over 7 days. 

 

This miscalculation often results from...
ss: Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) calculations in your payroll system may produce incorrect payment amounts when the system divides SSP over 7 days instead of the standard 5-day workweek. This miscalculation typically stems from incorrect employee work patterns or system configuration settings at the organizational level. Open this document if your SSP payments appear lower than entitled or if you need to verify whether your system is using employee work patterns or qualifying days to calculate SSP. The guide walks you through reviewing SSP configuration settings in your portal under UK Tax Rates to ensure the correct calculation method is applied.
sl: This document explains how Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is calculated in the system and addresses the problem of SSP being incorrectly divided over 7 days instead of the standard 5-day workweek, which results in employees receiving lower payments than they are entitled to. The miscalculation typically stems from either incorrect employee work pattern configuration or system-level setup errors. SSP payment configuration is managed at the organizational level and can be set to prioritize either an employee's work pattern or qualifying days. To review and correct the SSP configuration, users access the Settings menu in the portal, navigate to UK Tax Rates, and select General. Within this section, users can choose the Work Pattern indicator if the employee's Time/Workforce Management work pattern should take precedence over OSSP qualifying days, or alternatively select the Qualifying Days indicator to manually enable the appropriate days of the week for SSP eligibility. This document is primarily used by HR professionals, payroll administrators, and system configuration specialists who need to diagnose why SSP calculations are producing incorrect amounts and resolve the underlying configuration issues causing the discrepancy.

t: SSP not generating
s:
According to SSP guidance, an employee's average earnings must exceed the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL). The Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) is calculated based on the eight weeks prior to the start of the Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW).

 

To qualify for SSP, ensure that employees have an average ...
ss: Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) generation requires employees to have average weekly earnings above the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL) based on the eight weeks prior to their absence. If an employee's SSP isn't generating because their average earnings fall below the LEL, you can override this by enabling the Average Earnings toggle in Settings under UK Tax Rates > General for the relevant pay group. Be aware that enabling this toggle applies system-wide to all employees and will pay SSP regardless of earnings level. Open this article if SSP payments aren't being generated for eligible employees or if you need to manually adjust earnings calculations.
sl: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) that is not generating in the payroll system, specifically addressing situations where employee average earnings fall below the Lower Earnings Limit (LEL). It explains that SSP qualification requires an employee's Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) to exceed the LEL, calculated over the eight weeks prior to the start of the Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW). The document describes a configuration process for users who need to override this requirement: accessing Settings > UK Tax Rates > General, selecting the relevant pay group from the Pay Group Code dropdown menu, and toggling on the Average Earnings option. A critical caveat is provided noting that enabling the Average Earnings toggle applies system-wide to all employees, meaning SSP will be paid regardless of AWE levels, and this setting cannot be configured for individual employees only. The document also advises checking whether incorrect AWE calculations for Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) might be affecting SSP calculations, as these are interconnected. If an employee does meet the AWE threshold above the LEL but SSP is still not generating, users are instructed to raise a support case online, referencing the article title and providing the date range for which SSP should have been generated along with the employee number. This guidance is primarily aimed at payroll administrators and HR professionals managing UK statutory sick pay compliance and system configuration.

t: No salary offset in payroll for an absence recorded in CoreTime
s: If no salary offset appears for an employee regarding an absence recorded in CoreTime after running the future calculation of hours, generating salaries, and completing a full validation for the pay group, it likely means the employee has not been assigned an Absence/Sickness Category. Without this ...
ss: When an absence is recorded in CoreTime but no salary offset appears in payroll after running future calculations, generating salaries, and validating the pay group, the employee likely hasn't been assigned an Absence/Sickness Category. Without this assignment, no sickness rule applies and the salary won't be offset. Open this document if you need to assign a sickness category to an employee in Back Office or set a default absence category code to resolve missing salary offsets. Follow the step-by-step instructions to navigate CorePay, maintain employee details, and re-run validation to make the salary offset visible.
sl: This document explains how to resolve the issue of missing salary offsets in payroll when an employee has an absence recorded in CoreTime, even after running future hour calculations, generating salaries, and completing full validation for the pay group. The root cause is typically that the employee has not been assigned an Absence/Sickness Category, which prevents any sickness rules from applying and stops the salary from being offset accordingly. To fix this problem, users must navigate through Back Office by selecting CorePay, then Employee, followed by Maintain Employee Details and Sundry to access the Sickness Category field. If the Sickness Category field is blank, it indicates that the company has not configured a default absence category code, which must be set before the employee can have the proper offset applied. After setting the default absence category code and saving the changes, users need to re-run the validation job to ensure the system recalculates the payroll. Once these steps are completed, the salary offset should appear for the employee in the next payroll run. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee absences and sickness categories in the CoreTime and CorePay integrated system and need to troubleshoot missing deductions related to recorded absences.

ss: When an occupational salary offset shows an incorrect hourly rate that doesn't match an employee's daily rate, check the absence daily rate calculation settings in the portal—specifically looking for any overridden settings at the sickness category, pay group, or company level. This document walks you through the Absence Configuration and Absence Pay Parameters sections to identify whether a Daily Rate Override or Days In Year Override is causing the discrepancy. sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving incorrect hourly rates in occupational salary offsets when the calculated rate does not match an employee's daily rate, which occurs when an absence daily rate calculation setting has been overridden for that specific employee. The document outlines a systematic checking process within the portal that requires navigating to Settings, then Absence Configuration, and examining the Absence Daily Rate Calculation section, specifically the Absence Rule Setting tab and its Daily Rate Override settings for the relevant sickness category. If no overrides are found at the category level, the user must check the Daily Rate Override settings for the employee's pay group, and if still unresolved, check the Daily Rate Calculation settings in Company Settings. For situations where no override is set and the company uses annual salary configurations, the document instructs users to access Settings, Absence Configuration, then Absence Pay Parameters, where they select the company from a dropdown, navigate to Absence Rules in the Select Detail dropdown, and examine the Days In Year Override setting within the three-dot menu for the relevant sickness category. The document emphasizes that any Days In Year Override value set at the category level takes priority over pay group settings when calculating the hourly rate using the formula ((Annual Salary / Days in Year) × Days in Week) / Employee Hours. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, or system configuration specialists who manage absence records and salary offsets in Access Group's payroll system and need to diagnose why occupational salary offsets are calculating incorrectly based on wrong hourly dates.

sl: This document addresses a configuration issue in the Access Group payroll system where sickness pay fails to process correctly after an employee's entitlement band changes, or where an employee becomes newly eligible for occupational sickness payment but does not receive it due to accumulated historic sickness days. The resolution involves navigating to Settings, then selecting Absence Configuration followed by Absence Pay Parameters, where users must select their company from the Company Code drop-down menu and then locate the relevant absence rule through the Select Detail box and Absence Rules option. Users access the specific absence rule by clicking the three-dot icon next to it and selecting More, which opens the configuration for the Use Payment Multiplier to Get Taken field. The fix requires changing this field's drop-down selection from blank to Match Against Range Multiplier, as a blank field causes the system to count all sickness days without applying the pay multiplier calculation. After making this configuration change, users must click Save to apply the settings. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR configuration specialists who manage absence and sickness payment rules within Access Group systems and need to troubleshoot entitlement processing issues following employee band changes.

Use this process when an individual employee needs a different sick pay category than their assigned rule provides, but exercise caution when changing default category codes as this affects company-wide settings.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for changing an absence category assigned to an individual employee within the CorePay Back Office system. The process requires three main checks and tasks: first, identifying the absence rule an employee falls under by navigating CorePay > Input > Advanced Input Features > Absence Pay > Absence Manager Maintenance, entering the employee number, and reviewing the Rule ID in the Reference field for the relevant Payroll Period. Third, to manually assign a different absence category to an employee, administrators navigate to CorePay > Employee > Maintain Employee Details, enter the Personnel No, select "15 - Sundry Profile" from the Select Detail dropdown, and change the Sickness category code to an alternative code that exists within the Absence Categories screen. The document explicitly warns users to exercise extreme caution when modifying the default absence category code at company level, as this affects sick pay settings across the entire organization and should be extensively tested in UAT before implementation.
