t: Set up rolled up holiday pay
s:
Rolled-up holiday pay ensures that employees with irregular hours or patterns receive their holiday pay spread across each pay period, rather than as a lump sum when they take their leave.

 

This method complies with legislation requiring holiday pay to reflect regular earnings, including overtime...
ss: Rolled-up holiday pay spreads an employee's statutory holiday entitlement across each pay period as a percentage of earnings, rather than paying it as a lump sum when leave is taken. Set this up by creating a 12.07% pay code through the pay code wizard, specifying which earnings (basic pay, overtime, bonuses) should be included in the calculation, then assigning it to your employees. Use the 'Irregular Paid Employees - Absence Holiday Pay Calculation' Insight report to identify absences and manually override calculations when needed to ensure accuracy. Open this document if you need to implement rolled-up holiday pay for employees with irregular hours or patterns to maintain legislative compliance.
sl: This document explains how to set up rolled-up holiday pay in the Access Group system, a method that distributes holiday pay proportionally across each pay period rather than as a lump sum, ensuring compliance with legislation requiring holiday pay to reflect regular earnings including overtime and bonuses. The core setup process involves creating a percentage-based pay code using the pay code wizard set at 12.07% to reflect statutory holiday pay calculations, then configuring the pay code formula to specify which earnings should be included—typically all basic pay codes and overtime pay codes—so that rolled-up holiday pay accurately reflects an employee's regular earnings. Once configured, the pay code is assigned to employees, after which the system automatically calculates and adds a proportionate percentage of designated earnings to each pay period. To manage absences and maintain calculation accuracy, users can download the 'Irregular Paid Employees - Absence Holiday Pay Calculation' report from the Insight report store, which identifies absent employees and provides detailed earnings history over a specified period such as 52 weeks. The report enables manual overrides of rolled-up holiday pay calculations for absent employees to ensure their holiday pay reflects average earnings accurately. For XD Workforce Management users, the document references a new Holiday Entitlement Accrual screen designed for UK customers managing irregular hour workers, and recommends configuring the enhanced holiday pay calculation feature to ensure correct calculation and disbursement when employees take leave. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel implementing holiday pay systems for employees with irregular hours or earnings patterns to ensure legislative compliance.

t: Error: 'ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision too large'
s:
If you enter a negate in the leave details field on the Maintain Leave Without Pay screen, you may encounter the following error:

**Start UnHandled Exception 

SOURCEREF: s37000_insert_day_history 

EMPNO: XXXXXX 

ERRNO: -6502 

ERRMESS: ORA-06502: PL/SQL: numeric or value error: number precision ...
ss: The Maintain Leave Without Pay screen in PeopleXD triggers an ORA-06502 error when a negate value exceeds 999 units, which causes the PAY140 payroll file to fail processing. This error occurs because the system has a maximum precision limit of 999 for the number_of_units field. Open this document if you're receiving an unhandled exception error during leave without pay entry or PAY140 file generation. The resolution involves splitting large negate amounts across multiple pay periods to stay within the 999-unit threshold.
sl: This document addresses a specific Oracle database error (ORA-06502) that occurs when users enter a negate value in the leave details field on the Maintain Leave Without Pay screen in an Access Group system. The error, which originates from the s37000_insert_day_history source reference, causes the PAY140 file processing to fail when the `number_of_units` value in the system log exceeds the maximum permitted threshold of 999. To troubleshoot this issue, users must retrieve the relevant PAY140.trcXXXX file (where XXXX corresponds to the specific pay group) and examine the ERRDATA row to identify whether the negate value has surpassed the 999-unit limit. The document provides a practical workaround for resolving the problem: if the negate value is greater than 999, users should split the amount into two separate negates across different pay periods rather than attempting to process the full amount in a single transaction. This splitting approach is necessary due to system limitations related to user access rights and numeric precision constraints within the PL/SQL database layer. The document is primarily intended for payroll administrators, HR specialists, and system users who manage leave without pay entries and need to troubleshoot PAY140 file failures related to negate processing in the Access Group Help Centre system.

t: Message - SMP not enough service, joined DD-MMM-YY needed to join by DD-MMM-DD
s:
When calculating SMP, the system uses the employee's latest start date. In this example, the employee left the company and rejoined the next day, which counts as continuous employment.

 

The system reflects the rejoin date as the joined date. The company has the TUPE date feature enabled, which me...
ss: Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) calculations use the employee's latest start date, which means rejoining after leaving counts as continuous employment for SMP purposes. This document explains how the TUPE date feature affects which start date the system uses as the joined date, and how to enable or disable the HR TUPE Date toggle in Portal settings. Open this if SMP isn't calculating correctly for an employee who has rejoined your company, or if you need to configure how the system determines joined dates for maternity pay eligibility.
sl: This document explains how the Access Group system calculates Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP) based on employee start dates, specifically addressing scenarios where employees leave and rejoin a company. The document describes a configuration feature called the TUPE date, which affects how the system determines an employee's joined date for SMP calculation purposes. When the TUPE date feature is enabled (set to Y) in the system settings, it uses the latest start date as the basis for the employee's joined date, ensuring that rejoining the next day after leaving counts as continuous employment rather than a break in service. To configure this setting, users navigate to Settings > UK Tax Rates > General in Portal and enable the HR Tupe Date toggle, then click Save. The document notes that as an alternative to using the TUPE date feature, administrators can either disable this option entirely or manually enter a TUPE date for an individual employee to ensure the system applies the correct start date for SMP calculations. This guidance is primarily intended for HR administrators and payroll professionals who manage UK employee statutory benefits and need to ensure accurate SMP calculations in scenarios involving employee departures and returns.

s:

The guide addresses a configuration problem where the calculation type needs to be aligned with the pay group's settings for days in the year. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR professionals who manage absence rules and need to ensure that daily rate calculations for absences are correctly configured within the system. The document also references related issues such as incorrect salary offset deductions, missing salary offsets in payroll, and incorrect occupational salary offset calculations, indicating it addresses a common configuration issue in the absence management workflow.

If these checks do not resolve the issue, the document directs users to raise a new support case online, providing specific information to include such as employee reference, absence start and end dates, absence pay code, currently applied entitlements, and expected entitlements. t: Shorter Working Year not marked in Maintain Leave without Pay screen for previous period (now closed)
s:

sl: This document addresses a specific payroll issue within the Access Group's Back Office system where Shorter Working Year (SWY) was not properly marked in the Absence Without Pay screen for a previous period, resulting in the employee receiving full pay along with both SWY Allowance and SWY Deduction payments in error. The document provides step-by-step instructions for correcting this mistake by navigating to the Maintain Leave without Pay screen through the CorePay menu (CorePay > Input > Advanced Input Features > Maintain Leave without Pay). Once the correct leave dates are inputted into the system, the Back Office software will automatically claw back the monies that were previously paid to the employee in error, reconciling the overpayment. The document includes an important caveat that depending on the length of leave being corrected, this clawback process could result in the employee having negative pay in the current period. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage leave and absence records in the Access Group Back Office system and need to correct historical SWY marking errors that have already been processed and paid.

t: Enter statutory absence record for a dormant employee
s:
When managing statutory absences, it's important to note that absence records cannot be entered for dormant employees. This is because dormant employees are not considered actively employed, which affects their eligibility for statutory payments.

 

 

Verifying employee entitlement

To determine w...
ss: Statutory absence records cannot be entered for dormant employees in the Access Group system because they're not considered actively employed and don't qualify for statutory payments. Before processing any statutory absence payment, use the HMRC statutory absence calculator to verify the employee meets entitlement requirements, checking their notice period and active employment status during the qualifying week. If eligible, you have three options: temporarily rejoin and manually process a lump sum payment, rejoin and enter the absence record before making them dormant again, or rejoin and process maternity payroll monthly until the statutory absence ends. Open this document when you need guidance on handling statutory absence payments for employees transitioning between active and dormant status, or to understand the system requirements for recording maternity, parental, or sick pay absences.
sl: This document explains how to handle statutory absence records for dormant employees within an Access Group payroll system, addressing a common constraint that absence records cannot normally be entered for dormant staff since they are not considered actively employed and therefore ineligible for statutory payments. The document guides users through verifying employee entitlement for statutory absence payments using the HMRC statutory absence calculator, which requires checking the correct notice period and confirming the employee was in active employment during the qualifying week, with reference to HMRC's Maternity Benefits Technical Guidance for additional detail. Three distinct processing options are presented: Option 1 involves temporarily rejoining the employee in Portal or Back Office and inputting a manual timesheet for a lump sum against the maternity code, though this approach carries no absence record and results in a 0T tax code requiring the employee to claim a tax return; Option 2 requires rejoining the employee the day after their leave date, entering the absence record via Employee > Search > Statutory and Absences > Absences > Add, then making the employee dormant on the same date while negating salary and offset amounts; and Option 3 similarly involves rejoining and entering the absence record through the same menu path, but instead processes the employee's maternity payroll monthly as usual before making them dormant when maternity ends. The document references the Maintain Statutory Payments (UK) user guide for detailed information on absence record procedures and includes related articles covering statutory maternity pay issues, error messages about absence entry screens, and parental payment management. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to process statutory maternity or parental payments for employees transitioning between active and dormant status while ensuring compliance with UK statutory payment regulations.

t: No salary offset in payroll for an absence recorded in WFM
s:
If an employee’s absence recorded in WFM does not result in a salary offset after running the Future Calculation of Hours, Generate Salaries, and completing a full validation for the pay group, you may need to assign a valid Sickness Category to the employee.

ss: When an absence is recorded in WFM but doesn't result in a salary offset after running Future Calculation of Hours, Generate Salaries, and validation, the employee may be missing a default Sickness Category assignment. Without a valid sickness category, the system cannot apply sickness rules and will not deduct salary. Open this document if you need to assign or update a Sickness Category in Portal, then re-run the Validation job to resolve the missing salary offset.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving a specific payroll processing issue in the Access Group system where absences recorded in WFM (Workforce Management) fail to generate salary offsets despite completing the standard payroll cycle steps of Future Calculation of Hours, Generate Salaries, and full validation for the pay group. The root cause of this problem is typically that the affected employee lacks a default Sickness Category assignment, which prevents the system from applying any sickness rules and therefore does not trigger the salary offset calculation. The document outlines a straightforward four-step remediation process conducted in Portal: users must navigate to the Employee section and search for the relevant employee, access their record by clicking VIEW followed by Sickness Category field, and then select Sundry Profile to assign a valid absence category code in the Sickness Category field. After saving this configuration change, users must re-run the Validation job to ensure the salary offset is now properly calculated and applied to the employee's pay. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, or WFM system operators who manage employee absences and need to troubleshoot instances where expected salary deductions for recorded absences do not appear in payroll calculations. The document also references related issues such as incorrect salary offset deductions, similar problems in CoreTime, and other absence-related payroll complications, indicating it is part of a broader support ecosystem for absence and payroll integration scenarios.

t: Configure the Absence Cut Off feature
s:

ss: The Absence Cut Off feature in PeopleXD Payroll lets you run payroll validation while controlling whether absences from PeopleXD Workforce Management are automatically included. Open this document if you need to enable the feature through Site Manager admin settings, monitor absence inclusion status on the Payroll Dashboard, or toggle WFM absence inclusion for specific pay groups. sl: This document explains how to configure and use the Absence Cut Off feature in PeopleXD, which allows you to run payroll validation while controlling whether absences from PeopleXD Workforce Management are automatically included in your payroll calculations. The feature provides greater flexibility by letting you decide when to include Workforce Management absences in payroll runs, though it only affects absences recorded in Workforce Management and not those entered directly in PeopleXD Payroll. To enable the feature, you must access Site Manager from the dashboard menu, navigate to Admin Settings, find the configuration field cp_manual_absence_run, and change its value to Y. Once enabled, you can monitor absence inclusion status on the Payroll Dashboard, where the Mode column displays a WFM ABSENCE indicator showing either green (absences included in the last validation) or red (absences not included), with the default setting including absences at the start of each payroll period. To change absence inclusion for individual pay groups, you access the Payroll Dashboard, click Manage Payroll, select the three-dot menu for the relevant pay group, and choose either Enable WFM Absence or Disable WFM Absence. The document also specifies that the Web Services menu option "Update paygroup parameter" must be added to your menu profile to use this feature, and references related articles addressing common errors and configuration of similar payroll cutoff settings.

sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on configuring the enhanced holiday pay feature in PeopleXD Payroll, which calculates holiday pay based on average earnings rather than standard rates. The document also covers configuring absence pay parameters through Settings > Absence Pay Parameters to exclude specific absence types from average calculations, and configuring payslip display using the Payslip Pay Code rule to group holiday pay payments on employee payslips. This configuration is typically used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to implement enhanced holiday pay calculations compliant with regulations that require payment based on average earnings rather than contracted rates. The system works with both PeopleXD Workforce Management and PeopleXD Payroll for recording annual leave, with different configuration requirements depending on which system is used. Users must have access to specific menu options in CorePortal Pay including Settings - Holiday Pay, Settings - Absence Pay Parameters, and Settings - Pay Codes to complete the configuration.

t: Error : 'The Complete update, (PAY355), has been run but there was no BIC and IBAN for an employee'

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error that occurs during SEPA file processing when employee banking information is incomplete or incorrect. An analyst will then run database scripts in the background to update these banking details, after which users must manually verify and update the employee's bank details on the relevant screen if the system changes have not already reflected them. Once the background update is complete, users are required to reset the paypath file and regenerate it to allow SEPA processing to proceed. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or finance professionals who encounter errors during SEPA payment file generation and need guidance on resolving banking data discrepancies in their payroll system.

t: Back Office: Reset a bank paypath file
s:
You may need to reset a bank paypath file if the original file contains errors, requires updates to the processing date, or needs to be saved in a different location.

 

Resetting the bank file ensures accurate payroll processing and helps avoid incorrect payments or file submissions.

 

📌Note: If...
ss: Resetting a bank paypath file in CorePay corrects errors, updates processing dates, or relocates files to ensure accurate payroll processing and prevent incorrect payments. Use this process when your original bank file contains mistakes or needs to be regenerated with different parameters. Open this document if you need to access the Reset Paypath Processing function in back office and resubmit corrected bank files to your financial institution.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for resetting a bank paypath file in the Back Office system, which becomes necessary when the original file contains errors, requires updates to the processing date, or needs to be saved in a different location. The process begins by navigating to CorePay, clicking Update, and then selecting Create Bank File/Paypath Processing from the menu. Users must select "Reset Paypath Processing" from the Report Name drop-down menu, choose the relevant company from the Company drop-down menu, and enter the original processing date in the Processing Date field; the system will automatically populate Sort Code/Account Number, BIC/IBAN, and User ID/Original ID fields as users tab through the form. A list of pay groups associated with the selected company number and processing date will appear, allowing users to check the Reset checkbox (or click Exclude Pay Group in older versions) and click the RESET icon to reset pay groups as needed. Resetting the bank file ensures accurate payroll processing and prevents incorrect payments or file submissions, though no report is generated as part of the reset job itself. After receiving a confirmation notification that the reset has been completed successfully, users must select Paypath Processing from the Report Name drop-down menu and regenerate the paypath file; notably, if the reset follows a Cancel Manual Payment job, the employee count remains unchanged but cancelled payments will be marked with a 'C' next to the affected employee names.

t: Payment Listing (PAY430) Report - Employees missing from paypath listing
s:
If some employees are not appearing on the paypath listing report while processing your payroll, it is because the employee's bank account and sort code need to be updated. 

 

To do this, follow the steps below. 

Update employees with bank account number and sort code.

On the Create Bank File sc...
ss: The PAY430 Payment Listing Report identifies employees missing from your paypath listing during payroll processing. This issue occurs when employee bank account details—specifically the bank account number and sort code—haven't been updated in the system. Use this document when you need to resolve missing employees on your bank file by updating their banking information and resetting the paypath listing. The fix involves updating employee bank details, clicking Reset Paypath listing on the Create Bank File screen, and regenerating the bank file.
sl: This document addresses a specific payroll processing issue within the Access Group system where certain employees fail to appear on the PAY430 Payment Listing (Paypath Listing) Report during payroll runs. The root cause of employees missing from the paypath listing is incomplete employee bank account information, specifically missing or outdated bank account numbers and sort codes in the system. The resolution requires a three-step process: first, employees must have their bank account number and sort code updated in the system; second, users navigate to the Create Bank File screen and click the Reset Paypath Listing button to clear the current listing; and third, the bank file must be re-generated to reflect the corrected employee data. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance teams who process payroll through the Access Group Back Office system and need to troubleshoot why employees are not appearing on their banking submission files. The issue is closely related to SEPA bank file processing, as referenced in the related articles section, which indicates the problem may also involve missing BIC and IBAN codes for affected employees in certain scenarios. Users encountering this issue may also need to consult related guidance on resetting bank paypath files for standard or third-party banking integrations depending on their organizational setup.

t: Portal: Set up a foreign bank account
s:
Establishing a foreign bank account is essential for businesses operating internationally, as it facilitates efficient handling of cross-border transactions, currency conversions, and timely payment of employee salaries in their local currencies.

 

📌Note: If you use back office, follow these steps...
ss: Setting up a foreign bank account in the Portal involves configuring banking details through the Settings menu, including selecting the bank country code, checking bank identifiers, and maintaining BIC details. This process is essential for businesses that need to process cross-border transactions and pay employees in their local currencies. Open this document when you need to establish a new international bank account and configure the required banking information before setting up employee pay details. You'll need access to the Banking settings section, and may need your superuser to grant permissions if the Bank Country Codes screen isn't immediately available.
sl: This document provides instructions for setting up foreign bank accounts in the Portal interface, which is essential for businesses that need to process international transactions, handle currency conversions, and pay employees in their local currencies. The setup process involves three main configuration steps accessed through the Settings menu under the Banking section: first, selecting the appropriate Bank Country Code from a dropdown list to establish which country's banking system is being configured; second, checking and configuring Bank Identifiers by navigating to Settings > Banking > Bank Identifiers and creating new lines if required identifiers are not already present; and third, maintaining BIC (Bank Identifier Code) details by accessing Settings > Banking > Bank Details, where users can add new lines using the Add icon and select Type as BIC. The document notes that users may encounter an access restriction where the "Bank Country Codes screen is not available," which requires contacting a superuser to grant the necessary permissions to proceed. For users needing to determine the correct BBAN (Basic Bank Account Number) length, the document references the IBAN Registry document as a supporting resource. Once all bank country codes, identifiers, and BIC details are properly configured through these steps, users will be able to proceed with setting up employee pay details for international payments. This guide is intended for Portal users in back office roles who are responsible for establishing the banking infrastructure needed for cross-border payroll and financial operations.

t: Bank details incorrect on bank file
s:
Incorrect bank details on the payroll bank file often occur when changes to employee bank details are made after processing the payroll file.

 

Once you process the payroll bank file, the background tables lock, preventing any updates for that payroll period.

 

You can still update the employee'...
ss: Bank details entered or updated in your payroll system after the payroll file has been processed won't automatically sync to the bank file, since the background tables lock once processing is complete. This covers the payroll bank file generation process and explains why employee banking information changes made after payroll completion don't appear in the output file. Open this article when you've updated an employee's bank details but noticed they're missing from the generated bank file, or when you need to understand the correct process for making banking changes and regenerating the file with the updated information.
sl: This document explains how to resolve issues with incorrect bank details appearing on payroll bank files, a common problem that occurs when employee bank information is updated after the payroll file has already been processed. The document describes the underlying cause: once a payroll bank file is processed, the background tables become locked for that payroll period, which prevents any subsequent updates to employee bank details from being included in the already-generated file. It clarifies that while users can still manually update an employee's bank details in the system after processing, these changes will not retroactively appear in the completed payroll bank file. To resolve this issue, the document instructs users to raise a support case that includes the specific payroll period that was run and the affected employee's number, at which point support staff will update the information. After support completes the update, users must regenerate the bank file to incorporate the corrected bank details. The document also references several related scenarios and error messages, including issues with missing BIC and IBAN codes, problems with bank paypath file resets, court order reference visibility on bank files, and specific validation errors related to invalid BIC identifier formatting.

s:

The document serves users who need to maintain accurate banking information for payment processing and provides cross-references to related articles covering both portal and Back Office methods for adding sort codes and bank identifiers.

s:

ss: Creating a bank file in Portal is an essential payroll step that generates a digital file containing employee banking information, payment amounts, and transaction dates needed for direct deposits. This file can then be submitted to your bank for processing employee salaries and managing financial transactions. Use this guide when you need to prepare payroll data for bank submission—simply navigate to Manage Payroll, select your pay group, go to the Outputs tab, and click Bank File to generate the required file. sl: This document provides instructions for generating a bank file in Portal, a critical process within the payroll system that enables direct deposits for employee salaries and facilitates other financial transactions. The generation interface includes a Company drop-down menu for selecting a specific company or enabling the All Companies toggle to include multiple entities, and an Exclude Pay Group toggle to omit certain pay groups from the file as needed. Once the appropriate selections are made, users click the Generate button to create the bank file. The resulting outputs—including PDF reports, CSV reports, and transmission files—can be accessed and retrieved from the Report Centre for review and submission purposes. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to process employee payments and manage bank file submissions through the Portal system.

t: Court Order reference not appearing on bank file
s:
If the Court Order reference does not appear on the bank file, it may be due to one of two reasons.

 

We’ve compiled a list of possible reasons and how to resolve them.

 

 

Building Society Reference not populated

The Building Society Reference field is empty. The reference on a Direct Earning...
ss: Court Order references may fail to appear on bank files due to a missing or outdated Building Society Reference field in the employee's deduction record. The Building Society Reference feeds the Direct Earnings Attachment (DEA) information onto the bank file, so this field must be populated in Portal before payroll processing. If you've already run the payroll job without this reference populated, the reference won't appear until the next pay period is processed. Open this guide when a Court Order reference is missing from your bank file and you need to troubleshoot whether the Building Society Reference field requires updating or whether support needs to rerun a payroll update.
sl: This document provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues where Court Order references fail to appear on bank files within the Access Group payroll system. The document identifies two specific scenarios that cause this problem: an empty Building Society Reference field, or a Building Society Reference that was updated after the payroll job has already been run. For the first scenario, users can manually update the reference by navigating to Employee in Portal, searching for the relevant employee, clicking VIEW, then accessing the Deductions section, selecting the three-dot icon next to the deduction, and entering the value in the Building Society Reference field before saving changes. For the second scenario where the Building Society Reference was populated after the payroll or Complete Update job has been executed, users must contact the Access Group support team by raising a new case online and referencing this article, providing the building society reference, employee number, and affected payroll period so that support can run an update. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee deductions and bank file processing in the Access Group system, particularly those dealing with Direct Earnings Attachments (DEA) and court order deductions that require building society references on bank files.

s:

ss: Resetting a third-party paypath file refreshes the data exchange between your payroll system and an external payroll service provider in Back Office. Open this guide if you've identified data transmission failures and need to reset the connection before processing your next payroll cycle—the process involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting your pay group, and using the Reset Paypath option in the Third Party EFT settings.
sl: This document provides instructions for resetting a third-party paypath file in Back Office, a process used to refresh or reconfigure the data exchange mechanism between a payroll system and an external payroll service provider. The reset is necessary when data transmission errors occur, file corruption is detected, or synchronisation issues arise between the internal system and the third-party provider, and should be performed immediately upon identifying such failures and before processing the next payroll cycle. The procedure requires navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing the Inputs tab, clicking General, and then selecting Third Party EFT from the dropdown menu to access the Reset Paypath option. Users must enter the company and start date (which represents the processing date), toggle on the Reset option, and submit the changes before regenerating the file. The document is designed for Back Office users responsible for payroll administration and managing third-party payment integrations. If errors occur during the reset process, users are instructed to raise a new case online and reference the article title along with specific details including the affected pay group(s) and processing date.

t: Updated BACS and Albany BACS file format
s:
Albany and BACS files are standardized formats used for processing electronic payments, such as payroll and supplier transactions, in the UK. These files ensure that payment instructions are accurately communicated to banks, enabling smooth and secure transfers

 

To generate and submit these files...
ss: Albany and BACS files are standardized payment formats used to process payroll and supplier payments electronically through UK banks. Use this document when you need to generate or submit payment files during payroll runs—it specifies the exact field requirements and data structure for both Albany .csv files and BACS files. Open this if you're setting up payment instructions and need to ensure your file format meets bank requirements for accurate, secure fund transfers. The document details mandatory field lengths and field order for each format, including sort codes, account numbers, payment values, and employee names.
sl: This document provides technical specifications for two standardized electronic payment file formats—Albany and BACS—used in the UK for processing payroll and supplier payments through banking systems. The document outlines the specific field requirements and data structures necessary for generating and submitting payment files when processing transactions through Albany or BACS systems during payroll runs. For Albany files in .csv format, the required fields include Sort Code (6 characters), Account No (8 characters), Account Name, Value, Building Society Ref, and Reference (employee name). BACS files have more detailed requirements with additional mandatory fields including a three-character '099' code, Company Sort Code and Company Account No (6 and 8 characters respectively), a four-character '0000' code, Value (11 characters), Company Name (18 characters), Building Society Ref (18 characters), Employee Name (18 characters), and RTI Hash Tag (4 characters), with the critical constraint that BACS files must not contain any headers or footers. This document is essential for payroll administrators, finance teams, and system users who need to ensure payment files are correctly formatted and structured before submission to banks, helping prevent transmission errors and payment processing failures. The document serves as a reference guide for maintaining compliance with UK banking standards while processing electronic payments through these integrated systems.

t: Reset a bank paypath file when a later payroll period has been completed
s: Bank paypath file failures can lead to significant complications, especially when earlier payroll periods have already been processed. This issue arises because the system maintains the sequential integrity of electronic fund transfer (EFT) files, which prevents you from regenerating earlier bank fi...
ss: When a bank paypath file fails and you've already completed a later payroll period, the system prevents you from regenerating the earlier bank file due to sequential integrity requirements for electronic fund transfer (EFT) files. This document explains how to resolve this situation by submitting a support case with the affected payroll period details. Open this article if you need to reset a bank paypath file after discovering a failure in an earlier period that has already been processed.
sl: This document addresses the problem of bank paypath file failures that occur when a later payroll period has already been completed, which creates complications due to the system's requirement to maintain sequential integrity of electronic fund transfer (EFT) files. The core issue is that once a newer payroll period has been processed, the system prevents users from regenerating or resetting earlier bank files, as doing so would compromise the chronological sequence of EFT submissions. The document explains that this sequential protection mechanism is intentional but can create situations where users need to resolve errors in bank paypath files from earlier periods. To address this problem, the document directs users to raise a new support case online, specifically referencing the article's title "Reset a bank paypath file when a later payroll period has been completed" and including details about the affected payroll period in their request. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and finance teams who manage electronic fund transfers through the system's bank file generation processes, particularly when they encounter errors or need to make corrections to previously generated bank files. The document serves as a procedural guide for escalating technical issues related to bank file regeneration that cannot be resolved through standard system operations alone.
