t: Configure Irish Statutory Sick Pay
s:
Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) allows you to automatically calculate and pay sick leave entitlements for Irish employees. The system calculates SSP at the statutory rate up to the maximum daily cap when certified sick leave is recorded.

 

To configure Irish SSP, watch the video or follow the steps below...
ss: Irish Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) configuration in your payroll system lets you automatically calculate and pay sick leave entitlements for Irish employees at the statutory rate with daily caps. This document covers the complete setup process in Portal, including creating SSP pay codes, configuring system and payment parameters, and establishing rules for three employee categories: salaried employees (Category A), timesheet-paid employees (Category B using Workforce Management data), and custom rule-based employees (Category C). Open this document when you're first implementing Irish SSP, need to adjust SSP parameters like maximum daily payment amounts or qualifying weeks, or are setting up different SSP rules for specific employee groups.
sl: This document provides comprehensive configuration instructions for setting up Irish Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) in the Access Group system, enabling automatic calculation and payment of sick leave entitlements for Irish employees at the statutory rate up to maximum daily caps. The configuration process begins by creating two SSP pay codes through Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, where users must select Allowance as the Payment Type, enable rules including Taxable, USCable, PRSIable, and Included in Gross Pay, and add general ledger rules. Users then configure the Irish SSP Settings screen (Settings > Absence Configuration > Irish Statutory Sick Pay Settings) across multiple tabs: the General tab to enable the new calculation method, the System Parameters tab to set SSP days allowed per year, qualifying weeks for eligibility, payment percentage, and maximum daily payment caps, and the Payment Parameters tab to specify which pay codes generate and override SSP calculations. The document addresses three employee categories with distinct configuration requirements: Category A for salaried employees (requiring pay multiplier application and SSP offset code selection), Category B for timesheet-paid employees (requiring SSP Hours from WFM Enabled toggle activation at pay group or employee level via Settings > Absence Configuration > Irish Statutory Sick Pay Settings), and Category C for employees meeting neither category (requiring custom rules configured through the Method C Rules and Method C - Average Periods tabs). Additional configuration steps include enabling the SSP Element and SSP Absence toggles in the Pay Codes tab for relevant pay codes, reviewing the Paid by Timesheet indicator in employee tax details, and ensuring percentage allowance pay codes are included as elements in daily rate calculations. The document also notes that employees enrolled in company absence schemes, identified by a sickness category code in their Sundry Profile, are automatically excluded from SSP calculations unless manually overridden through an SSP timesheet.

t: Pro rata Benefit in Kind (BIK)
s: Benefit in Kind (BIK) values are normally applied in full for each payroll period. The Pro Rata BIK feature changes this behaviour for employees who start or leave employment part-way through a period. When enabled, PeopleXD calculates a proportional BIK value based on the number of days the employe...
ss: Pro Rata Benefit in Kind (BIK) is a PeopleXD payroll feature that calculates proportional BIK values for employees who start or leave mid-payroll period, rather than charging the full BIK amount. When enabled via the apply_pro_rata_on_bik parameter in System Configuration (PAYUT009), the system charges only for the days an employee was actually active in that period. Open this document if you need to understand how to enable pro rata BIK calculations, how the calculation works, or determine whether this feature applies to your employees—particularly if you have frequent starters or leavers.
sl: This document describes the Pro Rata Benefit in Kind (BIK) feature in PeopleXD, a payroll system that calculates proportional BIK values for employees who start or leave employment mid-payroll period rather than applying full-period BIK amounts. The feature is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by payroll administrators via the System Configuration screen (PAYUT009) by locating the parameter apply_pro_rata_on_bik and setting it to Y, with changes taking effect from the next payroll run. Pro rata calculation is triggered when either a BIK start date falls after the period start date or a BIK end date falls before the period end date, and the proportional value is calculated using the formula: (Standard BIK Value ÷ Days in Period) × Pro Rata Days, where days are counted according to the employee's pay group basis (either 7-day calendar or 5-day working day). The document explains that the calculation automatically clamps the BIK active range within the current period without requiring manual date adjustment, and provides a concrete example where an employee leaving on the 10th of a 30-day period with a £600 monthly BIK receives £200 instead of the full amount. The feature applies only to starters and leavers in the current active payroll period and explicitly excludes arrears and retrospective calculations, which continue to apply full BIK amounts regardless of the parameter setting. Payroll administrators using PeopleXD should consult this guide to understand that the feature preserves backward compatibility when disabled and that enabling it will only affect employees whose BIK dates fall within the open period, leaving those active for full periods unaffected.

t: PRSI Class Automation
s: The PRSI Class Automation feature automates the update of Irish Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) classes for employees based on their age, date of birth, and State Pension Contributory (SPC) status. Without this feature, PRSI class changes for older employees must be applied manually. When enable...
ss: PRSI Class Automation automatically updates Irish Pay Related Social Insurance classes for employees aged 66 and over in PeopleXD based on their age, date of birth, and State Pension Contributory (SPC) status — eliminating manual class changes and reducing reporting errors. The feature transitions Class A or S employees to Class J or M according to Irish Revenue legislation and is disabled by default, requiring explicit enablement at either system-wide or individual pay group level. Open this document if you operate Ireland payroll, need to configure automated PRSI class transitions for older employees, or want to understand the specific age and SPC criteria that trigger class changes during each payroll run.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to the PRSI Class Automation feature in PeopleXD, which automatically updates Irish Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) classes for employees aged 66 and over based on their age, date of birth, and State Pension Contributory (SPC) status, eliminating the need for manual class changes that would otherwise be required under Irish legislation. The feature is controlled through a two-tier flag system accessible via the Payroll Dashboard, with system-level configuration at Settings > System Type > PRSI Class Automation (feature flag prsi_class_spc_effective) that applies to all pay groups, and optional pay group-level configuration at Settings > Pay Group > PRSI Class Automation for selective rollout. The document outlines specific class transition rules: employees aged 66–69 with SPC awarded transition from Class A1 to J1 or S1/S2 to M; those aged 66–69 without SPC but born on or before 01-January-1958 follow the same transitions; those born after that date see no change; and all employees aged 70 and over unconditionally transition from Class A to J or Class S to M regardless of SPC status or date of birth. Configuration prerequisites include confirming Ireland payroll operation within PeopleXD, having payroll administrator access to System Type and Pay Group Settings, identifying employees aged 66+ who have been awarded State Pension (Contributory), and planning rollout strategy since the system-level flag overrides any pay group-level settings. Related menu paths and reports referenced include the Employee PRSI Report (PAY155PN via PAYEMP form), PRSI/USC/PRD Rates (SYSTEMLEGRATE_MENU), and Maintain PRSI Class Details (YEAREND_MENU > MAINTAINPRSICLASSDETAILSIRE). Payroll administrators and HR teams managing Ireland payroll operations use this document to enable, configure, and understand the automated PRSI class transitions that occur during each payroll run, with the feature disabled by default and requiring explicit enablement to activate automation across the organization or specific pay groups.

t: Third-party EFT: Employment Allowance
s: Employment Allowance is a UK government scheme that allows eligible employers to reduce their annual employer (secondary) Class 1 National Insurance Contributions (NICs) by up to £10,500 per tax year. The allowance is claimed via the Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submission to HM Revenue and Custom...
ss: Employment Allowance is a UK government scheme that reduces employer National Insurance Contributions by up to £10,500 per tax year, claimed via the Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submission to HMRC. This document explains how to enable Employment Allowance in the Third-Party EFT output within PeopleXD so the allowance appears as a line item alongside other HMRC payment obligations. Open this if you need to configure the Employment Allowance EFT indicator, understand eligibility requirements, or troubleshoot why the allowance isn't showing in your EFT listings. The guide covers prerequisites, step-by-step configuration in PeopleXD's RTI settings, and answers common questions about mid-year enabling and multi-company setups.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring and implementing Employment Allowance within the Third-Party Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) system in PeopleXD, which allows eligible UK employers to reduce their annual employer Class 1 National Insurance Contributions by up to £10,500 per tax year through the Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submission to HMRC. The document explains that Employment Allowance was previously missing from Third-Party EFT listings but is now available as a line item once enabled, and covers eligibility criteria including a requirement that employer NICs were below £100,000 in the prior tax year and that the organisation has at least one non-director employee. Configuration is performed within PeopleXD's RTI settings by navigating to Settings > General > RTI > Detail: Company Allowance and enabling the Employment Allowance EFT indicator on the PAY3400 Maintain Statutory Pay Parameters screen, with this setting required separately for each payroll company. Once enabled, the allowance automatically offsets against HMRC payments each pay period until either the full £10,500 entitlement is used or the tax year ends, reducing only the net amount payable to HMRC without altering underlying individual employee NIC calculations. The document warns that failing to enable the indicator will result in Employment Allowance not appearing in EFT output despite a valid EPS claim, potentially creating discrepancies, and clarifies that any unused allowance cannot be carried forward and must be re-claimed annually. It addresses common scenarios such as mid-year enablement and multi-company configurations, directing users to HMRC guidance for eligibility questions and to Access support channels for technical issues with EFT output or indicator functionality.

t: Digital Employment Verification FAQs
s:
Digital Employment Verification allows your employees to share payroll data digitally with financial service providers, removing the need for manual payslip requests and giving them full control of their data and personal finances.

 

Access PeopleXD Payroll supports this through two provider integ...
ss: Digital Employment Verification in Access PeopleXD Payroll allows employees to securely share their employment and income data with financial service providers like banks and mortgage lenders through Experian Work Report™ or The Verification Exchange® from Equifax, eliminating manual payslip requests. Open this document if you want to understand how the integration works, what data is shared, what setup is required in your PeopleXD system, and what privacy safeguards are in place. This is particularly useful if your HR or Payroll team currently handles frequent payslip requests from employees, or if you're evaluating whether to enable this feature for your workforce. The FAQs cover employer setup, employee consent requirements, data storage in a secure holding database, and address common questions about costs, visibility, and data privacy.
sl: This document is a comprehensive FAQ guide that explains Digital Employment Verification, a feature within Access PeopleXD Payroll that allows employees to securely share employment and income data with financial service providers through two integrated platforms: Experian Work Report™ and The Verification Exchange® from Equifax. The document describes the overall process flow, including how employers enable the integration directly in Access PeopleXD via Admin Settings parameters (applying organisation-wide rather than employee-by-employee), and how employee data is stored in a secure 12-month rolling holding database hosted within Access Group UK until it is automatically deleted after that period or when the integration is disabled. It explains the technical mechanics of data access, specifying that verification providers can only access individual employee records via secure API on a one-time, transaction-by-transaction basis when an employee provides explicit consent during a credit application, with employees needing to reconsent for each new application. The document addresses key administrative and privacy concerns: employers receive no visibility into when employees use the service, cannot restrict the integration to specific providers once enabled, and cannot configure the feature by individual employee, while employees maintain full control through their consent requirements at point of transaction. It clarifies practical constraints such as the integration only functioning in live production environments (not test environments), the elimination of manual payslip request workload for HR and Payroll teams, and the zero-cost implementation for organisations. HR, Payroll, and IT administrators responsible for Access PeopleXD configuration would use this guide to understand whether to enable the feature, how it functions technically and operationally, and what employee privacy protections are in place.

You'll need to report cancelled payments to HMRC by running an FPS (Full Payment Submission) for the current tax year or an EYU for previous tax years. sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on cancelling payments within the Access Group payroll system, covering both the cancellation process itself and how to view cancelled payment records. The document also provides instructions for viewing cancelled payment payslips by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting Outputs, clicking Print Payslips, enabling Specific Employee, searching for the employee number, and enabling the Cancel Payment toggle when applicable. t: Criteria for a priority 1 case
s:
A priority 1 (P1) case refers to a critical issue that severely impacts business operations, such as system outages or payroll failures. You should classify a case as P1 when it meets the following criteria:

Business Critical Payroll Deadlines: The case involves a risk to a business-critical payrol...
ss: Priority 1 (P1) cases cover critical issues in PeopleXD and payroll systems that severely disrupt business operations—such as payroll job failures, missed bank file transfers, system or screen unavailability, or security breaches—when no workaround exists. Open this document when you need to classify a support case and determine whether it meets P1 criteria, or when reporting an urgent issue that threatens business-critical payroll deadlines. The guide helps you understand which scenarios justify P1 classification (like stalled payroll processing) versus lower priority classifications (like issues affecting only a few employees with available workarounds). Use it to ensure your case gets appropriate urgency routing and to clearly document any affected deadlines when logging a P1 ticket.
sl: This document defines the criteria for classifying a case as Priority 1 (P1) in the Access Group support system, which represents a critical issue that severely impacts business operations such as system outages or payroll failures. A case should be classified as P1 when it involves business-critical payroll deadlines with no available workaround, including situations where payroll jobs are stuck, have failed, or are unavailable and jeopardize meeting those deadlines. The document also specifies P1 classification applies when there is a risk of failing to transfer bank files to the bank on time, when critical software or specific screens are unavailable with no workaround available, or when security or data breaches occur that require resolution from the PeopleXD Support, Development, or Product teams. When logging a P1 case, users must outline any affected or potentially impacted deadlines to ensure proper escalation and response. The document explicitly clarifies what should not be classified as P1, including issues that affect only a few employees where a workaround exists such as manual timesheet input, issues impacting only a test environment, and next-day deadline issues which may be more appropriately managed under P2 classification. This guidance is intended for support staff and system users in the PeopleXD platform who need to determine appropriate case severity levels and ensure that only genuinely critical issues receive P1 treatment within contractual SLA commitments.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre explains how to process PRSI/NI (Pay Related Social Insurance/National Insurance) refunds for employees in the current tax year when an incorrect PRSI/NI class has been assigned due to setup errors or employment status changes that weren't updated in the system, which can result in overpaid contributions over extended periods. The document describes two primary methods for processing refunds: a system-generated refund approach that involves backdating the NI class effective period by navigating to Employee > View > Tax Details and entering the correct NI Letter and NI Letter Period Effective date, which automatically calculates the refund based on the applicable pay period; and a manual refund approach using NI override codes that requires accessing Settings > Company Parameters > Organisations to view the codes, then entering overrides via Employee > View > Timesheets Current Period. The manual override method includes important caveats: users must not use regular NI pay codes as this will not generate a PAYE Mod correction file, and manual overrides disable system-generated NI calculations, requiring adjustments for both Employers (ERs) and Employees (EEs). The document explicitly warns that the system does not accommodate PRSI/NI refunds for previous tax years regardless of transaction dates, and that refunding previous years via payroll is inadvisable due to the extensive manual amendments required that can introduce errors. This resource is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals managing employee PRSI/NI contributions in Access Group's portal-based payroll system who need to correct overpayments in the current tax year.

t: Current period or one view displaying incorrect rate for an employee
s:
The Payroll dashboard serves as a crucial tool for monitoring employee compensation accurately. However, discrepancies such as incorrect employee rates can occur for several reasons, including data entry errors, outdated information, or integration issues with HR systems.

 

To resolve an incorrect...
ss: The Payroll dashboard in Portal displays combined rates when an employee has multiple rates within the same period (such as after a mid-period salary change), which can appear as an incorrect total rate on the Current Period or OneView screens. This is a display issue only—the system calculates and pays the correct amount, but you can enable the Rate toggle to view individual rates and hours worked at each rate separately. Use this document when you need to verify pay calculations after a rate change, understand why two rates are showing as combined, or break down an employee's compensation by the different rates applied during a period. Enable the toggle in Portal by navigating to Employee > Current Period or OneView > BREAKDOWN > Rate toggle to clearly distinguish between old and new rates.
sl: This document explains how to resolve and understand display issues with employee compensation rates in the Payroll dashboard, particularly when incorrect rates appear on the Current Period or OneView screens in Portal. The core problem addressed is that when an employee experiences a mid-period rate change, the system displays a combined rate by default—for example, showing €25.50 when an employee's rate changed from €13.01 to €12.49—which, while visually confusing, is only a display issue and does not affect actual pay calculations. To resolve this and view individual rates clearly, users must navigate to Employee > search for the employee > click VIEW > select Current Period or OneView > click BREAKDOWN, then enable the Rate toggle and click OK. Once the Rate toggle is activated, the system separates individual rates applied during the period, distinguishes hours worked at each rate, and clearly differentiates between old and new rates including any appointment-based entries. The document emphasizes that this toggle functionality works for both standard pay and appointment-based entries, and notes that leaving the toggle disabled when an appointment contains multiple rates will result in those rates being combined into a single figure. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, HR personnel, or finance teams who need to verify accurate pay calculations when employee rates change within a pay period and want to ensure transparency in compensation records.

The process involves navigating to the Employee section, searching for and viewing the relevant employee record, accessing the Deductions area, and selecting the three-dot icon next to the applicable deduction to edit it. Once in the edit screen, users turn on the Hold Deduction toggle and specify the number of pay periods for which the hold should remain active in the Hold Periods field before saving the changes. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR staff who manage employee deductions in the portal and need to prevent non-compliance with HMRC regulations regarding multiple concurrent student loan repayments. The second step involves checking the Positive Indicator by navigating to the Employee menu, searching for the affected employee, clicking VIEW, then accessing Tax Details to verify that the "Paid from Timesheet" input toggle is disabled. If neither of these steps resolves the issue, the final resolution is to disable the employee entirely through the system. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee records and process timesheets, particularly when they encounter blocking errors during payroll observation reporting cycles.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for the ORA-06502 PL/SQL numeric or value error that occurs when users attempt to load new position rates for employees into CorePay through the Load Position Rates of Pay screen. t: Delete a position rate or scale for a position rate
s:
Position rates and scales determine how employees are compensated based on their roles and experience levels. However, once you establish these rates within the system, you cannot permanently delete them due to data integrity and audit trail requirements. 

 

This limitation ensures that historical...
ss: Position rates and scales in PeopleXD determine employee compensation based on roles and experience levels, but they cannot be permanently deleted due to audit trail and data integrity requirements. Instead of deleting, you can deactivate a position rate by setting its scale value to zero, which removes it from active use while preserving the historical record for payroll compliance. Alternatively, you can set the current scale to match a previous scale value to create a pay progression plateau. Open this document when you need to remove or modify position rates while maintaining accurate payroll records and audit compliance.
sl: This document explains how to handle position rates and scales in a payroll system when you need to remove them from active use, clarifying that permanent deletion is not possible due to data integrity and audit trail requirements that keep historical payroll records accurate and compliant with employment legislation. Rather than deleting, the document describes two alternative approaches for deactivating position rates: the first method involves navigating to the position rate you want to deactivate, locating the scale value field, and changing the scale value to 0, then saving the changes, which effectively removes the rate from active use while preserving the record for historical purposes. The second method requires accessing the position rate requiring modification, identifying the previous scale value in the sequence, setting the current scale to match that prior scale value, and saving the updated information, which creates a plateau in pay progression and effectively stops advancement at that point. This document is relevant for payroll administrators, human resources professionals, and compensation managers who need to manage position rate structures and ensure that changes to compensation scales comply with system requirements and regulatory standards. The document also references related articles including Load Position Rates of Pay, Configure Pay Scales, Update Pay Scales Using the Pay Increase Module, Access to Load New Position Rates Screen, and Amend Basic Rate on New Allowance Scale Rate, which provide additional context for position rate management within the Access Group system.

s:

ss: When viewing payslips in the Payslip History screen, communication timeouts can occur due to large data volumes or other database-intensive processes running simultaneously. The document provides step-by-step instructions for generating a copy payslip through the Portal, beginning with navigating to the Employee section and searching for the relevant employee record. Once the employee is located, users click the VIEW button next to the employee name, then access the OneView screen and select the desired payroll period from the Payroll Period dropdown menu. After selecting the period, users can download the payslip directly from this interface. This workaround is intended for Portal users who need to generate historical payslips but are experiencing timeouts or communication failures in the standard Payslip History view, making it particularly useful for employees or administrators managing payslip retrieval across multiple pay periods.

ss: Error code 7877 occurs in FPS (Full Payment Submission) file generation when a payroll period has no transactions and results in nil pay for an entire pay group. You'll encounter this error when attempting to submit a blank FPS file, which isn't required for periods with no payments. Open this document if you need to understand why this error appeared during payroll processing or if you need instructions on how to request deletion of an erroneously generated FPS file. The solution involves raising a support case with specific details about your pay group, payroll period, and reason the FPS isn't needed.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses error code 7877, which occurs when an FPS (Full Payment Submission) file is generated for a payroll period containing no payroll transactions and resulting in nil pay. The error appears because FPS files are unnecessary when there are no payments for an entire pay group during a specific payroll period. Users can continue processing the payroll period normally, but they will be unable to submit a blank FPS file as the system prevents this action. To resolve the issue, users must raise a new support case online and reference this article's title, providing specific details including the pay group, payroll period, sequence of events, the reason the FPS is not required, and confirmation that they wish to delete the incorrectly generated FPS file. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and finance professionals working with Access Group's payroll system who encounter this specific error when managing payroll periods with no employee payments. The help centre entry also cross-references related RTI (Real Time Information) and FPS submission errors for users who may encounter similar issues during payroll processing.

sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error message that appears when users attempt to submit a complete update job in their payroll system. t: Check if an employee is receipt of SPC
s:
If the employee’s PRSI class value displays incorrectly during payroll processing, it happens because the employee’s letter reverts to incorrect PRSI class values set within the pension tax limits.

 

PeopleXD will not be able to detect whether an employee receives SPC. As a result, it will not aut...
ss: PeopleXD cannot automatically detect when an employee receives State Pension Contributory (SPC), which causes PRSI class values to revert to incorrect settings stored in pension tax limits during payroll processing. This document explains how to manually correct PRSI class values by removing incorrect settings from the Old Age Pension Rates configuration in Ireland Tax settings. Use this guide when an employee's PRSI class displays incorrectly after pension tax limit updates, or when you need to prevent automatic PRSI class reversion for employees in the SPC age group. You'll also learn when to disable automatic updates and manually adjust PRSI class based on revenue RPN instructions.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving PRSI class value display issues that occur when employees receive State Pension Contributory (SPC) during payroll processing in PeopleXD. The core problem addressed is that PeopleXD cannot automatically detect SPC receipt, which prevents it from applying correct PRSI rules or updating PRSI class values for affected employees, causing the system to revert to incorrect values stored within pension tax limits configuration. When pension tax limits contain wrong PRSI class settings, these values override employee records during system updates, creating persistent inaccuracies. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to Settings > Ireland Tax Rates > Old Age Pension Rates > Pension Tax Limits and manually remove the incorrect PRSI class values from the From and To PRSI Class fields for the relevant age and pension tax limit entry, then save the changes. The document also notes that automatic PRSI updates for employees in SPC age brackets may need to be disabled entirely, requiring payroll administrators to manually update PRSI class values based on Revenue RPN (Revenue Personal Number) instructions. This document is typically used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage Irish payroll in PeopleXD and need to ensure correct pension and PRSI handling for older employees receiving state pensions.

t: Absence pay code is not being offset in payroll
s:
If the absence pay code is not being offset correctly in payroll, it is often due to a misconfiguration in the absence rule. This misconfiguration can prevent the absence pay code from being applied accurately in payroll calculations.

 

Additionally, it can affect specific types of leave, includin...
ss: Absence pay codes in payroll may not offset correctly due to misconfiguration in absence rules, which can impact various leave types including maternity and paternity leave. Open this document if your payroll calculations are showing incorrect amounts for recorded absences in CoreTime. The guide walks you through reviewing and correcting absence rule configurations in PeopleXD—specifically checking pay codes and entitlements under Absence Pay Parameters to ensure they match your employee's service and benefit ranges. Use this when you need to troubleshoot why absence deductions aren't applying as expected during payroll processing.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the issue of absence pay codes failing to offset correctly during payroll processing, a problem typically caused by misconfiguration within absence rules. The document explains that such misconfiguration can impact various leave types, including maternity and paternity leave, resulting in inaccurate pay calculations. To resolve this issue, users must navigate to Settings > Absence Configuration > Absence Pay Parameters, then search for the relevant company code and select Absence Rules from the dropdown menu. The troubleshooting process requires users to highlight the affected absence rule, access the Pay Codes section, and verify that the correct pay code is configured with either the Effect Ent. on Rest Day or Value on Rest Day option enabled. Additionally, users must review the Entitlements section to confirm that an entitlement row exists covering both the required Employee Service Range and Benefit Range; if missing, users can add new entitlements by completing the necessary fields. This document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage absence configurations in the Access Group system and need to diagnose and correct pay offset problems affecting employee leave calculations.

t: Employer PAYE reference or accounts office reference is incorrect
s:
An employer's PAYE reference number and accounts office reference are essential legal identifiers used by HMRC. Each company registered with HMRC must have a unique PAYE reference and accounts office reference.

 

If you submit an RTI or FPS file and it gets rejected, the cause is an incorrect PAYE...
ss: When RTI or FPS files are rejected in PeopleXD, the cause is often an incorrect PAYE reference or accounts office reference that doesn't match HMRC's records. This document walks you through updating both identifiers in Portal—the PAYE reference (split into a three-digit office number and business reference) via Settings > Organisations, and the 13-character accounts office reference via Settings > Other General Settings. Open this guide if your payroll submissions are failing due to reference mismatches, or when setting up a new company's tax details in PeopleXD.
sl: This document explains how to correct incorrect PAYE reference or accounts office reference information in PeopleXD when RTI or FPS file submissions are rejected by HMRC. It covers the specific steps required to update both identifiers in the Portal system, as these are essential legal identifiers that must match HMRC's records for successful payroll submissions. For updating the PAYE reference, users navigate to Settings > Organisations, select the relevant company from the Code dropdown, and split the PAYE reference into two parts: entering the first three digits (HMRC office number) in the Tax Office Number and District Number fields, and the second part (business reference) in the Registered No and Tax Office Ref fields. The document explains that PAYE references typically follow a structure like 123/A56789 or 123/AB56789, with worked examples provided to clarify the data entry. For updating the accounts office reference, a thirteen-character identifier typically formatted as 123PX00123456, users access Settings > Other General Settings, select the company from the Company dropdown, and enter the reference in the Inland Revenue Paypath Reference field. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employer compliance and handle HMRC submissions, particularly when they encounter file rejection errors related to incorrect tax office identifiers.

t: Full payment submission file generated in error for a payroll period already submitted
s: If a portal user generates a FPS file, also known as a RTI (Real Time Information) file, by selecting the wrong payroll period or by being unaware that the FPS file has already been sent, it is important to remove the newly generated file. Transmitting this additional live file can result in the dup...
ss: Payroll administrators who accidentally generate a duplicate Full Payment Submission (FPS) or Real Time Information (RTI) file for a payroll period that's already been submitted to HMRC can use this guide to prevent submission errors. The process involves confirming the original file was accepted, recreating the incorrect file in Test Mode to overwrite the duplicate, and transferring the test file on screen. Open this document if you've generated an FPS file for the wrong payroll period or didn't realize a file had already been sent, as submitting duplicates can cause pay value duplication issues with HMRC.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving a specific error scenario where a Full Payment Submission (FPS) file, also known as an RTI (Real Time Information) file, has been accidentally generated and submitted for a payroll period that has already had a submission sent to HMRC. The document explains that this situation occurs when portal users select the wrong payroll period or are unaware that an FPS file has already been transmitted, resulting in the risk of duplicate pay values being reported to HMRC. To resolve this issue, users must first confirm that the original FPS file was successfully sent and accepted by HMRC, then recreate the incorrect FPS file using Test Mode, which will overwrite the duplicate live submission without transferring any actual information to HMRC. The recreated test file can then be transferred on screen once the overwrite is complete. If these steps do not resolve the problem, users are instructed to raise a new case online while referencing the article title and providing specific details including the pay group, payroll period, and HMRC confirmation documentation. This document is intended for portal users and payroll administrators who need to prevent erroneous duplicate RTI submissions that could cause compliance issues with HMRC.

t: Error: 'Pay Code : XXXX No Effective Position/Point (DD-MON-YYYY)
s:

To resolve this, we've compiled a list of how to solve the...
ss: The PAY140 Validation Observation report error occurs when a timesheet transaction date doesn't align with the employee's effective salary date in the Position History table, preventing payment processing in Back Office. This document walks you through resolving the mismatch by checking the salary effective date, amending the timesheet transaction date, or adjusting pay code settings like the Rate Seq Number field. Open this guide when an employee isn't receiving payment and you need to reconcile dates between the timesheet and position history, or when you need to verify pay code configuration in Back Office.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific payment error that occurs when the PAY140 Validation Observation report indicates that an employee's timesheet transaction date is earlier than their effective salary date stored in the Position History table, which prevents payment from being processed. The guide provides step-by-step instructions within the Back Office system to diagnose and resolve this issue through two primary approaches. To check the effective salary date, users navigate to Manage Payroll, select the relevant pay group, access the Inputs tab, click General, and then select Maintain Employee Position/Point. To correct the problem by amending the transaction date, users search for the employee through the Employee menu, click VIEW beside the relevant employee record, navigate to Timesheet Current Period, and adjust the transaction date to match the effective salary date. The document also addresses an alternative scenario where the timesheet transaction date is actually after the employee's position effective date, requiring users to verify the pay code setup by accessing Settings, selecting Pay Code under Codes, choosing the relevant pay code from the dropdown, and confirming that the Rate Seq Number field on the Allowances/Payments tab is set to 1 before checking the Analysis Code field. t: No pay or gross to nett generating on validation for employee
s:
If a validation report doesn't display the no pay or gross-to-net amounts for an employee, it is due to a Direct Earnings Attachment (DEA) assigned to that employee.

ss: When a validation report fails to display no pay or gross-to-net amounts for an employee, it's usually because a Direct Earnings Attachment (DEA) is assigned to that employee and lacks a negative value line in its scales. This situation occurs when an employee has reduced earnings or receives only statutory pay, resulting in a negative net amount that the DEA calculation cannot accommodate. Open this document if you need to resolve missing pay or gross-to-net values on validation reports by adding the appropriate negative value line to your DEA pay code settings in Portal.
sl: This document addresses a specific validation reporting issue in the Access Group payroll system where no pay or gross-to-net amounts fail to display for an employee on a validation report, a problem caused by a Direct Earnings Attachment (DEA) assigned to that employee. The issue occurs when an employee has reduced earnings or receives only statutory pay, which can generate a negative net amount during DEA calculation, but the DEA scales lack a corresponding negative value line to handle this scenario. The document provides step-by-step resolution instructions accessible through the Portal interface, requiring navigation to Settings > Codes > Pay Code (Classic). The fix involves selecting the DEA Paycode, accessing the Deductions tab to enable Nett Earnings under Court Order/AEO's, then navigating to the Scales section to add a negative value line (such as -9999 to 0) for both weekly and monthly columns. After saving these changes, users must return to Pay Code (Classic) and disable Nett Earnings to complete the configuration. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and system configuration staff who need to troubleshoot validation report discrepancies related to DEA processing and ensure proper handling of edge cases involving negative net pay scenarios.

The document is intended for HR personnel or system administrators who encounter this error during employee record management or updates and need guidance on escalating the issue to technical support. t: Error: 'LEL must be entered'
s:
If you encounter the above error message while attempting to issue a manual payment in the portal, there are two potential causes:

The NI Breakdown area in the manual payment has not been fully completed.

A row has been added to the "Manual Payment Pay Codes" area in the manual payment for Employe...
ss: The "LEL must be entered" error occurs when issuing manual payments in the portal due to incomplete NI Breakdown information or zero-value rows in the Manual Payment Pay Codes area. To resolve this, ensure the NI Breakdown section—including the LEL (Lower Earnings Limit) field—is fully completed with actual values or zeros where no amounts are due, and remove any zero-value NI rows from the Manual Payment Pay Codes section. Open this document if you're processing manual payments and encounter this validation error, or if you need guidance on properly completing National Insurance fields in the portal payment process.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre addresses the error message "LEL must be entered" that users encounter when attempting to issue a manual payment through the portal. The error has two specific root causes: either the NI Breakdown area within the manual payment form has not been completely filled out, or a row has been added to the "Manual Payment Pay Codes" area for Employee NI or Employer NI that contains a zero value rather than actual figures. To resolve this issue, users must ensure the NI Breakdown area is fully completed, including specifically the LEL field, and should enter a zero ("0") if no values are applicable rather than leaving the field blank. Additionally, users should not add rows with zero values to the Manual Payment Pay Codes section on the Manual Payment screen when no NI is due, as this triggers the error. The document is intended for portal users who process manual payments and encounter this validation error, helping them understand the specific field requirements and data entry rules for National Insurance calculations. The guide also references related processes including portal and back office manual payment procedures, other NI-related errors, and post payroll corrections, providing context for the broader manual payment workflow.

sl: This document provides guidance on escalating support cases within the Access Group Help Centre by directing users through a four-level escalation framework based on the technical skill level (IC level) required to resolve the issue. For Level 1 escalations, users should email the Salesforce Case system and update the case with a request for escalation. Level 2 escalations require contacting the dedicated Escalation Mailbox at PeopleXDEscalationManagement@theaccessgroup.com, which is monitored Monday through Friday by the support leadership team. For the highest level of escalation (Level 4), users must contact the Support Manager, either Graham Mynott for Payroll, Expense and Pensions or Earl McFarlane for People Management, Recruitment, Talent and WFM. t: Configure file definitions for our financial management system
s:
In PeopleXD, the file definition feature allows you to configure how output files are structured, ensuring they meet the format requirements of your financial management systems(FMS).

 

You can customise the different parts of the output file independently, including:

Header File: Defines the hea...
ss: File definitions in PeopleXD allow you to structure output files that integrate with your financial management system (FMS), letting you customise the header, detail, and footer sections independently. You configure journal files by selecting a file code, choosing which accounting and costing fields to include, and setting the position and size of each field in the output. Open this document when you need to set up or modify how data is formatted and exported from PeopleXD to your FMS, or when you're mapping specific costing fields to appear in your General Ledger output.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide to configuring file definitions in PeopleXD, a financial management system tool that allows users to structure and format output files according to their specific FMS requirements. The document explains how to customize three independent sections of output files: the Header File, Detail File, and Footer File, enabling organizations to tailor file structure to their needs. The core process involves navigating to Settings > General Ledger Costing > General Rules & Settings, selecting File Definition from the Select Detail drop-down menu, and then choosing or creating a file code that uniquely identifies the output file for the FMS system. Users must configure record types (such as Detail Record) and select from available definition elements—accounting and costing fields that PeopleXD pre-sets and maintains—choosing only those fields relevant to their specific FMS and GL requirements. For each selected field, users specify three key parameters: the Field (which definition element to include), the Posn (position in the output), and the Size (number of characters the field can hold), with the system displaying all available fields in a grid format at the bottom of the screen. This document is primarily used by financial management system administrators and costing specialists who need to configure journal files and ensure that output data from PeopleXD correctly maps to their financial management systems with proper field sequencing and character limits. The configuration process concludes by saving changes, and the document references related tasks such as generating Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) files and managing GL Matrix Definitions.

t: GL file layout incorrect with columns in the wrong order
s:
When the columns in a GL file are not displayed in the correct sequence, this can result to processing errors. This issue arises when configuration changes are made to the GL file definition. 

 

To resolve this issue, you need to update the file layout by ensuring each required field is positioned...
ss: When GL file columns appear in the wrong order, it can cause processing errors—typically after configuration changes to the GL file definition. Use this article to fix column sequencing by updating file layout in portal Settings under General Ledger Costing, where you'll adjust position values for each field to ensure they're correct and unique. Open this guide when you're experiencing GL processing failures or need to reconfigure field positions after making changes to your GL file setup.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving a GL file layout issue where columns appear in the wrong sequence, which can cause processing errors when configuration changes are made to the GL file definition. The document contains step-by-step instructions for updating the file layout through the portal by navigating to Settings, then General Ledger Costing, and selecting Create File Definitions. Users must locate their required GL file using the File Code drop-down menu and then review each field by scrolling to the bottom of the screen. The resolution involves clicking into each field individually and overwriting the position value (Posn) to ensure that every position reference is correct and unique according to the desired column order. This process must be repeated for every column that will be in use to ensure proper positioning. The document is intended for financial management system users who have encountered GL file layout errors after making configuration changes, and it references related articles covering file definition setup, GL file generation, and other general ledger interface issues.

t: Set up new expense code
s:
Setting up a new expense code for financial reporting purposes in the GL is essential for ensuring accurate financial reporting and analysis. 

 

This process allows you to monitor spending in specific categories, assess budget compliance, and generate detailed financial reports.

 

To set up a ne...
ss: Setting up a new expense code in the General Ledger (GL) enables you to track spending across specific categories and ensure accurate financial reporting. This process makes expense codes available in timesheets, pay codes, and the GL matrix so you can monitor budget compliance and generate detailed financial reports. Open this document when you need to create a new expense/GL code in your portal by navigating to Settings > General Ledger Costing > Expense/GL Codes. You'll also find troubleshooting guidance if expense codes aren't generating correctly in your GL interface or pay code screens.
sl: This document provides guidance on creating new expense codes in the General Ledger (GL) system for accurate financial reporting and analysis. The process enables users to monitor spending across specific categories, assess budget compliance, and generate detailed financial reports while making the expense code available across timesheets, pay codes, and the GL matrix. The setup is performed through the portal by navigating to Settings, then under General Ledger Costing, clicking on Expense/GL Codes, where users can view existing codes before proceeding. To add a new expense code, users click the Add Expense/GL Codes button and complete required fields including the Expense/GL Codes name, Description, and Tax Code, then activate the code by toggling the Active switch before clicking OK. The document addresses several common issues that users may encounter during or after expense code setup, including scenarios where expense codes fail to generate on View History Details or GL interface files, where changes to expense codes on pay codes do not update in the GL interface, and where the system returns an error stating "No Expense found on GL matrix for Pay code." This resource is typically used by finance administrators, payroll managers, and GL accounting personnel who need to configure the chart of accounts and ensure proper expense tracking and reporting across the organization's financial systems.

t: Expense codes are not generating on View History Details or General Ledger Interface file
s:
When running the PAY300 job, you may encounter an issue where expense codes appear as 0 instead of the correctly mapped codes from the GL matrix for pay codes. 

 

This discrepancy prevents the correct expense codes from being output to the History Details or the GL Interface file. This issue often...
ss: Expense codes are not generating correctly on View History Details or General Ledger Interface files when running the PAY300 job, appearing as 0 instead of the properly mapped codes from the GL matrix. This issue typically affects only one registered company within your organisation while others work normally, and is usually caused by incorrect GL matrix configuration (set at company level instead of organisational level) or the background indicator being enabled. Open this document if you're troubleshooting missing or incorrect expense codes in your payroll GL interface output, or if you need to verify your GL matrix setup and understand when to contact support for background indicator fixes.
sl: This document addresses a specific issue within the PAY300 job where expense codes fail to generate correctly, appearing as 0 instead of the properly mapped codes from the GL matrix for corresponding pay codes, which prevents accurate output to both the View History Details and General Ledger Interface file. The problem typically affects only one registered company within an organisation while others operate normally, suggesting a configuration-specific issue rather than a system-wide failure. The document identifies two primary causes: incorrect GL matrix setup or configuration, and the background indicator being enabled, both of which can prevent expense codes from mapping correctly. To troubleshoot GL matrix configuration, users navigate through the portal to Settings > General Ledger Costing > General Rules and Settings, then select Matrix Classifications from the Detail dropdown menu, verify the Payment Classification and Employee Classifications fields are configured correctly, and check that no conflicting company-level matrix has been set up to override the organisational-level settings. If the background indicator is the cause, users must contact the support team by raising an online case that references the article title and includes specific details: a sample employee number, pay group, expense code, and pay code. This document is intended for finance, payroll, or system administrators who manage GL matrix configurations and need to resolve issues where expense codes fail to populate on reports and interface files, and it includes references to related articles covering expense code setup and updates on the PRSI Pay Code screen.

t: General Ledger Journal report (PAYB236) is not balancing against control totals
s:
If the GL file does not balance with the payroll control totals report after cancellations have been made for several employees, it is likely due to a timing issue. Specifically, a cancellation payment may have been applied before the GL was run.

 

When a payroll period concludes, the payroll cont...
ss: The General Ledger Journal report (PAYB236) in CorePay may not balance against payroll control totals when employee cancellations are processed after the GL is generated. This happens because cancellation payments applied before the GL run create a timing mismatch—the payroll control reports don't update to reflect cancellations made after period closure, while the GL pulls from the updated employee history in View History Details. Open this document if your GL report is showing different totals than your control reports following employee cancellations, and you need to understand why the discrepancy occurred and how to reconcile it.
sl: This document explains how to diagnose and resolve discrepancies between the General Ledger Journal report (PAYB236) and payroll control totals in the Access Group payroll system, with a focus on timing issues caused by employee cancellations. The core problem occurs when cancellation payments are processed after the GL has been run, causing the two reports to fall out of balance since payroll control reports do not update retroactively once the payroll period has concluded. The document describes how to verify whether cancellations have been recorded by navigating to CorePay > Enquiry > View History Details to check an employee's cumulative details, as this View History Details screen is the source data used to generate the GL report. When the GL is run after a cancellation has been recorded, it accurately reflects those changes; conversely, if the GL was generated before the cancellation was processed, the reports would balance correctly. The complete update report (PAY355) displays total values for all employees processed up to a given point, but subsequent cancellations that occur after this report is generated do not affect the payroll controls. Since it is not possible to modify payroll reports once the payroll process has been completed, the document advises that manual adjustments should be made to control totals to account for any cancellations or manual payments that were entered after the initial GL run. This document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to reconcile GL and control total reports and understand the sequence of events that leads to imbalances.

t: Error: 'KEY-COMMIT TRIGGER Raised unhandled exception ORA-29282'
s:
If generating a GL causes the screen to hang and the GL does not run, you may be facing one of three potential issues.

 

We have compiled a list of these issues along with their resolutions.

 

 

Hourly, daily or annual rate of pay

This issue may relate to the employee's hourly, daily, or annua...
ss: When generating a general ledger (GL) in your payroll system causes the screen to hang or the GL fails to run, this document outlines three root causes: incorrectly configured hourly or daily pay rates, system-level data mapping errors with missing or duplicated entries, or missing company references in back-end tables. Open this article if you're experiencing GL generation failures and need to understand which issue might be responsible before contacting support. Each issue requires support team intervention to run diagnostic scripts, so the document also tells you what information to gather (pay group, payroll period, and relevant rate or company details) when raising a case online.
sl: This document from Access Group Help Centre addresses a specific error (ORA-29282) that occurs when generating a GL (General Ledger) causes the system screen to hang and the GL fails to run. The document identifies three distinct potential causes of this issue and provides troubleshooting guidance for each scenario. The first potential cause relates to the employee's hourly, daily, or annual rate of pay, where excessively high values in the daily or hourly rate fields may trigger GL failure, or a system-level data mapping error may be present. The second cause involves data mapping issues at the system level, which could include missing or duplicated entries that prevent proper GL generation. The third potential cause is a missing company reference in back-end tables, which can similarly prevent the GL from running successfully. For each of these three scenarios, the document advises users to contact the support team by raising a new online case and referencing the article title, while providing specific details including the pay group, payroll period, and—depending on the issue—either the correct daily or hourly rate, company reference, or confirmation of data mapping problems. This troubleshooting guide is intended for payroll and finance professionals who encounter GL generation failures within the Access Group system and need structured guidance on identifying and resolving the underlying cause.

s:
If you run the GL in Back Office and encounter the following error, it means that the user lacks access to the drive where the file is being saved.

 

To resolve this issue, follow the steps below.

Click CorePay then click Reference.

Click Advanced Reference Features then Reference D-J.

ss: The General Ledger (GL) process in CorePay Back Office may fail when attempting to transfer or save log files if the user account lacks sufficient permissions to the destination drive. This error prevents the GL from completing and requires checking the file location settings in CorePay's GL Parameters and verifying drive access rights. Open this document if you encounter a log file transfer error in Back Office and need to diagnose whether the issue is a permissions or access problem. You'll also find the steps to contact IT for read/write access requests to the required file location.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides troubleshooting guidance for resolving a file transfer error that occurs when running the General Ledger (GL) in Back Office, specifically when a user lacks the necessary access permissions to the drive where the file is being saved. The document walks users through a specific navigation path to verify the file location: starting by clicking CorePay, then Reference, followed by Advanced Reference Features and Reference D-J, then GL Parameters, where users should select "File Association" from the Select Detail dropdown menu. After entering the relevant pay group, users can check the configured file location and then navigate to that location on their computer to verify whether they have the required access rights. If the file location is inaccessible, the document directs users to contact their IT department to request full read/write access to the drive in question. This document is intended for Back Office users and system administrators who encounter this user-defined exception error during GL operations and need to resolve access permission issues related to file storage locations. The guide assumes users have basic familiarity with the Back Office interface and the GL parameters configuration area.

t: Expense code changed on pay code not updating in GL interface
s:
If you updated an expense code on the pay code screen but the old expense code is still posting to the General Ledger, you need to update the PRSI codes in the payroll parameters.

 

To resolve this, follow the steps below. 

Click CorePay then click Reference. 

Click Payroll Parameters then query...
ss: When you update an expense code on a pay code but the old code continues posting to the General Ledger, you need to update the PRSI codes in CorePay's payroll parameters. Access CorePay > Reference > Payroll Parameters, query your company, and enter the new PRSI code details on Page 3, then save. Open this document if expense codes aren't syncing correctly between your pay code setup and GL interface, or if historical pay records show incorrect coding after an update. Note that this fix applies only to future pay periods and won't retroactively change codes on previous transactions.
sl: This document addresses a specific integration issue in CorePay where updating an expense code on the pay code screen fails to reflect the change in the General Ledger interface. The problem occurs when the old expense code continues posting to the GL despite the pay code modification, requiring a secondary configuration update to resolve the discrepancy. To fix this issue, users must navigate to CorePay, then Reference, followed by Payroll Parameters, where they query their company and proceed to Page 3 to enter the new PRSI Code details. After entering the updated PRSI codes on Page 3 of the Payroll Parameters screen, users save the changes using the save icon to complete the process. The document includes an important caveat that this change will not retroactively affect existing pay codes and may have implications for the General Ledger in previous accounting periods, meaning historical data will not be automatically corrected. This guide is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who manage pay code configurations and need to ensure that expense codes sync correctly between the payroll system and the GL interface.
