s:
If the General Ledger run only produces PDF and text files, even though the user has pay group access, the issue is due to the missing .CSV file extension in the file association for the pay group.

 

To resolve this, follow these steps in Back Office:

Click CorePay then click Reference. 

Click A...
ss: When running the General Ledger in CorePay, the CSV file may fail to generate even though the user has the correct pay group access. This issue occurs when the .CSV file extension is missing from the file association settings in GL Parameters. Open this document if your General Ledger run is only producing PDF and text files instead of the expected CSV output, and you need step-by-step instructions to add the missing file extension in Back Office and regenerate the file.
sl: This document addresses a specific technical issue that occurs when the General Ledger run in an Access Group payroll system fails to generate CSV files despite the user having appropriate pay group access. The problem stems from a missing .CSV file extension in the file association configuration for the pay group, which causes the system to output only PDF and text files instead of the expected CSV format. To resolve this issue, users must navigate through the Back Office system via a specific menu path: CorePay > Reference > Advanced Reference Features > Reference D-J > GL Parameters > File Association. Within the File Association screen, users need to locate the File Name column and manually add the .CSV file extension to the end of the existing file name entry. After making this configuration change, users must re-generate the General Ledger run, which should then produce the CSV file output as expected. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, finance teams, and system configuration specialists who encounter missing CSV outputs during General Ledger processing and need to troubleshoot file generation problems related to pay group settings. The guide also references related articles on topics including General Ledger journal report balancing issues, log file transfer errors, and other General Ledger generation procedures, providing context for broader General Ledger functionality within the system.

t: Cost centre not appearing on GL for employee deduction pay code
s:
If an employee's cost centre does not appear on the General Ledger for a deduction pay code, it's due to the Timesheet Override indicator. 

 

When you enable the Timesheet Override indicator, the cost centre specified on the timesheet will be used. If it is not enabled, the system will default to ...
ss: When a deduction pay code isn't showing the correct cost centre on the General Ledger, the issue is usually the Timesheet Override indicator setting. Enabling this toggle in the Pay Code configuration allows the timesheet cost centre to override the default pay code cost centre. Open this document if you need to configure deduction pay codes in Portal so they pull cost centre data from timesheets rather than using a fixed default. Follow the steps to navigate to Settings > Pay Codes (Classic), select your deduction code, and enable the Timesheet Override toggle on the Deduction tab.
sl: This document explains how to resolve an issue where a cost centre fails to appear on the General Ledger when processing employee deduction pay codes, with the root cause being the Timesheet Override indicator setting. The document clarifies that when the Timesheet Override indicator is enabled, the system uses the cost centre specified on the timesheet, whereas if disabled, it defaults to the cost centre assigned directly to the pay code itself. To configure this setting, users must navigate through the Portal interface by clicking Settings, then selecting Pay Codes (Classic) from the Codes section. Once in the Pay Codes configuration, the user selects the relevant deduction pay code from the dropdown menu and accesses the Deduction tab where the Timesheet Override toggle can be enabled or disabled as needed. After making the necessary adjustment to the toggle, users must click Save to apply the changes. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and system configuration specialists who manage pay code settings and need to ensure that cost centre information correctly flows through to the General Ledger for accurate financial reporting and cost allocation tracking.

t: Changed expense code on PRSI Pay Code screen is not showing on GL interface
s:
If you change the expense code on the Pay Code screen for PRSI codes and the new code isn't reflecting on the General Ledger Interface, this is because the PRSI codes haven't been updated in payroll parameters.

 

To resolve this, follow the steps below in Back Office.

Click CorePay then click Ref...
ss: When you change an expense code on the PRSI Pay Code screen in CorePay, the updated code may not appear on the General Ledger Interface because the PRSI codes haven't been refreshed in payroll parameters. Open this document if you need to update PRSI codes in Back Office Payroll Parameters to ensure the new expense codes sync with GL. The fix involves navigating to CorePay > Reference > Payroll Parameters, entering your company code, and updating PRSI details on page 3. Note that this change won't apply retroactively and may affect GL reports for prior periods.
sl: This document addresses a specific synchronization issue in payroll accounting where changes made to expense codes on the Pay Code screen for PRSI codes fail to appear on the General Ledger Interface. The problem occurs because PRSI codes must be independently updated in the payroll parameters for the changes to propagate to the GL system. The resolution requires navigating through the Back Office system via CorePay > Reference > Payroll Parameters, where users enter their company code number and access page 3 (using the right arrow navigation icon) to update the PRSI code details before saving the changes. This document is intended for payroll administrators and GL accountants who manage PRSI configurations and need to ensure expense codes are properly synchronized between the pay code setup and general ledger reporting. The document includes an important caveat that this process will not retroactively update existing pay codes and may impact the running of GL reports for retrospective periods, requiring careful consideration of timing when making these changes. The documentation also references related articles covering PRSI class changes, similar GL interface update issues, PRSI relief options, and GL matrix error messages, indicating this is part of a broader suite of payroll-GL integration guidance.

t: GL Report cancel and manual payment values are not showing
s:
If you're running a GL report and the cancel and manual payment values are missing, it's because the corrected values should appear in the period when the cancellation and manual payment were made.

 

For example, if you cancel a payment for period 202308 in period 202330, it should reflect in the ...
ss: GL reports may not display cancel and manual payment values because these corrected amounts should appear in the period when the cancellation or manual payment actually occurred, not the original payment period. If the values are still missing after checking the correct period, the issue is likely caused by the "Generate GL for Supplementary Run" toggle being enabled in your General Ledger settings. Open this document if you're troubleshooting missing cancel or manual payment entries in your GL report, or if your General Ledger journal isn't showing the expected transaction values. Follow the steps provided to disable the toggle and re-run your report to resolve the issue.
sl: This document addresses a specific issue encountered when running General Ledger reports where cancel and manual payment values fail to display in the expected locations. The core principle explained is that cancelled payments and manual payments should appear in the General Ledger journal for the period in which the cancellation or manual payment action was actually performed, not the original payment period—for instance, if a payment for period 202308 is cancelled in period 202330, the adjustment should reflect in the period 202330 journal. When values remain missing even after understanding this timing principle, the document provides a troubleshooting procedure that requires navigating to Settings, then General Ledger Costing, then General Rules & Settings to access the Parameter Settings dropdown menu. The specific resolution involves verifying that the "Generate GL for Supplementary Run" toggle is disabled, as an enabled setting can prevent values from appearing correctly. Users must save their changes after confirming the toggle status and then re-run the General Ledger report to display the previously missing cancel and manual payment values. This document is typically consulted by payroll and finance professionals managing General Ledger reporting and reconciliation tasks, particularly when investigating discrepancies in payment adjustments across accounting periods.

t: Generate a General Ledger file
s:
Generating a GL file for seamless integration with an external Financial Management System (FMS) ensures accurate financial data transfer and streamlines accounting workflows. 

 

You should perform this task when you need to export payroll or financial data to an external FMS for reporting, reconc...
ss: Generating a General Ledger (GL) file exports payroll and financial data from your payroll system to an external Financial Management System (FMS) for accurate accounting integration. Use this process when you need to transfer data for financial reporting, reconciliation, or compliance purposes. The task is performed in Portal by selecting your pay group, specifying the relevant period, and generating the file through the Outputs tab. Once generated, you can access the GL file from the Report Centre for import into your FMS.
sl: This document provides instructions for generating a General Ledger (GL) file from a payroll system to enable seamless integration and accurate financial data transfer with an external Financial Management System (FMS). The process is performed when users need to export payroll or financial data for reporting, reconciliation, or compliance purposes. The task involves navigating through Portal by clicking Manage Payroll and highlighting the relevant pay group, then accessing the Outputs tab and selecting General Ledger. Users must specify the pay group from the Pay Group drop-down menu and define the reporting period by entering values in the From Period and To Period fields. After clicking the Generate button, the exported files can be accessed through the Report Centre for further review or distribution. The document also references related troubleshooting articles addressing common issues such as cost centre data not displaying as expected on the general ledger output and General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) imbalances against control totals, which may be consulted if generation or reconciliation problems arise.

t: Employee cost centres are not being mapped to correct expense code
s:
The general ledger matrix is defined by cost centre and pay code. Ensure that the correct combinations exist in the general ledger matrix.

 

When the payroll update runs, it will select the expense code from the matrix if it is available for the combination of data in the history. If no matrix is ...
ss: Employee cost centre and expense code mapping relies on correctly configured entries in the general ledger matrix, which matches cost centre and pay code combinations. When payroll runs, the system pulls the expense code from the matrix for each employee's cost centre and pay code pairing—if no matching entry exists, the output defaults to 0. Open this document if expense codes aren't displaying correctly on payroll reports, or if cost centre information from HR records isn't mapping to the general ledger as expected. This is particularly relevant in non-post management environments where the system references HR records to populate cost centre data.
sl: This document explains how to resolve issues where employee cost centres are not being correctly mapped to expense codes in a payroll system, specifically addressing problems with the general ledger matrix configuration. The general ledger matrix is defined by the combination of cost centre and pay code, and the system relies on this matrix to assign the correct expense code during payroll processing. When the payroll update runs, it attempts to locate the appropriate expense code from the matrix based on the combination of cost centre and pay code data in the employee's history; if no matching matrix entry exists, the system outputs 0 instead of a valid code. The document clarifies that adding a matrix entry after payroll has already run will not retroactively update pay history for periods that have already been processed. If the issue stems from missing or incomplete appointment records in the history data, the general ledger program will reference the employee's HR record to determine the correct cost centre, making it essential to verify both the cost centre value on the HR record and ensure a corresponding matrix entry exists for that cost centre and pay code combination. This mapping problem can be particularly prevalent in non-post management environments. The document appears designed for payroll administrators, HR professionals, and system configuration specialists who need to troubleshoot expense code allocation issues and configure the general ledger matrix correctly.

t: Available fields on GL Matrix Definition
s:
To learn more about the available field names in the GL Matrix Definition, please refer to the description of the GL matrix field elements below.

 

Analysis code: Every pay code is linked to an analysis code so effectively this means that pay codes can be grouped into analysis codes for the purpos...
ss: GL Matrix Definition outlines the field structure used in CoreHR and CorePay to organize and report on payroll data. It covers how pay codes, analysis codes, labour cost groups, and employee classifications work together to categorize pay information, organizational structure, and cost allocation. Use this document when you need to understand which fields are available to configure in the GL Matrix, how different grouping options relate to each other, or when troubleshooting GL posting errors related to pay codes and cost centres. This is essential reference material for payroll administrators, HR teams, and finance users setting up or managing the GL Matrix configuration.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive reference guide to the field elements and configuration options available within the GL Matrix Definition in CoreHR's payroll system. It describes the foundational pay structure elements, including pay codes as the lowest transactional unit (such as Salary, OT@1, PAYE, NI EE, NI ER, EE Pension, and Student Loan), analysis codes used to group pay codes for reporting purposes, and labour cost groups which function similarly to analysis codes but are optional rather than mandatory. The document outlines employee classification structures including Category and Sub Category fields for professional or bargaining groupings, Status and Sub Status fields for employment type (such as permanent or part-time), and organizational hierarchy fields encompassing Management Unit, Department, Division, and Location to structure the business. It explains payroll-specific configuration settings such as the requirement for at least one CorePay company code (with additional codes needed only if the organization has separate registered companies requiring multiple Revenue Returns) and HR Company definitions for single or grouped legal entities, along with Pay Groups which logically group employees sharing a common pay frequency for processing. The document further details employee assignment fields including Job Title, Work Group for team assignment and line management, Cost Centre for cost allocation aligned with the financial system, Project codes for temporary endeavors, and Position Code which determines pay based on grade and scale point relative to job responsibility and tenure. This reference guide is typically consulted by payroll administrators, HR configuration specialists, and finance teams who need to understand how to structure and map organizational and compensation data within CoreHR's GL Matrix, particularly when troubleshooting errors such as missing GL expense assignments for specific pay codes.

t: What is a project code and what impact does it have on an employee's record
s:
What is a project code? 

A project code is a character alphanumeric code, used to represent a project that an employee may be assigned to, and is used for reporting and/or General Ledger purposes. Project codes are not mandatory.

 

In PeopleXD, a project code can be set in the employee’s appointm...
ss: Project codes are alphanumeric codes used in PeopleXD to assign employees to projects for reporting and General Ledger purposes. You can set project codes in three ways: on an employee's appointment/contract record in People Management, through cost allocations, or against individual timesheet entries in the Workforce Management module. Open this document if you need to create a new project code, assign one to an employee's record, or understand how project codes affect payroll and timesheet reporting. This is particularly useful if you're managing employee records and need to allocate costs or hours to specific projects.
sl: This document explains what project codes are and how to implement them within the PeopleXD system for employee record management and financial reporting purposes. A project code is an alphanumeric code used to represent projects assigned to employees for reporting and General Ledger purposes, though they are not mandatory. The document describes three primary methods for setting project codes: through the employee's appointment/contract record in People Management (accessed via Dashboard > People Management > Employees > VIEW > the specific employee > Contracts > Update, where the project code is entered in the Project field with an effective date and reason), through Cost Allocations as an alternative approach, or via manual timesheet entries in the Workforce Management module. The document also covers the process for adding new project codes to the system by navigating to People Management Dashboard > Data Centre > View All, searching for Project Codes, and clicking Add to enter the code and description. An important note highlights that if a cost allocation or project code is specified on a manual timesheet entry, it takes precedence over the project code set on the employee's appointment/contract record. This document is used by HR administrators, payroll professionals, and managers who need to assign employees to projects, allocate labor costs across different projects, or configure the system for project-based reporting and financial tracking.

t: Back Office: Create a file definition
s:
Creating a file definition in your system establishes the structure and format for data imports and exports. It ensures consistent formatting, supports automated processing, and maintains data integrity during transfers between systems or external partners.

 

Apply this process when setting up new...
ss: Creating a file definition in CorePay establishes the structure and format for data imports and exports, ensuring consistent formatting and data integrity during transfers. Use this process when setting up new data integration workflows, configuring automated reporting outputs, or establishing standardised file formats for regular data exchanges with your financial management system. You'll access this feature through CorePay > Reference > Advanced Reference Features > GL Parameters > File Definition, where you can specify elements and their positions within the file. This is essential when you need to configure journal files for output to your financial management system or standardise how data is exchanged with external partners.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for creating a file definition in the back office system, which establishes the structure and format for data imports and exports while ensuring consistent formatting, supporting automated processing, and maintaining data integrity during transfers between systems or external partners. The document applies to scenarios involving setting up new data integration workflows, configuring automated reporting outputs, or establishing standardised file formats for regular data exchanges, with a specific focus on configuring the journal file for output to the financial management system. The process begins by navigating through CorePay to Reference, then to Advanced Reference Features and Reference D–J, followed by GL Parameters and File Definition. Users must enter a new file code and press enter, then enter the description of the file and press enter again, at which point all available definition elements are displayed for configuration. Within the File Detail Description section, users can specify the various elements and designate the position each element should occupy in the file. Once the file configuration is complete, users save their changes by clicking the save icon. This document is typically used by back office administrators and financial system operators who need to establish consistent data exchange formats with external partners or between internal systems.

t: Error: 'No Expense found on GL matrix for Pay code [PAY CODE]'
s:
If you encounter an error on the View Gross to Nett Observation report for a pay group, it may stem from one of two causes.

 

We’ve compiled a list of potential reasons for the error message and how to resolve them.

 

 

Pay code not set up

The specified pay code is not configured in the Profit...
ss: The View Gross to Nett Observation report in PeopleXD throws an error when a pay code lacks General Ledger matrix configuration or cost center mapping. This document helps you resolve the "No Expense found on GL matrix" error by walking through two common causes: pay codes not set up in the Profit & Loss or Balance Sheet matrix, or pay codes mapped at company level without cost centers assigned to employee allowances. Open this guide when you encounter GL posting errors during payroll processing or need to configure pay codes in Portal or CorePay to ensure expenses route to the correct cost centers.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving an error that occurs on the View Gross to Nett Observation report when expense codes are missing from the General Ledger matrix for a specific pay code. The document outlines two distinct root causes and their corresponding resolution procedures within the Access Group payroll system. The first scenario addresses situations where a pay code has not been configured in either the Profit and Loss or Balance Sheet matrix, requiring users to navigate to Portal Settings, access General Ledger Costing, and then General Rules & Settings to manually add new rows containing the pay code, department, and expense information for each matrix type before re-running the GL. The second scenario covers cases where the pay code has been mapped at the company level but lacks a cost center entry in the employee allowance screen, which users can resolve either through Portal by navigating to Employee, selecting an employee, accessing Employee Allowances, and amending the cost centre field, or through Back Office by following a similar path via CorePay. The document emphasizes that users should test all configuration changes in the UAT environment before implementing them in the LIVE environment to prevent disruptions. This resource is primarily used by payroll administrators and system configurators who need to troubleshoot General Ledger integration issues and ensure proper pay code mapping across the organization's cost center structure.

t: Bring a new employee into Payroll from People Management
s:
To ensure timely and accurate salary payments from the employee's start date, you need to integrate newly hired employees into the payroll system.

 

If employee records exist in the People Management system but are missing from the payroll module, this creates a disconnect that hinders proper comp...
ss: When a new employee's record exists in People Management but hasn't yet been added to the payroll system, you need to approve them for payroll to ensure timely salary payments from their start date. This process involves connecting the two systems—either through the Portal (using Manage Payroll and Approvals) or the Back Office (using CorePay)—and completing their tax details. Without this integration step, newly hired employees won't be properly set up for compensation processing, which can result in delayed payments and administrative issues. Open this document when you've finished setting up a new employee's personal details and employment terms in People Management and are ready to activate them in the payroll module.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for transferring newly hired employees from the People Management system into the payroll module to ensure timely and accurate salary payments from their start date. The document addresses a common integration problem where employee records exist in People Management but are missing from the payroll system, which can cause disconnects that lead to delayed payments and administrative complications. Once an employee's personal details, contract information, and employment terms have been recorded in People Management, the next step is to formally approve them for payroll using one of two system interfaces. For Portal users, the process involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing the Input tab, clicking Approvals, and then clicking JOIN beside the employee's name to open the Tax Details screen, where required fields must be completed and saved. For Back Office users working in CorePay, the process requires clicking CorePay then Employee, selecting Maintain Employee Details, using the list icon beside the Personnel No. field to display employees not yet transferred to CorePay, selecting the required employee number, pressing Tab to navigate through relevant fields, and clicking the save icon to complete the transfer. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel who need to ensure proper system integration during employee onboarding to avoid compensation processing delays.

t: Migration to the new PeopleXD Ideas Portal
s:
As part of our continued efforts to improve the way we collect and action feedback from our PeopleXD clients, we are migrating to a new Ideas Portal hosted within the Access Aha! environment.

 

This new portal provides a more modern interface, enhanced tracking features, and a stronger foundation ...
ss: The PeopleXD Ideas Portal is migrating to a new platform hosted in Access Aha! on 30th June 2025, with the legacy portal being permanently retired. Open this document if you need to understand how to access the new portal, whether through an automatic invite (if you submitted or voted on ideas in the last 12 months) or by registering manually. It covers what's changing, how to log in or set up your account, and what to do if you can't locate previously submitted ideas. Use this guide when transitioning your idea submissions and feedback to the new portal environment.
sl: This document guides PeopleXD clients through the migration from a legacy Ideas Portal to a new portal hosted in the Access Aha! environment, which takes effect on 30th June 2025 when the old portal becomes permanently inaccessible. The new portal offers enhanced functionality including modern interface design, improved tracking features, better two-way communication capabilities, and AI-assisted idea prioritisation to help collect and action client feedback more effectively. Ideas submitted in the last 12 months or containing 10 or more votes will be automatically transferred to the new portal, while older ideas not meeting these criteria will be retained internally by the product team for roadmap planning but will not appear in the portal. Users can access the new portal either through invitation emails sent to those who previously submitted or voted on ideas within the last 12 months—which automatically creates user accounts requiring password setup—or by manually registering through the portal's Sign up function by entering email address and name. The document provides troubleshooting guidance for users who cannot locate previously submitted ideas, recommending they search with alternative keywords or resubmit ideas as new entries, and directs users encountering registration, login, or search issues to raise a case online or contact their customer success manager. This document is essential for PeopleXD clients and portal users who need to transition their accounts and understand how their existing feedback and ideas will be managed in the new system.

t: Data is not updating on the External HR interface screen or in the tables
s:
The External HR interface file is a crucial component that enables the transfer of employee data between HR systems and CorePay.

 

This file ensures that all relevant employee information including personal details, job roles, and compensation, is accurately reflected in CorePay for effective payr...
ss: The External HR interface file transfers employee data—including personal details, job roles, and compensation—between your HR systems and CorePay for payroll and benefits processing. Open this document if data is not updating correctly in CorePay or the External HR interface screen, or if employee information changes aren't being reflected in payroll. It covers three main causes: incorrect data within the file, incorrect file format (column count or data type issues), and configuration problems with the check_accept_changes_ind parameter. Use this troubleshooting guide to diagnose data sync failures and determine whether you need to fix your data file or contact support for configuration adjustments.
sl: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting data synchronization issues between HR systems and CorePay through the External HR interface file, which is responsible for transferring critical employee information such as personal details, job roles, and compensation data into CorePay for accurate payroll and benefits processing. The document outlines three primary categories of issues that prevent data from updating on the External HR interface screen or in associated tables, along with corresponding resolution steps for each scenario. Users should first verify that their data file conforms to the standards specified in the External HR Interface User Guide before proceeding with troubleshooting. The first potential cause is incorrect data within the file itself, which requires manual review and correction to ensure accuracy before resubmission. The second issue involves incorrect file format, specifically mismatches in the number of columns or data format structure, which must be corrected to align with system requirements. The third cause relates to a configuration parameter called check_accept_changes_ind being set to 'Y', which prevents proper data updates and requires Access Group support to change this parameter to 'N' by submitting a support case that includes the problematic External HR interface file. This document is primarily used by HR administrators, payroll specialists, and system users responsible for managing employee data imports into CorePay who encounter synchronization failures or incomplete data updates.

This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and support staff who encounter scheduling or log file generation failures in the PeopleHub system. t: Portal: Change an employee's pay group
s:
A pay group is used to categorise employees with the same pay frequency. All employees within a pay group are processed together for payments. Each employee needs to be assigned to a pay group, and every pay group will need to be associated with a company.

 

You may need to change an employee's pa...
ss: Pay groups categorize employees by pay frequency, and all employees within a pay group are processed together for payments. Use this guide when you need to change an employee's assigned pay group due to changes in pay frequency (weekly, monthly, etc.), payment type, tax jurisdiction, or contract modifications. The process differs depending on whether the pay groups are in the same company or different companies—same company moves don't require making the employee dormant, but cross-company moves do. Follow the step-by-step portal instructions provided to update the employee's pay group assignment in the system.
sl: This document provides guidance on changing an employee's pay group within the Access Group Portal system, explaining that pay groups categorize employees by pay frequency and that all employees within a pay group are processed together for payments. The document covers multiple scenarios requiring a pay group change, including modifications to pay frequency (monthly, weekly, etc.), payment type (wages or salary), tax jurisdiction, or employment contract terms. It establishes critical prerequisites and constraints: if pay groups belong to different companies, the employee must first be made dormant through the standard process and then rehired after the change; if pay groups are in the same company, no dormancy is required, but the new pay group's payroll period must be the same as or after the current pay group's period, and moving an employee to an earlier payroll period is not permitted. The specific process for same-company pay group changes involves navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, accessing Inputs, clicking General, then selecting Amend Employee Pay Group, choosing the employee from a dropdown menu, and overwriting the current pay group with the new one in the Pay Group field. The document notes that if the Pay Group dropdown menu appears blank, users should click Open Legacy Form to complete the process. This document is designed for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee compensation structures within the Portal system and need to understand both the procedural steps and the system constraints governing pay group transitions.

t: Items to consider when moving an employee's pay group
s:
Before you change an employee's pay group, you need to consider several items, which we've summarised below.

 

There would be several reasons as to why an employee's pay group will need to be changed, such as:

Changing pay frequency (monthly, weekly, etc.).

Different payment type (wages/salary)....
ss: Moving an employee's pay group in Corepay requires careful planning to avoid payroll errors and system issues. This document covers the key considerations before making the change, including user access permissions, timing within payroll cycles, adjustments needed when switching between weekly and monthly schedules, and special handling for cross-company or cross-jurisdiction transfers. Open this guide before initiating a pay group change to understand cumulative value transfers, amendments reporting impacts, and whether the employee needs to be processed as a leaver or new hire. It also clarifies payroll period matching rules and configuration updates required for allowances and deductions.
sl: This document provides guidance on critical considerations and prerequisites before changing an employee's pay group within the Access Group payroll system, addressing scenarios such as changing pay frequency, payment type, tax jurisdiction, or contract terms. The document outlines user access requirements, explaining that employees can only modify pay groups if they have been allocated access to that specific pay group via the Portal (Settings > Pay Group Access) or Back Office (Corepay > Reference > Pay Users), and warns that attempting changes without proper access will trigger an error message stating "This Pay Group has not been allocated to your Username." It describes how the PAY300 Control report update process transfers employee gross pay, tax, and PRSI details to the new pay group, with these amendments appearing in the payroll control report and potentially causing opening and closing balance mismatches. The document emphasizes the critical timing requirement to always move employees at the start of a payroll cycle to ensure correct handling of cumulative values, and explicitly warns against making changes during active payroll cycles. For cross-company transfers, it specifies that employees must first be processed as leavers and marked as dormant before completing the pay group change, as all data including cumulative values will transfer to the new company. When changing between weekly and monthly pay schedules, the document requires manual updates to all periodic allowances and deductions unless the annual allowance indicator is set to 'Y', and when moving to a different tax jurisdiction, it mandates creating a new employee record rather than processing as a rejoiner. Finally, it clarifies that payroll periods must match or follow the current period, with no ability to transfer to an earlier period, otherwise an error will be generated.

t: Move an employee to a different company
s:
When moving an employee between companies, you need to process the employee as a leaver in the old company and rejoin them in the new company to comply with RTI requirements. 

 

The FPS will need to show the employee as a leaver in the previous company and a rejoiner in the new company. To do this...
ss: Moving an employee between companies in CorePay requires processing them as a leaver in their old pay group and a rejoiner in the new pay group to meet RTI and HMRC reporting requirements. The process differs depending on whether the move is within the same tax jurisdiction or to a different one (such as UK to Ireland). You'll need to set the employee as a leaver, run payroll and submit an FPS, change their pay group through either Portal or Back Office, then rejoin them in the new pay group. Open this document when transferring an employee to another company and you need step-by-step instructions for updating their employment status and pay group in the system.
sl: This document provides instructions for transferring an employee between companies while maintaining compliance with Real Time Information (RTI) requirements for HMRC reporting. The process requires marking the employee as a leaver in their original company and then rejoining them in the new company, with the Full Payment Submission (FPS) reflecting both statuses appropriately. For moves within the same tax jurisdiction, the document outlines a five-step process: setting the employee as a leaver in the old pay group, running payroll to make them dormant, submitting the FPS to report them as a leaver to HMRC, changing their pay group using either the Portal route (via People Management Dashboard > Employees > Actions > Change Pay Group) or the Back Office route (via CorePay > Employee > Advanced Employee Features > Amend Employee's Pay Group), and finally rejoining the employee and running the new pay group payroll. For cross-jurisdiction moves (such as UK to Irish or Irish to UK), the process requires fully processing the employee as a leaver and creating a separate new employee record in the destination company rather than simply changing pay groups. The document also references related articles addressing common issues including the "Cannot leave and rejoin in the same period" error, impacts on the RPN process, temporary reinstatement payments, and special considerations for rejoining in a new pay group. This resource is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR personnel managing employee transfers between entities within the Access Group system.

t: Remove non-starters (joiners) from approval screen
s:
If you have employees that are due to start in your employment but don't start (non-starters), you will not be able to remove them from the approvers list. 

If you previously requested the removal of employees from this list but now need them reinstated, please note that support will need to run so...
ss: Non-starters (employees who don't begin employment) cannot be removed from the approvers list through standard processes in this system. If you need to reinstate an employee who was previously removed from the approval screen, support must run database scripts to complete this action. Open this article when you're unable to remove non-starter employees from approvals or need to restore access for someone after a previous removal request. You'll need to raise a support case with employee details, payroll period information, and the original case number if requesting reinstatement.
sl: This document explains how to handle non-starter employees within an approval screen management process in the Access Group system. The document addresses a specific limitation: employees who are scheduled to start employment but do not actually commence cannot be removed from the approvers list through standard processes. If users have previously submitted requests to remove employees from the approvers list and now need those employees reinstated, the system requires database-level intervention that only support staff can perform. To request either removal or reinstatement of non-starter employees, users must raise a new support case online and reference this article's title, providing employee details and the relevant payroll period. For reinstatement requests specifically, users must also supply the original case number that was used when the employee was initially removed from the approval screen. This document is typically used by payroll administrators or HR personnel managing employee records and approval workflows who encounter situations where non-starters need to be added back to or removed from approval processes. The related articles referenced suggest this is part of a broader suite of tools for managing employee data, payroll submissions, and approval workflows within the Access Group's HR and payroll system.

t: Portal: Load personal rates of pay in bulk
s:
Loading personal pay rates in bulk allows you to efficiently update multiple employee pay rates simultaneously, saving time and reducing the chance for manual errors.

 

This process is essential for applying new pay agreements, implementing salary adjustments, or onboarding a large group of employ...
ss: Loading personal pay rates in bulk through the Portal allows you to update multiple employee pay rates at once, which is faster and more accurate than manual entry. Use this process when applying new pay agreements, implementing salary adjustments, or onboarding large groups of employees. The task involves navigating to Uploads > Employee New Rates of Pay and following specific formatting rules, including ensuring employees on personal rates are assigned scale point 9999 with a multiplier of 1. You can verify employee position codes and current rates using CorePay's Employee Rate Listing report.
sl: This document provides instructions for efficiently updating multiple employee pay rates at once through the Portal interface, which is particularly useful when applying new pay agreements, implementing salary adjustments, or onboarding large groups of employees while minimizing manual errors. The bulk loading process begins by navigating to Uploads, then selecting Employee New Rates of Pay, with additional guidance available in a separate step-by-step guide covering the required file format and layout specifications. The document emphasizes critical configuration requirements for employees on personal rates of pay, specifically that these employees must be assigned to scale point '9999' to indicate they are not placed on a specific point within the standard pay scale. Users must ensure that any employee on a personal rate has their multiplier set to 1, and should only populate the relevant pay columns (Hourly, Daily, Weekly, or Annual) with actual values rather than entering zeros. To verify an employee's current position code and pay point before or after loading rates, the document directs users to generate a report by navigating to CorePay, then Reports, followed by Employee Reports Selection Criteria and Employee Rate Listing. This guide is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel responsible for managing bulk pay rate updates in the Portal system, and it references related processes including back office bulk loading, position rate uploads, and new deduction detail loading.

t: Portal: Put an employee on positive input
s:

ss: Positive input restricts an employee's pay to timesheet entries only, making it ideal for staff with irregular hours or special payment arrangements. This process involves navigating to the employee record in the back office, enabling the "Paid from Timesheet" toggle in Tax Details, and running a validation afterward. Use this guide when you need to set up an employee so they can only be paid based on hours submitted through their timesheet rather than standard payroll calculations.
sl: This document provides instructions for placing an employee on positive input in the Portal system, a configuration that restricts an employee's payment processing to timesheet input only. Positive input is typically applied to employees with irregular payment schedules or special pay arrangements that require manual timesheet entry rather than standard payroll processing. The process involves navigating to the Employee section, searching for the specific employee, clicking the VIEW button beside their name, then accessing the Tax Details tab where the "Paid from Timesheet" toggle must be enabled and saved. After completing this configuration change, users must run a single validation for the affected employee to ensure the system processes the change correctly. Related documentation addresses managing employee timesheets, resolving the error message "Employee has No Associated Timesheet Entries," and the reverse process of removing an employee from positive input, providing a comprehensive reference set for timesheet-based payment administration.

t: Back Office: Put an employee on positive input

sl: This document explains how to place an employee on positive input in the Back Office system, a configuration that changes how an employee's pay is calculated by using only manually entered values instead of automatic payroll rules. Positive input is typically applied to employees who receive irregular payments or have special pay arrangements that don't fit standard payroll processing. The process requires navigating to CorePay, selecting Employee, and then accessing Maintain Employee Details, where users enter the employee number in the Employee field and select the Positive Input check box indicator before saving the changes. After placing an employee on positive input, users must run a single validation for that affected employee to ensure the configuration is correctly applied. The document is designed for Back Office users who manage employee pay settings and need to accommodate non-standard payment scenarios. Related documentation covers the equivalent process in the portal interface, removing employees from positive input status, and the Employee Cumulatives report (PAYB084B) for monitoring affected employees.

t: What are increments and what are the rules surrounding them
s:
What is an increment?

An increment is an increase or addition to an employee's pay, especially one that is part of a series based on a fixed scale.

 

What is the Increment Process?

This process applies only to employees who have a pay scale salary. 

 Increments cannot be automatically generated...
ss: Increments are automatic salary increases applied to employees on pay scales, managed through either CorePay (during payroll runs) or CorePersonnel (via nightly system jobs). This document explains how the increment process works, including how increment due dates are set and managed at the post appointment level, how the system automatically progresses employees through pay scale points, and what controls like increment hold indicators and bar points do. Open this if you need to understand how increments are calculated and applied, how to set or update increment due dates on employee records, or how to manage increment holds and pay scale progression rules.
sl: This document provides a comprehensive overview of salary increments in the CorePay and CorePersonnel systems, defining an increment as a fixed pay increase typically applied annually or at specified employee milestones. The increment process applies specifically to employees on pay scale salaries and eliminates the need for manual salary amendments by automatically advancing employees to the next point on their designated pay scale. Increments can be processed either through CorePay during payroll runs with reference codes starting with "PAY," or through CorePersonnel via a nightly system job that generates increments a fixed number of days before the increment due date to allow time for HR and payroll approval or rejection. The document explains key configuration elements including the increment due date (captured and updated on the pay profile screen during appointment or later as needed), the increment hold indicator (which temporarily prevents increment processing while allowing for back-dated pay if removed), and pay scale point increment rules that control progression, maximum points, tenure requirements, bar points, and age restrictions. The increment system job automatically reviews all employees' increment due dates, creates new salary records based on pay scale rules, and updates the next increment due date—typically 12 months forward—unless the employee has reached the top of the scale or other restrictions apply. The document clarifies that increment details are managed at the post appointment level rather than the employee level, making it crucial for employees with multiple post appointments to have the increment due date recorded separately for each position.

t: What are Increments and what are the rules surrounding them
s:

ss: Increments are automatic salary increases that move employees up a fixed pay scale point, removing the need for manual salary amendments. You'll use this document to understand how to set and manage increment due dates, configure pay scale point rules (including bar points and age restrictions), and control increments using the increment hold indicator. sl: This document explains what increments are and describes the automated process for applying salary increases within the Access Group's CorePersonnel and CorePay systems. An increment is a pay increase that moves an employee to the next point on a fixed pay scale, and the increment process automatically creates new salary records rather than requiring manual salary amendments for standard annual increases that can be applied organization-wide on a common date or on employee-specific dates such as work anniversaries. The document details how increments are managed differently depending on where they are run: when executed from CorePay, they generate during payroll runs with specific reference codes, while CorePersonnel increments are generated by a nightly system job several days before the increment due date to allow for HR/Payroll approval or rejection. Key attributes and management tasks include the Increment Due Date (which can be captured during the appointment stage or updated directly on the Pay Profile screen) and the Increment Hold Indicator (which prevents the increment job from processing on the scheduled due date, though backdating will occur if the hold is removed). The nightly increment system job automatically reviews all employees' increment due dates, moves eligible employees to the next pay scale point by creating an approved salary amendment, and generates a new increment due date typically 12 months later. The document also explains pay scale point increment rules that control progression, define alternative pay scales when maximum points are reached, set length of time requirements on each point, establish age restrictions, and use bar points to prevent progression beyond certain levels. Additionally, it clarifies that increment due dates are only removed when the increment process itself brings an employee to the top of the scale, not when manual salary amendments or bar points prevent further progression.

ss: Changing an employee's pay group in Back Office allows you to update their pay frequency, payment type, tax jurisdiction, or contract terms within the CorePay payroll system. Use this guide when an employee needs to move between pay groups in the same company—no dormancy process required, though the new pay group's payroll period must be the same as or later than the current one. If moving an employee between pay groups in different companies, you'll need to make them dormant first before reassigning and rehiring them. Follow the step-by-step instructions in Back Office under CorePay > Employee > Advanced Employee Features > Amend Employee Pay Group.
sl: This document explains how to change an employee's pay group in the Back Office system, where pay groups are used to categorize employees by pay frequency and ensure all employees within a group are processed together for payments. The document outlines two distinct scenarios: when pay groups are in the same company, employees can be moved directly without additional steps, though the new pay group's payroll period must be the same as or after the current pay group's period; when pay groups are in different companies, the employee must first be made dormant through the standard process, then after the period is closed, the pay group can be changed and the employee rehired. The specific process for same-company transfers involves navigating to CorePay, selecting Employee, then clicking Advanced Employee Features and Amend Employee Pay Group, where users select the employee via a list icon, overwrite the current pay group field with the new pay group, and save using the save icon. Common reasons for changing an employee's pay group include changes in pay frequency (such as monthly or weekly), different payment types (wages versus salary), moves to different tax jurisdictions, or contract modifications. The document emphasizes an important system constraint: employees cannot be moved to a payroll period that is earlier than their current pay group's period. This guide is intended for Back Office users responsible for payroll administration and employee management who need to update employee pay group assignments due to organizational or employment changes.

t: What happens when an employee has a DEA and DEO
s: If an employee has both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA, the DEO will take priority over the DEA. The system will check the employee's net wage and ensure that it is equal to or greater than 60% before calculating the DEA. If the net wage falls below this threshold, the DEA will not be calculate...
ss: When an employee has both a DEA (Attachment of Earnings) and a DEO (Child Maintenance) order, DEO takes priority and PeopleXD protects a minimum of 60% of the employee's net wage before applying the DEA. The system evaluates net pay each period to determine if the DEA should be deducted in full, partially, or not at all, ensuring the employee never receives less than 60% of their net earnings after both deductions. Open this document if you need to understand how PeopleXD handles competing deduction orders and the protected earnings threshold that applies to DEA calculations.
sl: This document explains how the People XD payroll system handles situations where an employee is subject to both a DEO (Child Maintenance) and a DEA (Attachment of Earnings Order) simultaneously. The core process involves a priority hierarchy where the DEO takes precedence and is deducted first, with the DEA calculated only after the DEO deduction is applied. The system enforces a protected earnings threshold of 60% of the employee's net wage, meaning that if either deduction causes the net pay to fall below this 60% threshold, the DEA will not be calculated or will be calculated partially. During each pay period, People XD automatically evaluates the employee's net wage to determine whether the full DEA deduction should apply, a partial deduction should apply, or no deduction should occur, with calculations designed to comply with HMRC guidelines. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who use People XD and need to understand the interaction between multiple earnings deductions, particularly the compliance requirement that employees must retain at least 60% of their net earnings after all deductions are applied. The document references related articles on setting up a DEA pay code, troubleshooting incorrect attachment of earnings deductions, and resolving issues with AEO protected earnings functionality.

t: Impact of periodic employee hours setting on the Minimum Wage Exception report
s:
The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage(NMW), the National Living Wage (NLW), or the minimum apprenticeship rate. The report compares the employee’s hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age.

 

T...
ss: The Minimum Wage Exception report identifies employees whose hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage, National Living Wage, or apprenticeship minimum rate by comparing calculated hourly rates against statutory thresholds. The Periodic Employee Hours setting in Payroll Checking controls how the hourly rate is calculated—enabling it uses pay-per-period divided by contracted hours, while disabling it annualizes pay based on pay frequency multipliers and minimum wage report weeks. Open this document if your pay groups use non-weekly pay frequencies (fortnightly, monthly, etc.) where contracted hours don't represent weekly hours, or if you need to understand why minimum wage exceptions are being flagged for specific employees.
sl: This document explains the Minimum Wage Exception report, which identifies employees whose calculated hourly rate falls below the National Minimum Wage (NMW), National Living Wage (NLW), or minimum apprenticeship rate by comparing each employee's hourly rate against the statutory rate applicable to their age. The document provides step-by-step instructions for accessing and configuring the Periodic Employee Hours setting within the payroll system by navigating to Manage Payroll > Payroll Checking > View Gross to Nett > Minimum Wage tab, where users can toggle this setting on or off depending on whether contracted hours represent weekly hours or alternative pay periods. The critical function of this setting is to control how the system calculates hourly rates: when enabled, the hourly rate is calculated as Pay in Period divided by Hours at Appointment Level, while when disabled, the system uses a multi-step calculation involving annual multipliers based on pay frequency (12 for monthly, 52 for weekly, 26 for fortnightly, 4 for quarterly, and 2 for half-yearly), the Minimum Wage Report Weeks field from the Pay Group configuration, and hours at appointment level. Users can verify the Minimum Wage Report Weeks setting by navigating to Settings > Pay Groups, selecting the relevant pay group from a dropdown menu, and reviewing the field, which defaults to 52 weeks if blank. The document is designed for payroll administrators and compliance officers who need to ensure accurate minimum wage calculations and resolve discrepancies between contracted hours and pay periods, and it includes worked examples demonstrating both calculation methods along with links to related error resolution articles and the full Minimum Wage User Guide.

t: Attachment of earnings deduction incorrect
s:

For both AOE and DEA, the net earnings for an employee are calculated using the following formula:

Net Earnings = Gross Pay – ...
ss: Attachment of Earnings Orders (AOE) and Deduction of Earnings Administration (DEA) calculations in your payroll system depend on net earnings derived from gross pay minus specific deductions like PAYE, National Insurance, and pension contributions. If an AOE or DEA repayment amount appears incorrect, the issue likely stems from net earnings not matching the expected calculation formula, which uses tiered rates applied to earnings bands. Open this document if you need to verify why a deduction amount doesn't match what you expected, or to understand which deductions are included (and excluded) when calculating net earnings for court-ordered or administrative earnings deductions.
sl: This document explains how to troubleshoot situations where the repayment amount for Attachment of Earnings (AOE) or Deduction of Earnings Administration (DEA) deductions appears incorrect, typically due to misalignment between calculated and expected net earnings values. The document outlines the precise formula used to calculate net earnings for both AOE and DEA: Net Earnings equals Gross Pay minus Applicable Deductions, where applicable deductions include only PAYE (Income Tax), Employee NI/PRSI, and Pension contributions—notably excluding other deductions such as student loans. Once net earnings are determined, the deduction amount itself is calculated using a two-tier formula: (Lower band × lower rate%) + (Remainder of net earnings above lower band × balance rate), with the lower band, lower rate, and balance rate values stored on the specific pay code used for AOE. The document provides a worked example for a monthly employee earning £2000.00 with £350.00 in applicable deductions, demonstrating how the net earnings of £1650.00 are used to calculate a final AOE deduction of £336.60 using lower band (£1480), lower rate (17%), and balance rate (50%) parameters. This document is intended for payroll administrators, HR professionals, or finance staff who use Access Group's payroll system and need to validate or correct AOE and DEA calculations when the deduction amounts do not match expected values. The document references related setup tasks such as configuring DEA pay codes and notes other related scenarios involving DEA and Deduction of Earnings Orders (DEO).

For the changed pay groups scenario, the resolution requires a specific sequence: delete the old timesheet from the old pay group, re-run the PAY290 job in the old group first, and then re-run it in the new pay group to ensure clean payroll processing. t: When are PAYE Modernisation correction submission files generated
s:
If an error has occurred within payroll and the incorrect data has already been reported to Revenue, the inaccurate submission data can be corrected and sent again.

Normal submission

Full resubmission

ss: PAYE Modernisation correction submission files are automatically generated when specific payroll changes occur, such as updating an employee's PPSN, leave date, or recording a cancel payment, or when an employee passes away. You can also manually create three types of correction submissions—normal submission, full resubmission, or delete submission—depending on the error that occurred and whether data has already been reported to Revenue. Use this document to understand which correction file type to generate for your situation and the specific scenarios where the system creates correction files automatically. Open this if you need to correct inaccurate payroll data that's already been submitted to Revenue.
sl: This document explains when and how the PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) system automatically generates correction submission files to fix inaccurate payroll data that has already been reported to Revenue, along with the three manual submission types available: Normal submission, Full resubmission, and Delete submission. The system generates correction files automatically in four specific scenarios: when an employee's PPSN (Payee Public Services Number) is updated and differs from what was previously reported to Revenue (except when only changing from a PPSN ending in "W"), when an employee's leave date is updated and differs from previously reported dates, when a cancel payment is entered for a previous period, or when an employee is recorded as deceased. A Full resubmission option is used when the original file contained errors such as an incorrect pay date, and it deletes all previously sent payslips for that pay group and period while submitting corrected ones with updated details. A Delete submission file contains only delete line IDs and is used to remove employees who were incorrectly included in a submission or to delete duplicate files by specifying the submission ID, though it should not be used if a payment needs to be cancelled—a delete cancel function should be used instead. This document serves payroll administrators and finance professionals who use the Access Group's payroll system and need to correct submission errors, access the PMOD processing interface, and understand which correction method applies to their specific situation, with related guidance available through articles on creating PAYE Modernisation files, reviewing pay group parameters, and managing deleted or resubmitted payments.

t: Impact on RPN process for leavers, rehires and temporary rejoiners
s:
The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) is a real-time system from the Irish Revenue that provides employers with up-to-date tax information for each employee, including tax credits, cut-off points, and USC rates. 

 

This system automatically updates employee tax details as circumstances change, en...
ss: The Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) system provides real-time tax information from Irish Revenue, and managing it correctly is critical when employees leave, rejoin, or return temporarily. This document explains the specific RPN procedures to follow in CoreHR for leavers (whose RPN details update automatically), rehires (using either existing or new employee numbers), and temporary rejoiners (with different processes depending on whether they rejoin in the same tax year or the previous year). Open this if you're processing employee departures, rehires, or temporary returns and need to ensure accurate RPN retrieval and tax compliance throughout these transitions.
sl: This document explains how the Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN) system, a real-time tax information service from Irish Revenue, is affected when employees leave, are rehired, or return temporarily, and provides specific procedures for maintaining tax compliance during these employment changes. For leavers, the payroll submission file automatically notifies Revenue during the employee's final pay period, after which the employee no longer appears in the RPN retrieval system once processed in CoreHR. When rehiring employees, the document outlines two scenarios: reactivating an existing employee record with the same employee number (recommended) or creating a new employee record (not recommended), both requiring the Retrieve New Employee RPNs process and generation of a new Employment ID with valid characters [A-Za-z0-9_\-]. For temporary rejoiners within the same tax year, users should retrieve the employee's RPN using their most recent Employment ID without treating it as new employment, whereas temporary rejoiners from the previous year are treated as new employment requiring retrieval of a new employee RPN and generation of a fresh Employment ID. The document clarifies important field-level distinctions, noting that when retrieving RPNs at the employee level the company last updated field is unavailable, but when retrieving at company level the employee reference is blank and company last updated defaults. If no RPN is returned during retrieval, the employee will be placed on emergency tax at the updated RPN step, and specific submission file details—such as start and end dates matching the pay date—inform Revenue about one-day temporary employment situations.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for resolving the situation where an employee has been mistakenly excluded from the PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) file submitted to revenue, which prevents their payroll details from being transmitted and can create reporting and compliance discrepancies. The document explains that exclusions typically occur when an employee is accidentally marked as excluded during payroll processing, and the system will not automatically correct this omission in future submissions. To resolve the issue, users must follow three primary steps within the Portal system: first, unexclude the employee by navigating to Manage Payroll > relevant pay group > Outputs > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Employee Parameters, then disabling the Exclude Employee toggle and saving the changes. Second, users must enable the Previous Periods toggle in the pay group parameters by accessing Manage Payroll > relevant pay group > Outputs > ROS > PAYE Modernisation > Pay Group Parameters to allow submissions for earlier pay periods. Third, users generate a normal submission through the PAYE Modernisation Files Process by selecting Generate Submission File, choosing Normal Submission type, selecting the relevant pay group and employee, and entering an Override Payment Date to ensure the submission reflects the original pay period. The document includes an important warning that if the employee was excluded before the payroll was finalized, users must raise a case referencing the article and providing the employee reference, payroll period, and confirmation of the erroneous exclusion. t: Transfer the Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) file to Revenue
s:

sl: This document provides an overview of Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR), a mandatory reporting system introduced by Revenue in January 2024 that requires employers to submit details of relevant employee payments to Revenue on or before each payday. The document clarifies important exclusions: payments made via company credit card and expenses to non-employees or non-directors do not fall under ERR requirements. For the 2018 tax year, when cancelling payments that were not previously reported to Revenue, users should tick the Previous Year Recoupment option but must not tick the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option, allowing the cancellation to be reflected in the payroll submission file through negative values that appear in the CorePay Control report. For the 2019 tax year and later, when cancelling payments that were already reported to Revenue via a submission file, users should tick the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option instead and avoid using Previous Year Recoupment, which sends a required DELETE instruction to Revenue in the submission file without generating negative values in the CorePay Control report. The document explains that deceased employees are identified by either checking a populated Date of Death field or by ticking a Deceased indicator within the system. In both scenarios, the net payment must be recouped from the deceased individual's estate, and users should ensure that the previous payment in the current tax year is cancelled in the current period when viewing submission file details. This guidance applies to payroll administrators or finance personnel who handle payment cancellations and estate recoupments for deceased staff members within the Access Group payroll system.

Use this guide to understand how your cancellation will appear in the submission file and what happens when you adjust the recoup indicator.
sl: This document explains the outcomes that occur when a previous payment made in the current tax year is cancelled during the current period, focusing on how the system handles the cancellation based specific configuration settings. The document describes two distinct processes depending on whether the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option is enabled or disabled in the system configuration. When the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option is enabled, the system writes a delete line item to the Payroll Submission file for the current period to record the cancellation. Conversely, when the PAYE Modernisation Deletion option is disabled, the cancelled values are netted off within the Payroll Submission file for the current period rather than creating a separate deletion record. The document also directs users to consider the impact of not selecting the recoup indicator when processing cancellations. This guidance is relevant for payroll administrators and finance professionals using Access Group's payroll system who need to understand how payment cancellations are processed and recorded in PAYE submissions. The document references related scenarios including cancelled payments from previous years, cancellations involving deceased personnel, payslip status issues after submission file transfers, and provides links to portal resources for PAYE Modernisation deletion files and resubmission procedures.

Open this if you're experiencing invalid payslip statuses after cancelling or manually processing payments, or if you need clarification on when to use recoupment versus PAYE Modernisation deletion options.
sl: This document explains a specific issue that occurs in payroll processing when payslips display an "Invalid Payslip" status after transferring submission files following a cancelled or manual payment. The problem arises when both the "Previous Year Recoupment" indicator and the "PAYE Modernisation Deletion" indicator are selected simultaneously, and the resolution requires selecting only one of these options at a time. The document emphasizes that the PAYE Modernisation Deletion feature should be used sparingly and only in situations where an employee was erroneously reported to revenue and should not have been submitted, as this option deletes the payslip previously sent from the revenue system. To troubleshoot invalid status errors, users should review the response file from Revenue, where common error messages such as "Unable to delete line item because it has already been deleted" may indicate that the software attempted to delete the same payslip or line ID multiple times due to both recoupment and deletion indicators being selected together. The document clarifies that despite this error message appearing, the delete instruction can still be successful and should not adversely affect Revenue figures. As a best practice, the document recommends always verifying that figures in the Revenue system are accurate for any affected employees following these cancellation and deletion procedures.

t: Processing non-taxable advances
s:
Revenue have recently announced that non-taxable advances will be allowed in certain scenarios. 

 

This change is being implemented following feedback on the ERR release in relation to advanced not being allowed.

 

What this means?

Irish Revenue will introduce an optional administrative practic...
ss: Non-taxable advances for travel and subsistence expenses are now allowed under Irish Revenue's optional administrative practice, following changes to Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR). This document explains the conditions employers must meet—including reasonable estimates, timely reconciliation with actual claims, and proper controls—plus how to report advance payments to Revenue using the new "Advances" subcategory in ERR. Open this if you need to understand whether your organisation should opt into processing non-taxable advances, what governance controls are required, and how PeopleXD (or your payroll system) will handle the reporting. The document also clarifies that advance payments must be manually reported via Revenue screens until PeopleXD's software update is released in approximately two months.
sl: This document explains the process for handling non-taxable advances following Irish Revenue's new optional administrative practice, which was introduced in response to feedback on the Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) release regarding restrictions on advance payments. The document covers the conditions under which non-taxable advances are permitted, specifically for anticipated travel and subsistence expenses only, and requires employers to establish appropriate controls to track and reconcile all advance payments. Advances must be reported to Revenue under ERR using a designated "Advances" subcategory, and as the advance is drawn down, this drawdown activity must also be reported under ERR to maintain compliance. The document emphasizes that advance payments must represent reasonable estimates of expected claim amounts and qualify for relief under section 114 TCA 1997, with employers required to promptly reconcile advances against actual claims and recoup or tax any excess payments without delay. While employers have discretion to opt into this practice with no advance notification to Revenue required, they must maintain appropriate governance and controls; those choosing not to participate will have standard tax rules apply, with advance payments taxed through payroll instead. The document explains the implementation timeline, noting that Revenue ROS screens will be updated within approximately two months to allow manual capture and reporting of advance payments, and that the Access Group's PeopleXD software solution will be updated to accommodate ERR reporting requirements, with manual reporting via Revenue screens required until that update is released. Employers using non-PeopleXD systems are advised to discuss new functionality plans with their respective software vendors, and further guidance can be found in Revenue Tax Duty Manual (TDM) part 38-03-33.

The Check ERR Run generates a response file that classifies each expense into one of three statuses: Completed with all valid expenses (indicating successful validation and process completion), Completed with invalid expenses (requiring corrections to be made in PeopleXD Payroll followed by generation and transfer of a new ERR file to Revenue), or Pending (awaiting validation at the Revenue end).
