Open this document when you need to correct pay date changes that have already been reported to Revenue.
sl: This document provides step-by-step instructions for generating a Full Resubmission ERR (Enhanced Reporting Requirements) file when an employee's pay date has been amended after the initial ERR file has already been submitted to Revenue. The Full Resubmission file contains only amendments made since Revenue accepted the normal ERR file for that period, and the document distinguishes between processes for the current period and previous periods. For the current period, users navigate through Manage Payroll > Outputs > ROS > Enhanced Reporting Requirements > ERR Files Process, then select "Generate submission file" from the Select ERR action dropdown, choose "Full Resubmission" from the Submission type dropdown, select the pay group, and enter an override payment or cheque date. The document explains a specific error scenario—the message "You cannot generate a file for this pay group and periods as the last file sent got no response from Revenue - Please run a Check ERR Run"—which indicates either that no normal file was submitted for the period or that Revenue rejected the normal file. To resolve this, users can follow steps to check file submission status by selecting "Transfer submission file" from the Select ERR action dropdown and reviewing the Status column. For previous periods, the process is similar but requires first enabling the Previous periods toggle in Pay Group Parameters before accessing ERR Files Process. This document is used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to correct pay date information that was already submitted to Revenue through the Irish ROS (Revenue Online Service) system.

t: Generate the Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) file for a previous period
s:

sl: This document provides instructions for generating Enhanced Reporting Requirements (ERR) submission files for previous payroll periods within the PeopleXD Payroll system. The procedure involves enabling the Previous periods toggle for the relevant pay group, then using the ERR Files Process with the Generate submission file action, selecting Normal Submission type, choosing the appropriate pay group, and specifying the target period, with an optional field to override the payment date. After generating the file, users may encounter an ERR Submission Exception Report that identifies errors requiring correction directly in PeopleXD Payroll, after which a new submission file must be regenerated. This iterative error-checking and resolution process should continue until no exceptions remain, and Access Group strongly recommends resolving all errors before transferring the completed file to Revenue. The document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to resubmit or generate corrected ERR files for compliance with Revenue requirements when initial submissions fail or have not yet been created.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive guide for creating and processing full resubmission files in PeopleXD Payroll's Portal when amendments are needed for PAYE Modernisation submissions. sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on creating and processing full resubmission files within PeopleXD Payroll when amendments to pay dates or Shadow Payroll indicators are necessary for PAYE Modernisation compliance. t: Arrears not calculating correctly in salary processing
s:
When processing salaries, arrears may not generate correctly for an employee due to several factors.

 

Below, we outline common scenarios that can cause inaccuracies in arrears calculations.

 

 

Null or zero multiplier for previous rate

If the multiplier for the employee's previous rate is nul...
ss: Salary arrears may fail to calculate correctly during payroll processing in your system due to issues such as null multipliers on previous rates, incorrect pay group assignments, multiple salary changes in one period, or missing net pay rows. This document outlines over a dozen common scenarios that prevent arrears generation and provides specific fixes for each—including when to enter manual timesheet entries, run retrospection jobs, or contact support. Open this if your employees' arrears are not appearing as expected after a salary change, pay group transfer, or during standard payroll runs. It's also useful if you need to troubleshoot why the system isn't automatically calculating back-pay owed to staff.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides a comprehensive troubleshooting guide for resolving arrears calculation errors in salary processing, detailing multiple scenarios where arrears fail to generate correctly and offering specific remediation steps for each. The document covers common configuration and data entry issues including null or zero multipliers for previous rates, incorrect pay group assignments, incorrectly entered new rates with wrong effective dates, and transaction dates that fall outside the payroll period. It addresses complex payroll scenarios such as multiple salary changes within the same period, timing misalignments between input dates and complete update dates, discrepancies between configured pay days and calculated days, and employees transitioning between pay groups (e.g., from weekly to fortnightly pay cycles). The guide explains that many of these issues require manual timesheet entry as the system cannot automatically accommodate them, and provides specific configuration instructions such as enabling the Retrospection toggle under Settings > Codes > Pay Groups for individual pay groups. For certain issues involving incorrect units on net pay rows, incorrect rejoin dates, or other data anomalies, the document directs users to raise support cases for analyst intervention, while for hourly pay codes it specifies that the positive input retro (PIR) job must be run to generate retrospection payments. This resource is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who process salaries and need to diagnose and correct arrears calculation failures within the Access Group payroll system.

t: Portal: Issue a manual payment
s:
There may be times when you need to make changes to an employee's pay after you've closed the payroll period. In this case, you need to issue a manual payment.

 

⚠️Important: When correcting errors from previous periods near the Financial Year End, ensure you verify that payroll corrections are ac...
ss: Issuing a manual payment in PeopleXD Payroll lets you adjust an employee's pay after the payroll period has closed, which is essential for correcting errors or making changes that weren't captured in the regular pay run. The process involves navigating to Issue Manual Payments, entering employee and payment details (including reference number, period, PAYE code, and appointment information), and ensuring all pay codes and National Insurance details are accurate before saving. Open this document when you need to make post-payroll adjustments, especially near Financial Year End when HMRC compliance is critical, or when you need to correct previous tax year payments by submitting a Previous Year Full Payroll Submission (PYFPS).
sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on issuing manual payments in PeopleXD Payroll when corrections or adjustments to employee pay are needed after a payroll period has been closed. The process begins by navigating to Manage Payroll, selecting the relevant pay group, then accessing General and Issue Manual Payments, where users must enter specific details including employee reference number, payroll period, issue date, PAYE code, and number of days. The document emphasizes the critical importance of HMRC compliance when making corrections near Financial Year End, requiring verification of pension adjustments, overpayments, and accuracy of employee records for payslips and P60s. Users must ensure appointment IDs and expense codes are entered for all fields, verify that employer NI or PRSI amounts are correctly entered (with the option to enter 0 if there is no NIable or PRSIable pay), and carefully check all Manual Payment Pay Codes before saving, as these cannot be amended after entry. The document also addresses corrections made in previous tax years, explaining that year-end must be completed before cancelling and reissuing manual payments, after which users must submit a Previous Year Full Payroll Submission (PYFPS) to HMRC and update P60 cumulative details through either the Portal (Year End > Manage > Post Cleardown Activities > Maintain Cumulatives) or Back Office (CorePay > Update > Advanced Update Features > Year End > Maintain Year End Cumulative Details). This document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to correct pay errors, process additional payments outside standard payroll cycles, or ensure compliance with HMRC regulations for year-end adjustments.

t: Portal: Update P60
s:
A P60 is an official document issued to employees at the end of the tax year, summarising their total pay and tax deductions. 

 

It is important for tax returns and proof of income. P60S are processed after the final payroll of the tax year, but you may need to update the details if there are corr...
ss: P60 documents summarise an employee's total pay and tax deductions at the end of the tax year and are essential for tax returns and proof of income. Use this guide when you need to amend P60 records through the Payroll Dashboard by accessing Year End settings and the Maintain Cumulatives section. Open this document if your organisation has identified errors on P60s that require correction before they're released to employees.
sl: This document provides guidance on updating P60 details in the Portal system after the final payroll of the tax year has been processed. P60s are official end-of-year documents issued to employees that summarise their total pay and tax deductions, making them essential for tax returns and proof of income. The document explains that updates may be necessary when there are corrections needed to earnings, tax paid, or employee information following initial P60 generation. Users access the update process by navigating from the dashboard menu to Payroll Dashboard, then selecting Year End and highlighting the relevant company before clicking Manage. Within the Manage section, users locate and click Maintain Cumulatives under the Post Cleardown Activities area to make the required P60 updates. This process is typically used by payroll administrators or finance teams who need to correct P60 records after the year-end payroll cycle and before P60s are released to employees. The document also provides references to related articles covering back office P60 updates, P60 production and release procedures, troubleshooting for employees on absence, and P60 access controls.

sl: This document provides guidance on updating P60 records in the Back Office system, which are official year-end tax documents issued to employees that summarize total pay and tax deductions. P60s are essential for employee tax returns and proof of income, and while they are typically generated after the final payroll run of the tax year, updates may be necessary to correct errors or changes in earnings, tax paid, or employee information. The document outlines the specific menu navigation required to access the update function: users must click CorePay, then click Update, followed by selecting Advanced Update Features and Year End, and finally clicking Maintain Year End Cumulative Details to access the screen where P60 data can be modified. This process is used by payroll administrators and back office staff who need to make corrections or adjustments to P60 records after the initial generation but before they are issued or released to employees. The document references related functionality including Portal-based P60 updates, P60 production processes, manual payment issuance, P60 release procedures, and the ability to produce blank P60 forms from Back Office, all of which are interconnected with the update process described.

t: Cancel a manual payment
s:
Cancelling a manual payment is necessary when a payment has been made in error or contains incorrect details. 

 

If you’ve recorded an incorrect manual payment and wish to cancel it, your options depend on whether a payment has already been cancelled in the payroll period.
​
If you've cancelled a ...
ss: Manual payment cancellation in your payroll system becomes necessary when a payment has been recorded in error or contains incorrect information. Your approach depends on your payroll period status: if you've already cancelled a payment in the current period, you'll need to issue a negative manual payment matching the incorrect amount; if no cancellations have been processed yet, you can cancel all payments for that period and then reissue with correct details. Open this document when you've made a payroll error and need to correct it while understanding the constraints of your current payroll cycle.
sl: This document provides guidance on cancelling manual payments that have been recorded incorrectly or with inaccurate details. The document outlines two distinct scenarios for cancelling manual payments, depending on whether a payment has already been cancelled within the current payroll period. In the first scenario, if a payment has already been cancelled during the payroll period, users must issue a negative manual payment with identical values to the incorrect payment rather than performing a full cancellation. In the second scenario, if no payment has been cancelled during the payroll period, users can perform a cancel payment action, which will cancel all payments for that period including both the incorrect manual payment and any other payments that were made. After completing either cancellation option, users can then issue a new manual payment containing the correct details. The document is designed for payroll administrators and finance users who need to correct manual payment errors within their payroll processing workflows. The guidance references related processes including issuing manual payments, cancelling payments, correcting figures reported to HMRC, and resolving payslip display issues that may occur following manual payment cancellation.

t: Change payment type after the complete update
s:
Changing the payment type after the complete update job has been run typically occurs when an employee has received an incorrect payment method, such as a bank transfer or cheque, during payroll processing and needs an update.

 

However, users cannot update the payment type once the complete updat...
ss: Changing an employee's payment type (such as bank transfer or cheque) in payroll becomes restricted once the complete update job has been run. If an employee received an incorrect payment method during processing, you'll need to contact support rather than making the change yourself, as the system prevents direct updates after this point. Open this document when you need to correct a payment type error and discover you can't modify it through normal channels. Have your employee number, payroll period, and desired payment type ready when you submit your support request.
sl: This document explains the process for addressing payment type errors that occur after the Complete Update payroll job (PAY355) has been executed in the system. It describes a common scenario where employees receive incorrect payment methods—such as bank transfers or cheques—during payroll processing and require correction. The document identifies a significant system limitation: users cannot directly update the payment type through standard functionality once the Complete Update job has been completed. To resolve this issue, the document directs users to contact support, who will need to run specific database scripts to manually correct the payment type. Users requesting assistance are instructed to raise a new case online and reference this article's title while providing three essential pieces of information: the employee number, the payroll period affected, and the correct payment type that needs to be applied. The document also provides cross-references to related articles covering similar post-Complete Update issues, such as incorrect expense codes, incorrect cost centres, and BIC/IBAN errors, as well as articles about Complete Update job failures and payroll report retrieval.

t: Allowances not generating
s:
Allowances are a crucial part of employee compensation and must be accurately reflected in payroll to ensure correct payments and compliance.

 

If an assigned allowance does not appear or calculate correctly, several reasons may be responsible.

We’ve compiled a list of possible causes and how to ...
ss: Allowances in PeopleXD Payroll may fail to generate or calculate correctly due to several configuration and processing issues. This document covers the most common causes—including the Generate Salaries and Allowances job not being rerun, incorrect allowance setup, positive input timesheet gaps, zero multiplier settings, and GL posting errors—along with specific steps to resolve each one. Open this guide when an assigned allowance isn't appearing in payroll or is calculating an incorrect amount, and you need to identify and fix the underlying cause quickly.
sl: This document provides comprehensive troubleshooting guidance for resolving issues when allowances fail to appear or calculate correctly in payroll processing within the PeopleXD Payroll system. The document identifies multiple specific causes and their solutions, including scenarios where the Generate Salaries and Allowances job has not been re-run after allowance configuration changes, allowance configuration errors such as missing Balance Due fields for reducing balance allowances or unset percentage pay codes, and situations where employees on positive input lack timesheet entries or are on zero multipliers without the Pay in Full indicator enabled. It details step-by-step procedures for accessing relevant screens in both the Portal and Back Office interfaces—such as navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes to enable the Pay in Full rule, or CorePay > Employee to amend employee sundry profiles for those who have moved from quarterly pay groups. The document also addresses advanced scenarios including zero multipliers with date-effective entries, incorrect end period settings for 54-week years requiring support analyst intervention, GL posting override errors in the pay290.logXXXX file when cost centers are not configured, and salary lines that have not been commenced before pay period completion. This resource is essential for payroll administrators and HR professionals in organizations using PeopleXD Payroll who need to diagnose and resolve allowance generation failures and ensure accurate employee compensation processing.

t: Payslip with negative net pay
s:
A payslip with negative net pay occurs when an employee’s total deductions exceed their earnings, resulting in a negative amount payable.

 

The payroll system cannot process employees with negative net pay amounts.

 

 HMRC regulations prohibit the submission of negative payment amounts through t...
ss: Negative net pay occurs when an employee's total deductions exceed their earnings, creating a negative amount payable to the employee. Both the payroll system and HMRC regulations prohibit processing these transactions, so you'll need to resolve the issue before submitting payroll. Open this article if you encounter negative net pay calculations in your payroll processing and need to understand why the system is blocking submission or how to recover from this situation.
sl: This document explains the issue of payslips with negative net pay, which occurs when an employee's total deductions exceed their earnings, resulting in a negative amount payable to the employee. The payroll system is designed to block and cannot process employees with negative net pay amounts due to regulatory constraints, as HMRC regulations explicitly prohibit the submission of negative payment amounts through their systems. To maintain compliance with both HMRC requirements and software restrictions, the system actively blocks any attempts to process negative net pay calculations. Users must resolve any negative net pay issues before submitting payroll data, as both HMRC and the payroll software will reject these transactions if they proceed. The document references several related topics including the error message "*** Negative Pay After Processing Pre-Tax Deductions **", guidance on making negative payslips, steps for setting up negative net pay recovery, instructions for removing a pay code from a payslip, and configuration of Intelligent Payslips. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who encounter negative net pay scenarios during payroll processing and need to understand both the system limitations and the regulatory reasons behind them.

t: End an allowance in CorePay
s:
An allowance represents additional payments provided to employees for specific purposes, such as travel, housing, or professional expenses. 

 

Ending an allowance is important to ensure that payroll records accurately reflect current compensation structures and prevent overpayment, and maintain co...
ss: Ending an allowance in CorePay removes additional employee payments (such as travel, housing, or professional expenses) from active compensation records. Use this process to prevent overpayment, maintain accurate payroll records, and comply with company policies—and as best practice, end an allowance before assigning a replacement rather than modifying an existing one. You can end an allowance either in CorePay back office by searching for the employee and pay code, then entering an end date, or through People Management on Portal via the Allowances tab. Open this document when you need to stop a current allowance for an employee or when making changes to allowance values.
sl: This document explains how to end an allowance in CorePay, which is essential for maintaining accurate payroll records, preventing employee overpayment, and ensuring compliance with company policies. An allowance represents additional payments provided to employees for specific purposes such as travel, housing, or professional expenses, and the document emphasizes that when amending an allowance, best practice is to end the existing allowance and assign a new one rather than modifying the current allowance value. The document provides two distinct procedures: the first is the back office method in CorePay, which requires navigating to CorePay > Employee > Employee Allowances > Amend An Existing Allowance and entering the Employee Reference (personnel number), Pay code, and Start date to retrieve the allowance, then entering the Allowance End Date and saving. The second procedure uses the People Management portal, where users access the dashboard, navigate to an employee's Current salary section, select the Allowances tab, highlight the relevant allowance, and update the Payroll End Date field before saving. The document includes important warnings that the allowance end date cannot be updated after saving from the back office screen, and that entering a past end date may generate arrears. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR personnel who manage employee compensation in CorePay or use the People Management portal to administer allowances.

t: Salary offset deduction is incorrect
s:
A salary offset deduction reduces an employee's salary to account for their absences, aiming to ensure fair compensation during periods of sick leave.

 

Incorrect salary offset deductions can happen for the following reasons:

 

Cause 1: The daily rate looks incorrect.

The daily rate is determin...
ss: Salary offset deductions in payroll reduce an employee's pay to account for absences like sick leave, but they can calculate incorrectly due to wrong daily rates or pay group settings. The most common causes are an incorrect "Days in Year" value at the pay group level, or the employee's pay group being set to daily rate when they should be on an hourly rate. Open this document if your payslip shows an unexpected deduction amount for absences, or if the deduction doesn't match the number of sick days taken. Follow the troubleshooting steps to verify your pay group settings in the portal and recalculate what the correct deduction should be.
sl: This document provides guidance on troubleshooting incorrect salary offset deductions, which are reductions applied to an employee's salary to account for absences such as sick leave and ensure fair compensation. The document identifies two main causes of incorrect deductions: an incorrect daily rate calculation and pay group configuration mismatches between hourly and daily rate settings. For the daily rate issue, users access the portal by navigating to Settings > Codes > Pay Groups, selecting the relevant pay code from the Pay Group Code drop-down menu, and verifying the Days in Year field value; the daily rate should be calculated by dividing the employee's salary by the number of days in the year and then multiplying by the actual sick days taken, with reference to override settings in the sickness category if needed. The second cause occurs when an employee's pay group is incorrectly configured to apply a daily rate instead of an hourly rate, resulting in doubled deductions—for example, deducting 80 hours instead of 40 hours when an hourly employee takes 10 sick days. To resolve hourly employee deductions, users must check the pay group settings assigned to the employee and ensure the pay group is set to HOURLY rather than a daily rate setting. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to investigate and correct payslip discrepancies related to absence deductions in the Access Group payroll system.

t: Populate Scottish arrestment order rates
s: Scottish Arrestment Order rates specify the statutory deduction amounts that employers must apply when court orders instruct them to withhold money from an employee's wages to satisfy debts or legal obligations. Set by Scottish legislation, these rates determine the maximum amounts that can be deduc...
ss: Scottish Arrestment Order rates are the statutory deduction amounts employers must withhold from employee wages when court orders are issued to recover debts such as unpaid council tax or maintenance payments. You'll need to configure these rates in Portal by navigating to Settings > Pay Codes, then entering the earnings bands and deduction amounts in the Payment Orders section according to government-specified banding. Open this guide when you receive formal court instructions to set up wage deductions, or when you need to understand which earnings thresholds and deduction percentages apply to Scottish arrestment orders. The configuration ensures you withhold the correct amounts while allowing employees to retain sufficient income for essential living expenses.
sl: This document provides instructions for configuring Scottish Arrestment Order rates in the Access Group Portal system, which are statutory deduction amounts that employers must apply to employee wages when complying with court orders for debt recovery. The document explains that Scottish Arrestment Order rates determine the maximum amounts that can be deducted from earnings while ensuring employees retain sufficient income for essential living expenses, and are used when receiving formal court instructions to recover debts such as unpaid council tax or maintenance payments through salary deductions. To implement these rates, users must navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes in Portal, search for the relevant pay code, click the three-dot icon, and select Edit to access the configuration screen. Within the Pay Code section under Payment Orders, users must populate several fields including Nett Earnings Week From and To dates (drawn from government banding), Lower Band Week, Lower value, Balance the %, and The Sum, with specific instructions to follow government deduction guidance when determining whether toggles should be enabled for "value OR %" versus "value PLUS %" calculations. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and compliance personnel who process court-ordered wage deductions in Scottish jurisdictions and need to ensure their payroll system correctly reflects the statutory rates and banding requirements set by government legislation.

t: Adjust or refund a deduction
s:

To adjust a deduction for an employee or process a refund, follow the steps below in portal.

ss: Correcting payroll deductions in your portal covers situations where an employee has been charged an incorrect deduction amount or a deduction needs to be cancelled entirely. You'll navigate to the employee's record, locate the specific deduction, and use the Adjust Normal Amount section to either modify the deduction value or process a refund across one or more payroll periods. Open this document when you need to reverse an erroneous deduction, adjust a deduction amount retroactively, or refund an employee for an overpayment.
sl: This document provides instructions for adjusting or refunding employee deductions within the Access Group portal when incorrect amounts have been deducted from pay or when a deduction needs to be reversed entirely. The process involves navigating to the Employee section of the portal, searching for and viewing the relevant employee record, then accessing the Deduction area to highlight and edit the specific deduction requiring adjustment. Users must enter the number of payroll periods for the adjustment in the "Number of Periods" field, with the example that entering "1" applies the adjustment value only to the current payroll period while restoring the normal deduction value in subsequent periods. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to correct deduction errors or reverse deductions that were applied in error or are no longer due. The guide references related portal-based processes including loading new deduction details, placing deductions on hold, and resolving scenarios such as AVC deductions being applied when not due, providing context for when this adjustment process fits within broader deduction management workflows.

t: Error: 'An error has occurred, please try again. If the issue persists please contact support…'
s:
Loading rates of pay in bulk involves entering multiple employee pay rates at once into a payroll system. This method streamlines payroll management by enabling administrators to efficiently update compensation rates for a group of employees, rather than processing each change individually.

 

Appl...
ss: Bulk loading of pay rates in your payroll system allows administrators to update compensation for multiple employees at once rather than individually. If you encounter an error when uploading a CSV file of pay rates, it's typically caused by formatting issues (such as blank lines in the file) or data issues (such as invalid employee numbers or inactive appointment IDs). This document walks you through troubleshooting steps to fix the file format and verify your data, and explains what information to include if you need to contact support.
sl: This document addresses the specific error message that appears when users encounter problems loading personal rates of pay in bulk into a payroll system. The document explains that bulk loading of pay rates is a critical payroll administration function that allows multiple employee compensation rates to be updated simultaneously rather than individually, which reduces errors and ensures timely, accurate employee payments. The guide identifies two primary categories of issues that trigger the error: formatting problems and data problems. For formatting issues, the document instructs users to verify the CSV file structure matches the expected layout and specifically to check for blank lines at the end of the file by opening it in Notepad, navigating to the last row, using Backspace to remove extra blank lines, and saving before re-uploading. For data issues, users must validate that each rate of pay is linked to a valid employee number and ensure that any included appointment IDs are both valid and active for the listed employees. If these troubleshooting steps do not resolve the persistent error, the document directs users to raise a new support case online while referencing the article title and attaching both the problematic file and a screenshot of the error message. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage employee compensation data in bulk within their organization's payroll system.

t: Employer national insurance (NI ER) not considering benefit in kind (BIK) in calculations
s:
When processing payroll, it's essential that employer national insurance (NI ER) contributions accurately reflect all taxable benefits, including benefits in kind (BIK). If BIK values are missing from NI ER calculations, the issue is likely due to incorrect pay code configuration.

ss: Employer national insurance (NI ER) calculations may not include benefits in kind (BIK) values when pay codes are incorrectly configured in your payroll system. ss: Occupational absence entitlements in PeopleXD are automatically pro-rated based on FTE multiplier when staff work part-time hours. sl: This document explains how occupational absence entitlement—the amount of leave employees are entitled to take for situations such as sick leave or parental leave—is calculated and adjusted in the Access Group system. The resolution involves removing any selected value in the Entitlement Basis field and saving the changes. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators, HR managers, or system configurators who manage absence policies and need to ensure that part-time or full-time employees receive the correct entitlement calculations. s:

ss: PRSI refunds for previous tax years cannot be processed through the payroll system in PeopleXD—the system only handles current tax year PRSI refunds and does not support backdated refunds regardless of the timesheet transaction date recorded. Any PRSI refunds for prior years must be managed directly between the employee/employer and the Department of Social Protection outside of payroll. Processing these refunds via payroll is not recommended because it requires extensive manual amendments that increase the risk of errors. Open this document if you need to understand why a previous tax year PRSI refund cannot be completed in the system and where responsibility for handling it should lie.
sl: This document clarifies the limitations and recommendations for handling PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) refunds within the Access Group payroll system. It explains that PRSI refunds for previous tax years cannot be processed through payroll, as the system does not have functionality to support refunds dating back beyond the current tax year, regardless of the transaction date recorded on the timesheet. The document warns that if a timesheet is recorded for a refund, the Validation report will only display PRSI paid in the current tax year, and supplementary runs will not work for National Insurance (NI) arrears. It emphasizes that refunding PRSI via payroll is not recommended because it requires extensive manual amendments that may introduce errors into payroll records. Instead, the document advises that any PRSI refund should be handled as a matter between the employee or employer and the Department of Social Protection, managed entirely outside the payroll system. The document is designed for payroll administrators and finance professionals who need to understand the proper procedures and system limitations when employees or employers request PRSI refunds, particularly for prior tax years. It provides cross-references to related articles covering current-year PRSI refunds, manual PRSI/NI weeks overrides, and validation report issues to guide users to appropriate alternative solutions.

t: General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) not balancing
s:

We have compiled a list of possible causes for the PAYB236 report not balancing, along with steps to res...
ss: The General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) tracks payroll financial transactions and ensures they balance correctly within the general ledger. If your PAYB236 report is not balancing, this document outlines common causes including incorrect employer pension deductions entered through timesheets, missing balance sheet indicators, invalid or missing category codes, broken links between categories and pay codes, and unmapped pay codes. Use this guide when you discover discrepancies in your payroll posting to the general ledger and need to troubleshoot and resolve the imbalance. The document provides step-by-step corrections for each issue, from adjusting employee pension records in CorePay to escalating cases to support when database updates are required.
sl: The General Ledger journal report (PAYB236) is a critical payroll processing tool that ensures all financial transactions are accurately recorded and balanced within the general ledger, and this document provides systematic troubleshooting guidance for resolving instances when the report fails to balance. The document identifies and explains six primary causes of imbalance: ER deduction issues where employer pension adjustments entered through timesheets lack proper system linkage to pension schemes, reset indicator problems requiring navigation through CorePay > Update > General Ledger Interface > Generate General Ledger Interface to toggle the Balance Sheet Ind setting, missing category codes at the employee level that may require support team intervention if assigned after payroll closes, missing links between category codes, expense codes, and pay codes where the expense code must match the `gl_link` field value on the `gl_matrix` table, and pay codes not mapped to employee cost centers. For ER deduction issues, the document provides specific remediation paths depending on payroll completion status: if payroll is complete, the incorrect payment must be cancelled and reissued manually, but if incomplete, users can access either the Portal (Employee > VIEW > Pension) or Back Office (CorePay > Employee > Maintain Employee Pension) to delete the timesheet entry and properly enter the ER Pension adjustment. For issues requiring system-level updates—including missing category codes, missing links, and unmapped pay codes—users must raise a support case online, providing relevant details such as employee information, affected period, GL PDF report, payroll period, impacted company, and description of the discrepancy. This document is typically used by payroll administrators and finance teams who need to diagnose and resolve General Ledger reconciliation failures within their payroll processing systems.

t: Incorrect overtime calculation
s:
Accurate overtime calculation is crucial to ensuring fair compensation for employees who work beyond their standard hours. If the overtime is calculated incorrectly, it may be due to one of the following reasons.

 

We have compiled a list of potential issues that could lead to incorrect overtime c...
ss: Overtime calculations in Access Group's payroll system depend on three key settings: pay code multipliers, pay group pay periods, and employee FTE hours. If your employees' overtime pay appears incorrect, this document walks you through checking each of these components in Portal—including where to find pay code formulas, pay period configurations, and FTE hour records. Open this document when you've noticed discrepancies in overtime compensation and need to diagnose whether the issue stems from misconfigured multipliers (like 1.25 for overtime or 2.0 for double time), incorrect pay period day settings, or FTE hour mismatches. It's especially useful for salaried employees, as their overtime calculation requires dividing annual salary by specific pay group and FTE variables.
sl: This document provides guidance on diagnosing and resolving incorrect overtime calculations within a payroll system, addressing a common issue that affects employee compensation accuracy. The document identifies three primary areas to investigate: pay code multiplier settings, pay group pay period configuration, and employee FTE (Full-Time Equivalent) hours, each with specific step-by-step instructions accessible through the Portal interface. For pay code multiplier checks, users navigate to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes, search for the relevant pay code, access the three-dot menu, click Edit, and review the multiplier on the Pay Code Formula screen, with the guidance that multipliers should be set to 1.25 for overtime and 2.0 for double time. To verify pay group pay period settings, users follow the same initial navigation path to Settings > Codes > Pay Codes and check the pay period days and days in the year on the Edit screen. For FTE hours verification, users access the People Management Contract Screen or Payroll Employee Screen, and can validate calculations by entering 1 hour for the pay code and running payroll validation to review gross to net figures and the gross pay drilldown screen. The document includes an important formula note for employees on annual salary: (Annual Salary / Pay Group Days in Year) * (Pay Group Pay Period Days) / Employee FTE Hours, which determines the overtime rate calculation. This resource is designed for payroll administrators, HR professionals, and finance teams who need to troubleshoot and correct overtime calculation errors within their organization's payroll processing system.

ss: Control totals in your payroll system may not balance if you're using the wrong reports or if employee cumulative details weren't entered correctly. Always use the Complete Update controls from the final pay period to reconcile against the next period's totals, and avoid the validation control report since it changes when payroll is re-run. New employees added to the system should show amendments for previous Gross, Taxable, and PAYE amounts—if these are missing, the employee may have been set up incorrectly in CorePay's Maintain Employee Details screen. Open this document when your control totals aren't matching and you need to troubleshoot which report to use or how to properly record employee cumulative details.
sl: This document provides guidance for resolving control total balancing issues in a payroll system, specifically addressing problems that arise when control totals fail to match expected values. The document recommends using the Complete Update controls for the last pay period as the authoritative source for balancing against control totals for the next period, while advising users to avoid relying on the validation control report since it can change if the payroll is re-run. When new employees are added to the system, users should review detailed amendments to verify that previous cumulative details for Gross, Taxable amounts, and PAYE appear correctly; if the system shows only previous USC details without amendments for other fields, users are instructed to contact support with the employee number. The document identifies a common configuration error that occurs when employees are set up in the Maintain Employee Details screen with previous pay and tax information entered simultaneously, which prevents proper amendments from appearing. To correct this issue, the proper procedure involves first setting up the employee without previous cumulative details, then navigating to CorePay > Employee > Cumulatives and using either the Maintain Tax Details Future screen or uploading a tax certificate. This document is intended for payroll administrators and finance users who encounter control total discrepancies during payroll processing and need to diagnose whether the issue stems from reporting methodology, employee setup errors, or system configuration problems.

t: Set up a reducing balance allowance
s:
Before setting up a reducing balance allowance, you need to be aware of the following: 

A reducing balance allowance is setup with a capital sum that reduces each time it is paid by the employee. The capital sum can be set-up as a standard value or percentage-based.

The balance due is reduced by t...
ss: Setting up a reducing balance allowance in PeopleXD lets you create deductions that decrease over time from a set capital sum, paid out in regular installments until the balance reaches zero. You can configure this allowance either through the Portal (via Payroll Dashboard > Pay Codes) or the Back Office (via CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes), with the key requirement of setting a minus multiplier value and enabling the Reducing Balance toggle. This is useful when you need to deduct a fixed total amount from an employee's pay across multiple payroll periods—such as loans, advances, or other installment-based deductions. Note that the system calculates reducing balance deductions from the current or future period only, not retrospectively.
sl: This document provides a complete guide to setting up a reducing balance allowance in the PeopleXD system, which is a type of allowance that deducts from an employee's pay by reducing a capital sum with each payroll run until the balance reaches zero. The document explains the foundational concept that a reducing balance allowance requires both a capital sum (the total annual value to be deducted) and a periodic value or percentage assigned to the employee, with the balance automatically decrementing each payroll period until it reaches zero and the allowance ceases. It includes step-by-step instructions for setting up this allowance through two different interfaces: the Portal method (accessed via Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Pay Codes under Codes) and the Back Office method (accessed via CorePay > Reference > Pay Codes), both of which require creating or duplicating a pay code and configuring specific settings. Both setup methods require configuring the multiplier as a minus value (such as -1) on the General tab and enabling or selecting the Reducing Balance toggle or indicator on the Allowances/Payments tab before saving and completing employee-level setup. The document also highlights an important limitation: the system will not process retrospective arrears for a reducing balance pay code with a past date, and these allowances will only calculate from the current period or future start dates onward. This guide is typically used by payroll administrators and HR professionals in the Access Group system who need to implement allowances that systematically reduce an employee's entitlements over multiple pay periods.

sl: This document provides comprehensive instructions for loading new employee deduction details into the CorePay payroll system through the Portal interface, a process essential for maintaining accurate payroll management and ensuring compliance with tax and benefit regulations. The document specifies the exact CSV file format required, detailing seven fields (Employee number, Pay Code, Value, Account Reference, Capital Sum, Number of Deductions, Deductions Taken, and Percentage Rate) with their mandatory or optional status and maximum sizes, and clarifies which deduction types can be included, such as standard periodic value voluntary deductions, reducing balance voluntary deductions, percentage rate voluntary deductions, and installment voluntary deductions. Users follow a specific step-by-step process in Portal, starting from the Payroll Dashboard menu, navigating to Uploads > Load New Deduction Details, selecting the file type, entering End Date and Start Date fields (in DDMMYYYY format) for the old and new deductions respectively, providing a load reference (maximum 16 characters), and then browsing to locate and process the CSV file. The document addresses common validation errors and rejection scenarios, explaining that reducing balance deductions will be rejected with a "Not a Reducing Balance Pay Code" message if the Balance Due field is incorrectly associated, installment deductions will fail if Number Of Deductions and Deductions Taken fields don't match an installment pay code, and percentage rate deductions will be rejected if the Percentage Rate field is paired with a non-percentage rate pay code, all appearing on an exceptions report. Upon successful completion, the system generates either a control report or an exceptions report, and the document is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to update employee deductions to reflect changes in benefits or tax laws to ensure employees receive correct net pay and avoid regulatory penalties.

ss: The bulk allowance upload process lets you add or update multiple employee allowances at once using a CSV file instead of manually entering each record. Open this document when you're ready to streamline allowance updates for multiple employees or need guidance on the CSV file format and upload steps.
sl: This document explains how to use the bulk allowance upload feature in the Access Group payroll system, which is an optional tool designed to streamline payroll administration rather than a required processing step. The bulk upload functionality allows users to add multiple new allowance records or update existing ones simultaneously using a CSV file, eliminating the need to manually enter each employee's allowance information individually. The CSV file must be formatted with exactly four columns containing no headers and no blank columns: Employee number (mandatory), Pay code (mandatory), Standard value in decimal format to 2 places (mandatory), and Appointment ID (optional), with particular attention required to ensure no blank lines appear at the end of the file when saved in Notepad. Users can initiate the upload process at any time by navigating to Uploads > Employee Uploads > Load New Allowance Details in the portal, where they must specify both an End Date for the existing allowance record being replaced and a Start Date indicating when the new allowance should take effect. Once the CSV file is prepared and the dates are entered, users click the Load button to upload the file and then OK to save it. It is critical that all allowance changes be completed before payroll processing begins to ensure the system recognizes and applies the new or updated data correctly.

sl: This document provides a comprehensive checklist for UK employers setting up salary sacrifice schemes and determining how to pass employer national insurance (NIC) savings to employees, covering both the technical configuration and compliance considerations necessary for these arrangements. sl: This document provides comprehensive guidance on generating Third Party Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) files within the Access Group payroll system, enabling users to transfer deduction payments electronically to external organisations such as healthcare providers, credit unions, and pension schemes. The document outlines four main configuration and operational processes: configuring pay codes with bank account details and Third Party Returns rules via the Settings tab, configuring payment percentages and discounts on the Payroll Dashboard's Manage Payroll > Outputs > Third Party EFT section, extracting deduction data from payroll history into the Third Party EFT module for a specified period, and generating bank files for payment through the Generate/Reset tab. It addresses common scenarios such as the need to reset extracted data before making amendments and regenerating files, with an important warning that extracting data multiple times will overwrite all previously extracted information. For UK customers specifically, the document describes additional HMRC payment configuration including enabling the Inland Revenue Paypath indicator for statutory payments like PAYE and National Insurance contributions, and configuring recovery percentages for payments such as SMP, SAP, and SPP. ss: Use this guide when you need to issue a manual payment for a closed payroll period in PeopleXD's CorePay system. It covers the step-by-step process for entering mandatory fields (employee reference, payroll period, PAYE code, pay codes, and NI/PRSI details), ensuring cumulative records and FPS figures are updated correctly. ss: Redundancy and sporting testimonial payments require specific tax treatment in PeopleXD payroll, with different rules depending on whether payments fall under or over £30,000. To configure these payments in the system, users must navigate to the Portal's Settings section, access Pay Codes under the Codes menu, locate the relevant pay code, click the three-dot icon, select Edit, and then click Rules to add the taxable redundancy configuration from the dropdown menu before saving changes via the OK button. ss: When loading a new tax certificate or RPN in the payroll system, a duplicate LPT (Low Profit Threshold) deduction may be created instead of updating the existing one, especially if the previous deduction has an incorrect tax year. Open this article if you've discovered duplicate LPT deductions after uploading a new tax certificate or RPN, or if an employee's deduction amounts appear incorrect following a certificate update. sl: This document describes a specific issue that occurs in the Access Group payroll system when users load a new tax certificate or RPN (Revenue Program Number), where the system creates a new LPT (Local Property Tax) deduction without accounting for any existing LPT deductions that have already been applied. The problem typically arises when the tax year recorded on the old LPT deduction is incorrect, causing the system to fail to recognize and carry forward the previously deducted amount to the new deduction, which results in calculation errors and potential payroll inaccuracies. The document provides guidance for resolving this issue by instructing users to submit a new support case online, and specifies that they should reference the article title, provide the affected employee numbers, and identify the LPT pay code associated with the problematic deduction. This document is intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage tax deductions and handle RPN or tax certificate uploads within the Access Group system, particularly those who encounter discrepancies in local property tax deduction amounts after processing new tax documentation. ss: When a deduction fails to appear on an employee's payslip, the issue often stems from incorrect analysis type assignments in your pay code configuration. This document explains how to properly configure deduction pay codes by selecting the correct analysis codes—such as DN for statutory and voluntary deductions, TR for tax relief deductions like pensions, or EN for employer pension contributions. Open this guide if you're troubleshooting missing deductions in payroll processing or need to verify that your pay codes are using the appropriate analysis types to ensure deductions display correctly on payslips.
sl: This document addresses the issue of deductions failing to appear on employee payslips within the Access Group payroll system, explaining that the root cause is typically an incorrect analysis type assigned during pay code configuration. The guide emphasizes the critical rule that the Nett Pay analysis code should only be used for the nett pay pay code itself and must not be applied to any other pay codes, as this misconfiguration directly prevents deductions from displaying correctly. When setting up deduction pay codes, administrators must assign them an appropriate analysis code from the available options, which include GP (Gross Pay), BK (Benefit in Kind), NT (Non-Taxable), DN (Deduction for statutory and voluntary deductions), TR (Tax Relief for pension and AVC deductions), NP (Nett Pay), EN (Employer Pension), ER (Employer NI/PRSI), and AL (Apprentice Levy). The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who configure pay codes and troubleshoot payslip discrepancies, particularly when employees report missing deductions. Related resources mentioned include guidance on configuring payslip parameters and Insight views for Payroll, along with other related articles addressing similar payslip display issues such as Employee PRSI weeks overrides not showing and AVC deductions appearing incorrectly.

Users must then enter the desired number of periods in the Hold Periods field to specify how long the deduction should remain suspended before resuming normal processing. After entering the hold period duration, clicking Save finalizes the changes and puts the deduction on hold. The Deduction screen serves as the central tool for managing holds effectively, allowing users to adjust hold periods as needed to accommodate various employment scenarios and deduction management requirements.

ss: Loading new deduction details into PeopleXD Payroll via CorePay allows you to update employee tax withholdings, retirement contributions, and other deductions in bulk using a CSV file. This process is critical for maintaining payroll compliance and ensuring employees receive the correct net pay when benefits or tax laws change. The document covers the required file format (including mandatory fields like employee number and pay code), step-by-step loading instructions, and validation rules for different deduction types such as reducing balance, installment, and percentage rate deductions. sl: This document provides instructions for loading new employee deduction details into CorePay payroll system within PeopleXD Payroll to ensure accurate tax withholdings, retirement contributions, and compliance with regulatory requirements. The process requires preparing a CSV file with mandatory fields including Employee Number (10 alpha characters), Pay Code (4 numeric), and Value (up to 9999999999.99), along with optional fields such as Account Reference, Capital Sum, Number of Deductions, Deductions Taken, and Percentage Rate depending on the deduction type being loaded. The document specifies that the file must support four deduction types: standard periodic value voluntary deductions, reducing balance voluntary deductions, percentage rate voluntary deductions, and installment voluntary deductions. To load the file, users navigate to CorePay > Employee > Employee Deductions > Load Employee Deductions in the Back Office, then enter an End Date for old deductions (or the day before the start date for new deductions), a Start Date for new deductions, and a reference identifier in DDMMYYYY format not exceeding 16 characters before browsing to and processing the file. The system validates each record against its associated pay code type and generates an exceptions report for rejected records, such as when a reducing balance deduction is paired with a non-reducing balance pay code or an installment deduction lacks the required pay code configuration. This document is primarily used by payroll administrators and back office staff who need to bulk update employee deductions in response to changes in employee benefits or tax law requirements.

s:

ss: Student loan plans can continue deducting mid-payroll period even after receiving a stop notice from HMRC, requiring manual intervention to halt deductions immediately. This document covers how to update student loan deduction codes in your payroll system when you receive an SL2 or PGL2 stop notice and need to prevent further deductions. Open this article if you've received a stop notice from HMRC and want to understand when deductions will cease or how to adjust end dates to stop them before the next payday. It's essential reading if your student loan deductions aren't stopping as expected despite receiving official notification.
sl: This document provides guidance for updating student loan deduction codes in payroll systems when employers receive notices to stop student loan deductions. It addresses the specific scenario where an SL2 or PGL2 stop notice is received from HMRC, requiring employers to cease student loan deductions starting from the first available payday after the deduction stop date indicated on the notice, where "first available payday" is defined as the earliest payday when implementation is feasible. The document highlights a critical system behavior issue: if the end date falls within the current payroll period, the system will continue to deduct student loans automatically, which may not align with the stop notice requirements. To resolve this timing problem and ensure deductions stop immediately rather than continuing through the current payroll period, employers must manually adjust the end date in their payroll system. The guidance is primarily intended for payroll administrators and HR professionals who process HMRC stop notices and manage student loan deduction codes within their payroll software. The document references related topics including scenarios involving multiple concurrent student loans, year-end software changes for 2026/27, and the process for uploading student loan details, suggesting this is part of a broader set of student loan administration resources within the Access Group Help Centre.

ss: The PAYE Modernisation (PMOD) deletion file process handles canceled payments for deceased employees in payroll systems. If deletion files aren't generating, the issue is typically a stuck submission status—the original file remains PENDING instead of COMPLETED. This guide walks you through accessing the PAYE Modernisation screen in Back Office, running a check to move the submission to COMPLETED status, and then re-generating the deletion file for the canceled payment. Open this document when you're troubleshooting failed PMOD deletion files or need to manually complete a stalled submission in the payroll system.
sl: This document provides guidance on resolving issues with PAYE Modernisation deletion files that fail to generate for cancelled payments related to deceased employees within the Access Group's payroll system. The core problem addressed is when deletion files are not automatically generated, which occurs when the original submission file maintains a PENDING status instead of a COMPLETED status. The resolution process involves navigating through the Back Office interface by selecting Manage Payroll, highlighting the relevant pay group, then accessing Outputs followed by ROS and PAYE Modernisation. Within the PAYE Modernisation screen, users select "Transfer Submission Files" from the Select PAYE Action drop-down menu and then click "Run Check" if the submission status shows as PENDING. This check must be repeated until the submission status changes to COMPLETED for all valid payslips associated with the original submission. Once the status has been updated to COMPLETED, users must re-generate and transfer the submission file for the cancelled payment to ensure the deletion file is properly created. This document is intended for payroll administrators and Back Office users who manage PAYE submissions and need to process cancellations for deceased personnel within their organisation.

ss: Deduction pay codes in CorePay can be configured to post the employee's cost centre (rather than the pay code's default cost centre) to the general ledger by enabling the Timesheet Override indicator. Use this feature when you need deduction transactions to reflect the cost centre from an employee's timesheet instead of a fixed pay code assignment. sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre provides guidance on configuring deduction pay codes to ensure an employee's cost centre posts correctly to the general ledger during payroll processing. The document explains that by enabling the Timesheet Override indicator on a pay code's Deductions tab, the system will use the cost centre from the employee's timesheet rather than the cost centre assigned to the pay code itself, allowing for more accurate cost centre allocation. The specific process requires users to navigate through Back Office by clicking CorePay, then Reference, then Pay Codes, querying the desired pay code, and locating the Deductions tab where the Timesheet Override check box must be selected and saved using the save icon. This configuration is particularly useful for resolving scenarios where cost centres are not appearing on the GL as expected or where the wrong cost centre is being output during deduction pay code processing. The document addresses common issues including cost centres not outputting as expected on the general ledger, situations where "No Centre" appears on the View History Details screen instead of the employee's home cost centre, and GL matrix errors related to missing expense configurations for specific pay codes. This document is typically used by payroll administrators, finance teams, and Back Office users who need to configure pay codes and ensure accurate cost centre posting for employee deductions.

t: Enhanced Holiday Pay annual leave dates
s:
Enhanced Holiday Pay allows you to calculate holiday pay based on average earnings. You can record annual leave, generate calculations, and view pay history.

 

If you use Enhanced Holiday Pay, you need to update your annual leave start and end dates each year. This ensures that the system applies ...
ss: Enhanced Holiday Pay calculates holiday pay based on average earnings, but requires you to update your annual leave start and end dates each year to ensure the correct entitlement period is applied. The system provides a 12-month grace period during which dates roll forward automatically, but if you don't update them within this window, it will continue deducting from the previous year's entitlement, causing employees to exhaust holidays incorrectly and requiring manual payment corrections. Open this document if you need to update your holiday year dates in the Payroll Dashboard, or if you're experiencing issues with employees' holiday balances or Enhanced Holiday Pay calculations referencing the wrong year. Update your dates in the Pay Group Parameters tab during the first or second pay period of your new holiday year to prevent processing errors.
sl: This document explains the Enhanced Holiday Pay feature in the Access Group system, which calculates holiday pay based on average earnings and requires annual maintenance of entitlement dates. The core process involves navigating to Payroll Dashboard > Settings > Enhanced Holiday Pay > Pay Group Parameters tab, where users must update the annual leave start date and annual leave end date fields for each pay group to reflect the current holiday year. The system operates with a 12-month grace period that automatically rolls forward entitlement dates by one year, allowing employees to transition smoothly between holiday years—for example, automatically switching from 2024 to 2025 entitlements—but this automatic roll-forward only functions once, meaning a second manual update is required to prevent the system from incorrectly deducting from outdated entitlements. Failing to update these dates causes critical processing errors, including employees exhausting their holiday entitlement incorrectly, Enhanced Holiday Pay calculations referencing the wrong entitlement year, and the need for manual payment corrections. Users should perform this update during the first or second pay period of their new holiday year, though the system allows up to 12 months from the end of the old holiday year to make the change. The document is designed for payroll administrators and HR professionals who manage Enhanced Holiday Pay in their organization and need to ensure accurate holiday entitlement tracking and payment calculations across multiple pay groups.

sl: This document provides guidance for preparing non-production environments ahead of Payroll Year End processing, specifically covering environment cloning and backup procedures. Before requesting a clone, users must verify internally whether other teams use UAT, whether any projects are in progress, and whether non-Production data exists that should be preserved, as these factors may make cloning inappropriate. t: P60 NI Figure does not match March payslip
s:
When the P60 figure differs from the March payslip, check whether there was a break in the employee’s service. The P60 reflects only the National Insurance (NI) contributions for the current period of employment.

 

For example, if the employee left in April and rejoined in May, the P60 will only d...
ss: P60 figures can differ from March payslips when an employee has had a break in service, as the P60 only reflects National Insurance contributions for the current employment period. If an employee left and rejoined within the same tax year, the P60 shows NI only from their return date, while the payslip may show the full year's total depending on your system settings. Open this article if your P60 NI amounts don't match what appears on the March payslip, or if you need to adjust how National Insurance is displayed across multiple employment periods. You'll learn how to enable the Multiple Periods of Employment toggle in Company Parameters to control whether payslips show partial or full-year NI contributions.
sl: This document addresses discrepancies between P60 National Insurance figures and March payslip amounts, particularly in situations involving breaks in employee service. The P60 form displays NI contributions only for the current continuous period of employment, whereas the payslip may show the full tax year NI total (April to March) depending on system configuration. The document explains that if an employee left and rejoined during the same tax year—for example, departing in April and returning in May—the P60 will only reflect contributions from the return date onwards. To resolve this discrepancy, users must navigate to Settings > Company Parameters > General Settings within the portal and select the appropriate company code from the dropdown menu. The document then instructs users to click Next and enable the "Multiple Periods of Employment" toggle to allow the system to display cumulative NI contributions across multiple employment periods on payslips. Changes must be saved by clicking the Save button to take effect. This guidance is primarily used by payroll administrators and HR professionals who need to reconcile P60 figures with payslip records and configure system settings to accurately reflect employee NI contributions across interrupted employment terms.

t: Who can defer their State Pension Contributory
s:
Individuals who qualify to defer their State Pension Contributory are those born on or after January 1st, 1958. They can claim the Contributory State Pension between ages 66 and 70. 

 

However, once you begin claiming your Contributory State Pension, you can no longer choose to defer your pension ...
ss: State Pension Contributory deferral eligibility applies to individuals born on or after January 1st, 1958, who can delay their pension claim between ages 66 and 70. Once you begin claiming your Contributory State Pension, deferral is no longer an option, even if you continue working, because PRSI contributions stop upon pension receipt. Open this document if you need to understand who qualifies to defer their State Pension, the age window for deferral decisions, and the permanent nature of claiming once you start receiving payments.
sl: This document from the Access Group Help Centre outlines eligibility criteria and key constraints for deferring State Pension Contributory benefits. It specifies that individuals born on or after January 1st, 1958 are eligible to defer their State Pension Contributory and have the option to claim between ages 66 and 70. The document clarifies an important limitation: once an individual begins claiming their Contributory State Pension, they can no longer choose to defer their pension claim, regardless of whether they continue working. This restriction exists because PRSI (Pay Related Social Insurance) payments cease once pension payments commence, preventing further deferral options. The document serves as a reference guide for pension administrators, HR professionals, and individuals managing State Pension claims within the Access Group system who need to understand deferral eligibility and the permanent nature of the claiming decision. Related functionality in the system includes processes for deferring the start date of State Pension Contributory and PRSI Class Automation, which are referenced as connected topics for users seeking more comprehensive pension management information.

ss: Deferring your State Pension Contributory allows you to delay claiming your pension between ages 66 and 70, giving you flexibility in when to start receiving payments. sl: This document explains the new State Pension Contributory deferral option available from January 2024, which allows individuals aged 66 to 70 to choose when to begin claiming their pension within that age range. The State Pension Contributory is available to those who are at least 66 years old and have made sufficient Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI) contributions, specifically requiring a minimum of 520 contributions equivalent to 10 years of service. The document outlines three primary reasons individuals might consider deferring their pension start date: the ability to continue working and contributing to PRSI during the deferral period, which can increase their personal rate of payment or help them meet the 520-contribution qualifying threshold; the opportunity to become eligible for State Pension if they did not qualify at age 66; and the potential to receive a higher State Pension rate by waiting rather than claiming at 66. The document is designed for pension administrators, HR professionals, and system users working with the Access Group payroll or pension management system who need to understand and implement this deferral functionality. Related topics covered include guidance on employees assessed but postponed for auto-enrolment who wish to start their pension earlier, general State Pension Contributory information, and PRSI Class Automation configuration, all of which provide context for managing pension deferrals within the broader pension administration framework.

t: Manage corrections during year end process
s:
This explains how to process payroll corrections when the year end cleardown job affects your payroll data. Following these procedures ensures that payroll corrections are applied correctly and maintains data integrity during the year end transition period.

 

You should apply these procedures when...
ss: Managing payroll corrections in your system requires different approaches depending on where you are in the year end cycle—before the last tax period closes, after it closes but before year end cleardown, or after cleardown completes. This document outlines which correction methods (supplementary runs, cancel payments, manual payments) are allowed at each stage, since timing significantly impacts what you can do and your reporting requirements. Open this guide when you've discovered payroll errors that need correcting and need to understand whether you can process them immediately or must wait until after the year end cleardown job runs. The procedures differ for Ireland (December/January tax year) and the UK (March/April tax year).
sl: This document provides guidance on how to manage and process payroll corrections within the Access Group payroll system when they are affected by the year end cleardown job, ensuring data integrity is maintained throughout the year end transition period. The document addresses the critical timing issue that corrections must follow different procedures depending on whether they are discovered before or after the year end cleardown job is executed, and it outlines the specific allowable correction actions at each stage of the year end process. Before the last period of the tax year is closed (December for Ireland, March for the UK), users can perform supplementary runs for the last closed period and process cancel and manual payments as normal. After the last period closes but before year end cleardown runs, supplementary runs for the final tax year period are permitted, but cancel and manual payment processing are restricted until after cleardown completes. Following the year end cleardown execution, in the first period of the new tax year (January for Ireland, April for the UK), users may cancel and process manual payments for any previous period, though supplementary runs are not available since no previous period exists within the new tax year. After the first period of the new tax year has been completed, both supplementary runs for the previous period and standard cancel and manual payment processing become available again. The document references related articles including procedures for canceling year end cleardown status on UAT or Live environments, required reports before supplementary runs, pre-year end data checks, and comprehensive year end FAQs to support users through the full correction and cleardown process.

sl: This document provides guidance on reconciling pre year end reports as part of the payroll year end process in the Access Group system. The core task involves comparing three key reports: the pre year end data check report, the employee cumulatives (all) (PAY084B) report, and the final control report (PAY355CT), reconciling them for each pay group across the company. The document specifies four main reconciliation checks: current taxable plus previous P45 taxable must equal taxable pay less pension on the final control report; current PAYE plus previous P45 taxable must equal PAYE on the final control report; NIC EE all employment must equal NI employee on the final control report; and NIC ER all employment must equal NI employer on the final control report. It clarifies important technical distinctions, such as that taxable pay figures on the pre year end data check report are net of pension (aligned with P35 and P60 returns), while the employee cumulatives and final control reports combine current and previous employment figures rather than splitting them. The document also addresses reconciliation of the pre year end statutory pay report by comparing the other statutory all employments report to figures on the detailed observation report for relevant pay codes, and notes that post year end taxable pay figures (including P60s) are always whole numbers, requiring allowance for rounding when reconciling totals.
